title: Ben Johnson on emphasizing growth throughout offseason | Press Conference
text: Just want to piggyback on what Ryan said about thank you to the organization, McCaskey family, front office, really the whole support staff. This this place is phenomenal. We're we're in tip-top shape and every coach, every player, they have every resource that they could ever need to to get better over the next 6 weeks and and really for the whole season. So, we're really excited about that. Speaking of excitement, few things about training camp that just get me get me going. The first one is our team, obviously. This is uh This is our chance to forge our identity and you know, a lot of coaches come up and they say we're going to be this, we're going to be that and the other and and yet this is where it all all happens. This is we got a whole different group of guys than we did a year ago and and this is where it gets fun is call it half the roster was here, half the roster's new. There's a lot of getting to know each other and yet you know, it's it's a chance for us to create a new chapter of Chicago Bears football, the 2026 version. So, excited about that, excited about the competition that's going to unfold as well. You just talked to Ryan about some particular spots where that might occur, but for each player it's it's an opportunity to earn a spot on the roster, it's a spot to earn a role. Um Could be a starting spot, could be depth piece. Of course, we know special teams plays a huge part of that as well. So, for for us as coaches and personnel staff, I know we're we're really going to be having our lens out and evaluating each and every single day. And then finally, I'm really I'm really excited about this coaching staff. The continuity that we have is a little bit unique in the NFL right now. You look around, there's 30-plus new play callers in the NFL and fortunately here we we were able to have a lot of the same faces come back and and with that I really expect another layer of sophistication to occur within this building and and with our players. Um Um I've already felt it over the course of the spring time. Uh I feel it right now getting ready for training camp. Uh there's things a year ago we're trying to speak the same language. Now we're we're past that and everyone's kind of reading each other's thoughts. And so um on with the the the elementary is a thing of the past and we we can level things up as a coaching staff as well. So it's a really exciting time to to be here and with that I'll go ahead and open it up. >> And with the success and the momentum that was built last year, what in your mind are the ingredients to sustaining it going forward? I know last year's in the past, but how do you >> Yeah, it it starts all over again. And and we talked about this when last year ended. Um it's a brand new group of guys. We're in a race right now to develop the same chemistry that we had a year ago. I felt that was one of the things that was our secret sauce was guys playing for each other. We had a really close-knit group and and here it is. This is a this is the time of year where you stay in a hotel or you go on the road for some joint practices like we'll do later on in camp and and uh we got to come together as a group. And there'll be some trials and tribulations. Uh coaching staff, we're going to apply pressure and stress on these guys. I think that's where uh the best version of yourself comes forward. And so um yeah, I don't think there's you talk about sustaining success Well, shoot, we're starting all over again. That's been the consistent message. >> Ryan talked about the hunter's mentality. How do you describe that to your players? What that what that requires? >> Oh man, that's for team meetings. We we keep that there. Yeah. >> And with with Caleb [clears throat] kind of the things that are kind of top of your checklist for maybe that might not have been on last year's checklist now that there's a little more comfort [clears throat] in the system. >> Yeah, yeah, he and I were just talking yesterday about that is you know, I I have this urges an offensive guy to want to continue to evolve and uh you can say innovate and push the limits a little bit. And yet at the same time at the back of my mind, what's what's best for him is to continue to bank some of these reps. He said two offseasons and one training camp so far in a full season, obviously, um to where he's had a lot of the similar concepts repeat for him, and now we're at the point where he's not thinking about the play call, he's not thinking about the cadence, the motion, and all the the jigmaroo before the snap. Things are starting to slow down. And so, what we need to see here in camp is that anticipation take it up a notch. Um I think with that the coverage recognition gets taken up another notch. I think there's other ways we're going to continue to challenge and push him, more of which are going to happen post snap. Last year we talked about that pre-snap operation quite a bit. Feel a lot better about that this time of year um than we did. And so, now we're just moving on to the next stage. >> Do you feel uh differently >> and the continuity that you guys have, will camp look different? >> Uh yeah, I mean every camp looks different. I mean, the way it's laid out in terms of having these two away joint practices, particularly week two and week three, it it is going to be different. Um I'm I'm excited about that though. I think it's a great chance for our team to come together. Uh you know, when you go on the road in particular, there there's there's really not family, there's it's you, it's your buddies, it's the hotel, and you know, I think it's a great a great opportunity for us to bond together. So, um >> [snorts] >> that'll be different, but I mean, the pillars all stay the same. I mean, it's going to be a a physical, it's going to be a tough, it's going to be a demanding uh ordeal. Anything worth doing is is going to be challenging. Um these guys all know that, and I I think they embrace it as well. >> Now that you've had time to to really spend with Caleb over the last really year and a half, what what are you What do you need to see from Caleb this season? >> Oh, shoot. Um I mean, it's he's got it all, Stacy. He There There's really nothing I don't think that he can't do. It's just it it elite arm talent, um play making ability, escape ability, um you know, he he has his legs that he can hurt a defense with. I mean, there's just so many layers to who he is as a player. I think that that word consistency comes up over the course of a 60-minute game or more if we need it to where we're playing high-level quarterback play throughout that game. I mean, you see flashes of it and and yet we're trying to tap into that where we're just consistently um delivering the ball where it needs to go, giving it to our guys around us, and then we all know that he has that that ability to put on that Superman cape when when the time calls for it. >> Do you feel [clears throat] any differently Do you feel any differently about the left tackle position >> today than you did on this day last summer? >> Um I would say I I've got a better feel for our guys. I mean, there's a number of them that were here last year. You know, Jedrick's really the new face, so um I I feel better about uh Braxton in terms of his health and his his outlook, so I feel like he he's got another um another step up in terms of his confidence level than than he did a year ago at this time. Uh you know, I I Theo was a guy last year I didn't know a whole lot about. I've got I got high hopes for Theo as a as a player in this league as well. I mean, I can go on and on and on. So, I I know those guys a lot better and and I think another year of mentorship under um Dan Roushar and Kyle Shanahan is going to do nothing but but help all of them play better. >> What's been your message to Kyler Gordon? >> Get healthy. >> And with the uncertainty of of when he'll be available to you, what's your vision for fortifying the depth there so that you have options? >> Yeah, we'll we'll see. I mean, we got we're we stocked back up in that DB room again, and we'll see how it all plays out and and you know, there'll be certain players that certainly flash here, and we'll give them opportunities to run with the ones Um, you know, while while Kyler's out, and we'll we'll see where it goes from there. But, we have a lot of options from from rookies all the way to some of these veteran players, the uh free agents that we brought in. Uh I think we're going to we're going to have a healthy competition in that room. >> Coach, I know you've talked about building the offensive system around the players that you have. But, with another year of player acquisition, another year of player development, are you closer to what your ideal version of football looks like? >> Uh I think you're always striving to to reach a Yeah, re- re- I talked about those buzzwords before. You want when the tape comes on to be a physical, a sound, a poised group. Um each year you try to define that for your guys and and uh see how close you can come to to put that on tape on a consistent basis. And so, um we we got a high level of talent on this roster. I'm not I'm not concerned about that at all. I'm more concerned about how we come together as a group right now. >> A couple more, please. >> Kyler, you wanted him to be a little more efficient and higher completion percentage, things like that. What are the different factors [snorts] of that equation that you're looking for? Like the specifics that will lead to that for him? >> Well, I mean, I think fundamentally he he's done a great job over the spring and summer just looking at himself body position wise, um from an accuracy standpoint, are my feet aligned to to where I want to throw the ball? Um and I think that's the time of year that you do that. And then, when you get into to the uh bullets flying and we we got uh full speed reps here with with over speed, I think that's where the uh the ability to see where I should go with the football, the process a little bit faster. That's that's what I'm hopeful for is that we see another step in terms of the processing speed um because we do have these banked reps at this point. >> Is the 70% still the >> It's it's always going to be the goal, guys. It's always going to And that's going to be every quarterback in this league, always. 70%. You're going to have a darn good offense if if your quarterback's completing 70% of his balls. >> When you watched all the incompletions, like what was that exercise like for you and him? fun. >> [laughter] >> Yeah, now I mean it it's it's good. It's good. Cuz I mean there's a number of times for me as well. It's like I I need to He's having to throw the ball away and you're like, well, shoot, I didn't give him a a good opportunity there on that one. And so um you know, that's why I talked about in the springtime us as a staff, we got to continue do the best we can to get the primary receiver open. That makes his job a little bit easier. Um >> and then he's going to do his part and elevate his game as well. So it it's a balancing act. We're all going to be better this year in a lot of ways than than what we were. >> Last two, Dan and Steve. >> And I guess I'll stick with the primary receiver conversation since you brought it up a handful of times throughout the offseason. What specifically didn't meet your expectations in terms of your ability to get that guy more regularly >> I I mean it it's it's Listen, it's it's almost impossible to do it every single snap. And yeah, we take a lot of pride as a coaching staff to uh put our homework in and and and study the defense and figure out where we could, you know, was it to get access or attack a certain player matchups, whatever that is. Um and I just felt like we could we could take that up another notch. That's uh without any state secrets getting out of there. It's That's the gist. >> What about you, Ben? Any Where are you at in your evolution as a head coach? Anything you feel different in doing look >> Still feels like I'm drinking out of a fire hose, if that's what you mean. Um But I did it's it's like I alluded to a year ago. I mean, I got a great staff around me. Um I continue to learn from them. I mean, every day DA says something to me that that's uh gold nugget. Richard Smith, same thing. Bill Johnson, we we've got all these veteran coaches and uh you know, a guy like Harry Freed with the game management. I mean, we I think we took a step forward in that department here this offseason. Uh I got to spend a lot of time with Coach Hightower in the special teams room. So, you know, I I always think as the head coach you're trying to bring all three phases together the best you can on game day and I'm hopeful that I'll I'll be able to do that better this year.

title: Ryan Poles excited about talented roster | Press Conference
text: Welcome back. Hope everyone had a good break. Uh is ready to roll. So, I do want to start off um by sending our thoughts and prayers to Eric Bieniemy. They mean a lot to us here. Obviously going through some hard times. So, I want to make sure I start off by saying that. Um You know, as we start training camp, I want to thank our crew here um that set up campus. Obviously, it's a lot of work to to get this thing going. And plus, we had the storms yesterday. So, there's a little bit of cleanup underway to get it started. Um And as I think about campus, too, the other topic is just thanking George and the McCaskey family, Kevin, uh for their support in our football team. Um You guys will notice we got two brand new fields on three and four. Totally resided. Make sure our players are in good, you know, on good surface. And um you'll also notice the state-of-the-art film setup that we have on all the fields. Again, making sure that our coaches have the film right after practice so we can get to work. Um Obviously excited to to kick the season off with training camp. I think there's some really good competition on our roster. And obviously, when you have competition, uh you get growth, you get development. Um And you get to find out what you what you have on your football team as we prepare for this upcoming season. Uh In terms of the injuries, uh want to go through the designations. So, T.J. Edwards is going to be NFI. Um he's got a right calf. Um he was training off offsite, came back in with a sore calf, soft tissue. We don't see that as anything major. Um shouldn't be too long with that. Uh Keshawn Elliott um has some discomfort in his back. Uh we took care of that. Um he's in a really good shape. If you saw him walking around, you would have no idea. He's running. Obviously, there's a return-to-play uh protocol where you're getting back to be a football player in terms of your strength, your conditioning. Um so, he'll be in that. Um, Kyler Gordon on PUP uh with his calf. Um, he was here all off-season training uh getting right. Um, we had a delay in that. Um, all hands on deck to get him back. Um, coach alluded to it uh before in terms of his availability. Um, or the lack thereof. Um, obviously, he's frustrated. We're frustrated. We just want him back. He helps our football team. Um, but we have to move forward with with the guys that we have. And when he's ready to go, he'll be ready to go. Um, everybody here is is putting all their time and effort to get him back right. So, that's where that's at. Elijah Hicks has some discomfort in in his shin. We got that taken care of. Um, so, that's going to take a little bit of time. But, he's on the mend. He's walking around. We don't see that as anything major. Um, and then our guys that had surgery. Uh, Noah Sewell, um, he's rehabbing. On his way back, but he'll be PUP. Uh, Aussie's doing a great job. He's working his butt off. Um, he looks good. So, he he's uh working to get again back into being a football player again. And then lastly, Shammar Turner. Um, he's working to get back as well. He did some really good work this off-season. He's starting to move around really well. Um, again, I don't have timelines for all these guys, but they're they're on their way back. So, I'll open up to questions. >> Can you give a a minimum amount of time you expect Kyler to miss here at the start of camp? >> I don't. I really don't know. Um, he's got to get right. And I think the important thing that we've all talked about is when he gets back, we need him to stay back. >> You mentioned the frustration factor obviously on both sides with Kyler [snorts] Gordon and you guys. Has he done everything that you guys have wanted him to do as far as rehabbing and getting better? >> Yeah, like I said, uh I think he gave up a lot this break to stay here and and put the time in. Um, that's what he did. and again, a little bit of a repetitive situation that we got to get fixed. And then when he gets back, he's going to have to earn that trust back and that dependability. So, you know, cuz we got to put all the guys in a good position to be successful. And the up and down moving the guys around is is really tough. So, he'll have to earn that back when he gets back. >> Considering how long this has gone on for him, has there been some type of disconnect between him and the team at some point to explain why this [clears throat] is >> Yeah, I think that's the frustrating thing is I think the communication um in terms of the plan our guys have put together has been on point, but it's it's just hasn't stuck. So, again, we're turning every stone to get that thing right. >> When you get you talked about him being here late in the off-season, he he didn't show up on time for the off-season program. Is it >> You talking about last year? >> Yeah, does he need more consistency from him? >> Yeah, this year's been consistent. Like I said, he stayed here the whole whole break trying to get right. Um, we got to keep that uh consistent as we move forward. >> Well, one guy you did not mention was Dao. How encouraging has it been to see him? What did What did you see from him in the spring? >> Yeah, Dao did a great job with his return to play. I think it's always good if you can get one of the guys who was injured in the season to be in that vet mini camp, at least, where they can start I think the part that we don't talk about enough is just getting your confidence back as a football player. There's some balance and body control things when it starts moving, where it's more reactive than proactive. So, he was able to get that phase in and then add another 5-6 weeks of of training, so it's really positive. Um, obviously we'll keep an eye on him as we go, but really encouraging encouraged by not only his work that he put into it, but our staff and pouring it to him to get him right. >> We've talked to you about the pass rush all off-season. How important is Dao's development during camp for you and and whether you weigh can you add, should you add? >> Yeah, I think really the development of all those guys is going to be really important. You know, Sweat, I like to see him continue to to improve and and take what he did last year and add to that. You know, we don't talk about Booker. Like, last off season, he was coming on strong before he had a little bit of an injury there that kind of set him back, but he was able to kind of help us down the stretch. So, he's another guy we're taking eye on. So, I don't think it's different than any part of the roster. We're going to evaluate and see how they do. And then if we got to make adjustments or obviously investigate what where we can get better, we'll do that. >> That's not a That's not a decision you plan to make any time >> [snorts] >> in the couple of weeks. That's more of a trade at the end of the camp. >> Yeah, well, I've told you all for last four or five years, well, we're going to investigate any opportunities to get better. But, at the end of the day, we got to make sure we know our our team. So, we evaluate on a daily basis and and see what we need to do. >> With the few veterans that are out there on the end, I know how do you decide whether that's a fit not only for you, but for them, too? I imagine that some of these major household names that might not be comfortable with a very with a smaller role. Do you know what I mean? >> Yeah, I mean, we can cross that bridge if we ever needed to to go across it, but um yeah, everybody, you know, we're looking for competition, guys to come in and compete and and really fall into the role to help us win football games. >> You mentioned a couple times the growth you saw from Caleb last season as a professional. What was most notable to you about the strides you saw him take? >> I think what we saw down the stretch is like the desire to win. The desire to win. And I and I think we'll see development in all those, you know, other areas, uh the technical areas, um understanding the offense, defense. Um Ben's done a great job with him and I I expect him to continue to develop, but I think at the end of the day, we want our guys to have a strong desire to find a way to win football games. And and that was clear to me. >> As you've watched him and Ben grow together, what's been the reason in your eyes that that relationship has worked the way it has? >> They both want to be great and win Super Bowls, and that's all that matters. >> How does your perspective change at this time of year when you go from being the hunter to the hunted in the division and does that alter anything you do? >> No, I think it's important to have the mindset that you're always hunting. Um and that's what we're going to do. I'm sure coach will talk about our mentality as we move forward, but um we're going to be hunting at all times. >> As you head into this season, is there any position group that you look looking at that you saw last year and said, "We nailed it in this off season. That's exactly where we wanted to improve and we were able to do that." >> Uh you know, I feel really good about the competition across our roster. I've learned being in this league long enough that you know, to sit here and feel comfortable today could change tomorrow. Um so we stay on edge for all of these positions cuz you might be deep today and you might be thin tomorrow. So we're just going to keep at it. Um so I don't think I'll ever feel comfortable with with anything. So um but I love the competition that we have across the board. >> How are you looking at K'Lavon Chaisson? What do you want to see out of him in this camp and heading into year three for him? >> Yeah, I'll just keep it broad, just to continue to get better. Um you know, be a master of his craft. Um if he does that, we'll be in good shape. >> How are you How are you looking at the left tackle competition? >> Yeah, it's it's going to be a great competition. Um I think, you know, we got Braxton in a really good spot, probably the healthiest he's been since his first year. Um so he's going to compete and he's got a lot of snaps under his belt. Um Theos has done a great job, like see what he's done with his body this off season and he's just continues to get bigger, stronger, faster, um understand what we're trying to do. Uh I was really encouraged by Jawaan Taylor and his progress that he's made. I think he's put over double-digit lean mass on his body, which was something we were looking forward to as he gets to getting back to what he was. Um so that whole group and then, you You Ozzy's working his tail off. So you know, we get a couple layers to that and we'll see how it all plays out. And Crown, Crown as well. >> Ryan, what's the uniqueness of Garrett and then Logan behind him and how you how you kind of envision your centers? >> Yeah, you have a guy with a ton of NFL experience. just played in a Super Bowl. I think he's one of those glue guys for offensive line that brings everyone together. Um has a ton of knowledge and wisdom on how to play the position, especially with the young quarterback behind him. Um and then Logan's hungry, he's got great football character, strong uh from a physical standpoint, is in a really good place, but obviously he's a young center, you know, this game's a lot different at this level. but we expect again competition there um as we go, but really happy with with how Bradbury's been going about his business. >> Uh when you talk about Caleb's intensity and desire to win and how encouraging that is to you, have you seen a connection between that and his understanding of how important just mastering some of the basics and some of the less exciting parts of the job are to those goals? >> Yeah, and again, I'll let you hit that with with coach cuz he sees it closer than than I do, but um I think anytime these guys mature, they start to realize um what the work looks like and those small little details matter uh when you show up on game day. Um and again, I expect him to continue to grow in that area. >> Ryan, we're at a point now in your roster development where you have you know, veteran guys [snorts] already in place, but you also start to acquire younger players for the future. You look at the depth at center, like say if you just asked you look at tight end, maybe linebacker. How do you evaluate that process in terms of when the time may come to transition to the younger guys? >> Yeah, it goes back to competition. Um we're going to let it play out and see where they're at. Um obviously, you know, if the young guys haven't played a lot of football before, it's going to take a little bit of time to understand what this game's all about, but we just we we look at the competition and and how that stacks up and if guys are separating themselves or not. Um it's always a tough call. Again, when you haven't played NFL snaps, um it's very different than even the preseason. So, you know, I think what's really important at this time is being really good evaluators of your own roster. Um so, we got to be honed in on that and that's coach and I talking through this whole process. >> All right. With with your desire to to keep Darnell as a kind of core piece for you going forward, what is the next frontier for him and his growth as a as a tackle? >> Yeah, I think it's just consistency. Um we all see the the the flashes and and and the stacks of plays that he puts together and it's really impressive. Um can he be consistent day in and day out? Um that's the key part for Darnell. >> Is that a deal that you would like to get done sooner than later with Darnell, right? >> Uh I think there's a window to get a deal done and and then, you know, at some point we got to go play football. Um so, we'll we'll figure that part out. but I see I I think I've said it before, Darnell's a guy we want here long-term. it takes two sides to get things done. Um but at the end of the day, I don't want any distractions or anything like that. So, when it's time to go play football, we'll go play football and and keep it moving, but um yeah, he's a guy we would like here for a while. >> I'm >> Last one, Pat. >> Uh Ryan, we talked to Pat about Luther Burden and his excitement about Burden in the off season. Uh from what you evaluated in college and from where you think his ceiling is, >> how far along is he? What more is there for him to do? >> Yeah, we we got to go play games and he's got to, you know, finish this thing off, but if there's a guy that I'm really excited about, it's Luther Burden because of his just how much he's grown from the day he walked in this building. Um I mean, he was I heard he was just texting and calling these quarterbacks just looking for an to throw to him every day of the week. The guy loves football. He's passionate about it. Um He wants to help this team win and he wants to be the absolute best receiver he can possibly be. And uh you can feel the fire um inside of him and and uh I'm excited to see that that show up.

title: Roy Lopez | Training Camp 7.28.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: Are you known around these parts as Mr. Arizona? Is that what I'm gathering? >> Uh no, but I saw they gave that uh title to Cole Pepper. Shout out Cole Pepper, man. That's That's so cool. I can't wait to >> [snorts] >> wear wear a Pete jersey to the to the stadium, man. So, that's cool. >> What do you remember just cuz you brought it up? What do you remember about him playing basketball in the valley and then in Arizona? >> I've heard about him since he was a little kid, man. The whole family. I've heard about their whole family. Uh I got to play against Andres last year and uh Yeah, man. The whole whole family that's a legendary family, man. Legendary last name, for sure. >> I don't think [snorts] it applies like the whole group is talented. >> They're They're stacked. They're all tall and you know, big-boned, man. They're Yeah, so now I've known them for a long time. They've known me and my family for a long time, as well. So, it's really cool to see him get drafted. You know, when he got drafted it was like one of my one of my family members getting drafted, man. It's all in our group chat and everybody was proud and happy. So, great pick. Great pick. >> You going to rock that jersey to the game at some point? >> I will. I will. I'll be rocking the Pete jersey, for sure. >> Uh Roy, [snorts] what how's it being back and just being back home full-time now? >> Yeah, it's a blessing, man. It's really cool. Just to be around the guys, um the new guys, the same guys, um and just kind of laughing about everything, you know, and and cuz, you know, at the end of the day they are your teammates and people you work with, but um they truly are your best friends, right? And so, to come back and see everybody smile and walking in the building has been has been great since day one, since the moment um the news came out and um here we are in camp and um it's a blessing. >> What are you liking about this new coaching staff? >> Yeah, I think everybody's on the same page, man, of just the mindset we need to have going forward, you know, and and we hear everybody. And um you know, it's got to be in you to to to earn respect in this league. And then that's what we're going for, man, at the end of the day. And it's it's really cool to be in the a room with a group of guys like this. And uh they attack meetings. They attack practice. They attack post-practice, pre-practice, recovery, everything. And um it's got to be in you, man. >> What do you like about uh Walt Nolan's game? You you you look at him for kind of for the first time close up here. What do you What do you see out out of, you know, just like first impression? >> Yeah, that's what I like about his game. >> Yeah. >> Everything. Guys a dog, man. >> [laughter] >> No, but he's uh Man, that kid can play football. Um he's he's excited. He's excited He's excited. It's exciting to watch him play. It's exciting to watch him be excited. And um you know, just getting to know him, you know, I wasn't here last year for his rookie year. Um so, getting able to know him, where he comes from, his family, and and uh what he likes and stuff like that, and uh it's a privilege to be able to play with with a guy like that, for sure. And him being, you know, so so young in age is is kind of crazy cuz um his football years he's he's light year ahead of his his real world age, you know, so. >> Well, begin to play with one of camp's rules with pads. Like, what are the What are the rules for day one putting on the pads? >> Line it up. Line it up. That's it. >> Yeah, is there something that makes it kind of official though about putting on the pads? Like, you do so much Bruce Arians used to call it soccer practice. Does this feel like real football? >> Yeah, um but also there is the side to it that, you know, when you when you playing this league for some years, and you learn that there's a professionalism to it. And um you know, you can still get great practices in in jerseys and shorts, but you know, when the pads come on, you can hear the noise of of making a tackle, and um hear the thuds, and kind of you know, the smack talk comes a little more, and means a little more at that time. And uh you know, you call it real football for a reason cuz, you know, pads starts clacking, voices get a little lower, some voices get a little higher, so. It's fun. >> Yeah, line it up. >> What do you What do you miss most about home being being gone for a year? >> Um looking up in the stands and seeing 50, 60 just Lopez shirts and jerseys in the stands just screaming and um tears in her eyes, man. Just cuz, you know, people can't travel like that to every game. So, um yeah, just seeing everybody, you know, cuz when during the season you're busy and you don't get to, you know, see everybody throughout the week. So, sometimes you don't The only time you get to see them is at the game, you know, and um my nona text me uh I think yesterday or the day before she got her 51 jersey, right? So, she's ready, man. New number, she need a new jersey. So, um it's really cool. >> Did you get her the jersey? >> I did. Me and my dad. Yeah, my dad was able to come to practice and uh and take it home. >> With that said, you know, what about that year in Detroit? Like what did that do for you? I'm sure you learned a lot from a different system, different coaching staff. What can you take from there and to bring here? >> Yeah, that year was it was great for me. It was great as a player, as a man. I learned a lot being around a group of guys like that, coaching staff like that. Um they hold themselves to a high standard and being able to just, you know, see their routines, um see what they lean their their hat on and and who they are as humans and and people and and I've created friendships that, you know, I have to this day. We text all the time and joke around. It's a great group of guys over there, you know. So, I my time over there was was was amazing. I loved every minute of it, for sure. >> Do you think Steve took a step back last year after what seemed to be a trajectory? Is there a little bit of a chip on the shoulder, do you think? I know, you know, >> Yeah, I think, you know, if anybody ever gets to sit in a meeting room of our defense, you know, and and Nick Rallis is up there talking and you get to understand real fast, you know, the mindset of this defense and and what we got going forward. And um when you're in the room with a group of guys like this, they have that chip on their shoulder, have the mindset of being disrespected for so long. And in this league respect is everything, right? And so, and we understand We understand what we're saying, but like you tell you tell that to a guy like Buddha, like come on, man. Like You tell that to a guy like Mack, Walt, Sweat, like All right. All right. So, it's all about respect and and you know, that's that's the biggest thing on our mind.

text: You get the pads today and I know you're saying the other day you're looking forward to it. Do the Do the players you think look forward to pads? >> Uh yeah. Is it kind of a cram session or is it you have enough time? >> I try to cram it. Uh, the way these things are structured, you get 11 hours in the day. We're going to utilize all 11 hours. Um, if they want to get a little extra time, I'm talking any player, they can. Uh, but, you know, when you think about like when we get to work tomorrow, so we'll get through this practice. You think about tomorrow, um, the amount of I mean, I I want to say quarterbacks get like 2 hours and 45 minutes of total meeting up until lunch before we we head over here. Within that, the last half an hour of every meeting, we do what we call like a stage walk-through. So, just at the hotel, we'll end up going through every single play we're going to run in practice. Then when we come out here and walk through, we'll run every single play again. Um, and then, you know, sometimes twice. So, by the time he actually gets out there, he's going to already called the play two, three, maybe even four times. Uh, and that's how we we will structure it every single day. Instead of just giving the whole gamut in in in training camp, like sometimes training camp can be harder because it's like, what are they going to run today? The whole offense is up. Seven of the last 9 years have been in California, which you're talking some of the better weather. Now, I'm not saying it's here, but, uh, 2024 first week versus Detroit, I mean, it got up to 110 and it was It was all of 110. Um, but but you knew it wasn't going to stick for long. The next week it was back down to normal LA kind of temperatures there. So, again, not a copy and paste from anywhere we've been. Um, I was at San Diego. Geez, I'm I I know you guys caught me there, but the Chargers. Um, and so, we'll get six practices and we're going to go in the morning. Um, I I haven't exactly decided what time. I I I think 8:00 is too early. Um, when when you don't need to mess with the heat. We're not in time constraints. So, that is going to feel a little bit different for our guys in terms of our days are going to be flipped. We'll practice and then they're going to meet and do all those kind of things. But, then that mock week is going to be kind of what we're going to end up doing in the regular season. So, um, we'll be out there. Uh, it's not going to be at 3:00 or 4:00, um, you know, in the afternoon, but it's going to be kind of midday and we're going to have to and I'm going to have to figure out, you know, some different things, but I've talked with, uh, you know, there was a lot of thought going into April and May. I talked to Larry Fitzgerald, you know, just about all of that. So, we'll we'll figure out as we go. The the the good part is we do, you know, we'll do as much as we can in that indoor over there, right? Uh and that obviously keeps him out. But, also getting a team >> Yeah, they got to I mean, they you know, there's there's going to be collisions out there, obviously. And and when when the ball carrier is going particularly between the tackles, and there's opportunities to to thud up frontal, they'll do that. And then they'll let them go. You know, it's uh like I told Fro initially, um because these centers that have had that access to to making the call I mean, he's obviously making the calls, but changing, you know, different sorts of protections and stuff like that. So, just our our system takes care of itself. Hey, we get two to the back, we'll throw hot. If if it's the other side, we'll slide. We'll always pick that kind of stuff up and there's always going to be some stuff that are scheme beaters that that, you know, all these teams, particularly in our division, know. And we got to have answers for that and that's that's part of building that menu and giving these guys those answers, I guess you could say starting back in April when we first started going. So, uh but with that being said, I mean, he is capable and um you know, Matthew Stafford was very capable, but it helped him out to have Coleman Shelton up there just taking some off of him every once in a while. I mean, that that center, for obvious reasons, needs to be the best friend of the quarterback and those guys were and you can see Fro um you know, is tight with all these guys, but uh I know that those quarterbacks, as we build this thing even more, will appreciate when Fro, you know, has the ability to to make such changes. >> Mhm.

That's gonna be fun to watch to see how he jails all those pieces together to get the best out of what he wants for that defense to surround it with. Also, yeah, you got, you know, 15 DBs back there that's fighting for jobs, too. So, it's going to be fun to see how I think that middle unit in there adapts to the front end as well with the back end, >> which to your point, you were talking about this guy, that guy, this guy. Remember, at the end of training camp, the number that has to work with is not as big as what you think. So, that's what has to transpire over the next five or six weeks, Arch, is he's got to figure out which combination of I don't know what the number is going to be. Five, six, seven, if you're counting outside linebackers and edges as part of that group, but the the numbers aren't necessarily like I can take all these guys that we're talking about. He's got to find out like which four or five are the ones he can go to battle with. >> Well, and and give credit to Ian Cuttingham and his staff and obviously Matt Ryan and what they did in the offse to go to that raise the floor scenario we've talked about so often too. They've raised So now you're you're you're probably letting a couple guys go, I don't want to let that guy go, but I only have so many spots for it. Um, as far as my group, I'm going to go with a little bit of an abstract group. maybe a group that we probably wouldn't have picked out, a room that you sat in from time to time, and that's the tight end room. >> With the evolution of the game, we we've seen it go from pounding and running it like when I was playing uh you know, two maybe three wide receiver sets to all of a sudden five wide receiver spread spread spread across the field. Don't forget about Hoop now. Hoop was really good. He's had an outstanding career. He comes at it as the old man now of the group. But those three guys and then you throw in and Simon. Simon is a guy that I'm really intrigued about. Played his last year at South Carolina, led them in receiving, both touchdowns, catches, and yards from a receiving standpoint. I'll still be able to throw the football, but now be able to come off the ball and run it. Some of that gap running scheme they're going to use with the tight ends getting out in front and blocking. I'm excited about the tight end group, man. >> I like that. >> Like that. Um, so you're you talked about the tight end group as an additional option to me. Yes, you're talking about running the football, but in the passing game, like who's going to who's going to end up providing some production there. I'm going to take that a step further, and I'm intrigued to know who's going to be the number two wide receiver. We know who's going to be the number one. And again, it's another it's a position group where there's some good guys. They raised the floor there. We know I know I talked about it in our pre-draft. Like I was pounding the table for Zachariah Branch and they got him. And it's one thing to know shock that they got a really talented player, but it's another thing that the really talented player is able to ingest all the information and he's able to retain it and let it go in a snap of a finger. Right? That's the challenge that Zachariah Branch has. Or is it going to be Zakius, another guy coming back? Is it going to be Jan Dodson? But I think that's the element. We always knew when Drake London was healthy that he was going to give us his 110%. But I still believe that we got to find that number two. Like who's going to be the consistent number two that if they try to roll coverage over the top of Drake London? If a defensive coordinator says this guy is not going to beat us, >> who's the guy that's going to beat him? Maybe it's going to be somebody else. But I think that's an area where we've we've had guys that have been serviceable, but not necessarily like guys that have been shut down. And I know it's hard in the NFL to have two shut down corners. The the the finances don't necessarily work out that way, but that's another position group that I think that we we'll have an eye on at some point. >> Yeah. And I think that we can probably go to every position on the field and find an intriguing story. I think the Nickelback story is an interesting story. Does Does Avon slide inside and play nickel, which is something they're they're interested? Sydney Brown comes over. Sydney comes from Philadelphia. you get in get in a in a free agent deal with him or a trade with him. So you get him here in in Atlanta. Uh then you got Billy Bowman who is really making really good progress on returning from the Achilles tendon injury. Is it somebody else? Is somebody else stepped forward and able to play in that spot. But it seems like there's a little story everywhere. That interior defensive line on is gone. We got, you know, Rukaruro's gone. We got new people coming in to step into those roles. Uh, you know, can you be bigger and tougher in the middle to create opportunities for those linebackers to run and hit? There's a lot of great stories, man. All right. My last one is a player, a player aside from quarterback that you guys think has the most to prove in this training camp. All right. We know that the two guys that are battling at the quarterback position, we're going to talk about them at Nauseium over the next few weeks. But a player that has the most to prove during training camp this year to say either yep, he won the job or yep, we can count on that guy. Shock, let's go with you. It >> it starts with Doris. I I think that's the guy that uh to me I look at and say okay here he is in year three uh year two did some really good things and you got really his counterpart who he came with who Archer talked about in Rukoro and now you got a guy in Brandon Doris can he be that guy that sits in that middle for the next six seven years and become the dominant player that we saw uh who we had here for 10 years in Grady Jerry can he be that next guy yeah you brought some other guys in here yeah you brought in uh some some other guys through free agency and uh you want to see who who can fill that void as well and sit beside him. But I think Doris can be that guy that you say, you know what, >> when he sits in there, we know exactly what we got. And I want to see him take that game to the next level. We've talked about it for, you know, the last couple years being able to stop the run. I think it starts with the Dline to be able to create penetration, to be able to get off blocks, to be able to, you know, make those plays in the back field, get TFLs, be a guy who can't be blocked by one guy. Can Brainer Doris be that guy for us? Can he be the guy that in year three becomes a guy we say, you know what, we're going to have this guy for a very long time and we know we can depend on him. So, I'm looking forward to Brandon Doris taking that next step and becoming that guy that, you know, we want to see in the middle and say, you know what, ain't nobody going to be to run the football up the middle while this guy's in the ball game. >> Hope he can go out and do that. >> Love it. Impressive sophomore campaign for Doris. Let's see what happens here next year. What do you got, Arch? Well, I I think that uh as much as he's a young guy, we didn't get to see enough of him because of injuries in training camp and it slowed him down during the season. When he did play, he was impactful. I think Jaylen Walker, you took him 15th overall in the draft. He was he was a guy that you thought would come in and dominate. Like I said, there were some things that derailed him a little bit from an injury standpoint. How much more does he have on his plate? Shock alluded to the fact that is Walker just going to be on the edge. I think at this point um what they tried to do is he was drinking through a fire hose to know how to play the edge in the National Football League. He learned how to do that. Now you begin to tap into the versatility we saw at Georgia where he's off the ball. Is he the guy that steps in the Kaden Ellis role? But I think because of the expectation, because of how hard he works, the kind of person he is, he's an unbelievably good person and teammate. I'm looking for him to take that next step much like you're talking about with Doris and what can he do from a run stop standpoint. How much can Jaylen Walker affect the game like that? I'm talking about the entire game no matter where they line him up. >> Love that. Um, and I cuz I was actually thinking about I was going to answer the question by saying whoever plays alongside Divine Diablo because of when when he and Kaden Ellis were healthy on the same field, you had a really versatile linebacker group. You could do a lot of things there. You could play Kaden behind the line. You could put him up at the line of scrimmage because, you know, Devon Diablo had the speed, the experience, and the athleticism to kind of go chase down a lot of different things. But because you touched on Jaylen Walker, who knows what's up the sleeve of Jeff Albert in year two. Maybe he ends up bringing him back there. I'm going to say Avon >> Terrell >> because we all know that he's an impact player and we all know that he's a dog in a sense of going out and competing, but he's going to play with his brother and it's what position does he go out and earn? Is he going to be the starting corner? Is he going to be the starting nickel? Is he going to come in off the bench and he's going to end up playing special? I don't know what it is, but he was the top pick. He's extremely talented. He's going to play next to his brother. So, he's got all kinds of familiar. He's got the guy that can just help coach him through it on the field that he has so much trust and chemistry with. Like, it's his bro. >> Yeah. So, I want to see him and come in here and win a job, whichever one it is, because whichever one the coaching staff feels like he's best equipped to do and help this team win. That's one that I'm very interested to see how that plays out. >> I got a question with what Rack just mentioned. I know you've had opportunities to be around Avon and talk to him since being drafted. Do you think there is a little sense of I got a lot to prove because my bro is here? Yeah, I don't think there's any question about that, Shock. But the thing that I love that AJ's doing, and you've seen it, AJ wants Avon to be his own man. He loves that he's his brother, and obviously he loves him, >> right, >> because he's family and all that kind of stuff, but he feels AJ feels a little bit like Avon's not getting enough just do. Hey, my arms around little brother. He wants him to burst through that and be Avon Terrell, not AJ's little brother. And I think that's a pretty cool way, like you're talking about. title: Brandon Dorlus and Nick Folk speak to the media after arriving at Atlanta Falcons AT&T Training Camp
text: What was it like getting ready to come on in here and get this thing started? >> It's always exciting, man. You know, uh, back at home in Miami training, uh, like my usual trainers. Uh, >> you know, I'm excited to get back with this new staff, get back with Coach Nate and the guys, the new guys in the room. Uh, get this defense going and then, man, school win some games. >> You mentioned new staff. What's the biggest difference walking into this year's training camp? >> I don't know yet. See, I don't know. See, that's I'm excited for, you know, I can't wait. Uh, Otto Stfansky was really fun. Uh, you know, we got the same guys on defense. You know, we got uh Nate, Brick, you know, those are my guys that I work with. Uh I like coach defense, getting the new guys he brought in. You know, great staff and uh can't wait to see what they got on offense. >> Brandon, you mentioned some of the same guys, but they're also some new faces on the defensive line. Um what are you looking forward to getting to know about them? And then also, what's your mindset kind of coming in year three? Some new faces. How do you ingratiate yourself to some of the veteran new guys? >> Yeah, so we got some guys like, you know, Deshawn, Chris, and Mason. you know, those guys showed a lot of good football during OTAAS and uh the energy in the room is going to be different. You know, um I feel like I have a bigger role coming into this year three now and uh I feel like, you know, I got to put on tape every every uh every day and uh you know, just make sure I'm accountable for, you know, through getting some sacks. Yes, sir. >> You've done this for a few years, but what is it about just the excitement of starting? >> I hate waiting, bro. I hate waiting. You know, you do a lot of the training, no pads. I'm decided to put the pads back on, man. get get it booming. >> To that point, you'll have like an acclamation period over the next like four days of of practices before the pads come on on on Monday. What's the next chunk of of practice look like for you in terms of the intensity because obviously in the trenches can't go 100% until the pads go on and even then not really. >> Yeah, they say not 100% but you I already know how these guys going to go, man. It's it's it's not going to be full goal but it's going to be nice speed. just getting getting the feedback, you know, get uh make sure that everybody know the place. Make sure everybody was studying over the break and, you know, biggest thing is is, you know, don't get hurt during these during these times. So, stay healthy. Uh, you know, just just excited to get back out there with the guys, man. I miss the guys, you know. >> Jeff Goldberg was saying toward the end of last season that he was feeling like the defense was really starting to master the system. Um, is it a lot of the same stuff this season? Is it any changes or or what do you think so far? >> You trying to get some details off me now? No, no, you don't got to be too specific, but you know, throw a nugget, baby. >> Uh, no, it's, you know, nothing's going to really change. No, it's the same thing. We got some some kinks here and there. That's some some changes, you know, to make the defense better, but, you know, at the end of the day, it's the same thing that we learned from the first time he was here last year. You know, I'm excited. It's it's a great great defense and uh can't wait to get out there. >> Brandon, is there a different feeling for you personally when you're coming off of a year like last year versus the year prior where you were trying to kind of work your way into that core group on defense? >> Of course. just, you know, that last year I feel like I had to, you know, make sure that they knew I could go out there and play ball. Now they seen what I could do. Now I got to, you know, do it two times better than I did last year. You know, I want to, you know, get more sacks. You know, my goal this year is to win a lot of games, get to play that Super Bowl game and be a pro bowler. >> You mentioned kind of the larger role this year. How do you view your role? How do you view kind of where you're you're at in your career? >> Uh, man, Coach Nate Ali makes it really simple for me. He said, "But you out there to go get sacks." So my job is out make sure I'm out there getting the quarterback on the ground. What do you think makes a a good training camp? Like for for you a month from now to kind of look back on this and say, "We had a really good month. We're in a good spot. What do you need to see?" >> Uh, you know, great intensity, make sure uh everybody's healthy. That that's that's that's a big thing. And um, you know, just see the comfortability and make sure everybody's, you know, just doing what they got to do and, you know, it's not really something that you're really looking forward to. Y'all going to see it during camp. Uh, it's going to be a lot of a lot of intensity, a lot of I don't want to say, but maybe some fights, but you know, that's It's a good and bad sign, but in my my opinion though, it's a good sign that you know, we got guys who want to compete, we got guys who want to go win games. So, that's what I'm excited about. >> At what point in camp do you feel like you know what a team like like what it kind of can be and kind of how how high it can reach >> like how how high of a ceiling like how how early on do you think you can tell in camp what a team can kind of be eventually? >> I mean, you don't really know, man, until you get to them that that first game, man. You know, you you get a good feeling about, okay, you got a good team. you know, ot we know we had a great team, but you know, that's that's no pads on there. So, we really don't know till, you know, the first game. >> Brandon, given that uh Nate Ali has said, you know, sacks as your number one goal, did you spend time this off season refining your pass rush anymore? Did you add anything to the to the toolbox? >> Uh, man, no, I just I stick to my routine, man. I I did the same thing I did last year. I did a little bit more and uh take care of the body. You know, my biggest thing is to make sure I play all the games, you know? I don't want to miss no games this year. I want to stay healthy throughout the whole season. Do you have to uh kind of take also Rook's trash talk from last year, make that part of your game as well? Because that's going to be like a missing a little bit of a hole, right? >> Yeah. Yeah. I'm going miss that for sure. But, you know, I got some I got some of me that I could I'll bring out there for sure. >> Okay. Yes, sir. >> Okay. So, more trash talk this year from brand. >> Of course. You'll see that. You'll see it for sure. >> What are your training camp essentials? >> My training camp essentials? Uh a mattress topper. Uh my memory foam pillow. Uh you got to bring a toothbrush for sure. Uh, and a nice comfy blanket. >> Love it. >> Yes. >> You know your roommates? >> Not yet. >> Not yet. I don't know. It's >> Is there anyone you're dreading getting? >> Dreading to get. >> Is there anyone's like, "Oh, no. Not that guy." >> Oh, no. Not that guy. No. No. [laughter] I don't I wouldn't mind anybody in the D line. I know there's going to be some some Dline guys in there, but you know, I don't mind who whoever it is. >> What if you're the guy that they're dreading? [laughter] >> I hope I'm not that guy, man. I know. I know. I'm not that guy for sure. like random. >> No, no. I'm excited. I don't I really don't know yet. I I got my packet over there, so I I'm I'm going to see after this. >> What's the excitement level here? Get ready. >> I mean, I'm I'm excited for it. I mean, you're 19, long time, but uh I'm excited for it. It's an exciting time. Um new place. Um I'm just excited to get going. >> What do you think around this time? >> What do you look for in a team that that can be really good? What's important about the next handful of weeks out here, do you think? I just think building chemistry as a team. Uh continuity, chemistry, um having a good locker room. Uh on the field stuff will take kind of take care of itself, but you know, being a good locker room, being good teammates, and I think that's that's the a big part of training camp. >> What was their pitch to you to get you to Atlanta? >> Uh Craig Aerman was a lot of it. I enjoyed playing for Craig. Um having Jake come as well. I've played with him for four years in New England. So, um, it was just a whole bunch of things that, you know, closer to my family, which is good. My family's in Dallas, so, uh, closer for us to get back home, uh, for them to come out here. So, there was a lot of positives to it. Um, I like the the way the team is going. Um, so hopefully we can get over the top and get in the playoffs. >> You said year 19 for you. Is there still those feelings of like nervousness and excitement as you arrive at a new facility? >> Always excitement. Um I don't I tell us everyone that there's nothing like playing on Sundays. Um you know being in front of people, being in front of your fans and playing there's nothing like it. So training camp's just the start of that and um just excited to kind of get rolling. >> What are your impressions so far of Kevin Sebastian and the coaching staff? >> I enjoy it. I I I really enjoy Kevin. I enjoy obviously Craig playing with him uh for a year and then Chase knowing I played against Chase for a long time. Um, and then a couple of other coaches I've had on staff before. So, um, I think it's a good cohesive group. Um, and hopefully we can kind of all gel together and, um, enjoy it. >> What's your weather expectation for training camp here? >> Uh, I think it'll be not as hot as I was in Dallas. So, I looked it up. I sent a picture to uh, my family group chat the other day in Dallas. It was 106, like 120. So, I think I'm ready for it. >> [laughter] >> I think we are going to have a heat index fairly significant the first week or so. What have you learned through the years about how to how to do that? >> Um just staying hydrated really. That's the biggest thing that I've noticed. Um as long as you kind of stay hydrated and and you can kind of make it through and uh their NFL and teams have all the rules that you have to kind of follow protocol for heat index and all that. So, uh, the the trainers and everyone will have a good plan in place and I'm sure the coaches will as well. Um, to make sure that everyone's safe. I think that's kind of number one priority training camp. Get out safe, get out healthy. So, um, I think they'll have a good plan for that. >> Nick, knowing how often games come down to one score in this league, what's kind of your approach to staying levelheaded in those pressure moments? >> Uh, just to kind of know that I've done it. It's one more kick. Um, one kick doesn't kind of determine anything really. It's just one more. uh do it again. Uh I've kicked a I don't even know millions of footballs at this point. So uh it's just one more kick. Um you know, and and enjoy it. Enjoy the moment. I think that's a big thing that I try to do my entire career is just enjoy the time that I'm on the field cuz as a kicker, there's times we don't get a a ton of time on the field. So enjoy it and um have fun, put a smile on my face, and you know, just kind of do my part. >> I believe it was around 2023 when the accuracy just had a huge uptick, right? I believe that's when you were with A in Tennessee, correct? Was there a thing that that he taught you or a thing that kind of flipped, I guess, that that kind of helped you? Cuz I think your accuracy jumped around like 10% from 22 to 23. >> Um, I I don't know if it was one thing. I mean, I've always felt like I've been a pretty accurate kicker for the most part. Um, there's a lot of things that go into kicking and statistics, if you will. Um, so I don't know if it's one thing or anything like that. just kind of just like I said, enjoy the moment, enjoy the time, and then um just sort of do my part. >> Like strength-wise, I guess like max number for you right now, do you think? >> That depends on the day. You guys will find out every day. [laughter] >> What is it about Craig that you specifically enjoyed about your time working with him? >> Uh his energy. He's kind of got this in infectious energy about him and then he's also with the specialist, he's got a a very calm nature about him with the specialist. So, um I've just enjoyed it. Uh he kind of when I got to Tennessee, he's like, "What's your kind of routine?" I did my routine and he kind of let me do it and it ended up working out pretty well. So, um we've kind of have a plan for training camp, a plan for the season on how we want to do things. And uh it's just easy to communicate with him and and Chase. And so, um that's kind of the probably the biggest things. >> Besides Craig, is there anyone else in the organization you have a really close relationship with or any players that you spend a lot of time with? Uh the probably the most would be Jake Bailey. Uh just my time in New England. Um got a couple other guys, Trevor Simeon when I was in Tennessee. Uh Corey Leaven when I was in Tennessee as well. So there's a couple guys I know. Um but a lot of the old guys are they're cycling out with younger guys. So a lot of my old old teammates are are gone now.

title: Ochocinco Drops in for Training Camp | Carolina Panthers
text: We are joined by one Chad Ochocinco Johnson. Ocho, we know that you have uh really kind of become a fan of this wide receiver group over the past year. What is it about them that first impressed you and getting to see them here today in person? >> Well, obviously last year understanding what we had, Terrace Marshall McMillan, Ickey Ekwonu, and some of the other fellows No, Horn, and some Coker, and some of some of the other fellows, I understood how good they could be. When it comes to a team in general, in order for a team to do well, you have to have a supporting cast around the quarterback. The quarterback The answers are already there. You have your quarterback for the future. Now, it's all about putting the right pieces around him in order for things to work. And I understood that long before the season started, which is why I was so high on the Panthers making the playoffs, and they did just that. >> TM Ack of course wins Rookie of the Year, too. You are are a familiar with what it takes to be a successful wide receiver in this league and to sustain that. What is the advice you would give him to sustain it going into year two? >> Uh two words. Two words, and they both start with the letter C. Consistency and confidence. And that that that'll take you as far as you want to go. Obviously, you want to minimize the errors, you want to minimize the mistakes. Uh but they're going to happen at some point, but just be as consistent as possible because consistency is all it comes down to, especially at the position of receiver. >> You said you realized what we had. Are you a full-blown Panthers fan now? >> Yeah, I've been a Panthers fan for a very long time. Obviously, Steve Smith, very good friend of mine. Um and anyone who's played here, it just you know how I am. I always show love to everybody. I've never I've never I've never, you know, vilified another team or another player. And just I can appreciate a team that's being well built, you know, from the bottom up. And um that exactly was happening here. >> Nothing but love from Ocho. One last thing, we saw you tweeted last night that you were going to be out here. You wanted to meet the wide receiver coach and learn the kicker's name. Have you done both of those things? >> homework on on who Rob Moore was. Obviously, phenomenal player. Yeah, storied career back in the day. Obviously, I was a baby. I was a young pup in high school during those days. Uh, Fitzpatrick, you know. >> So close. So close. We can call him Fitz money if you want. Ryan Fitzpatrick. The quarterback. We hope Ryan Fitzpatrick is around just as long as Ryan Fitzpatrick. One last thing before we let you go. You know what you have to do. Look at the camera and tell them. I know that's what I want that's why I'm asking. Keep pounding. Thank you. Pleasure.

title: Jonathon Brooks: 'It felt good to be back out there' | Carolina Panthers
text: I feel good. Feel good to be back out there. Just trusting the process that the trainers and coaches have for me. Just hoping and believing in myself throughout the whole rehab process. It was a blessing to be able to be back out there. No ma'am. No ma'am. Happily I don't. I don't. Yes. Yes sir. I feel like I was. I feel like I'm back to 100% getting out there having fun with it. Did you have were you looking forward sort of to the first day of pads just as another benchmark in this road to recovery? I think that was a part of the process. Yes. I think in the back of my mind you know obviously as a football player you have to get back out there and and be able to learn how to take hits, learn how to get your contact balance right back and you know obviously first day of pads it was it was good. I think I think as a team we could have had a better day but it was good to be able to be out there have fun with our teammates. It was a blessing. The balance you have shown the ability to really be able to juke and move out here today in pads like what is the process of trusting that knee again and knowing that it's fine to do that and or is it just a you have to do it till you can? I think I think that was the whole process of rehab throughout the whole year and a half that I've had to rehab and train and and learn to do that again. Obviously it didn't just come back right away. It's something that took a lot of time. Something that took a lot of training and a lot of trusting the the trainers and coaches in the plan that they had me on and have me on is great. So it's been awesome. I think I I as a human you know it's good for you to reflect. To to know where you come from. It also helps to for motivation to where you're going. Um and for me, being back out there it was it definitely is a confidence booster to know that that I'm fully healed and I can take hits again and I can be out there with my teammates um full speed having fun cutting doing everything that I need to do to help the team. >> You had a play at practice where you made some cuts and I think you ended up on the ground. I don't know if you got knocked down, but are the cuts almost to you more of a validation or as as much of a validation as the speed the speed as the run speed? >> Uh I think so. I think I think cutting is a is a part of a running back's game where you have to be out there and be able to cut. Um and then the speed por- portion of it, unfortunately, I know in OTAs I said that I was faster than Chuba. I'm just go ahead and get this out the way. Said that I was faster than Chuba. And um this summer we we re- we ran. We didn't race. It was a part of the workout and he recorded a higher top speed to me, so I'll take my comment back. I'm not faster than Chuba. >> I like that you take accountability. >> But you said you weren't racing. >> Yeah. >> No, we weren't racing. It was just uh like top speed on the Catapult. Just that was the top speed of the day. We ran like a certain distance and and that's just he recorded it. >> That you had to acknowledge that publicly in front of us? >> No, ma'am. That's just me taking accountability of of what I said in OTAs. >> But if you did have a race, you could have beat him. >> Uh I don't know. I don't know. I guess we'll have to see another day. >> John, Frenchy is special. But where would you be without Chuba? >> Uh to be honest, um it sounds cliche to say, but um I think I would I I don't I don't know where I would be because um he's helped me throughout since I first got here. Um you know, I came in with the injury and he helped me. He took me under his wing. Um and really guided me how to rehab, how to how to practice, how to learn, how to take notes and all of that. Um and then especially when I got hurt again, he was he was right there with me. You know, he helped me throughout the whole way. He was there when I got baptized and that just goes to say how much we've grown our brotherhood and um how close we've gotten and then just to be able to work out with him this whole off season has been amazing. Um just to see how he trains um he trains pretty hard. So it was it was good for me to to tag along and and learn how to build my body right for training camp and for the season. >> And what are you expecting from yourself this season? You set any goals or >> Uh for me just wherever the coaches and wherever the coaches want to put me, wherever and however, I just want to be able to help the team. >> Jonathan, you said that y'all didn't have pads on Sunday, but you had to experience Derrick Brown's called tackle close like to step into one of those. >> Uh you know, it's different. DB's he's a big dude. Um but you know, it's good. It that's a part of the game that helps me be able to uh learn and build a course to like understand that that's just a part of the game. >> Jonathan, you mentioned Chubba kind of the role he played in your own recovery process and every time we talked to you, you talk about you know, how important mentality is and then having been through it twice, do you feel like you're now in a position to kind of help guys like Nick who are going through something similar and then making sure they're keeping their their head on straight through >> Definitely. Definitely. I I check in every time I see him throughout the facility. I don't want to blow his phone up too much right now. You know, a lot of people probably hitting him up, but you know, I text him. I let him know that God's with him. Um that this injury is is something small to where he's going and uh it's something he can he can bounce back from because um there's proof in the pudding and and and whenever you trusting God, um he's always going to make things right whether it's on your timeline or his. You know, from from me, it took me two times to really understand it for him to set me back and and be able to I think it was a blessing in disguise for me to learn more, build my body more, um become smarter for the game of football. >> Is there a part of you that still wants to get past the the being tackled part, you know what I mean? And you know, full contact, you know, 100%. Is there is there a part of you in your mind that just wants to get that hurdle over with? >> Uh I mean, sort of definitely. Um I think I think that's also a part of the game, also a part of the mentality, um part of part of coming back from injury, especially a lower body injury, being able to be tackled again. And I feel like it that'll be another confidence booster getting tackled uh for the first time. >> Do you have any idea what some of those near mind, like some of the benchmarks will be in the weeks and months coming forward? >> I'm just taking it day by day. I want to I want to be able to be um focused on each day that I'm in for camp. Um I just want to be able to be out there, know what I'm doing, help the team in any way I can, and just have my brothers' backs. >> It was a pretty chippy practice for these moments of of aggression, including the fight, but also, you know, you and Corey um after play very briefly. What was it like to kind of be in that aggressive mode again? >> Uh it was good. I think I think that's a part of the game. I think that's what comes with it whenever you're playing at the highest level. Um you know, everybody wants to get out there and and you know, that's I think that's good for our team. That goes to show the the the bond that we've made this off season working out together. Um some of it's friendly and some of it's not friendly on the field and friendly right when you get off the field, and that's just a part of what football is. >> Coach praised your work in the receiving game today. You know, with Chad Ochocinco and Steve Smith out here, you know, what were you hoping to take away from guys like that? And you know, did you interact with them at all today? >> Uh no, I didn't get the chance to interact with them. I just um and and I wish I did. Uh I just wanted to stay focused. You know, I'm I really want to be focused on what I have in front of me um this year and just stay focused. I think that was pretty cool that they were out there to see two guys like that that I've looked up to my whole life um and watched growing up. I think that's pretty cool. >> Do you have anything from this summer besides training? >> Um this summer I got engaged this summer. Um I went to Banff, Canada, and got engaged. Um and it was it was it was beautiful. Um my fiance has been wonderful in my rehab process, wonderful in my faith process, pushing each other to be better with our faith and our religion. And she's just been really awesome. >> The fan fest is coming up on Friday. I don't think you've been able to participate in those before. How excited are you just to get out there in front of fans? >> That's awesome. I think it's going to be a lot of fun to be able to be out there in in front of fans, let them see the work that we're that we've put in all all season. And just to be able to interact with them, see the smiles on their faces, allow them to have fun while we get to work is is it's a pretty amazing feeling. >> Shout out. Thanks, guys. >> [music] [music]

title: Jaelan Phillips: ' Competition breeds success' | Carolina Panthers
text: Felt great. It's always good to get back into pads and you know go through the off season, go through the beginning of camp kind of just waiting for this day. You know there was a lot of what ifs and oh man if I had pads on I'll do this, I'll do that. So it's nice to finally get to be able to do that and it just brings up the level of competition and feels like real football. So it's always exciting. >> Jaylen, Dave said that he had to challenge the defense in the middle of practice essentially to say hey we need to bring the physicality up. How do you think that impacted today? >> I mean I think it's a good reminder. I think that in general you know physicality obviously is the name of the game when it comes to playing a good brand of defense and you know that's something we want to bring every play. So you know obviously some parts of it weren't good enough today. So just you know analyze that, be critical in film and come back tomorrow with with a great intention and and a great effort. >> Jaylen, he also mentioned he I think he said he wants the defense to drive practice. Why do you think it's important for your unit to be the ones to set that tone? >> Because like I said I think like our team in general is trying to play a physical brand of football and I think that you know when you look at defense in general you know obviously there's some physicality involved to offense especially up front but you know I'd say the best defenses are physical ones and so you know for us to be able to go out there drive the energy you know they always say defense wins championships all those type of things. So you know I think that it's important to have a vocal and high energy defense and that's the potential that we have so we got to bring that every day. >> What did you see going up against Roquan Smith today just from rookie pads on >> Yeah he's looking great. I mean he's really strong you know definitely works his hands very well. You know I think there's as a rookie obviously there's always things to improve. I think he's you know getting accustomed to the speed, physicality, the playbook all those different things but you know he's very promising and I love going against him. I think that he's going to get me better I'm going to get him better And so yeah he's looking good. >> You were not here, obviously, to see Jonathan Brooks pre-injury. So, just [snorts] wondered what your assessments are as you've seen him a little bit this spring so far. >> Yeah, we worked out a lot together this off-season. You know, he's tried incredibly athletic, fast, works really hard. Him and Chuba, you know, they're kind of inseparable when it comes to their training regimen and things like that. So, I think that, you know, them together they're pushing each other and ultimately, you know, iron sharpens iron and competition competition breeds success. So, you know, I think having them two there is is going to be great for both of them. >> Being here in the building all summer, is that what you mean by you would work out together? >> Yeah, I mean, we trained together. We work out here at the facility. Like I said, him and Chuba are always competing whether we're working out, racing, doing anything. So, you know, I think that's great about both of them. >> Talk to you since the extraordinary went down. Can you speak to that and the impact on that room and guys having to step up to fill that void? >> Yeah, it's devastating. You know, Nick is him and I have gotten very close in the short period of time that I've known him. He's a guy that has an extremely high level of passion and care about this game and about everything.
