And so, you hate to see it happen to anybody, but especially someone who invests so much and loves this game so much. You know, it's it's brutal and it's not fair. But ultimately, you know, I've obviously experienced several season-ending injuries and from coming from my experiences, like I literally ran to the locker room to to talk to him because I just know he's the type of guy that is going to be able to handle this adversity and I just wanted to instill the experience and the wisdom I had when it came to that. You know, I think that ultimately, you know, there's always a silver lining in any adversity and truthfully, you just have to find it and you have to have that positive outlook and that positive perspective. And for him, understanding, you know, at this time of his career, he's going to be able to get healthy, he's going to be able to, you know, work on other areas of his body, going to be able to do things off the field that he might not be able to do. And so, you know, ultimately, it's it's a blessing and you know, he's just got to see it as that and you know, we're going to miss him and we do miss him every day. Uh, and I'm just excited for him to recover and come back and and get back into full form cuz he's a absolute stud when he's on that field. >> Jaylen, knowing you said you introduced yourself and talked to him about it, how helpful is it for him to be here and engaged the way he was out here today? >> I think it's super helpful. You know, being hurt is something that nobody really understands how alienating it can be until you've been in that position. You know, the way football is, we're so regimented and we have to be so present and focused that, you know, if something's not in front of you, you really don't really pay a lot of attention to it. So, you know, as somebody who's hurt, you have a completely different schedule. You know, you're never really around us, whether it's the locker room banter or the warm-ups, the training, you know, there's a lot of closeness that comes from the blood, sweat, and tears that we go through together on a daily daily basis. And so, when you're outside of that routine, it can be very alienating. It can be depressing. It can be just a really shitty experience. And so, you know, for him to be around, I think it's super helpful just given the fact especially that he's young. You know, we're all very close like I said. You know, to each their own. The first time I got hurt, I stayed around the facility. The second time I went home and spent time with my family. So, you know, I think that he'll have a good mixture of both and but right now I think it's important for him to be around and for us to be able to uplift him and vice versa cuz he's he is a a special energy that you know, really it's not the same without him. So. >> Jaylen, close to Nick. Um, can't feel the latest news in the spring. Last couple days, what is your first impressions of him? >> He's twitchy. He's twitchy. He's explosive. Um, you know, he's dedicated. You know, high focus, high energy. Uh, so I think he's a a great player for us to have in. So, I mean, I I said I'm still getting to know him but uh, he's a cool guy and I think he's done a great job his last couple days. >> Same question about that Nick stuff or like Mike Jackson with his helmet there. You guys see that? >> I didn't see that honestly. I was I was probably working on some drills or something, so I'm going to look at our film and ask around. So, I I didn't hear about it until afterwards. >> Yeah, what about Prince talk about him a little bit getting to know him this past year? What stands out to you his second year coming up? >> Yeah, I mean Prince, I think he's probably the best pass rusher on our team. You know, I think that he is extremely naturally gifted and I think that as he continues to develop, he can be a very special player. I think that he already has crazy attributes and you know, he's definitely learning. He's young, so I'm excited to watch him grow. >> What stands out to you the most? >> I just athletic. He has crazy bend. You know, really good feel. Pass rushing is an art and so ultimately, you know, it's it's very nuanced. It's very It's not just like, oh, run full speed ahead and don't get blocked. It's you know, setting things up. It's a chess game. It's a you know, game within a game. So, I think he has a very good natural feel for pass rushing and I think his ceiling is extremely high. Cool. Thanks, guys. >> [music] [music]

title: Dave Canales: 'We have to capture these opportunities' | Carolina Panthers
text: Okay, what a beautiful day. Back in pads. Um really near and dear to my heart. Just uh one of my favorite days from high school, Pop Warner, whatever it is, and now we're all the way in the NFL uh getting back to banging and and playing a physical nature. Um I would not say today was to the standard uh that we're capable of and um the practice got better and better as we were playing more physical, the more guys getting comfortable just being back out there, and uh kind of challenged them halfway through and um we got more attempts on trying to punch the ball out. We got more physical play as it went on. Um and that's to be expected, but we got to we got to make sure we capture all these opportunities. Uh they're few and far between to get into pads and to make sure that we're in the the right place to be able to play uh game time football. So, but again, just a just a great day. Offense won the day, so bounced back. Defense took the first two, offense has taken the last two. Um so, it's starting to even out a little bit. Um but, it's I I can't wait to watch the film to kind of see some of the things I was looking for, especially up front, you know, as we get in pads, what do guys look like uh when they're in those one-on-one opportunities. >> Why would you say your practice wasn't up to the standard? >> Yeah, just the physical nature that we play with. Um the way that we're used to practicing, it just didn't start that way. That was really the first period. We had three team periods and um you know, right in the middle of that period, I kind of went over to the defense and said, "Hey, you guys drive this thing. Like, we got to show up and everybody's got to get to the ball." And so, uh they took to the challenge and they responded well, but let I want I want them to drive it. And they know what to expect. Um they know what to expect from each other. And so, I want them to make sure that they take ownership of that part and we'll remind them as coaches, but uh we got to have it. That's the way this uh this game is played. >> Any update on Mitch? >> Yeah, um you know, it it they're tested him. It was an ankle injury. Um rolled it up. Um they're pretty optimistic, but we're going to do a full evaluation just to make sure uh there's nothing happening in there, but um they were pretty optimistic coming off the field and I'll I'll give you more information as we uh do the full uh evaluation. >> Coach, how have you guys like Chad Ochocinco, been out here at practice today? What does that do for your receivers and the energy around the building? >> I mean, for all of us, you know, these are guys that I grew up watching in in Southern California junior college football. And the Sunday paper, you pick you open up the paper and it was it was Steve Smith, it was Chad, it was T.J. Houshmandzadeh, the guys making plays, you know, 100 plus yards a game, couple of touchdowns. And I coached at El Camino College back in the day and so got to be in that world and some some amazing talent come out of there. So, it goes way back for me. So, when they come out, these are still like my heroes. Um but I love the support. It's not just the receivers, but the DBs as well. And some of these guys have had exchanges you know, over the years in the off season. Some of our guys were able to be in Southern California around them. And so, I just love the support. And I'm sure that they're you know, giving them their two cents about what's going on. So, really glad that they're out here. >> Dave, you mentioned that the physical standpoint wasn't up to standard immediately. >> Yeah. >> And there was a fight in the middle of practice. >> Uh can you kind of address what perhaps you liked about that extra aggression or what you didn't like about it? >> Uh we always got to push things to the limit. This game is played with a lot of passion and a lot of aggression by nature. And we're going to be on edge. That's going to happen in games. We can't cross the line. It just hurts the team, you know, and that's you know, personal foul set you back. And 15 yards is huge, especially if it's a special teams play, it really flips the field. If you got to re-kick, offensively speaking, it could put you in a hole. Defensively, you're allowing that offense essentially to have an explosive play with a personal foul. So, we got to be able to keep our heads. But day one, guys are fired up, you know, words are said. That stuff happens. We just got to make sure you go to the line, you can't cross it. So, we had good conversations about it and I don't think that'll happen again. >> When you interviewed Jonathan told us he had not yet opened it up 100%. Has he done that yet? And how do you think he looked first day of practice? >> I I think that's a question for Jonathan, you know, only he knows what his body's capable of and we've seen what we've seen on film, but um he'll be able to tell you best and I'm sure you'll have an opportunity to talk to him here and ask him that um to see how he feels, but I don't see any hesitation in his play. He's pressing runs. Um he's hitting the ground popping up, so that's what I like to see. >> On that fine line of sweet sort of aggression and getting out of control, in year three have you found yourself more comfortable sort of walking that line and pushing it sort of right to the edge there? >> Um yeah, I mean, I just know it's a part of the game and it's something that we have to be aware of and you know, years and years of being an assistant in different scenarios, these kind of things come up and um the best case of action is to be clear-headed and talk to how it affects the game and we practice for the game. That's what every rep is about, every situation and now you're talking about like a potential fight situation, guys are in each other's faces. The first person that throws a punch, you're out of here, you know, and you're gone for the game and that can hurt your team, so it's a good teaching moment. >> On did Jonathan Brooks talk about the evaluation process since going back to college and how you utilize utilization of the passing game, how excited are you to get him back into that that role? >> Yeah, I mean, it's a fun YouTube watch if you ever get a second to just go back and, you know, they got a bunch of his plays and I would say half of them are on screens and, you know, check-downs in the flat where he's able to make somebody miss and, you know, when he gets a beat on it, he can finish. He's got finishing speed, so that's a that's a big part of his game and, you know, while we know we can utilize that part, first and foremost, he's a running back and just making sure that he's on the right track, he's reading the runs the right way, pressing the blocks to help his O-line out, stay connected and all that. That's first and foremost and then all the other things will come off of it. >> Hey, this was Monroe Freeling's first training camp day, correct? And had how do you think he fared against Jaelan Phillips today? >> I got I I have to watch the film, you know, I I watched him off and on on a couple plays and he looked he looked good, you know, and he looked stout and all the things you expect, but I can't wait to get into the film and and really see how it panned out. >> Did consider throwing Felipe out today for the fight or just Did Did you not feel >> Not at all. Not at all. I think, you know, with Felipe, with anybody else, my conversation with them is always, "Okay, you got to get your wits about you. Now, if you can't get get it together in the next couple of plays, I'm going to have to send you in." And that's kind of how I share with any of our guys. Like, things happen. Okay, are we good? And I'm looking at him in the face, and I'm watching what happens the next time they're out there in the 11-on-11. If they're playing within themselves and not head hunting and trying to do something out of character, then let's them let them play ball. You're going to have to bounce back from different adverse situations throughout the season. And so, I want to see guys respond in the right way. He certainly did. Went right back to a special teams period, came back and made another play later on. And so, uh he was able to get himself back together. And same thing with the defensive guys. >> Dave, what's the status of J.C. and thoughts of getting him back out there on the field today? >> Yeah, just sprinkled in today, but just watched him in individual. He looks great. You know, he's moving laterally. Really don't see anything you know, in any direction in terms of just his movement. So, I'm excited to just kind of ramp him up and just catch him up to the group so that he can handle his normal load and just get back to work. >> And Jack sprinkled in, also. >> Same. Yeah, same with Mike. Um felt good. They both had great um great sessions a couple of days in a row um in return to play. So, you know, Denny and his crew did a fantastic job just getting those guys ready. And we'll dose them the right way and get them back going. >> How do you assess the tight end position? You know, we were talking about Mitch, Mitchell, and um I mean, is it kind of going to be a by committee thing? It's kind of been really the last couple of years or what? Or are you looking for one guy to step up and be >> Yeah, we'll let them show us. You know, we'll let them show us how we can use them in different ways, but it's a group that we really trust um with J.T., with Mitch, and with Tommy. Uh a bunch of tough guys who do things right. And you know, there are other roles in this offense, and we'll let those roles emerge as guys show us what they can do. That's the exciting part about camp um as we get to get these opportunities in the joint practices in preseason, uh, to see if somebody presents something unique for us. >> Hi. Uh, Damien Lewis, any >> Yeah, Damien just had a little calf, uh, grabbed on him. Uh, really good evaluation following that up. Hoping to get him back, uh, pretty quickly. But again, with calves, you got to be cautious because if you try to load it too soon, they can turn into longer injuries. But he's in good spirits. He had a great training day today. We'll keep him on that program for a couple of days and see where we're at. >> Do you know when you're expecting him >> Rob's getting better. Yeah, Rob's getting better. I can't tell you it's tomorrow, um, but he's doing a great job again. Um, feels strong, starting to move around really well. Um, again, you know, we'll kind of just keep pushing him off the field in controlled situations before we throw him back into team sessions. >> You see the depth at inside of guard, you know, with those absences and everything, where is that group right now? >> Well, it just to speak to the group in general, a bunch of guys that we know, uh, that we're excited about. You know, you talk about Chandler Zavala who's played a lot of ball for us and has had some some challenges, you know, over the last couple years. Um, but he knows the system, a guy we really trust. Saadiq Charles has really made jumps, um, in the off season. We were able to acquire him later last season, so he's he's starting to get really comfortable with our schemes. But he's a really powerful guy and he can move. Of course, Brady in the mix, you know, can play all along the front, but really focusing him on the guard spots because we do have that depth at tackle right now. Um, and, uh, uh, JT Carter, Isaiah Glass who was working at tackle, will see some guard action as well. So, it's a really good young group, some veteran guys that are able to challenge and push each other. >> Obviously, coach, injury, you know, it's still great to see him on the sideline smiling and everything. How important is that to still have that good energy even though likely you're not going to play? >> Yeah, I mean, as long as we can have him around his guys, he was out there doing, uh, some metabolics, moving around, um, just walking and making sure he has good flexibility and mobility in his leg. I mean, if you watch him if you look over there and and you see him walking around, you don't even know. Um and uh but they're just keeping him in shape and strong. That really helps going into the surgery in that process. And for people who've had ACLs, you know how that is. The stronger you go in, the quicker you can recover. So, um but again, having him out there, having him on the sideline around his guys, being involved in football, even as we have even even after he gets surgery and he comes back to us, you know, the more we can just have him being involved, um it's good for the team and it's good for Nick. >> Hey coach, Cam Jackson was like a different player in the second uh uh training camp. What What changes have you noticed in his play and his confidence and his overall demeanor? >> Yeah, just being comfortable in the system, understanding how we want certain plays to be executed. And he's a big, powerful man, 6'6, 350-something. Um and uh pair all that up with the knowledge of where I'm going to be, the more he starts to anticipate what's happening before the snap, the better he'll perform. So, that's what I'm expecting from here for Cam is to just keep dialing into the concepts. He's going to see some repeat plays here pretty soon in camp to dial in those things so he can take his shots when they're there. >> Uh Just Laken Tomlinson seemed pretty solid on the left today. But what have you seen from him during camp? >> Yeah, I mean, just one day at a time, just being able to like, you know, just challenge the group, um bring out the best in the group. And I just, you know, without getting into any specifics, you know, um I'm just excited that, you know, we have a veteran guy um that can uh really just create a level of comfort, as you can imagine, for the quarterback on that left side, you know, where he knows what he's doing. He's been around it all, he's seen it all. Um and uh you know, what as as we have different guys popping in at guard, you know, it's really nice to just have that piece there. So, um but he's got a lot of great energy. Things I didn't know about him and his personality, he enjoys it. Uh he celebrates stuff even when he's not in and there's There's big play on the offense, He's first one with his hands in the air. Love that about him. Love that he's bringing that kind of veteran leadership. All right. Thank you. [snorts] >> [music] [music]

title: Panthers Live Press Conference
text: [music] >> What a beautiful day to be back in pads. Um really near and dear to my heart. Just uh one of my favorite days from high school, Pop Warner, whatever it is. And now we're all the way in the NFL, uh getting back to banging and and playing a physical nature. Um I would not say today was to the standard uh that we're capable of. And um the practice got better and better as we were playing more physical, the more guys getting comfortable just being back out there. And uh kind of challenged them halfway through. And um we got more attempts on trying to punch the ball out. We got more physical play as it went on. Um and that's to be expected. But we got to we got to make sure we capture all these opportunities. Uh they're few and far between to get into pads and to make sure that we're in the the right place to be able to play uh game time football. So, but again, just a just a great day. Offense won the day. So, bounced back. Defense took the first two. Offense has taken the last two. Um so, it's starting to even out a little bit. Um but it's I can't wait to watch the film to kind of see some of the things I was looking for, especially up front, you know, as we get in pads, what do guys look like uh when they're in those one-on-one opportunities. >> Why would you say your practice wasn't up to the standard? >> Yeah, just the physical nature that we play with. Um the way that we're used to practicing, it just didn't start that way. That was really the first period. We had three team periods. And um you know, right in the middle of that period, I kind of went over to the defense and said, "Hey, you guys drive this thing. Like, we got to show up. And everybody's got to get to the ball." And so, uh they took to the challenge. And they responded well. But let I want I want them to drive it. And they know what to expect. Um they know what to expect from each other. And so, I want them to make sure that they take ownership of that part. And we'll remind them as coaches. But uh we got to have it. That's the way this uh this game is played. >> David, any update on Mitch? >> Yeah, um you know, it it they tested him. It was an ankle injury. Um rolled it up. Um they're pretty optimistic, but we're going to do a full evaluation just to make sure uh there's nothing happening in there, but um they were pretty optimistic coming off the field and I'll I'll give you more information as we uh do the full uh evaluation. >> Okay. Uh how do guys like Chad Ochocinco and Steve Smith out here at practice today? What does that do for your receivers and the energy out here? >> I mean, for all of us, you know, these are guys that I grew up watching in in uh Southern California junior college football and uh the Sunday paper you pick you open up the paper and it was it was Steve Smith, it was Chad, it was uh T.J. Houshmandzadeh, the guys making plays, you know, 100-plus yards a game, couple of touchdowns, and I coached at El Camino College uh back in the day and so uh got to be in that world and uh some some amazing talent come out of there. So, it goes way back for me. So, when they come out, these are still like my heroes. Um but I love the support. Um it's not just the receivers, but the DBs as well, and some of these guys have had exchanges, you know, over the years in the offseason. Some of our guys were able to be in Southern California around them, and so um I just love the support, and I'm sure that they're, you know, giving them their two cents about what's going on. So, uh really glad that they're out here. >> Hey, you mentioned that the physical standpoint wasn't up to standard immediately. >> Yeah. >> And there was a fight in the middle of practice. >> Uh can you kind of address what perhaps you liked about that extra aggression or what you didn't like about >> Uh we always got to push things to the limit. Uh this game is played with a lot of passion and a lot of aggression by nature, and we're going to be on edge. That's going to happen in games. We can't cross the line. It just hurts the team, you know, and that's you know, personal foul set you back, and 15 yards is huge, especially if it's a special teams play, it really flips the field. If you got to re-kick, offensively speaking, it could put you in a hole. Defensively, you're allowing that offense essentially to have an explosive play with the personal foul. So, we got to be able to keep our heads. But, day one, guys are fired up, you know, words are said. That stuff happens. We just got to make sure you go to the line, you can't cross it. So, we had good conversations about it, and I don't think that'll happen again. >> How healthy is he in training camp? Jonathan told us he had not yet opened it up. >> Has he done that yet? And how do you think he looked first day of practice? >> I I think that's a question for Jonathan, you know, only he knows what his body's capable of. And we've seen what we've seen on film, but um he'll be able to tell you best, and I'm sure you'll have an opportunity to talk to him here and ask him that um to see how he feels. But, I don't see any hesitation in his play. He's pressing runs. Um he's hitting the ground popping up. So, that's what I like to see. >> On that fine line between sort of aggression and getting out of control, in year three, have you found yourself more comfortable sort of walking that line and pushing it sort of right to the edge there? >> Um yeah, I mean, I just know it's a part of the game, and it's something that we have to be aware of. And, you know, years and years of being an assistant in different scenarios, these kind of things come up. And um the best case of action is to be clear-headed and talk to how it affects the game. And we practice for the game. That's what every rep is about, every situation. And now you're talking about like a potential fight situation, guys are in each other's faces. The first person that throws a punch, you're out of here, you know, and you're gone for the game, and that can hurt your team. So, it's a good teaching moment. >> On Jonathan Brooks, talk about the evaluation process going back to college and how you utilized uh utilization in the passing game. How excited are you to get him back into that uh that role? >> Yeah, I mean, it's a fun YouTube watch if you ever get a second to just go back and, you know, um they got a bunch of his plays, and I would say half of them are on screens and, you know, check-downs in the flat where he's able to make somebody miss. And, you know, when he gets a beat on it, he can finish. He's got finishing speed. So, that's a that's a big part of his game. And, you know, while we know we can utilize that part, first and foremost, he's a running back and just making sure that he's on the right track, he's reading the runs the the way, pressing the blocks to help his old line out, stay connected and all that. That's first and foremost and then all the other things will come off of it. >> If this was Monroe Freeling's first training camp, how do you think he fared against Jaylen Phillips in the slot? >> I got I'll I'll have to watch the film, you know, I I watched him off and on on a couple plays and he looked he looked good, you know, and he looked stout and all the things you expect, but I can't wait to get into the film and and really see how it panned out. >> Did you consider throwing Felipe out today for the fight or >> Did did you not feel like he was ready? >> all. Not at all. I think, you know, with Felipe, with anybody else, my conversation with them is always, "Okay, you got to get your wits about you. Now, if you can't get get it together in the next couple of plays, I'm going to have to send you in." And that's kind of how I share with any of our guys. Like, things happen, okay, are we good? And I'm looking at him in the face and I'm watching what happens the next time they're out there in the 11-on-11. If they're playing within themselves and not head hunting and trying to do something out of character, then let's let them play ball. You're going to have to bounce back from different adverse situations throughout the season. And so, I want to see guys respond in the right way. He certainly did. Went right back to a special teams period, came back and made another play later on. And so, he was able to get himself back together. And same thing with the defensive guys. >> Dave, what did you see out of JC in terms of getting him back out there on the field today? >> Yeah, just sprinkled in today, but just watched him in individual. He looks great, you know, he's moving laterally. Really don't see anything, um you know, in any direction in terms of just his movement. So, I'm excited to just kind of ramp him up and just catch him up to the group so that he can handle his normal load and just get back to work. >> Sprinkled in also? >> Same. Yeah, same with Mike. Um felt good. They both had great um great sessions a couple of days in a row um in return to play. So, you know, Denny and his crew did a fantastic job just getting those guys ready and we'll dose them the right way and get them back going. >> How do you feel about the tight end position, you know, we're talking about Mitch Mitchell and um I mean, is it kind of going to be a by committee thing? It's kind of been really the last couple of years or are you looking for one guy to step up and be >> Yeah, we'll let them show us, you know, we'll let them show us how we can use them in different ways, but it's a group that we really trust with JT, with Mitch, and with Tommy. A bunch of tough guys who do things right and you know, there are other roles in this offense and we'll let those roles emerge as guys show us what they can do. That's the exciting part about camp as we get get these opportunities in the joint practices and preseason to see if somebody presents something unique for us. >> I Damien Lewis can you update us on him? >> Yeah, Damien just had a little calf grabbed on him. Really good evaluation following that up hoping to get him back pretty quickly, but again with calves you got to be cautious because if you try to load it too soon, they can turn into longer injuries, but he's in good spirits. He had a great training day today. We'll keep him on that program for a couple of days and see where we're at. >> Rob, do you know when you're expecting >> Rob's getting better. Yeah, Rob's getting better. I can't tell you it's tomorrow, but he's doing a great job again. Feels strong starting to move around really well. Again, you know, we'll kind of just keep pushing him off the field in controlled situations before we throw him back into team sessions. >> You see the depth inside at guard, you know, with those absences and everything. Where is that group right now? >> Well, it just to speak to the group in general a bunch of guys that we know that we're excited about. You know, you talk about Chandler Zavala who's played a lot of ball for us and has had some some challenges you know, over the last couple of years, but he knows the system a guy we really trust. Saadiq Charles has really made jumps in the off-season. We were able to acquire him later last season, so he's he's starting to get really comfortable with our schemes, but he's a really powerful guy and he can move. Of course Brady in the mix, you know, can play all along the front, but really focusing him on the guard spots because we do have that depth at tackle right now. And JT Carter, Isaiah Glass who was working at tackle will see some guard action as well. So, it's a really good young group. Some veteran guys that are able to challenge and push each other. >> Nick's injury, you know, it's still great to see him on the sideline smiling and everything. How important is that to still have that good energy even though likely he's not going to play? >> Yeah, I mean, as long as we can have him around his guys. He was out there doing uh some metabolics, moving around, um just walking and making sure he has good flexibility and mobility in his leg. I mean, if you watch him, if you look over there and and you see him walking around, you don't even know. Um and uh but they're just keeping him in shape and strong. That really helps going into the surgery in that process. And for people who've had ACLs, you know how that is. The stronger you go in, the quicker you can recover. So, um but again, having him out there, having him on the sideline around his guys, being involved in football even as we have even even after he gets surgery and he comes back to us, you know, the more we can just have him being involved, um it's good for the team. It's good for Nick. >> Hey coach, Cam Jackson was like a different player in the second uh training camp. What What changes have you noticed in his play, in his confidence, and his overall demeanor? >> Yeah, just being comfortable in the system, understanding how we want certain plays to be executed. And he's a big, powerful man, 6'6, 350 something. Um and uh pair all that up with the knowledge of where I'm going to be, the more he starts to anticipate what's happening before the snap, the better he'll perform. So, that's what I'm expecting from here for Cam is to just keep dialing into the concepts. He's going to see some repeat plays here pretty soon in camp to dial in those things so he can take his shots when they're there. >> Uh just Lot Walker, he seemed pretty solid on the left today. But what have you seen from him during camp? >> Yeah, I mean, just one day at a time, just being able to like, you know, just challenge the group, um bring out the best in the group. And I just, you know, without getting into any specifics, you know, um I'm just excited that, you know, we have a veteran guy um that can uh really just create a level of comfort, as you can imagine, for the quarterback on that left side, you know, where he knows what he's doing. He's been around it all, he's seen it all, um, and, uh, you know, as as we have different guys popping in at guard, you know, it's really nice to just have that piece there. So, um, but he's got a lot of great energy, things I didn't know about him and his personality. He enjoys it. Uh, he celebrates stuff even when he's not in, and there's a big play on the offense, the first one with his hands in the air. Love that about him, love that he's bringing that kind of veteran leadership. All right, thank you. >> [music] >> Felt great. Uh, it's always good to get back into pads, and, uh, you know, you go through the off season, go through the beginning of camp, kind of just waiting for this day. You know, there's a lot of what ifs, and, oh, man, if I had pads on, I'd do this, I'd do that. So, it's nice to finally get to be able to do that, and, uh, it just brings up the level of competition, and it feels like real football. So, it's always exciting. >> Jaylen, uh, Dave said that he had to challenge the defense in the middle of practice, essentially, to say, "Hey, we need to bring the physicality up." Um, how do you think that impacted you today? >> Uh, I mean, I think it's a good reminder. I think that, uh, in general, you know, physicality, obviously, is the name of the game when it comes to the playing the good run defense, and yeah, that's something we want to bring every play. So, you know, obviously, some parts of it weren't good enough today. So, just, uh, you know, analyze that, be critical in film, and come back tomorrow with with, uh, great intention, and and, uh, great effort. >> Jaylen, he also mentioned, he I think he said he wants the defense to drive practice Why do you think it's important for your unit to be the ones to set that tone? >> Uh, because, like I said, I think, like, our team in general is trying to play a physical brand of football, and I think that, you know, when you look at defense in general, you know, obvious obviously there's some physicality involved to offense especially up front. Um but, you know, I'd say the best defenses are physical ones and so, you know, for us to be able to go out there and drive the energy, you know, they always say defense wins championships, all those type of things. So, uh you know, I think that it's important to have a vocal and high-energy defense and that's the potential that we have. So, we got to bring that every day. >> What have you seen going up against Bro Freeling today? Just how he's developing >> Yeah, he's been great. I mean, he's uh really strong. Uh you know, definitely works his hands very well. Uh you know, I think there's as a rookie, obviously there's always things to improve. I think he's, you know, getting accustomed to the speed, physicality, the playbook, all those different things, but, you know, he's very promising and I I love going against him. I think that he's going to get me better, I'm going to get him better. Uh and so, yeah, he's looking good. >> You were not here obviously to see Jonathan Brooks pre-injury. Just wonder what your assessment is so far and what you've seen down the little bit of this spring. >> Yeah, we we worked out a lot together this offseason. Uh you know, he's tried incredibly athletic, fast, uh works really hard. Him and Chubba, you know, they're kind of inseparable when it comes to uh their training regimen and things like that. Uh so, I think that, you know, them together, they're pushing each other and uh ultimately, you know, iron iron sharpens iron and competition competition breeds success. So, you know, I think having them two there is is going to be great for both of them. >> See him here in the building this summer. Is that what you mean by work ethic? >> Yeah, I mean, we trained together, we work out here at the facility. Uh like I said, him and Chubba are always competing uh whether we're working out, racing, doing anything. So, uh you know, I think that's great about both of them. >> You had a talk to you since the injury and what can you speak to that and the impact on that room and then guys having to step up to that void? >> Yeah, it's devastating. Uh you know, Nick is him and I have gotten very close in the short period of time that I've known him. Uh he's a guy that has an extremely high level of passion and care about this game and about everything. And so, you hate to see it happen to anybody, but especially someone who invests so much and loves this game so much, you know, it's it's brutal. And uh it's not fair, but ultimately, you know, I I've obviously experienced several season-ending injuries, and from coming from my experiences, like I literally ran to the locker room to to talk to him because I just know he's the type of guy that is going to be able to handle this adversity, and I just wanted to instill the experience and the wisdom I had when it came to that, you know, I think that ultimately, you know, there's always a silver lining in any adversity, and truthfully, you just have to find it, and you have to have that positive outlook and that positive perspective. And for him, understanding, you know, at this time of his career, he's going to be able to get healthy, he's going to be able to, you know, work on other areas of his body, going to be able to do things off the field that he might not be able to do. Uh and so, you know, ultimately, it's it's a blessing, and uh you know, he's just got to see it as that, and you know, we're going to miss him, and we do miss him every day. Uh and I'm just excited for him to recover and come back and and uh get back into full form because he's a absolute stud when he's on that field. >> Jaylen, knowing you said you you encouraged yourself and talked to him about it, how helpful is it for him to be here and engaged the way he was out here today? Just kind of looking around. >> I think it's super helpful. You know, being hurt is uh something that nobody really understands how alienating it can be until you've been in that position. You know, the way football is, we're so regimented, and we have to be so present and focused that, you know, if something's not in front of you, you really don't really pay a lot of attention to it. So, you know, as someone who's hurt, you have a completely different schedule, you know, you're never really around us, whether it's the locker room banter or the warm-ups, the training, you know, there's a lot of closeness that comes from the blood, sweat, and tears that we go through together on a daily uh daily basis. And so, when you're outside of that routine, it can be very alienating, uh can be depressing, uh can be just a really shitty experience. And so, you know, for him to be around, I think it's super helpful, just given the fact especially that he's young. Uh you know, we're all very close, like I said, you know, it's each their own. First time I got hurt, I stayed around the facility. The second time I went home and spent time with my family. So, you know, I think that he'll have a good mixture of both. And uh but right now I think it's important for him to be around and for us to be able to uplift him and vice versa cuz he's he is a a special energy that you know, really it's not the same without him. So. >> Jaylen, replacing Nick. Um, can you talk about his students and spring the last couple days? What is your first impression of him? >> He's twitchy. He's twitchy, he's explosive. Um, you know, he's dedicated, [snorts] you know, high focus, high energy. Uh so, I think he's a great player for us to have in. Uh so, I mean I I said I'm still getting to know him, but he's a cool guy and I think he's done a great job these last couple days. >> Did you see the picture of Nick dancing that Nick saw that looked like Michael Jackson did? >> I didn't see that, honestly. I was I was probably working on some drills or something. So, I'm going to have to look at it on the film and ask him about it. So, I I didn't hear about it until afterwards. >> What about Prince Tega Wanogho? You got to know him this past spring. What stands out to you with his second year coming up? >> Yeah, I mean Prince Tega I think he's probably the best pass rusher on our team. Uh you know, I think that he is extremely naturally gifted and I think that as he continues to develop, he can be a very special player. I think that he already has crazy attributes and uh you know, he's definitely learning. He's young. So, I'm excited to watch him grow. >> What stands out to you about him? >> I mean he's just athletic. He has crazy bend. Uh you know, a really good feel. Uh pass rushing is an art and so ultimately, you know, it's it's very nuanced. It's very it's not just like, oh, run full speed ahead and don't get blocked. It's you know, setting things up. It's a chess game. It's a you know, game within a game. So, I think he has a very good natural feel for pass rushing and I think his ceiling is extremely high. Cool. Thanks, guys. >> I feel good. Feel good to be back out there. I'm just trusting the process that the trainers and coaches have for me. Um I just hope and believe in myself throughout the whole rehab process. And it was a blessing to be able to be back out there. Um no, ma'am. No, ma'am. Happily I don't. I don't. Yes, sir. Yes, sir. I feel like I was. I feel like I'm back to 100% getting out there having fun with it. I think that was a part of the process. Yes, I think in the back of my mind, you know, obviously as a football player you have to get back out there and and be able to learn how to take hits, learn how to uh get your contact balance right back. And you know, obviously first day of pads it was it was good. I think I think as a team we could have had a better day. But it was good to be able to be out there have fun with our teammates. It was a blessing. Um I think I think that was the whole process of rehab throughout the whole year and a half that I've had to rehab and train and and learn to do that again. Obviously it didn't just come back right away. It's something that took a lot of time. Something that took a lot of training and a lot of trusting the the trainers and coaches in the plan that they had me on and have me on is great. So it's been awesome. >> So, you get marks like that after a long recovery like that. >> Do you reflect? Do you not want to reflect? Like sort of on on the on the journey back? >> Um I think I think as a human, you know, it's good for you to reflect. To to know where you come from. It also helps to for motivation to where you're going. Um and for me, being back out there it was it definitely is a confidence booster to know that that I'm fully healed and I can take hits again and I can be out there with my teammates um full speed having fun cutting doing everything that I need to do to help the team. >> There was a play in practice where you made some cuts and I think you ended up on the ground. I don't know if the guy got knocked down, but are the cuts almost to you more of a validation or as as much of a validation as the speed uh the speed as the top speed? >> Uh I think so. I think I think cutting is a is a part of a running back's game where you have to be out there and be able to cut. Um and then the speed por- portion of it, unfortunately, I know in OTAs I said that I was faster than Chuba. I'm just going to get this out the way. Said that I was faster than Chuba. And um this summer we we we ran we didn't race. It was a part of the workout and he recorded a higher top speed than me. So, I take my comment back. I'm not faster than Chuba. >> But you said you weren't racing. No, we weren't racing. It was just uh like top speed on the catapults. Just that was the top speed of the day. We ran like a certain distance and and that's just he recorded it. >> That you had to acknowledge that publicly in front of us. >> No, ma'am. That's just me taking accountability of of what I said in OTAs. >> But if you didn't say it was a race, you could have beat him. >> Uh I don't know. I don't know. I guess we'll have to see another day. >> John, the Hurricanes are special, but where would you be without Chuba? >> Uh to be honest, um it sounds cliche to say, but um I think I would I I don't I don't know where I would be because um he's helped me throughout since I first got here. Um you know, I came in with the injury and he helped me. He took me under his wing um and really guided me how to rehab, how to how to practice, how to learn, how to take notes and all of that. Um, and then especially when I got hurt again, he was he was right there with me. You know, he helped me throughout the whole way. He was there when I got baptized, and that just goes to say how much we've grown our brotherhood, and um, how close we've gotten. And then just to be able to work out with him this whole off-season has been amazing. Um, just to see how he trains. Um, he trains pretty hard. So, it was it was good for me to to tag along and and learn how to build my body right for training camp and for the season. >> And what are you expecting from yourself this season? Have you set any goals or >> Uh, for me just wherever the coaches and wherever the coaches want to put me, wherever and however, I just want to be able to help the team. >> Jonathan, you know you all didn't have pads on Sunday, but you had the experience of Derrick Brown talking to tackle clothes >> Uh, you know, it's different. DB's he's a big dude. Um, but you know, it's good. That's a part of the game. That helps me be able to uh, learn and build a course to like understand that that's just a part of the game. >> Jonathan, you mentioned Chubba and kind of the role he played in your own recovery process. And every time we talk to you, you talk about, you know, how important mentality is and then having been through it twice, do you feel like you're now in a position to kind of help guys like Nick who are going through something similar and then making sure they're keeping their their head on straight through >> Definitely. Definitely. I I check in every time I see him throughout the facility. I don't want to blow his phone up too much right now. You know, a lot of people probably hitting him up, but you know, I text him. I let him know that God's with him. Um, that this injury is is something small to where he's going. And uh, it's something he can he can bounce back from because um, there's proof in the pudding and and and whenever you trust in God, um, he's always going to make things right whether it's on your timeline or his. You know, for me for me, it took me two times to really understand it for him to set me back and and be able to I think it was a blessing in disguise for me to learn more, build my body more, um, become smarter for the game of football. >> What part of you is still wants to get past the the being tackled part, you know what I mean? You know, full contact, you know, 100%. Is there Is there a part of you in your mind that just wants to get that hurdle over with? >> Uh I mean, sort of, definitely. Um I think I think that's also a part of the game, also a part of the mentality, um part of part of coming back from injury, especially a lower body injury, being able to be tackled again. And I feel like it that would be another confidence booster getting tackled uh for the first time. >> Do you have any idea of what some of those benchmarks will be in the weeks and months coming forward? >> I'm just taking it day by day. I want to I want to be able to be um focused on each day that I'm in for camp. Um I just want to be able to be out there, know what I'm doing, help the team in any way I can, and just have my brothers' backs. >> It was a pretty chippy practice for these moments of aggression, including the fight, but also, you know, you and Corey after play very briefly. What was it like to kind of be in that aggressive mode again? >> Uh I I it was good. I think I think that's a part of the game. I think that's what comes with it whenever you're playing at the highest level. you know, everybody wants to get out there, and and you know, that's I think that's good for our team. That goes to show the the the bond that we've made this off season working out together. Um some of it's friendly, and some of it's not friendly on the field, and friendly right when you get off the field, and that's just a part of what football is. >> Coach praised your work in the receiving game today. With Chad Ochocinco and Steve Smith out here, you know, what were you hoping to take away from guys like that, and you know, did you get to interact with them at all today? >> Uh no, I didn't get the chance to interact with them. I just um and and I wish I did. Uh I just wanted to stay focused. You know, I'm I really want to be focused on what I have in front of me um this year, and just stay focused. I think that was pretty cool that they were out there to see two guys like that that I've looked up to my whole life um and watched growing up. I think that's pretty cool. >> Do you have anything from this summer besides training? >> Um this summer I got engaged this summer. Um I went to Banff, Canada and got engaged. Um and it was it was it was beautiful. Um my fiance has been wonderful in my rehab process, wonderful in my faith process, pushing each other to be better with our faith and our religion. And uh she's just been really awesome. >> John, the fan fest is coming up on Friday. I don't think you've been able to participate in those before. How excited are you just to get out there in front of fans? >> That's awesome. Um I think it's going to be a lot of fun to be able to be out there in in front of fans, let them see um the work that we're that we've put in all off season. Um and just to be able to interact with them, see the smiles on their faces, allow them to have fun uh while we get to work is is it's a pretty amazing feeling. >> Shout out. >> Thanks, guys.

title: Team Leaders Excited for Jesse Minter's First Training Camp | Baltimore Ravens Final Drive
text: The veterans have arrived at the facility and Ravens training camp is officially underway. It will be the first training camp with Jesse Mentor at the helm and the team's veteran leadership has been impressed with our head coach listening to their feedback. Tight end Mark Andrews talked about what he's seen from Mentor so far. He's been great about, you know, coming to the older guys and um just just hearing them out um and uh and listening and um you know, kind of incorporating that within um our day-to-days on the field, whatever it may be. So, I think that's incredibly important. Um I think having both Coach Weaver and Coach Monken in our defensive meeting room is is great. How does that system play out? Do you think that's going to help this defense? >> 100%. I think when you have guys who can play all over the place and you know, guys that know the jobs of the people beside you, it just allows everything to flow better and allows everyone to to play faster and and know and be able to help out your brother beside you if he doesn't, you know what I mean? I think he's going to have a great year for sure. >> What has Trey brought to that room just behind closed doors? What's his presence been like in that room for you? >> Yeah, Trey's honestly one of the hardest workers I've been around. Um he's been here since the first voluntary workout and he was here all summer. So, you know, the past six weeks we've just been grinding and getting after it. So, to see a guy like him who, you know, with the career that he's had, he doesn't have to be at anything that's not mandatory and he's been here since day one. So, it's been great to have his leadership in the room as well, for sure. >> Okay, so what do you think having a clean slate means to just this locker room at large with, you know, so many of these coaches being new guys to Baltimore? >> Yeah, I think honestly, I think every year is a, you know, on this day is the it's a clean slate. It's been great. Um you know, so it's exciting. I feel better than I've ever felt, and I think it's going to be a big year, for sure. >> Davis, what are you looking to improve individually this season? >> Yeah, I think every year I'm just trying to grow as a player every year. I want to get better in the pass, and I just want to be a better player than I was last year, and continue to do that every year I play, for sure. >> Davis, just um going back to what you were saying about the way things are built defensively and so forth, what's maybe different or kind of stood out to you along those lines, um you know, so far? >> Yeah, I think there's just little different things that allow us to play, um you know, there's different ways we can play things, I'll say. So, it just kind of allows us to play um fast, you know, allows us to play free, and it's uh yeah, it's going to be exciting, for >> All right. >> Good. Appreciate you guys. All right, thank you.

title: Ronnie Stanley: 'Vega Ioane Looks Like a Seasoned Vet' | Baltimore Ravens
text: So, what kind of what would you kind of describe you know Jesse's coaching style and kind of what he has brought so far to this team? >> Uh I think he just brings a a positive, you know, mentality and optimistic outlook on, you know, every individual in the building. Um he just pumps belief into the players and I think that's just, you know, his his big focus on, you know, coming into this team. >> Ronnie, because of the leg injuries in the past couple of seasons, training differently this offseason. What did you do? >> Uh you know, I I do a lot of cross training in my offseason. I try to do a lot of different things. Um attack different parts of the body, different parts of the system, and um that's something I try to be pretty consistent with. I've been pretty consistent with the last few years. >> Ronnie, I mean obviously you you played for one head coach for for 10 years. I mean, we haven't talked to you since that happened. I mean, take us through, you know, how did you find out? How did you sort of process that news? >> Yeah, you know, I found out on social media. Just kind of um I don't forgot like early in the offseason. Uh you know, but uh like you said, I've been with the same coach for 10 years and Coach Harbaugh has been a great coach and I've nothing but love for him and you know, positive energy for him and his tenure with the New York Giants and I know he's going to be successful wherever he goes. >> Ronnie, how strange is it though? I mean, you're the longest-tenured player. The coaching staff's brand new. I mean, is it strange kind of being like the guy who's been around longer than just about anyone here? Yeah, you know, >> different um I would say this year more than most, you know, especially with the new coaching staff and as well with uh a lot of new players. You know, we saw a lot of a lot of former Ravens have been here for a while uh leave this past offseason. But, you know, change is inevitable. That's something that happens throughout life and you know, I pride myself as being someone that's um very adaptable to whatever situation I'm in. >> Do you think I mean, obviously you had a lot of admiration for for John and the time you were with him. But, do you think you know, when the change was change was made, do you think that sometimes from you know, from your perspective that you know, sometimes just things run its course and change is good? Is that Is that sometimes a perspective? >> You know, I think change is just inevitable, like I said, and um whether you look at it being good or bad, I think that's up to the individual. And um you can turn into a optimistic situation or pessimistic situation, and um you know, it's kind of it's subjective. So, I try to look at it as, you know, um glass half full, and try to uh focus on the positives that can come out of it. >> What do you think of your your new offensive line coaches? >> I think they're great. I think all of our coaches are great. Coach Leffers has done a great job of um you know, coming to the room, getting to know the guys um outside of the football player that they are, and just the person that they are, and um I think he's a great coach technique-wise, and um his scheme is great as well. >> Schematic change at all? >> Yeah, I think schematically it's, you know, a lot of different things going on, but uh football is football at the end of the day. >> Ronnie, how do you expect Jesse Minter to to run this training camp, and how it may differ from training camps previously? >> You know, I think Jesse's going to have his own uh style, um you know, uh how he structures uh the camp, the practices, the timing. Things are definitely going to be different, um but I think he's going to do everything that's going to benefit the players, and um everything will be for our benefit to be our best on game day. >> What is working with Declan been like? You know, he's very young. What is it about him that commands the room, and has gained all of your >> Uh I've been very impressed with Declan, and just his leadership abilities, especially for such a young guy to come in and uh control a room, you know, uh he's very intelligent, and he has a great way of conveying information to other people, and um I think there's just a a sense of wisdom and about him that is really going to, you know, bode well for us. >> How much do you think, like having such a young offensive coordinator, how much do you think you think how how can that play to his advantage do you think as as >> How can what play to his advantage? >> Being young, being so young and and you know what most offensive coordinators you see in the league, you know, these are sometimes 50, 60 years old. How can you know, maybe being so young work to his advantage do you think? >> Uh I think he can just learn from other people's experience, you know, a lot of these OCs quite a bit older than him and I think he can lean on experience that he's had in the past with a lot of great coaches as well as having his you know, new age creativity and mentality and kind of honing those two things together and you know, becoming the coach he is now. >> Ronnie, what do you think about Venga and how he's been so far and also just drawing the comparison with like, you know, big investment first round offensive lineman, you know, to yourself. How is that relationship been and how have you guys kind of bonded over that? >> Vegas been great. I I see everything I want to see from a pro, especially you know, an early draft pick and an offensive lineman. He comes in, he's all about his business. You know, he looks like a seasoned vet out there. I'm I'm not worried about him one bit. >> As a unit as an offensive line, what has to happen for you guys to have a have a better year than than last year? >> I think we just need to be more consistent, you know, we showed a lot of flashes, you know, there's a lot of games where we really controlled the game, but you know, there's a lot of inconsistencies you know, throughout the season. I think that's something that you know, we can do. >> How's the reunion with Johnson in the middle of the line? >> Oh, it's been great. Johnson's a great player, great guy. You know, I love his energy. He brings his energy to the room every day. He's always in a upbeat mood, doesn't matter what time it is and you know, it's been great. >> Ronnie, when you know, when they made the change, Steve Bisciotti talked about how he you know, spoke with the players ultimately came to to his decision, but I'm curious what interactions you've had with with Jesse in In of you know, sounds like he's kind of picked some of your guys some of the veterans' brains and in terms of gotten input from them and what's that been like for you? >> Uh it's been great, you know, it just shows that he wants to listen to us and he values what we say and he's going to take the time to hear us out, you know, we might not always agree, but I think it's just a matter of uh him putting that importance on our words and you know, that means a lot to players. >> Has there been a a message or you know, just broadly speaking even that that you conveyed? >> Uh I think, you know, just reiterating what I said earlier, just about the positive mentality and you know, things might go bad, there's going to be adversity, but it's all about how you look at things and how you're going to approach, you know, bad times as well as good times. >> Ronnie, uh Coach Minter talked about how he feels like the offensive line is really kind of the the unit that drives the team. Like how the offensive line plays, that's how the team plays. He's just a strong believer in the offensive line's importance. What what's that mean to you to hear that from the head coach? >> Uh it means a lot because, you know, I truly believe the same thing. Um you know, offensive line, I think a lot of the team uh whether they know it or not, they look to the offensive line for encouragement, um for leadership and you know, for a head coach to embody that same mentality, you know, I think says a lot to especially a defensive head coach to embody that mentality, I think says a lot to his understanding and knowledge of, you know, the game within the game. >> Ronnie, as somebody who has been through long injury comebacks and kind of uncertainty, what have you noticed in how now Non-Dame Eche has handled this whole situation and what would it mean for the rest of the players, particularly ones who've been around him for a while to see him back on the practice field? >> I mean, he's handled the situation great. He's done everything he's good to to try to help the team try to be back on the field and he's doing a great job right now. I see him out there every day working um and it'll mean a lot for the team. I mean, he's our he's our defensive leader on that line and you know, the trenches is where it all starts and you know, on that front, you know, people look to him for leadership. >> Ronnie, Lamar Jackson said that he has enjoyed being challenged by coach D'Alessio far. How do you think you and the rest of the offense have been challenged by coach D'Alessio in the off-season? >> Uh you know, he's a very detail-oriented person and I think that's that's really what he's about whether it be how you're how fast you're coming off the ball or um your assignment will leverage your taking. I think he wants details. He wants everyone to be focused and um that's really challenged everyone, you know, to be on their, you know, top game at all times. >> Ronnie, you've seen up close with Derrick Henry and how hard he works and what he puts in and how he takes care of his body. Do you ever think like how how much longer can this this guy Running backs aren't supposed to be around this league this long and producing at that level? How how long do you think he can go? >> He can go as long as he wants, you know, as long as he's having fun and he feels good, you know, he could play as long as he wants cuz they don't build humans like that, you know. So, there's not many challengers, um I'd say. >> Ronnie, Aaron Glenn said that he's seen he expects like a big step forward from Carson Vinson. From year one to the year two, just how much development have you seen from him? >> I've seen a ton of development. I mean, Carson came in a very uh raw tackle technically, but every single, you know, year, every practice, he's come in with the attitude and mentality to get better. Um he's always trying to learn. Uh he's always asking me questions. Uh he's been like a sponge. Um and that's something that's all you can ask for for, you know, a young tackle uh trying to make a name for themselves in this league. >> Ronnie, what have your initial impressions of Trey Hendrickson been? >> Uh I mean, I played against the guy for the last 8 years, so I kind of already knew what to expect, but um personality-wise, you know, he's a great teammate. Uh you know, that's the type of guy you want in the locker room. He's always been that way, you know, that's always been a guy that you play against, you're like, yeah, that's a guy you'd want on your team and I'm very blessed and fortunate to be working against him every day in practice cuz, you know, we're only going to make each other better and at the same time I feel like we have a great relationship to where we enjoy the process together. >> How different not having to face him or Miles Garrett in the AFC North anymore? >> Yeah, it's a lot of differences this year, I'd say. >> I think you can miss like >> I'm not going to wait two games since October 2023 and do you feel like you've kind of turned the corner from what you had gone with going through back in 2020? >> Yeah, definitely uh being able to consistently train and um improve over the years over the off-season since that injury has definitely helped build uh more of a consistent you know, output from me. >> Great. >> All right, thank you Ryan. >> Thanks, Ryan.

title: CB Pat Surtain II as training camp begins: ‘We’ve got the right guys with the right mentality’
text: What's your favorite part of this new digs? >> Um honestly everything's state of the art. When I first got in which was yesterday, I was looking and I was like wow, I was in awe. Um you know it's pretty special. I mean it's a testament to you know ownership group, Greg and Carrie for putting this together. So it's awesome. Feels like I'm in a maze right now though trying to figure out where to navigate, where to go but you know it's pretty awesome. >> Pat, there are few teams that could have a Super Bowl or close mentality going into the season. How close you got last year? Is that how you and this group feels? >> Um yeah, our expectations are pretty high but you know we just going to take it week by week. Um No obviously that's the main goal but you know we got to it starts right here in training camp. Starts early on in the season. I think our main focus is to start off fast, start off you know hot and early so that way we could propel ourselves to get you know to that stage. So >> You came from a program that just had championship standards before you got there. What can you say about those last couple steps? This group has come so far but my feeling is the last couple steps are the biggest ones. Do you agree or disagree but what's your thought on that? >> Yeah, I think it is. I think we got all the right pieces, the right team. Um and coaches invest a lot into us and pour a lot into us as well too. So Um I think you know when you put all that together, you know it makes for a great team and you know we got the right guys with the right mentality to start things off the right way. So you know this team is great you know all across the board. So >> Hey Pat, Jaymac got here your your second year. He was on the practice squad I think I think Smith, it was year on the practice squad. But, I'm curious if there were early signs that you had working with him and being alongside him that kind of, you know, made you believe he could become the player he has for you guys which is just sort of the >> Yeah. >> makes the biggest play. >> Yeah, I mean, his his mindset is off the charts and, you know, the way how he carry himself, you know, on and off the field. Uh his work ethic, you know, I mean, there's only a few that quite work like him. You know, I mean, like you said, being undrafted, uh coming in, uh nobody knew about him. But, now, you know, uh he's a hot commodity. Uh it goes to show, uh you know, the work he's put in. Um you know, and how much he value and how much he owns in on his craft. So, um you know, I'm excited for J'Mar. You know, obviously, he's a big-time player. But, I'm happy that he's finally getting, you know, his spotlight, you know. >> To have VJ back as the DC with all the continuity that you already have on your defensive unit, what can that do for you guys? >> Oh, it does a lot. Um you know, uh having VJ on our side, you know, a guy that's, you know, been in this league uh for a long time, but knows the ins and outs of this game and, you know, when you when you talk to him, I mean, everything is about him, you know, speaks volumes. You know, he's even a better person, you know, so, you know, having a guy like that on the defensive side of the ball, um you know, just translate to success. >> You guys have been a top five defense for a couple years in a row now. What what's the next step that this defense can take it to to improve it? >> Um sure, I feel like every year there's, you know, everybody got new goals, but I feel like as long as we continue to stay consistent. I think with us just like I mentioned before, starting off fast early on, uh not allowing, you know, not allowing anything to go by. You know, I just feel like that's our next step. Um and sort of just staying committed to the process, you know, trusting, uh you know, what VJ got for us, you know, trusting us, our defense as a unit, you know what I mean? We got the right pieces in the right places. So, you know, it just feels right right now. So, >> To be the best defense, do you need to get more takeaways in your mind? >> That's true. I think we could do that. When the ball is in the air, capitalize on more opportunities with taking the ball away. You know, obviously those [clears throat] game-changing plays are very vital, you know, in NFL games. Taking the ball away and uh this doing that would definitely help us a lot, too. >> Passer, kind of a two-part question on this facility. Broncos in recent years did well in the NFLPA survey with the exception of locker room. So, A, how much better is the locker room than it used to be? And then the same question I asked Quinn, how much can this help maybe luring free agents and what have you? >> Well, yeah, it's been a long time coming. You know, the locker room is crazy. It's quite unique as well, too. And it just gives a a different feel, different vibe. You know, it's like we're leaving that in the past and we're entering, you know, a new state, a new year. And yeah, I think it's um you know, it's well deserved for us as players, you know, with the amount of work we put in as well, too. But yeah, everything's starting to come together with the facility. And yeah, I'm looking forward to you know, building with the guys and you know, being able to be in this building. It's quite special. >> Can it be a recruiting tool for free agents, you know, when they start coming through next >> Yeah, pretty much so. It feels like I'm in college again. Feels like I'm immersing to that experience again. So, like I said, credit to Greg and Carrie for putting all this together for us. So, >> What was your first reaction when you walked into the facility? Did you walk into the locker room? Did you just take it all in? Did you >> Um you know, my expectations was high and it definitely exceeded my expectations. I don't think there's nothing like uh this in the league. I mean, it's state-of-the-art. Um very nice facilities, everything. Um and it's it seems like, you know, when you look at it, you know, obviously you look at the locker rooms, the facilities, it just seemed like it was meant to be, you know, uh and they put it uh in the right spot, in the right position uh with this team. So, um it's great that we have this to our disposal. >> Pat, obviously Jeff Allen left in free agency. Cooper's status is a little unclear for the season. Can you Can you talk to us and walk us through Obviously you haven't seen these guys during camp yet, but the depth on on the defensive front, the young guys, you know, any Savion, Sheldon Rankins. Like, what have you seen from those guys? Do you think they they can help you match/exceed the standard from last year? >> Yeah, I mean, that's you know, that's part of the business, as it says. Um you know, obviously when great players leave, uh you know, you got to count on other guys to step up. But, like like you mentioned, Savion, Any, uh those guys, you know, they've been, you know, working very hard. You know, obviously Savion, a young guy, uh stepping up last year in his role. And Any, he's been a baller as well, too, you know, stepping up in his role, too, you know, year in and year out. So, um you know, I feel like uh the expectations stay the same um even when Jeff Jeff Allen was here. I know that room uh hold each other to high standards. Uh and I feel like they expect the same out of uh both those two. So. >> Pat, when it comes to the secondary, P.J. Locke is also gone in free agency. Who, Pat, number three safety are you excited about taking advantage of those opportunities? >> Yeah, I mean, uh we got a lot of uh great pieces uh you know, to fill that void. You know, obviously P.J. uh was a great player, a very uh instrumental part to our team. So, um you know, we obviously you know, you got J.L., uh Devin Key, uh and a couple other guys as as well, too, to step up and fulfill that spot. So, I'm looking forward to it. It's going to be a fun camp. >> So, Pat, you got this year of continuity, but you have new coaches in in your room with Livingston and Bell. What When you've been in the league for a while and you've gotten new coaches, like how do you sort of pick their brain or or take things from them and learn [laughter] from them if maybe they use a little bit different language or whatever the case is? >> Yeah, you know, I think it's pretty awesome to have the opportunity to learn from them as well. And just to really be transparent with one another, you know, cuz obviously they come from different experiences. Obviously, with Coach Livingston, you know, he's coming from college from Colorado. Then you got Coach Bell as well coming from college as well, too, but sort of implementing that what they learned throughout their years and sort of me you know, just telling them what I learned throughout my years as well, too. I think it goes hand in hand collectively. And you know, they're great all in all. You know, very transparent with us as players and you know, I mean they're very great coaches and they understand everything to T to quite the detail, so I'm excited to work with them this year. >> How does it feel Does it feel like year six or is that kind of hard to believe? And how's your your mindset and perspective any changed? >> I mean, honestly, man, it doesn't even feel like year six. It feels like when I was a rookie just starting to come in starting to quite come in my shell, but yeah, time be flying and you know, just seeing you know, how far this team has came has been quite surreal, honestly, to say the least. So, yeah, I'm excited to enter year six and get it going again.

title: The Bengals Have Raised the Standard Entering Training Camp | Enter the Jungle
text: Bengals training camp is here, which means it's time for our training camp checklist. The latest from Duke Tobin, Zack Taylor, and more on a jam-packed edition of Enter the Jungle. So, there's just it's an hour straight of it being interviewed. And so, I get why 90-year-old Mike Brown isn't necessarily going uh through that. We'll see if that happens. But Duke Tobin did talk. Zack Taylor did talk. The coordinators did talk. A and my main thing before we dive into this checklist. There wasn't the lingering drama last year. Mike Brown saying, "Hey, we're working to get Trey done. Hopefully, it's done right now." Right? Think about that. Two years ago, it was Jamar and in what was going on there and in the hope that they would get that done. Years before that, there was more Trey involved. There was Joe Burrow's contract. Like, it's always been a contract. There were contract questions. We'll hear from Duke in a second, but it did didn't feel dramatic like some of these other negotiations and and conversations have been in the past. >> Yeah. And if you remember this time last year when Duke was speaking at this media lunch and the topic of Shamar Stewart had had come up. It was you know what the to your Yeah.
