So, that's how we identify those strengths is really important to us as coaches. >> Coach, no more Daniel Carlson. AJ said it was kind of fun to have rookies in camp. What has that looked like to you so far? >> Uh you mean just having as many rookies as we do have as part of the roster? >> Kickers, like rookie kickers kind of hanging out. >> Yeah, well, just having competition is always good at the snapper position, you know, at the kicker position. Uh competition um is great for the whole team. Um so, you know, look forward to watching those guys compete and making each other better. >> As you prepared to enter your first training camp as a head coach, is there anybody that you leaned on or anybody that you took advice from in developing your plan? >> Uh yeah, the guys that we hired, you know, we we got a a veteran staff. We got some mix of youth, but um just being being in constant contact with all of our coaches and making sure we're on the same page. But, uh you know, Mike McCoy as the as the assistant head coach, you know, Joe DeCamillis many years of experience, Rick Dennison uh many years of experience. Those are guys that I have leaned on every day. >> You are your coaching style, you embrace the grind. You like that. How much are you looking forward to watching that battle for those two guard spots? >> Yeah, absolutely. You know, we don't get to even put pads on, I think, till the you know, sixth practice. uh we got a lot of work to do before then, but um you know, we have we have a lot of talented players at that position. I you know, it'll they will uh they'll make the decision for us. So, uh we're going to coach them up, and we also know that uh whoever starting week one doesn't mean that's the starter in week 17. So, we're we're always developing and getting guys better throughout the entire training camp and throughout the whole season. >> What are you looking for at those spots? What How will they make that decision for you? >> Um just looking for consistency, looking for guys that are uh that are great teammates, that are um obviously solid in pass protection, excellent in the run game, and and guys um that just help make the team better, you know, the best the best athlete isn't isn't the one that's going to win the job. It's the guy that plays the best with the other five around him. And then, you know, offensive line-wise, unless you're playing tackle, you better be able to play multiple spots. So, having versatile guys is very important. >> Early to ask, but is there one person or position group who's won the off-season, do you feel? >> Is there a position group that has won the off-season? >> Excuse me. you know, I I just give a whole lot of credit to uh to Alex Guerrero and AJ and our training staff. I thought, you know, those guys do such a phenomenal job of putting our players' bodies in position to be successful and uh tracking data and just really taking it to the next level with uh the technology that we can to get the guys ready to go and challenge them. Um So, I you know, the players the players' challenge is up ahead. I'm really uh impressed with our, you know, the guys the training staff and the weight staff. >> How do you chart growth for Fernando over the next several weeks? What are you looking for? What do you want to measure? well, you know, it's it's not just charting charting picks and completion percentage. It is uh you know, we've put a lot on his plate in this off-season. Uh we expect a lot out of him as these practices start coming. So, the thing that stands out to me is, you know, he's going to have plenty of adversity like his teammates and how does he deal with it? Does he make the same mistake twice? Um how quickly can he correct himself, you know, when when he does make a mistake? What's his attitude like? What's his demeanor like? Um those are those are really important things for quarterbacks. >> You had mentioned uh you know, being able to watch a veteran quarterback and learn through osmosis. How how valuable has Kirk Cousins been so far for Fernando early on? >> Yeah, I mean, I would I would say his value as a player on our team is the most important thing, you know, where his leadership, his veteran presence, you know, the way that he played in the spring was was excellent. So, that's we brought him here to to play really good football and obviously the mentorship, that's that's a byproduct of that. That's the kind of guy that that Kirk is, but Kirk knows and Fernando knows and Aiden knows and Jacob knows that they're here to play great football and you know, that's our job as coaches to get them ready for the other stuff. >> What are you hoping to see out of Jack Besh and Dante Thornton when training camp starts? >> Uh yeah, just see him compete, you know, there's there's a lot of competition in that receiver room. Um so, let's just let's just go play ball and may the best man win. Also knowing that those guys got to be able to play special teams for us and play them at a high level. So, um just like we talked about with the line, whoever's, you know, starting and and getting more reps in week one, it's a long season and everyone's going to play. So, we just need those guys to compete and and make sure that they're available for all these practices so they can keep getting better. >> Coach, you Uh for you, um going into your first training camp as a head coach, what are your emotions like and how you feeling about, you know, being in this position and on a competing role? >> Just focusing, I mean, it's it's obviously that I'm in a new role, but it's a it's a we thing. Our coaching staff is making sure that that we're on our stuff so that we're the best versions of ourselves for these players so we can be great teachers and give these guys the information they need to have and put them through the stresses that we believe they'll see in the game so that the game you know, is not as hard as practice. So, it's just it's more about our staff working together with the scouts, with this training staff and being on the same page for these players. >> Outside of this building, obviously being the number one overall pick, Fernando gets a lot of attention, but Signetic said that what set him apart to him was his willingness to prepare before the game. Was that one of the things that really stood out to you as you went through the evaluation process? Is that willingness to prepare again, he's not Tom, he's a rookie, but you heard the same things about Tom. >> Uh yeah, I think I think that's what you expect out of a quarterback. And um just because someone says they work hard, there's totally different levels to that. And I would say in the evaluation evaluation process that he stood head and shoulders above others that I've been around. Um that doesn't guarantee you anything on Sunday. So it gives a it's a head start. Um gives him a great chance to go have a heck of a practice, but it's really what he does on the field, which is what's going to decide his fate. And um but the way that he prepares in a meeting room is what you want. >> What is the benefit or the drawback of having to do early morning practices on the field before you do other work inside the building? >> Uh yeah, the benefit is being outside on the grass. That's the benefit. Like these these players' bodies are uh are Ferraris and they perform better on the grass. The the negative is not having a meeting before practice. That's the way I see it. >> And how else is it important is that also with this heat? What are the things you're doing to protect the players? >> Uh yeah, well, you know, it's it's promoting, you know, all the things away from the from the field is is hydration and and nutrition and sleep habits and the things that that Ricky and our training staff are, you know, showing these guys in team meetings. So we have a we have a really great staff there, but it's uh you know, it's just part of our team meetings every day is how do we take the best care of our body and, you know, it starts with going to sleep early at night so that they're ready to practice tomorrow. >> Since you're not able to meet before practice due to how early you start practice, is there something that you guys do to to supplement that? >> Yeah, we do. We just uh you know, we use our our afternoon walk-throughs to uh to prepare for the next day's practice. Uh you know, uh we got, you know, great technology sending out the materials, the guys' iPads, film, and scripts. yes, there's quite a quite a few things that we do, and then that's where the players have to be self-motivated and and go back to their hotel room and uh you know, instead of shooting the breezes, getting down and studying their scripts on their iPad. >> Coach, you've had a few months to call Las Vegas home, but have you and your family had the opportunity to really experience this community? >> Yeah, we have. We have um really uh um ever ever since I got here, it's been it's been such an impressive place to be, you know, I'm really proud to to be a part of this community and, you know, I'm really looking forward to working working my tail off with our staff to to earn a spot in this community. So, I got a lot of work to do there. >> Do you have a favorite part about training camp or anything specific? you know, the the thing that I love about football is is teaching the players and building relationships. And when you're with the guys 11 hours a day is what the league gives you, uh you can't help but but build great relationships. You know, you can't hide from each other. Um those are the things that you love about about being a coach. So, um during during training camp, there is no wins and losses, you know, there's a lot less uh pressure that way for the players, but uh there is a lot of great time to get to know each other, and uh that's what stands out. >> You've told us a couple times leading, you know, leading up to this that your preference is to have a rookie watch a veteran quarterback, but do you do you categorize that as a competition? Is it Kirk as the starter with, you know, the other guys trying to catch him? Like, I guess how do you categorize that? >> Yeah. Um you know, for every position, it's there's got to be competition, right? The best player has has to play, And that's not just what I'm going to see, you guys are going to see it in the preseason games, you know, we as coaches, we're going to see who's the best guard is, okay? Best quarterback. Um across the board, there's there's battles everywhere on the roster. So, um it's important for me to be fair to players to put the best player out there. When we go out to practice tomorrow, Kirk Cousins is the starting quarterback. He's the guy. And uh he's going to get a ton of reps. And he deserves them because he's played really good football, but I want Fernando and I want Aidan to push him. >> That'll set. Thanks, coach. >> Thanks. >> Thank you. >> Thanks, coach.

I think Big Q came in the middle of the season and K came a little bit earlier in the season, so just about repetition now and bringing the guys, the young guys that we got now and bringing them along with us. >> Describe the juice your DC brings to the to the staff. >> Man, it's special, it's special, you know, CP's a young guy, smart, you know, obviously we've been playing him every year two two times a year and you know, seeing what he's been able to do with those defensive guys over in Philly, so you know, correlating that to here, but also adding a little more, you know, we talked about you know, guys talk about the defense of the Philadelphia Eagles and Vic's defense, you know, we we kind of built our own thing throughout the OTAs, so just looking forward to putting it all together and now just kind of getting the season rolling. >> Is there a chip on the defensive shoulder and if so, is it something good to embrace it? >> Absolutely, absolutely, you know, we always had, you know, on paper, you know, talented defense, but it's not, you know, just about being talented, it's about putting it all together and being disciplined with it, which we felt like we haven't been this past couple years, whether that be throughout the playoffs, you know, simple penalties and giving up big plays just off of miscommunication. We're looking forward to, you know, just kind of putting it all together and building off that, cuz like I said, we got a talented guys, we got a lot of young guys that's coming in that's very special after seeing them in OTAs and smart and willing to learn, so we're just looking forward to getting out there on the field and kind of just getting it rolling now at this point. >> Back-to-back seasons without the playoffs, is there a different hunger maybe already going into this training camp with you guys? >> Yeah, yeah, absolutely. I mean, just the guys we got, man, we got competitive guys on this team, not only just for, you know, you know, individually, but as a team overall, everybody wants to win. We got a lot of guys that come from winning cultures on this defense and you know, it's just about going out there competing and also having fun with it, you know, we felt like last couple years have been kind of uptight, you know, just off of the simple fact of, you know, our our standard not being met of what we wanted on the defense, so now it's just about having fun and also, like I said, just keep buying into it and tied into the details. >> What is the >> guys. What does a successful training camp look like for you individually and as a team? >> Uh first off, just kind of, you know, giving the knowledge that I have in my tenure career being in the league to the young guys and kind of teaching them what I know. But not all only that, but still proving to myself that I'm still able to do this at a high level. Like I said, it's been a long time of me being here, not only in Dallas, but in the league in general. So, just proving myself right year in and year out of being able to go out there and still be able to be the player and effective in ways that not only that I might not see on the stat sheet, but other people will not see, whether that be vocally, you know, whether that be just going out there and you know, telling guys what they can do and what they can do as far as the defensive scheme and you know, just having fun with it. You know, once you play for so long, some guys tend to lose the funness of it, but for me it's just about having fun, you know, still believing in my confidence and my capabilities of what I do as a defensive player and just going out there and compete. >> All right, guys. Thank you. >> Appreciate you guys. Thank you.

Um, the way you know he's an elite coach, Tommy, is when you walk by his office and players, I mean, multiple players are in there wanting to listen and talk to him about scheme and things like that. Um, but the organization, you know, the the way he's organized this camp on the defensive side of the ball from the individual section to the tackling circuit drills to the ball disruption drills to uh the install packages from first and second down fronts, pressures, coverages, things like that. Um, he is a firsttime coordinator that doesn't act like a first-time coordinator. >> How difficult is it to in your first year doing it, you had it as a head coach last year, like you mentioned, this is his year as a coordinator, to put together a plan like that for the first time. He's known that this is where he wanted to be in the defensive coordinator chair of an NFL football team. And, uh, again, maybe the hardest working coach I've ever been around. And um that's why we're so excited about not just him, but the staff that we put together, the amount of hours that went into identifying the strengths of Christian Parker, Chadera, Derek Ansley, these guys, I mean, it was tireless. And so that's why I laugh about it was a quiet offseason. It was on the outside, maybe with storylines, but for us, we worked our asses off. And I'm excited to finally see it all come out into real football. >> Michelle, >> Michelle Montaine, WFA. Derry, do you personally feel pressure to win this season? >> Yes. Yes, I do. >> For all the obvious reasons. Um um we've got certain things in place here >> that won't stay in place. Uh we've uh uh now I personally uh think that when you haven't done it before, when you're not necessarily young, you just haven't done it before. I think that is a huge value to your associates. I think that you not not ever uh not ever uh being uh some of the things you've always wanted to do. And I think we're going to get a lot of that. Obviously, it's a great thing to have experience of somebody that's done something for 20 years, but that is a good pressure to be involved with a group that has really they can do something they haven't been a part of. I saw where Williams said he's never been a part of a a playoff team. Now think about that player as as accomplished as he is hadn't been a part of a football of a playoff. Well, there is a big plus there. That's good. So, u I like the makeup. I I'm uh aware that we're doing some things for the first time in a lot of places, but I think that's going to be offset by uh with our coaching, the makeup of the coaching and frankly the mix of some of the new guys yet they are veteran players as they mix with some of the newer guys that are, if you will, last year were playing college. I think all that is a a big plus. We'll see. Uh if uh I don't care where whether they are rookies or whether they're 10-year guys, if they can't communicate with each other when they get out there, it didn't make any difference on an individual basis where they were. And uh one of the main things that I have heard us talk about and say in interviews, countless interviews, and after we made the decision of who's going to be doing the coaching, the word of communicate, talking to each other, understanding what it is that the other one is expects of the other one. This thing has been is adnauseium, the chant. If you listen real hard out there when you're watching practice, you'll hear it be one of the real focal points of this whole camp is communication. >> Deuce Mike Ducey, Fox 4. Brian, you may have answered this in part, but in spite of how long you've been around the game, were there things or maybe one thing in particular you experienced having gone through this yourself the first time last year that will serve you especially well in here, too? Yeah, I mean Mike, you know, it's a longer story than just one response. I mean, you learn things every day when you go through this process. I think, um, you know, there's countless lessons that you learn. I'm real big into doing afteraction reports on everything that we do. Uh, from the way we, you know, grade film, the way we throw a practice, the way we have a mock, the way we have a meeting, things like that. Um, and I'm also real big on not rinsing and repeating. What I mean by that is I don't like the first team meeting to feel like the same first team meeting that was last year, right? I think players in this era tune you out. So, um, but the big thing coming out here is is is I want us to practice and I want us to have, uh, you know, really physical practices and, you know, we know how to practice the right way. We know how to protect one another. Uh but uh you know, we're uh we're excited about getting out there on the grass and playing real football. And um you know, but there's a number of things I'm always learning and I honestly I lean on everybody. I lean on the players. I lean on Jerry and Stephen and Will and um you know, the way I make decisions is by talking and it helps me to to think out loud like that. >> Jerry, Super Bowl's come up a dozen times here already. With that said, what would have to happen for you to consider this a successful season for your football team? Oh, I think to contend for a Super Bowl, which would if you contend, you got a real chance of being in it and uh being in the game. I think those are the kinds of things that uh I don't believe are an outlandish or a reach to expect. And so u uh that's a successful season. I expect us to be significantly improved defensively. significantly improved and I actually expect us to improve over on the offense and I expect the enthusiasm that coach has talked about here to be contagious on the field and if something like that happen you can have somebody get in the get in the big hunt and get in the deal that maybe a lot of people didn't think were ready for it. So, u I've uh uh let me let me let me just say this. U u there's no way that I would do anything that would delay until next year or the next year to try to get to a Super Bowl this year. I feel that good about what we're starting with that and it kind of alludes over to what we were talking about. if a a trade or something like that came along. Uh we we certainly can think about uh as far as my focus, my individual focus is concerned. Uh I'm interested in being as good as we can opening day. >> Larence, there's so much talk. We talk about a quiet offseason and I guess what we mean is there's no drama, right? Had you ever done any work? Uh, did you learn anything from last year dealing with Micah and how you dealt with pickins to eliminate drama this off season? >> Well, they're two different really uh two completely different situations and u uh different people. Uh, I want to uh I want to give uh Shotti uh really accolade for how he worked through this uh with George and u in terms of not him but how he helped us communicate and work through it. Uh, this can be a very win-win thing that we've done here, us George and George being on the team. Make no mistake about it. George could be a cowboy cowboy for the rest of his career and that be a long time. Make no mistake about it. Uh, this just fit for us and thank goodness it fit for him. Uh, and we got it done. And let's uh let's look at that. Um, it's not uncommon with these teams around the NFL to have this tension going on regarding players and contracts and things. U, we of course are focused when it's us, but this is not uncommon to have happen. Um, it uh gave us an opportunity uh the process gave us an opportunity to make some decisions last year. A lot of people disagree with uh some of the decisions that we made, but it gave us an opportunity to make some decisions. I think going forward here, we're going to see hopefully the positiveness of some of those decisions reflected in this year's football team. >> Nick, >> want to talk about the the cornerback room. Obviously going to be one of the more heated competitions you guys see out here in Oxnard. What's your confidence level and how excited are you to see that competition? >> Yeah, I'm really excited. Uh, I think, you know, when you look at, you know, from top to bottom, uh, Don obviously did a great job coming back. He feels great. Uh, excited to get him back out there. Uh, you know, Siobhan Rebel is finally, you know, feeling great. And I thought he had a really good offseason. I'm really very very pleased with the the ability of, you know, DA and Ryan Smith and and Christian Parker, uh, to, you know, really dive into the finer details of how you play certain coverages and the techniques. like uh they spend, you know, at nauseium amounts of time talking about fundamentals over scheme. We all have the same scheme. It's the way you teach the fundamentals that make the difference. I thought Kobe Durant was uh an awesome uh pickup for us, you know, Darion Kendrick. Um it's going to be a uh a fun battle to watch and they're going to be able to go up against some of the most elite receivers in the league, which I think is important as well. And um but what I expect to see is the confidence of that group grow. And that starts by getting into these practices and and getting into the one-on- ones and some of the sevens and team drills that we do and watching those guys compete. And uh the thing that will be definitely different this year with CP is the trash talk. Uh cuz uh he's pretty good at it. >> Before we uh close out, I want to give a shout out to ESPN's Todd Archer who would have been here. He's uh he placed himself on the non-foot related injury list and we miss him, but uh I know he's watching, observing, monitoring, getting ready to write, tweeting, uh all of that. We look forward to him getting back at it and joining us back back here cuz he's he's one of our regular uh longtime beats and we miss him. So, thank you, Todd. All right, everybody. That's uh going to wrap it up for today. Thank you.

title: Colts GM Chris Ballard looks ahead to 2026 training camp
text: Welcome. Welcome back, everybody. Glad to see everybody. Um I'm going to open up by So, just you know, my heart goes out and prayers go out to Eric Bieniemy and his wife, Mia. Um Eric's a very dear friend. Um he's a special football coach, but he's even a better man. Um so, you know, life's life happens and um but thinking about thinking about him, without question. Um great to be back in Grand Park. Just love coming out here. It's a great I mean, just what everybody does to put on this event, training camp, behind the scenes. I mean, we show up and all this stuff is set up, but I mean, it it's a it's a production by, you know, not only people in our building, you know, what they have to do to get ready, but also by the city of Westfield, Grand Park, all the volunteers. So, just grateful and thankful. Um it's a great place one for training camp, for us to get our team ready, but two, for our fans, okay? Um expect to have, you know, our fans show up like they always do. Um and, you know, give them an access um that I think is really important to give. Um all right, now, on the injuries. So, Daniel Jones cleared. Um he's good to go. He's worked his butt off, you know, since the day of the injury, when it happened, he, you know, of course, a mourning period for a day or two, but then, all right, what do I need to do to get back? And so, he went to work. And, you know, he's been cleared. It'll be a day-by-day thing, but he's cleared to go. Um and and cleared to do everything. Um Buckner, kind of in the same boat. Um once he had his surgery, it was, okay, what do I need to do to get back? He's in a good frame of mind. We'll work him back in slowly. I mean, you know, Buck's had some years in the league, so we were we would take care of him anyways. Um but we'll work him back and get him ready for week one versus versus Baltimore. Um as you saw yesterday, CJ has a muscle strain, CJ Allen. We don't think it's going to be long. Um we're being taking some precautions here. We don't want it to just to linger. Um so we started him on PUP. We expect him back pretty quickly. >> [snorts] >> Um Pierce, who had his surgery in March, he's getting there. He's close. Probably still a week or two away. We'll kind of take it day by day. Um but making great progress. He's worked. Um I don't foresee it being a major issue. We of course would like to have him right now, but uh Pierce is working his butt off and he'll be he'll be ready to go when, you know, uh when he's completely cleared. other than that, questions? >> Real quick, you mentioned uh all the nice things about Westfield and training camp, but you guys >> This is your last year. >> Yeah. >> What what went into that decision? >> I don't you know, people you know, things change, you know, and and I I just think it was a you know, we've been here like 9 years now, and I think it kind of run its course, and now we're going to do things back at the facility. >> Was that a difficult decision? >> Oh, it it's yeah, it was never easy, especially with the relationship we have out here. Um but also it is a big undertaking. I mean, it is. It's a massive undertaking. Um and we're going to do some things to the facility. Carly and and her sisters have some ideas to do and still to be able to get fans out. So we still think we'll make it a a great experience, not only get ready for training camp, but also for our fans. >> What about at his age and with this serious of an injury, do you guys need to scale him back at all throughout the year and rotate him more, or are you expecting a full >> Um I think he'll have a full workload. Um, and there's no question we'd like to and I think we've got a little better depth inside this year. That's going to be one of the competitions going to be really fun to watch. It's hard to get three quarterbacks significant reps in camp. How are you going to do the backup? >> Uh, I'll leave that to Shane, but they'll get enough looks in practice and in games to where we'll be able to make a decision. I look, I'll say this it's it's probably the first time in a while felt really good about the in totality the position. I mean, we we feel like we have three guys that you know, with Daniel and and you know, and and AR and Riley that that all can play. So, that's a that's a good spot to be in right now. >> realistic that you could keep all three of them or what do you anticipate? >> Yep. Yep, absolutely. >> intention right now? >> That's my intention right now. Yeah. >> Is Anthony's trade request still on the table? >> Um, it is, but I you know, I mean, I think they're realistic and we're realistic. You know, we're not we're not just giving him away. Um, not going to do that. Um, and it's been fun to watch. Like I think I've told y'all this multiple times. Like one of the things that gets washed over sometimes with Anthony like he is an he is a great teammate. Um, and he's fun to be around and he is really grown and worked. It's been fun to watch. I mean, I you know, especially when you take a guy as high as we took him you know, you want him to come in and be the savior right away. Well, you know, everybody's developmental plan is different and you know, his was a little different. I still think that he is got a future. Um, we'll see how that plays >> There was reports that um, you all have you all have looked into possibly the future of Terron Arnold him signing here or whatever. Can you speak more to that? >> We look at every player that hits the market. We look at every player that hits the market. I mean, you know, and you got to dig into those issues. So, we have to be able to do our research on every single The same thing in the draft. We do our research on every single player. So, no different with >> Chris, we ask you every year, um somebody knows you lose the weight. Um are you How much pressure do you feel as a GM? How much pressure do you feel when we're out of the woods? >> [laughter] >> Um Well, are we running those answers, or do you have a different >> No. It's not Look, I am I have been able to It's my 26th year in the league. Okay? And if And as a kid, if you would have told me I was able to work in football and do this for a career, I would have signed up 100 times over. Okay? The journey's different for everybody. I don't I'm just a steward in this position. I've always believed that. And I'll always do the best thing for the organization, both short and long term. Um that's just how I tick and how I roll. Um but I I I don't Every I'm grateful that I've always had a job in this league that I have great respect for, and that will never change. Um Like, the fun to me is the journey. That that's the fun part. The ups Even the even the hard moments, like they're not compared to what other people have to go through like they're not really that excuse my language, they're really not that hard. I won't ever take one day for granted. Um and I'll never take one day for granted. So the pre- In terms of the pressure, Greg, I Look, nobody puts more pressure on me than myself to succeed. Um but like if I've learned anything over the years is you got to Sometimes you got to enjoy all of it. The good and the bad. The That's the That's the fun part of this. No. I wouldn't do one. >> Why not? >> I I'm in the last year of my deal, we need to win. We like I think I will always and I think you can Y'all all know me well enough. Like I'm always going to do the best thing for the organization. That's my day. Ultimately, that's my job. Um and when anytime you do selfish alternative ulterior motive in play, that's that's that's not good for the game. It's not good for the organization. We will always do what's best for this for this club. I have too much respect for the Colts. I have too much respect for what Mr. Irsay stood for as an owner. Um I don't necessarily see any checks. I've watched him work and he looks really good. He's not going to tell you he's 100% yet, but he's working towards that and he's getting close. But he is cleared and looks look really good when I watched him throw a few weeks ago. >> expect him to play in the preseason? >> I'm not I'm not there yet. Yeah. >> I mean maybe with Jones it's not going to be he's going to practice his day and take a day off. It's not he's not on that kind of program. >> No. No, not right now. No. >> What's your level of concern with Pierce being ready for week one? >> Well, he's not active right now cuz he's on PUP. I mean that's kind of a day-by-day thing. Look, I'm not going to make a prediction one way or the other. I learned a long time ago with another certain player you don't make predictions. And I'm not a doctor. So, we'll just play by ear. See how it goes. >> level of concern in general with him given the contract and everything? >> None. We None. None. He's good. He's really good. >> How much does his health impact you signing a veteran wideout? Like when you consider the veteran wideout, is his health top of that list on why you would do that or do you just No, just if we think we need to add another player to the position to help the team, that would be more of the reason. >> How do you avoid the playoffs? >> We'll do two more here. James and then >> you missed the playoffs. Obviously that's the goal. But beyond just health, what other things do you think need to change or shift for this team to be able to overcome the defense? >> We I mean I brought it up last year. And like if you look back, we got to finish, man. We got to finish at the end of the year better. I mean look all 17 games stuff they all count. You know, but if you look back, I mean like 21 a really good football team. 23, you know, we 21 we lose the last two games of the year. 23 we lose to Houston for the division. 24 we faded down the stretch. Last year with all with the injuries we fade. We've got to finish, man. That That last part of the season, that last five, six, seven games. I always say, "Look, the season starts at Thanksgiving." You got to keep yourself in it. And when Thanksgiving hits, you got to be playing good football. Because once December, that's when the teams that start to rise and play well usually do well. That's where That's where we've got to make real strides. That it? Awesome.

title: Indianapolis Colts report to training camp, Buckner cleared for practice
text: Good morning. So, we didn't see in the spring or >> Are you ready to roll as as far as tomorrow goes or do you have an expectation when it starts? >> Yeah, I'm excited to get back out there, get back on the field. Um obviously I was I was cleared yesterday. So, um you know, obviously they they everybody has a plan on, you know, getting me back on the field and uh yeah, I'm just excited to get out back out there with the guys. >> But do you have to ramp up at all or I guess what does that look like if you've been cleared? >> Yeah, I'm I'm sure it's going to be, you know, a ramp up period, you know, acclimation period to get back out there, you know, I haven't had contact in the spring and everything like that and obviously dealing with my situation, you know, want to be be cautious and be smart in what we do and uh yeah, like I said, I'm I'm excited for tomorrow. >> How much of an adjustment has it been not being able to do stuff in the spring and then you know, you kind of have to adjust those things moving forward? >> Yeah, I mean it was uh it was definitely frustrating, you know, not being able to get out there and obviously work on work on my craft, but you know, um this break that we had I was able to um do a bunch of field work and everything and um you know, do a bunch of D-line drills, go through some pop-up bags and um you know, shot you know, striking some things and stuff like that and I've been feeling good and yeah. >> How much of a relief is it to get cleared? I know you said when it first happened like okay, I got to think about my future in football. >> Yeah, yeah. It was it felt like a graduation day for me personally. You know what I mean? Getting to this point um from where I started on New Year's Eve, um you know, not being able to do a whole lot after surgery, you know, just pretty much being in the bed not being able to move around. I mean, I couldn't even pick my kids up and stuff like that, you know, I couldn't pick anything up for, you know, heavier than 10 lb for the first, you know, couple couple weeks. Um so, it was it was frustrating, but um you know, I just you know, I just kept my faith and kept kept working and you know, trusting the doctors and and my trainers and um you know, there was a there was a lot of uh you know, teamwork involved with the whole operation and everything and recovery and you know, I'm just happy to be at this point. >> Did you expect? Did you expect to be cleared? >> Yeah. >> Okay. >> What did you have surgery on? Did you ever actually >> Uh on New Year's Eve. Yeah. >> It's It's a physical game, so obviously a lot of contact with the punches. So, um do you need to sort of, you know, see how you respond to that or do you kind of already >> Yeah, that's Yeah, that's why we, you know, just slowly ramping it up, um you know, um throughout training camp. Um you know, and I think majority of it is just going to be a mental part. You know what I mean? Um with the physical all the physical things. I mean, I've, you know, I physically I feel great. Um you know, Doc Doc said, um you know, there was there's been guy cases of guys throughout the league who's gotten the surgery and, you know, felt better after and got back to, you know, going full contact and everything. And I And I just truly believe, you know, with a with a lot of major surgeries, you know, you know, you can be feeling physically great, but it's the mental part, you know what I mean? Getting you getting past that mental mental block of, you know, trusting yourself and um trusting that everything's fine. So, um yeah, that's probably going to be the, you know, biggest hurdle, but I I think I'm going to be fine. >> From a team standpoint, you know, when you were out last year, pass rush really struggled. What makes you think that you're going to have a little more help around you to get that get it done in that area this year? >> Yeah, just the the growth in the guys. Um you know, um obviously experience is the best thing, you know, obviously for any player, but especially as a pass rusher. And a And as a And a a young group, you know what I mean? For some of the young guys in the room, you know, especially for a guy like Laiatu, obviously coming off a year where, you know, it was um it was um a big year for him, you know? What he end up with eight and a half sacks. And um you know, I feel like, you know, he's he's one of those guys that can they can reach double digits. And um you know, he's been looking great throughout the spring. And um I know he's been putting a lot of work throughout the summer. Um so, you know, I think, you know, guys like him, um Tommy Togiai, you know, in the inside. I mean, he he showed some um some flashes last year and what he his ability and what he can do and um I just have great belief in the young guys, you know, the growth that they've had and the experience that they had, you know, with with me being out um and getting all those plays in um they're going to be able to take another step forward. >> A player like Jaylen you know, didn't get a ton of time last year when you were out. Didn't get a ton of time last year. Can can a guy like that with a second you know, he's a second round pedigree, can a guy like that take a huge jump? Cuz it feels like he's got to make a huge jump for you guys. >> Yeah, no, definitely. I think he can um he can he can make a huge jump. Um you know, obviously getting more reps and um more playing time, um getting on the field and everything like that and just the the work that I've seen him put in over the the off season. I mean, I think he's you know, we're going to be leaning on him a lot too to step up and make plays and I think he has the ability to do that. >> I know you said you were expecting to get cleared yesterday. This and this has been a really long process for you, seven months or over. So, what was like actually hearing that um knowing that you'll be back out there on Wednesday, what was that like to actually hear that even though I know you were expecting that to be the the case? >> Yeah, I mean, it was just uh joy, relief, you know what I mean? Just all the hard work that I was able to put in over the last seven months in recovering and getting back to this point. Um yeah, it was just a big sigh of relief, for real. >> It's a big year for you to talk about a sense of urgency. >> Mhm. >> Do you feel that or do you feel that every spring or every summer? >> Yeah, that's I mean, I live my life on urgency. I feel like uh but yeah, it is it is a great sense of urgency, you know what I mean? Um starting the season the way we did last year, um obviously there was great hopes, but you know, it's uh it's a marathon, not a race, you know, in this league and um you know, we just got to continue to keep chipping away and and it's the second half of the season, you know what I mean? It's over the past couple of years where we were so close and we just you know, we the team just starts to plummet towards the end and um we got to do a better job, you know, every single person in the in the building to keep that sense of urgency and continue to keep our foot on the gas um all through, you know, for 16 or 17 games straight. >> Through this injury last year, through this injury process, I know you've talked to us some a little bit um while you were going through this that you didn't know if you were going to be able to come back or if that was going to be the right decision for you. I know you're in a contract year. Do you know what you want to do beyond this year? Are you just going to use this year to kind of help you figure that out? >> No, yeah. I'm just Yeah, obviously it's my last year on contract. But, you know, I'm obviously coming off of an injury. And you know, obviously everybody else has questions. You know what I mean? You know, whether this guy is he going to be as good as he once was or whatever it is. And obviously speaking with, you know, obviously my age and all that kind of stuff. I mean, I try to stay away from all this stuff in the media, but obviously I see it. And you know, it's this is a this is a thing for me to prove to myself and and nobody else that you know, I you know, I can still play at a high level. And I'm still going to play at a high level. And you know, at the end of the season, we'll see where everything is. >> Josh Downs said Mark Pitts is gone. And Alex is coming back. I mean, this is this How do you look at this? Is this an opportunity or is this just just a continuation >> No, you know, definitely an opportunity, but also a continuation just of trying to show like I'm a really good receiver in this NFL. I feel like in college like I have I was like I was a heavy target guy. Like I I got a lot of targets. Had 100 catches like back-to-back years. So, for me being able to, you know, hopefully get back to something similar to that would be huge for me. I feel like, you know, I'm just as good as some of the best guys in the league. And I'm excited for for more opportunities. AP as well, Tyler, Ashton, and you know, JT best back in the league. So, we got we got some good weapons on offense. >> Chris Ballard has said repeatedly that you did have to sacrifice some things last year. I know you always loved getting the ball. How did you sort of work through that? And did you learn anything from going through that last year? And you know, how prepared are you for taking that bigger role? >> Yeah, you know, last year we had a kind of a packed packed room. We had a lot of good receivers in there. Shoot AD. I used to talk to AD. I feel like he was one of that really went through it even worse than anybody. Like great talent but just yeah, didn't didn't get a lot of playing time on the field just because we were so packed in as a room. But you know, teaches you patience, teaches you to you know, just be grateful for what you get. And I mean just keep working. I mean I was still doing all the stuff I was doing the years before and just got to just keep going, keep your head down and and and stay on the ground. >> Josh, you've seen very good in our season progress. What he did in the OTAs and all that. Was it just added optimism when he he's full go and come Wednesday he's out there. Is that just something of a relief for the offense? >> Of course you want to have your guy out there. I feel like quarterback's the most important position in the game of football and and he's put the work in and we we were in Florida a couple weeks ago throwing and I actually like forgot he had got injured before cuz he looked so good out there. So I'm excited to see him you know, be out there full go and and get after it. So I'm excited for Danny. >> Do you you remember how good it was the first eight to 10 games? >> Yeah, I mean he's I mean yeah, he's a he's been a great player in this league and he had a really good start last year and he just has some unfortunate injuries but you know, he looked good zipping the ball moving around. So we're excited for him. >> He obviously showed you a lot last year, you know, throwing the ball and operating the offense but what did he show you just in the the dedication you put into the process to get back on the field tomorrow? >> Yeah, you know, just a guy that's just going to you got to tell him to slow down when he's rehabbing because he's he's going to do do all he can and extra. But just I mean he's back what is it? July? I think he got hurt late in December or November. But the fact that he's already back in full go, I mean that should tell you what tell you what you want to hear right there. I mean the guy who's putting in the work. >> How confident are you that this offense can take what he did last year and have that success this season as well? >> Yeah, you know, like I said, position. You got a good quarterback at your on your team, you can do a lot. So, the fact that I mean we got three good quarterbacks, but obviously Danny's going to lead lead the pack. So, having him back is huge for us and you know, I feel like he'll be just as good. >> I don't want you to speak for Daniel, but I mean I'm sure there are a lot of people on the outside that'd be like, well, he's always good for a period last year, but then oh, you got hurt again. How can you do it again, you know, this year? Like I mean, how do you think he approaches all of that as a teammate or >> Yeah, no, I feel like it's just the game of football. Like it's just a sport of just what can you do for me today, not last week. So, you can have a great game the week before and then you play bad and they're going to be saying you're trash. So, it it I don't think he's really thinking that much into it. I think it's just you got to go out there and perform. >> Josh, you mentioned really just staying the course, but were there areas of emphasis that you had this offseason as you came back and got ready to go for training camp? >> Yeah, I just wanted to like run run a lot this offseason. Like get on the track and then run a lot of different routes, more than you know, like you see a lot of receiver trainers and stuff just doing drills. Like just running routes and and actually running, getting in getting in shape. So, those were the biggest things for me. >> Did you feel your speed improved or what did you benefit from >> Uh you know, like you run you run more, they say the more you run the faster you get. So, you we'll see. Yeah. >> We've seen big plays from you in the past. Do you feel like there's more of that to tap into this year? >> Yeah, man. I love I love making those big plays down the field and also in the intermediate short game. I feel like everything opens up the more you, you know, press vertical and do stuff like that. So, we'll see what Shane has cooked up for everybody in this offense, but you know, he's a great OC. >> What what does it is it a simple question. What does JT bring to this offense? >> Yeah, JT I mean, on the field, you know, he's like phenomenal. Shoot, he's a phenomenal on the field, but even off the field like in in his leadership. He's a guy that can you can talk to and he's really humble and he'll tell you like his own personal experiences and also like he'll he'll just give you a shot like even just give you an ear to talk to and and listen to you. So, he's a guy that that leads us in that way as well and and he's a hard worker. He's not he's not the guy that's off the field first and just trying to like get through the day. He's a guy that's putting in the work and and wants to be great and he doesn't complain at all either. I feel like being a great player like that, the fact that he doesn't complain about how we got to go out here and practice 5 days in a row or something or damn we got to lift today. He's just a guy that does it. It kind of sets a good example. >> Mentally for you, how is this season any different if at all from the last that you've been here? Like is it confidence boost? Has anything changed for you? >> Yeah. Um you know, just excited for different opportunities. Um hopefully. Uh but you know, been playing football since I was 6 years old. So, about to be 25. So, it's about to be 20 years playing. Um you know, just just another season but uh obviously there's more at stake. Um so, excited for excited I like the pressure in a sense. It's kind of cool to me. So, I'm I'm I'm um I'm definitely excited for this season. >> Do you guys all feel that sense of urgency to have a fast start like last year and then be able to finish it off? >> Um you know, you you won't have a good season every year and obviously last year we had some like unfortunate events happen but yeah, everybody wants to uh start how we did and and finish how we start. Um so, I feel like it's it's about how you finish not how you start and we can do better um than we did last year. >> Since it's the first day, it's always a little extra. It's just um like the energy in the air is just different. Um so, I'm excited to actually see everyone today. Um you know, we spend some time together in the off season but like to have everyone back is just so special and then um yeah, excited for first practice. >> Do you sort of feel feel like one of the old guys now? I mean, you used to be the the young guy. Now, you're still sort of young but you're one of the older guys, veteran guys. >> Yeah, I mean it's it's crazy how fast that changes. Um I mean, it's exciting but at the end of the day like the the plan is still the same. Try to improve every single day. Learn from your mistakes and uh get better and be your best version for the team. >> Bernard, we learned yesterday that Daniel's full go. What position does it put you guys in as an offensive line to know you've got QB1 starting full tilt, no restrictions day one of camp? >> I mean, that just gets you fired up. I mean, we're excited as an offensive line, as a whole team we're excited to have him out there. And you know, just just lead the offense the way he did last year. I mean, we all love the guy. We love playing with him. We love spending time with him. So yeah, it's it's super exciting to to hear that he's that he's healthy, feeling good. And yeah, just pumped for practice then. >> I talked to Q earlier in the summer. He was saying seeing Daniel attack that rehab process was really inspi- motivational for the offensive line especially. How did you feel that personally just seeing how hard he worked to get ready? >> Yeah, I mean, I could feel it every day obviously. Late in the season he was getting his his treatment done. But I was also like I I stay in the off season as well. So bless you. I could actually first hand, you know, see him in the training room get better even though when when nobody's watching, you know, that most people like leave town. Most people like do whatever, but he was he was in there doing the the dirty work every single morning. And you know, he's the first one in the training room. Um so it's just it's great seeing how he, you know, never, you know, gave up or anything. He never took it easy. So yeah, just just really excited about that. >> Is even though he is obviously a worker, is any part of you amazed, surprised, or anything? I mean, that's a pretty devastating injury. And here we are, right? He's ready to go. >> I'm not surprised. I mean, I know him. I know what what kind of guy he is. I mean, he's proven it over and over again that he would do anything for his team, so I knew he was going to do everything he could to to be ready and it just I think it shows his character for sure like how much he cares. >> What gives you confidence this offense can recreate what you guys did last year before the injuries, you know, because I mean that was like that was that was a unique, you know, run that you guys had. Can you guys >> Oh, absolutely. >> Oh, absolutely, but I think it's all starts with the work that we put in all off season and that we're putting in on these practice fields like the next couple weeks to get back to where we're at and you know, grow together and obviously every player can improve individually a lot in the off season, but these camp days is really when it comes together as a team. So, I think it's just crucial for us to to lock in and we've got plenty of time to spend together in our the next couple weeks, just, you know, make the most out of it. Put the work in, but also enjoy the time together because that's that's unique. You don't get to do that a whole lot, so. >> What's uh what's next for you? You know, what what do you think is the next step for you in your game? You know, obviously you're established as a starter, established as a really good left tackle. What's what's the next step for you? >> I mean, like I said, it's just a steady improvement, learning every day, but then also being there for my teammates, helping them improve, being the leader that I know that I can be and um hopefully the you know, the team over humps in the game, over some lows in the season, some rough days in camp and just uh make sure I I I bring the teammates, everyone with us because obviously this is not a one-man show. It's a biggest team sport in the world, so like if you don't have a good team around you, you can't can't go anywhere. So, I think it's just important to to bring everybody with you on the on the same mission to win every week. >> And obviously that's very important with guy like like Jaylen who's, you know, kind of ascending in the starting lineup. >> Oh yeah, absolutely. I mean, Jaylon's a great guy. He's already, um, I think shown a lot last season, but I think he's it's just the beginning. Like he's extremely talented. He he works hard. He he fits into the room. And uh, I know he has some some great great things ahead of him. So, I'm excited to be be playing on the opposite side of >> What's the level of excitement for you personally getting back to camp and getting things going? >> Yeah, I think everybody's really excited. And, you know, from my offensive standpoint, coming back with the same, you know, same coaching staff, same same core group of guys is is always exciting to kind of build off of what you were able to do last year. >> And what what will how can you guys recreate what you had earlier last year offensively, which is pretty impressive? >> Yeah, I think know what works and obviously being able to build off of it and and throw some new wrinkles in there, but I think it really starts here and just building that the chemistry and and getting back to the timing and everything, but but yeah, I think just trusting yourselves. Obviously, we're we're a good offense, so so just doing what we do best and not making it something bigger in your head. >> I remember that day in Jacksonville, you know, Daniel goes down and you were there. The whole locker room was devastated. Can you contrast that mood and that feeling to now, you know, getting ready to get back out there tomorrow? What do you think about it? >> Yeah, I'm just happy, you know, for Daniel. He's a, you know, obviously he's a great player, but he's a great, you know, guy off the field and a and a good friend. So, I'm I'm glad he he's doing better and and he has a chance to, you know, play football again, which he loves to do, obviously. And and we're excited to have him out there. So, I'm just excited for him and I'm ready to just play football with him again. >> This is not his nature maybe, but do you feel like maybe he thinks he has he wants to prove something? >> Yeah, I mean, I think he kind of just the type of guy he is, he's always going to play with a with an edge and a competitive spirit. So, I think that's whether he was, you know, coming off the best season of his life or like he is coming off an injury, he'd be I think he'd be the same guy kind of with his attitude coming into camp. >> Did anything feel different for you walking in the building today versus walking in it the first time last year? >> Um I mean, I think personally it is a little you're a little more relaxed just not, you know, being a rookie and kind of learning everything as you go. You You kind of know what to expect and stuff like that. So, that's nice for me and I think as a team, I think everybody's always going to be excited and we had a you know a good start last year and obviously we needed to finish, but I think the having this foundation of guys back that were here last year is is really important. >> For you, what can you what can you work on, you know, maybe as a little more relaxed in year two now that you have that full year of training camp? >> Yeah, I think you can just put more mental energy into the actual football stuff and and just, you know less stress about other stuff outside of football which you're supposed to be doing and just focus on football. >> Tyler, I know that obviously Daniel is still progressing back, but how much time, how much work were you guys able to get in together coming into training camp? >> Yeah, obviously the OTAs was was good for him to be able to do the what is it just 7-on-7 and and routes in there he was doing and then we got to do some throwing over the over the break and then a few days ago got some more throwing in. So, it's been it's been good just uh keep doing that and seeing him progress has been has been good to see. >> Where where were you guys able to get some work in together? Just at the team facility or >> Uh it was down in uh Florida. >> All right. >> Tyler, they always say that a rookie really the big jump here year one to year two. What's that big jump do you think will look like with you? You had statistically pretty good season. >> Yeah, um you know, I'm not I'm not sure. It's hard to judge I guess it's kind of in the eye of the beholder, right? Whoever whoever wants to deem it, but uh really for me it's just doing doing what I have to do each play and making sure I'm the best tight end and teammate I can be and you You I think the tight end position could look different game to game and year to year based off, you know, the the stats of of what it might look like. So, I think it's just focusing on, you know, being the best tight end and and best offensive teammate I can be. >> When you step back and look at last year when you had a chance to do things, not too bad. >> Uh yeah, I mean, I guess it it went well. I think there's still a lot of stuff I could do better and left on the table maybe in some games and and obviously as an offense we left a lot on the on the field, but uh but yeah, I'm excited to get back in and keep working on it. >> Are there parts of your game as you were able to review last year either with the team losing Michael Pittman and maybe giving you more opportunities or things that you feel like you're more comfortable doing in this offense? Are there parts of your game that you feel like you want to expand more? I feel like there are opportunities for you to do more. >> Yeah, I think uh you know, not having Pitt here is a big big deal just cuz he was such a big part of our offense and a great player, but uh but that is opens opportunities for for a lot of guys across the offense. So, I think it's just being able to uh be more diverse and, you know, maybe run some some different routes this year and stuff that Pitt would been running will be will be obviously sad to see him go, but but good for everybody here to kind of spread the ball around a little more. >> Offensively, there's a lot of continuity. Like coaches are back and all the players tight end room is pretty much the same. Like what's that mean for you, I guess, in your development but also comfort level? >> Yeah, I think it's that's uh that's a really big deal kind of for everybody just to It's not it's not you're coming in and learning a a new script every day or or installing stuff for every day. It's kind of just reinstalling it in into your head and and kind of getting back in the flow you already had last year. So, I think that's really important, you know, for for me as a player it it makes me a lot more comfortable. I think as an offense we're a lot more comfortable kind of not starting from the beginning, but just adding on to what we did last year. >> Dope. What's up, y'all? Good. >> How was y'all's team? >> It was good. >> Good work? >> Yeah, very good work. >> Um just Did you take a different approach at all this off season? >> I feel like I took I feel like I took the same approach just keeping my you know my body flexible eating right attacking you know my upper body strength keeping that you know continually getting continuously getting strong. And then just working with my guy Eddie close to Eddie getting on the field with him perfecting you know certain things yeah it was it was dope it was a good off season. >> Does this feel like a big year for you? >> I mean definitely for me I mean every year I wanted it to be a big year. But like going into my third year you know I want to make a statement for sure and you know continue doing what I was doing last year and just keep improving. >> Can you when you reflect have you seen this improvement rookie year to and what this year can be have you have you seen that or felt that? >> Yeah I did and I was able to go to the sack summit with you know Von Miller Cam Jordan Max and you know I definitely felt it there for sure like in terms of my improvement yeah and then just really just being over there was definitely a blessing and getting to improve off of guys that are you know good at great at what they do the best at what they do. >> When you when you reflected on kind of look back at year two after things were all said and done what what were the ways that you felt you made the biggest leap and then going into year three what are the areas of your game where you felt you're still focusing on trying to take another step? >> Really it was just taking the defense coach Lou coming in really just taking this new defense like and being able to do you know a lot of things and just kind of like learning it that first year and then being able to you know kind of just be all over the field and then this year I'm really just honing in on I feel like my get off and I feel like it's my get off for sure this year and just really just being able to get off the rock when I know it and then you know at certain points to being able to play off of that. >> Is that where you feel like some of those near sacks that you had that I know Christian and Shane have talked about like that will maybe kind of make the difference in getting from eight and a half sacks to double digits? >> Yeah cuz cuz definitely when I look back at it it's like tenths of a second where like you know I can get off as the ball moving or, you know, and there's times where like I was definitely a little late off the ball. So, that's definitely a big part of my game I'm trying to, you know, get better at. >> At the sack they named you the breakout player for this year. What went into that and what did it mean for you to be singled out by all those guys on trip to the combine? >> I mean definitely like I was saying like I wasn't like ready to do that. I was just kind of going there trying to learn from the other guys and, you know, enjoy the time, but I mean definitely being recognized like that kind of shows me like, okay, I'm, you know, I'm doing the right things and I'm getting better and like, you know, and keep doing that. Watt esque almost, but like, you know, being able to do things all over the field is hell of fun. >> Have you kept Have you talked about Have you kept footballs from >> Uh yeah, they're they're at my house for sure. So, I feel like that was the big thing that we talked about. And then them just being encouraging, for sure. >> I know you mentioned double-digit sacks. I I don't know if you're aware how rare that is for this team. We haven't had Colts haven't had a player reach that mark in several years. Were you aware of that and what would that mean to be able to kind of break that streak and and have a a breakout year in that one? >> I mean, I was definitely aware of that. And, um for that to happen, I feel like, you know, that would mean a lot to me. I know it'd mean a lot to everyone in the building, too. But, for me personally, you know, I want to be, you know, that guy that people, you know, look up to and, you know, able to do those things. >> Julien, you can move up a little more. >> Oh, my bad. >> Different circumstances for you entering this camp, you know, kind of penciled in there as the starter at right tackle. What does that mean for you versus last year when you're probably just trying to fit into the mix? >> Yeah, it means a lot. I think it's uh indicative of my growth that I've had throughout the, you know, last year and, you know, having the chance to step in there later on in the season and, you know, prove to to the team and the organization, my coaching staff, that I'm capable and willing. Um but also still have a lot of work to do. I'm excited to get into this camp, you know, especially in a very competitive O-line room to to prove that, you know, I can contribute to this offensive line in a very sustainable way going forward. >> Julien, when you the the time you did play last year, I'm sure you went back and you studied that tape. What were the things you took away that were positive and what are the things that you, you know, hope you can maybe reverse? >> Yeah. Yeah, 100%. Um I think, you know, I had extreme highs last year in terms of the competition that we were going against, your Danielle Hunters, your Will Andersons. Um, you know, week in and week out, especially those last four games, on the road at Seattle. Um, and I think I was proud of the way that I showed up, but I think the big step for me this year is going to be consistently showing up with my technique against some of these higher-level players to make sure that, you know, there there's no lapses. It was awesome. I don't think there's any better way to learn. Um, but had been working all year, obviously, behind the scenes and behind a very veteran offensive line, so I felt comfortable stepping in to that position when called upon. >> Having a very realistic opportunity to start, um, not just kind of having that like that trial by fire at the end of the season, like you mentioned, what how does that change the the urgency or the the motivation or the focus for you coming into this camp and into the eventual season? >> Yeah, you know, I think last year I was given an opportunity to really perfect my process, um, really understand what works for me, what doesn't work for me, um, you know, in a little bit smaller of a role. Um, I think Bernie, having someone in our offensive line room that, um, at our position who is as steady as they come, consistent ship, um, has been really calming for me and, you know, be able to, especially this past year, to lean into him for a piece of advice, you know, what do you look for when you're studying film? You know, what is your approach to game days against these particular rushers? Um, has been huge for me. >> Is what's what's his style of like helping you? Is it like he waits for you to ask the question? Does he stuff in your game? How's that work? >> It's a combination of both. Um like especially in our individual periods, like if he sees something, he'll come up to me. Um he'll be like, "Jaylen, like maybe we try this, right? A little bit more patient with your hands." I think his hands are, you know, of the best in the league. Um but also like if I'm struggling with something, um I know our my first step on the backside of outside zone, for example, last year, um I went to him a lot because I think his is also one of the best in the league in terms of getting defenders cut off. Um so it's definitely a combination of both. I think he's a very strong mentor for me in the room. >> Offensive linemen earlier in their in their career usually have to go through some sort of physical transformation, whether it's more weight, less weight, like muscle mass. Is there anything that you had to accomplish this offseason and where you got that? >> Yeah. Um I wouldn't say there is there's any drastic things, but I always look at, "Okay, how can I make sure that the weight that I have is working as efficiently for me as it possibly can?" Um so like this camp I'm coming in between 325, 330. Last year I was around 335, 330. Um and for me it's like, "Okay, decreasing body fat, increasing muscle mass is one of the huge priorities for me to make sure that weight is as efficient as possible and I'm as quick as possible, especially on the line of play." >> Thank you.

We're talking about different scenarios. He probably wants me out of his office plenty of time, but you're always going through different scenarios. And in our situation, say once we got into like 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, you start to look at, all right, who are the players that are available? Who are some of the players that we would consider taking? and you kind of create some buckets and then as you go through again we don't really know what other teams are going to do like you try to as best you can make an estimation of look at the the roster hey there are some players that they might be interested in it doesn't mean that for sure they're going to be you're going to be interested in the same player and then we look at it through the lens of in the end what's the best thing for the Houston Texans we can't worry about what other teams are doing they're going to make their decisions we have to make our decisions independent of what anybody else is doing so in terms of how chaotic it it's It's really not. It's pretty fluid. It's ongoing and we just kind of react and we're ready to go. And if you do a trade, you make a trade and you pick the player. If you can't consate the trade, then you prepare for the next opportunity in front of you. So, we're pretty consistent. It'll be no different here tonight when we get started here in a few hours. >> Keyn, have you had a chance to I know you haven't been in town. >> The main thing for me, you know, in this in this offseason cycle is really trying to enhance and improve our offensive line. Uh we've added, you know, a couple guys there. Getting Ed Ingram back was was really good for us. Thought Ed had a really great year. Shows he really improved. Coach Papovich did a great job of helping him with that. Adding Evan Brown, Wyatt Teller, Braden Smith, three tough guys, experienced guys, been in the league for a while.
