title: Matthew Stafford Talks Training Camp, Madden 99 Club & Season Expectations | Inside Rams Camp
text: Community America Credit Union takes us inside Rams camp for the first time in 2026 and we got the MVP Matthew Stafford with us JB Long Demarco Farr. Great to see you out there. How did it feel good to connect with Puka a couple times? >> It did. It was a it was a lot of fun. Spread the ball around a bunch. Puka obviously made some big time plays. We went down the field. Devante had one down the field. Puka made a great one-handed catch. Uh it felt great. I just I love playing. Um you know, I'm I'm totally respectful of trying to make sure that I'm as fresh as I can be come you know, the season. Um but at the same time when I'm out here it is it is a blast. >> It's all about this year 2026. This but I never got to say congratulations for the MVP. You played your butt off. >> Well, I appreciate that. >> You absolutely deserved it. Now, how when did you turn the page from holding that trophy to let's get ready for this year? >> Oh, pretty quick to be honest with you. I mean, obviously I enjoyed the heck out of that moment on stage with my uh with my kids and getting to have my wife there and a bunch of you know, coaches and teammates that that meant a lot to me in sharing that in that trophy. I mean, my my game is not Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson those guys that win it and run around and make plays by themselves. You know, I I need everybody and and uh I hope everybody and I know everybody on our team felt a big part of that. So, amazing to get to celebrate that that night. I don't know if there was too much after that that I was thinking about it to be honest with you. Frankly, I come out here they chant MVP. I get a little uncomfortable. And uh you know, I'm just like I just want to come out here and play ball. And so, uh got to do that today and and fired up to be a part of this team. And you know, write the write the story of whatever this season's going to be. >> You said pretty quick. Did it feel like relative to some previous decisions you made that this one was I don't want to say a no-brainer, but very clear cut that you wanted more? >> Yeah, it was. Um obviously, I knew how who we had coming back. Um I felt great about the guys around us uh and I felt healthy. I felt really healthy and and that was something that uh obviously, you never know. I just try to continue to maintain that and make sure that my body's ready to go. Um but was so excited to come back to come back to work with the guys that we have this year and and like I said, I mean every season is a new season. Last year, you know, it doesn't matter, you know, this time of year this year. So, we got to go out there and prove it every single day and we got the right kind of guys that want to do that. >> I mean, we all look to you. You're you're the quarterback, but have you just looked around and said, "Wow, Puka, Demonte, that's Miles Garrett. We're all on the same football team." That's got to build some sort of excitement for about what you guys can be. >> It is, you know, and and you know, rosters on paper don't win football games, but it is fun to show up to practice and look across the ball and see as many great players as we have on defense. I look down to my right and to my left at the line of scrimmage and I'm surrounded by great players and we all feel that way. We have a you know, a feeling of hey, I don't want to let that guy down next to me, you know, and and we have that respect for each other, respect for the game and understanding that hey, it's it's whatever it says on paper, it doesn't matter. We got to go out there and earn it every single day and we have guys that are you know, great talented players, defensive players of the year, all that kind of stuff, but they want to go out and earn it every single day and that's what it's going to take. >> That's how I feel about him. >> Yeah, get out of here. >> I love what you said though about that MVP, you know, representing a lot of Rams. And I want to talk about the running game for a second because though your stats were absolutely MVP-worthy, you're in so many great down and distances because of the way you're able to avoid negatives and stay on schedule with that running game. How important was that to last year and how much would you love to spin it forward to '26? >> Yeah, I mean, I correct me if I'm wrong, I think we're historically efficient, you know, handing the football off and that is so many things, right? That's our guys up front creating holes, our guys on the second level blocking and and our running backs just finding holes, making creases, making great runs and that just opens up the entire playbook. You ask Sean, you know, if we're getting five on a run on first down, how he feels about that. I mean, he is ecstatic, right? As a play caller, the pressure comes off, you just get to call the game, you know, put yourself in favorable situations. Not only were they great in the run game, they did a heck of a job for us in the screen game and in pass game as well. So, again, talented players all around me and I feel lucky to be the the trigger man. >> You don't get bored by the good run game? >> No, shoot. You [laughter] go back and look at that Arizona at their place where they were playing dime against us and I just kept looking at the sideline we were running at the first drive and I'm like, do not call a pass. Like just keep running this thing. You know what I mean? So >> Yeah. >> there's uh you know, there's a time and a place for everything and and I'm into winning football games however we can do it. How's your life changed since joining the Madden 99 club? >> Uh not much. I don't uh >> Do you Do you get on the sticks? Do you >> I don't. Um you know, that's I've retired that part of my life about 20 years ago probably is the last time I you know, played video games, but it is fun. You know, I interact with all these young fans out here and they get excited about it. Um I got four daughters. They're not playing Madden yet. They might get someday. Uh but I've got you know, their their friends that are little boys running around are fired up about and excited about it and and frankly, let's be honest. I I mean, I played in Madden 97. >> That's [laughter] kind of what I was on in Nintendo 64. You had the rumble pack. I mean, it was good stuff. >> That uh you know, if you would have asked that little kid me that you know, hey, do you think you're going to be a 99 uh someday? I would have told them heck no and and I'm I'm sure grateful to be one. >> Yeah. Uh you've been doing this a long time, but doesn't this blow your mind all this stuff? >> It is. The game is growing, man. It's crazy just to see what has happened in the last 18 years and and how it's progressed not only from a media standpoint, but just I look at our locker room and how everybody takes care of themselves. Such a such a great uh you know, model for like business. I mean, our guys just are workmen-like. We show up. We go to work. We take care of our bodies. We do everything we can to try to be as good as we can and um you know, I think that's the reason I'm still playing and it's it's fun to be a part of. >> You talked about that plan. You're not going to be out here every day. You're not going to be throwing like you did today every day. But how confident are you that you can get to where you want to be when you get on the plane to Australia? >> Yeah, I mean, it's it's a process. Um you know, you're going to have good days. You're going to have days you won't back. You're going to learn from all of it. Um I feel confident in it at the moment that I'm you know, healthy enough to continue to progress on this plan and keep getting better and better and and part of my role is hey, I want to be as good as I can possibly be and I want to help our team be as good as we can possibly be. So, uh when they ask me to be out there, I'm going to be out there giving it everything I possibly have and at the same time trusting the process and knowing [music] that hey, um you know, this is quite a few of these training camps under my belt at this time and you know, last year proved a little bit in an unforeseen circumstance that hey, with some time off you can still show up and uh you know, get yourself and the team ready to play. >> I I'm looking at Kevin Dotson, your your your starting right guard and he's got the horns in his hair. >> Oh, yeah. >> I mean, you you shouldn't encourage that, right? I love that enthusiasm. >> Dude, Dot Dot is one of a kind. We are so lucky to have him. We got him a couple years ago and what he's infused into our offensive line, not only from his physical play, nasty guard that's just so strong and effective in you know, inside doing his thing, but from a personality standpoint, you know, Shan does an unbelievable job of cultivating guys, letting them be themselves, you know, and and we're all part of this team. He's one of those guys that brings his own unique style and and vibe, but everybody loves it and appreciates it because we know what he's about. He loves playing the game of football. He loves being a teammate and uh you know, he likes doing some wild haircuts everyone smile. >> Would you ever consider >> No, no, [laughter] no, no. >> What about Stidham's mustache? >> Yeah, that >> That's strong. It's quite strong. >> I can't really grow one. That's not good. I just got the gray beard. I'll just be the old guy. >> Hearing you talk about Dotson though, I mean you're synchronizing your football for sure. But I remember last year you guys were talking about just wanting to earn one more week together. There's a lot of carry through. There's a lot of starters back. There's a lot of new faces too. How much is this time of year about building the trust and the confidence and the love for each other that's going to carry you through some of the darker days. >> Yeah, that's what it's all about, right? And and understanding hey, this you know, training camp is a little bit of a microcosm of what a season is, right? There's going to be days where, you know, offense plays good and defense doesn't play as well and next day the defense plays great, offense doesn't plays well. That's how you win football games. You don't go out and just dominate on offense, dominate on defense and everybody goes home. It's the NFL, right? We got to find ways to win games and that's you know, similar to what training camp is, right? There's ebbs and flows. There's good days and bad days. How do you come together, keep working, and and Sean made a great point the other night, right? Like you know, our ceiling could be potentially really high, you know, playing really good football with some of the talented players that we have. How do we continue to raise our floor? You know, when when everything's not right, hey, I don't have my best stuff or, you know, somebody's dinged up, how do we raise that floor so that the baseline, the bottom line of what we can go out and do is is really still effective? >> He looks good, too. Coach McVay running around, yeah. >> Absolutely. He uh he shared a couple off-season photos. I mean, he he looks great. He was ripped up. I saw Yeah, I mean, he's he's doing something. >> He's doing great. >> Do you believe in primes in sports? Like you hit your prime? >> Oh, man. I don't know. You know what? I It in this sport and in my position, I think there's multiple versions of that, right? Like physical prime, sure. Mental prime, yes. Emotional prime, understanding what it takes to win games, all those things, yes. Um I don't I don't think I'm in all three of those. Um but uh I do feel confident in uh you know, what it takes to go out there and win football games and and how I can positively affect it and make that happen. >> I I was meant for Puka. He's 25, year four. Physically, yes. What hasn't he seen? How much better can he get? >> Yeah, no doubt. I mean, I think he just continue to get, you know, stack those days and continue to get better and better. And and I love his energy. I mean, you guys have been around him and everybody that's been around him, they love him. Just the way he has an enthusiasm and a vigor for life. Um you know, we love him as a teammate. And like you said, I mean, he's physically extremely gifted, mentally as tough as they come, physically as tough as they come. And listen, the stats have been there, but even if he doesn't have those same stats, like the way he affects the game for us is is with and without the football. And so, we're lucky to have him and uh love being a teammate of his. >> Good to hang out with you, QB1. Thanks for stopping by. Wish you just the right amount of work, not too much, just the right amount here at training camp at LMU. All right, for Matthew Stafford, DeMarco Farr, and JB Long, Community America Credit Union taking us inside Rams Camp throughout the summer.

title: LB Jordyn Brooks meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Start of a new season. Um, shoot, football coming back. It's exciting time of the year. You know, it's always kind of like that dead period where there's no sports going on, so everybody's excited to watch football. We're excited to be back, so it's always a good time of year. >> Jordan, John Eric Sullivan said, "We're going to re-sign DeVante Parker, and we're going to re-sign Eric Brewer, and we're going to re-sign you." And then he pulls off all three. For a GM, especially in his first year, to say something and then follow it up with that action, what kind of message does that send to the rest of the locker >> Uh, I hope hopefully it sent the right message. Um, you know, uh, John coming in, being a man of his word, um, getting business handled, uh, for me, I'm grateful to to have the opportunity to still be here. Um, you know, I feel like it's unfinished business here in Miami for me, personally. And so, I'm excited for the opportunity to continue to team up my career here. Um, also excited for A Train and Brew, for them to, uh, have the same opportunity as I do. Um, and so, we take on the challenge to lead this team and, uh, do the very best that we can to help us win football games. >> Aside from the unfinished business, what is it about this program that makes you want to come back and be here long term? >> I just the relationships I built here, um, my teammates, obviously, and just the fact that we haven't accomplished what we've wanted to accomplish. Uh, and so, that's the unfinished business that we haven't, um, won our division yet. We haven't, made a playoff game. We haven't won a playoff game. We haven't made it to a Super Bowl. Haven't won a Super Bowl. So, it's a lot of goals, um, that we're trying to reach, and so, um, that's the goal each and every day, showing up here. >> What is it about a player like you? Why would you embrace being part of the rebuild? >> I mean, people could say it's a rebuild. I don't look at it as a as a rebuild because I'm in it and I play the game and I realize being in the league everybody is super talented and it's not always what it looks like on paper. You can have this superstar steady teams and they don't be worth a darn. You know what I mean? They don't have the right chemistry. They don't know how to connect the dots together. And you can have a bunch of no name teams um who know how to gel together, who know how to win, know how to buy in together and I think if you have that, you have the perfect team. And so that's the way I'm looking at it. I don't really care if people think that it's a rebuild or they think we're going 0 and 17 or whatever people have been saying. Um I look at it as and we got a bunch of football players who's hungry, super talented. Nobody in this locker room would be here if they didn't have what it takes. So my goal is to help lead the charge, be the very best that I can be and help us win. >> With that being said, the 13 draftees and the free agents and the new coaches, as a veteran and leader here, what's how do you instill a message and what message do you want to instill in in this group to bring them all together here? >> Yeah, just show up and work. I mean there's really no other reason for us to be here other than to work and work together and have fun as we do it, you know. Enjoy each other's company, get to know each other and and really put the time in and do whatever it takes to win, you know what I mean? And that's showing up every day, being consistent. If there's something extra we need to do as a group, we'll do that. Whatever it takes. But um that's the biggest thing that I want to locker room to understand is we're doing whatever it takes to win, whatever it takes to change the narrative around here, whatever it takes to turn the the page over. Um that's the that's the path that I'm taking. >> Coach Halfley mentioned that at some point this summer he expects to have live tackling, of course within the rules. Um how do you feel about that? >> I love it. I I love it. I think the only way you can get better at tackling is to tackle. Um it's hard trying to get your feet ready and and and and and get that work in in the first game of the season, you know what I mean? Um and it's always pros and cons each situation. Some teams want to take care of guys, don't want to get people hurt. Um so you don't get those real tackling reps. Um so first time you tackle is the first game of the season. It might end up good, it might end up bad, but I think it's great. Um I don't I don't believe in trying to be too careful. The game is the game. If you get hurt, it was meant to be, I guess, you know what I mean? So uh the live reps, I think it's going to be huge for us. Get practice going, get the juice going, um and shoot, just go hit somebody. So it'll be fun. >> A lot of one-year deals on this roster. As a leader, you know, how do you get guys to buy into the overall game plan amidst players really fighting for their NFL futures? >> Yeah, I mean the biggest thing is one to lead by example. Uh to get somebody to buy in, you have to be bought in. So I I got to make sure I'm bought in, you know what I mean? Every day that I come up here. Um cuz the guys will see that. Uh and then whatever I say after that, it'll make sense to what I'm saying. Cuz I'm doing it. And so that's the biggest thing is to do it. Um and let people see that you are bought in. Um and hopefully they follow suit. But like you say, guys being on one-year deals, I think that should be enough to motivate you. Um knowing that your future is uncertain, you know what I mean? And everybody's future is uncertain when you walk in this building. And so that should be enough to motivate you to go hard every day and uh give it the best that you got. >> What's your initial impression of Sullivan and Hafley and the culture they're building here uh to lead to that buying that you're talking about for yourself. >> I love it, man. They They just come in and work, put their head down. Haven't been didn't come in with a loud entrance. Um they didn't, you know, try to make themselves bigger than any anything or didn't They just came in ready to work. That's the best thing I can say, really. Um right away, uh half was pretty clear in what he expected from us uh personally and then as a team. Um same thing with with John Eric and so I appreciate the way that they come in and um excited to work with them and um you know, help them to help us be successful. >> Jordan, you said at one point during the off season you weren't like totally sure you'd be you'd be getting an extension done. When did you become confident that it was going to happen and was there a point where you were pressing yourself to to play your final year of your contract? you never know any situations. Uh it can always go either way. Truthfully, the whole time I really wasn't too concerned about it. Um purposely just trying to focus on football and letting the business side take care of itself. And so, uh I just stayed patient and if it worked out, it did. If it didn't, then I'd still be here, you know what I mean? And so um I'm grateful that it worked out. Um and now we just focus on football and winning football games. >> Howie mentioned you and Jaylen spent some time getting ready this summer spending time working together um during the break. Just what was that experience like and why did you decide aside from the obvious Texas A&M connection, why did you decide to take him there? >> Uh I think it's just something that happened natural. Um anytime I can, you know, spend some time with any of my teammates outside of the building, I'm always up for it. Um and him, just like myself, we ain't have too much going on outside of this and so we just decided to get some work in, train together, Uh hang out a little bit, him and a couple other guys as well, Traitor, Jackson Woodard. Um, spent a lot of time in the in the off season training and, you know, pushing each other, helping each other get better. And, um, just hanging out, man. So, that's pretty much do it. >> I've been seeing a couple linebackers, Lavonte David and Demario Davis, play some of their best ball into their mid to late 30s. Does that motivate you at all to like take another step in your career? And how do you make sure the next part of your career is the best part of your career? >> Yeah, those guys are, um, very inspirational to me, you know. Uh, I think Demario's 37. Bobby Wagner's 36, still playing at a high level. Um, and then Lavonte just just retired, but was still playing at a high level. Those guys encourage me, you know, whenever I get down there in age, um, then then you can still play this play this game at a high level. And so, um, it's motivating for me to see, um, as well as other linebackers in the league that, you know, you can stretch this thing out as for as long as you want. And so, uh, happy for those guys. Hope they continue to push it, you know. And so, that's where I'm trying to get to. >> What's your impression of what Coach Halfley is asking of the players for this training camp? >> Um, I think his idea is he wants us to be a tough, hard-working football team, you know, uh, smart football team, gritty, um, I think that's his mentality. Um, I think that's who he is as a person. And so, that's that's kind of what comes off. And so, and and that's right up my alley, you know. Uh, I think that I wouldn't want to be a part of any other team. A tough, gritty, hard-working football team that wins games the right way. And so, uh, I think his message and and what he expects from us has been great. >> Jordan, what would you consider a successful season for this team? And is the season record going to be the final determining factor of whether the season is a success? >> Success is is is is subjective. Um it's it's subjective, and you know, I'm a I'm a man of faith, [clears throat] and so I believe just being here already, we're successful. Um there's a lot of guys that I grown up playing with that uh didn't have these opportunities that we have right now. And so whether we win or we lose, we're cuz we're here. In football terms, I think what will make us successful um is winning our division, owning our division, um and getting a playoff berth, winning playoff games, making it to the Super Bowl, doing the things that nobody here thinks we can do. And so um in my opinion, that's what will make us successful. >> Jordan, this is my last question. Difficult to answer, but I read your story that you did with Knockon, I think last week or a few days ago. How do you get a team to play for one another? How do you get offense to care and play about care about and play for the guys on the other side of the ball, and and vice versa? I don't know. I think you got to have total buy-in. Um and the truth is, when you got so many guys on one team, I don't know, I mean, we got like let's just say there's 100 people on the team. 100 people being bought in is not realistic. Some some people have other interests, and so uh getting 100% buy-in is not realistic for any industry or organization or any team. But I think if you can have the majority bought in, I think that is what's going to help us to get over that hump. And I think the way that we do that is having our leaders at each position leading, you know what I mean? Leading in every way, on and off the field, uh cuz I think they they tie into both. Who you are outside of the building ties into who you are on the field. And so, I think that our leaders on this team we've got to be great in the way that in the way that we lead. Um and then everybody else follow suit and we turn this thing over.

title: QB Malik Willis meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: I'll just open it up for everybody and if they had the chance to make it, obviously I don't want to take people away from their family and their time off, but if you had some time and you could get up there, I opened it up for everybody. It was pretty cool. >> How vital is that just working that overtime beyond the OTAs and pre-training camp continuing to build that chemistry? >> I think all reps are good reps. Obviously when you can work through things and figure guys out, I think it's the best of both worlds really. >> What kind of turnout did you see in the in Jacksonville working out with your teammates? >> Oh, we had six or seven guys. It was pretty cool. Definitely just to see them get out there and work and they did everything that I did, so it was pretty cool to see. Even some of the workout stuff. We'd get in the weight room after we get off the field, so I'm just glad that they had a little time to spend and we can steal a couple reps before we get into training camp. >> What did you feel you took away from those workouts >> I try to take away little things that you probably don't notice just looking around like who gets out there breaks faster, who I can throw to a little earlier than later, who likes it right on them or do they like it above their head? I mean just all those type of things that can help you be successful as far as like minimizing risk. >> A lot of people on the outside say you don't have the weapons necessary to succeed here. After working with these guys, what's your take >> We all play football at a high level or we wouldn't be in the NFL. Every team has good players. It's just putting them in position to be successful and all the guys that have big names at one point didn't have a big name and I think that's how it goes. You just got to prove it and that's where we at right now. >> How does it feel to be I guess the guy in your first training camp taking on this big leadership role? I know you said before that doesn't really change much for you, but now you're now you're here, so I'm just wondering if if that respect has changed. >> No, I'm just trying to do whatever I can to earn that role every day. You know, put the work in, put the time in and earn the respect from my teammates. I think that's what's most vital and most important more than a paycheck or more than a position that other people say you're in. And I just try to focus on that and continue to get better. >> Sounds like you did a lot of work on the on the field, weight room, and the off-season. But how do you train your brain when there's no practices in terms of the mental, like getting the playbook, getting the film? What do you do to enhance that part of the game? >> I mean, just more than anything is mental reps and focusing on, okay, if I was in this position, like I'm throwing with the guys up there. I'm like, okay, this this position. And they're like bringing cloud or something, I could try to stop them with the ball and make a different type of throw. And just understanding that when you're working, you're working for a reason and not just out there throwing the ball around. Obviously, that would be a little pointless. It's never as easy as it is out there. >> We talked to the players all the time and about perception of other teams before the season, during the season, whatever. And they sometimes they say they don't watch TV or listen to social media or whatever. Are you the kind of player that allows that perception to filter in and are you motivated by that? >> Uh not really. I mean, I'm more than anything focused on what I have to say about me. That's what's most important just as it is with you guys. You don't care what other people say about you. When you have that issue, you have more problems than not. But I just try to focus on continuing to get better. I wouldn't be in this position if the hard work and dedication that we put into the sport, none of us would, but uh I just try to focus on that and continuing to get better cuz you could be one spot now and 6 months later you could be in another spot. So, just try to focus on that. >> What do you think every year a quarterback has to be a great quarterback in the league? What does being a great quarterback mean? >> Uh just impacting the guys around you. Uh doing all the things that take no talent at a high level every time you get the opportunity to. And uh winning. I feel like that's the most uh the great the greatest stat you can have as a quarterback. Just going out there and win games. >> Where do you feel you are as far as the new playbook? >> Uh I think it's pretty cool. It was very similar. Obviously, we had to work through a couple kinks in figuring out uh just the terminology sort of thing and that was easy to get through. Obviously, it just takes reps and continuous saying it and being in the huddle and actually going through it and that's whatever you do. Obviously, I had three or four offenses before this one and it's the same process and I think it was cool to have OTAs to work on that and uh figure out the differences between the offenses like, "Okay, this is the same route, but they teach it differently here." And the receivers know it from a different terminology standpoint, so uh that's the biggest thing and I think I'm at a good place and we get to go out in camp, get more reps at it. >> Malik, the start of training camp, what what does that mean to you? A lot of fans would say it's like the first day of school or like it's Christmas, but what does that mean to you and is it different now that you come in as a starting quarterback? >> I think it's exciting. I mean, I miss football. I get bored. And obviously, you were just talking about throwing on air and that's not fun at all, but it's a method to the madness. Uh and it is like the first day of school. It's the first time we get back and see all our buddies, all our coworkers, I guess. It's a business, but uh all the guys are excited to go. And we just got to continue that up throughout camp and through the preseason and take it into the season. Just building confidence and momentum. >> Malik, high school football practice started yesterday in Florida. Do you have any favorite memory of high school football or some advice you could give? >> I mean, every game in high school football was pretty fun. I mean, that's the best memory, but uh probably getting to the state championship, the game before the state championship my senior year. Uh we played the school I had left the year before and we ended up beating them 28-0. Put a whipping on Yeah. That was a That was a odd game feelings-wise. Obviously, I had been there 3 years prior, but that's probably my best memory cuz it was cool seeing all my boys out there and getting to play against them. It's just like if we got to play Miami Dolphins offense vs. defense in a real game, so but that was probably my best memory. A lot of touchdowns. >> Why'd you transfer? >> Uh our coach had left and I didn't have a bunch of offers, so I had to go somewhere that kind of had it together. It was going into spring ball and we still didn't have a head coach. And that's like, "Great." >> You get to play >> When it comes to leadership, are you more of a vocal leader or strike with your example? >> I feel like you can be both. I feel like there is moments and times that you need to be both. You have to understand people. Obviously, some people handle they can handle being talked to a certain type of way, others can't. So, you got to talk to them a certain type of way. And then sometimes, nothing needs to be said cuz they already know what they messed up on. And belittling them or just reiterating it might not be beneficial to help us, you know, succeed. And I feel like it's just a time and place type thing. >> A lot of one-year deals on this roster. Sometimes that can result in guys being like, "Me, me, me." But as a leader, how do you get the rest of the team to kind of buy into this overall goal, the overall mission amidst people literally playing for their NFL futures? >> Yeah, I feel like Half and Sully did a great job putting this team together. Uh they put it together with guys that have that same mindset that you're talking about that we have one goal. Obviously, our goal is to go out there and win games. And to do that, it's going to take all 11 each play. Nobody can go out there and win it by their self. It's not like basketball where you can have somebody drop 60, you know what I mean? Obviously, you can have players that impact the game in a positive way, but at the same time, we're all If I don't do the right thing and everybody else does the right thing, it could be a bad play for the offense. If a receiver doesn't do the right thing, it can make a bad play for the offense and everybody else does. So, it's all working together and continuing to, like I said, go out there and build confidence in that so you can trust the guy that's next to you. >> And what do you say about that? What What does it What does it say that this regime did extend H and Brooks Brewer? What do you take from that? >> I think it's awesome for those guys. It's a great to have them secure in in here. And I think that, you know, lit a fire in the locker room. Obviously, as far as it not being a rebuild, as they say, and more or less you putting people in position to lead your franchise to a a newer place, maybe build from where we're at instead of a rebuild. And I think that's awesome. >> What have you learned about yourself about the challenge of joining a new team? >> Uh I don't know. I'm pretty introspective if you if you would have guessed or not, but I don't know. I just try to keep it one day at a time, you know, take it for what it is, be grateful for where I'm at, and try to earn everything else. >> One more question, one more guys. What would you consider a successful season for this team, and how much does season record figure into that success? That how much of it is a determining factor? >> I mean, obviously, you want to put yourself in a position to not have expectations, but you obviously want to do everything you can to put the work in and take it one game at a time. That's the only way you can play this game. Uh you take it and go one and 0 each week. Obviously, you do enough of that, and you'll be a division leader at some point. Then you do more of that, and you'll be in the playoffs at some point and taking that one game at a time. And once you get to the playoffs, it's anybody can win as we see every year. You know, guys go and have a better record and end up losing to a team with a worse record. All it is is about taking it one game at a time and doing what we can right now, which is where we're at, and focus on building confidence and continuing to build momentum. >> Have you guys adapted to living in Miami? Was it something that you love from living here, and are you completely adapted to living here? >> Yeah, I'm integrated by now. I go to I got my little spots. They know me when I come in there. So, I think it's been great. Obviously, the weather is always amazing. If you like it hot, I mean, I like it hot. from Georgia. I like it hot. So, it's been amazing. All the food is great, and the people love Dolphin football, so all those things I can get behind. >> Do you get recognized a lot down here? >> It depend if I go out. I don't be outside like that. >> No, I'm just talking about like regular people who go to public places. >> No, that's what I'm saying. I don't go out for real for real. I I be Instacarting. Doordashing. >> [laughter] >> Yeah, so I don't be outside like that. I just be coming to work. >> Did you get some leisure time? Read some books, some movies, some kind off? >> Yeah, I did. I spent 3 weeks at home and spent a little time with them and got all my leisure, played a lot of golf, and the last 2 weeks been just working, so. >> That's it.

title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: We're in Florida. What do you expect? Everybody have a good vacation. What'd you do to your arm? Thought like you had a big gash or something in there. What a way to start it. You drop your hat and you come out with a full Yeah. No, that' be non non football. Um, I got good news for you. Everybody passed the conditioning test. You're welcome for that information. >> I know that was going to be your first question. [laughter] >> All right, let's go. >> Have um tell me about this time of year for you as a as a coach. You know, I guess the fans it's kind of like Christmas or first day of school. What What is it like for you as a coach? >> I guess it's probably the same thing. I mean, usually by the time I was we were finished with OTAAS and, you know, getting ready for vacation, I think we all needed it physically, mentally, the players certainly physical, the coaches, mentally. Um, and then you go on vacation and, you know, pretty soon towards the end, at least for myself, you're usually excited and ready to go again. Fresh mind, uh, rested and just it's what we do. So excited. It's it's real football. The pads will eventually come on. um you're not just gearing up for, you know, OTAAS, you're gearing up to play in real football games. So, there's a level of urgency, there's a level of excitement. Um it's what we love to do and it's why we do it. So, I can't wait and it's good to be back in the building. >> What sort of message? Yeah, I think it sends a really positive message. Um, you know, and I think Sully did a really nice job, the timing of it and, um, you know, the communication of it. Um, one, production, right? If if you're here and you do a really good job on the field, um, two, you do things the right way, you're a good teammate, you're a good person, um, you make good decisions on and off the field, you'll be rewarded. And I think that's a very clear, very good message to send the younger players on this team. Um that if if those things happen, there's a good chance that, you know, we'll take care of them and we'll want them around and we'll want to build this through guys that we see do that. So, congrats to those three. I think they've earned it. I was excited to talk to, you know, Han was done before we left, but Brew got done shortly after and then Brooks was after that. So, it was excited to talk to them. They deserve it. And as a coach, when you see a player get rewarded and can take care of himself and his family, um that's a really cool deal. Um because sometimes, you know, you got to take a step back and think about the lives that are changed, right? And and those are important. >> What would you say is the single most important thing you want to get across to your team on day one? >> Um getting back to how we want to practice. um the competitiveness eventually the physicality which we'll still have to wait until pads come on um but I want it to be competitive and I want them to feel a sense of urgency in that >> there's some first year head coaches and first year new team head coaches that have immediate success in the NFL I don't know if you studied that at all but is there anything that you can apply during studying that that you can apply to this team success >> I I think all those all those are different right where at when you take over, who's on the team, what the roster looks like, what the division looks like. Um, there's a whole lot that goes into that. So, no, I have not taken a lot into that. Rather taken into going through our offseason, figuring out who we are, um, who we have, what we can be good at, what schemes fit who we have and what we can be good at, and try to worry about ourselves. Um, I've learned a lot from other coaches around the league and I'll take a lot of that with me and I'll have questions along the way, but that is not just I'd be making it up if I told you I did. >> How do you work through whether to reference or not bother referencing sort of the national forecast? We're not oblivious to this. None of us have our head. So, do you bring it up or do you not? >> Not immediately. No. But I think there will be moments that I will um I don't think now is the time for that. Now is the time for us to focus on ourselves and for our guys to go out and win jobs and for our coaches to put together schemes and develop and get ready to play. I I think certainly there's a time and a place for that. I'd be lying to you if I just said we're going to ignore it. Um I'd rather not have that be the main focus. Um because I think that kind of goes in one ear. you get fired up for a couple minutes and then you leave and you it has to become real again. So, I think there's bigger things to talk about, foundations to build and maybe if we need a jolt here and there, throw it at them, but nothing I'm concerned about right now. >> When you when this fan base looks at this team whenever they have their availabilities leading up to the regular season, what do you hope that they >> practice wise, >> practice, exhibition season? Yeah, I want them to see a physical team that that lays it on the line, that plays together, that has fun together, um, and that can execute without making a lot of pre- snap, postnap mistakes. A smart football team who plays as hard as they can for as long as they can and enjoys playing together and that's really important because those are the things that we can control. >> It's a big class in both size and importance to the team's future. What did you take away with or from how they arrived back to training camp and back to the facility last week? >> Yeah, I mean they look good. They've been working and as far as you know what we did with them, it was all meetings and in the classroom to try to get them a head start. Bless you. Um try to get them going, reaclimated to the playbook because a lot of it's still new for them. But other than that, I mean, watching them in the conditioning test today, I think give us about four or five practices before we kind of get a view on what they look like and how they came back. I mean, again, I don't want to sit here and make anything up. We were in meeting rooms with them and talked to them and they look good. It looks like they worked out. So, that's a positive. >> That's right. >> In regards to Chris Bell's eventual return to practice, just so we don't ask every day, we >> You're going to ask me every day. That's okay if you do. No, just ask. looking more at months than weeks. >> Um, months than weeks. I think that's up in the air. I think he's in a really good place right now. Um, and and we'll see, but I I don't think it's like way off in the distance. All right. Um, but I am excited where he's at. I can get a smirk on my face and have some optimism there. He's worked really hard. Our training staff, Kyle and those guys and Todd, have done a great job with them. I think I think he's had a great summer and he's in a he's in a good spot. You're going to see him run run around out there. Did the conditioning test today with the team. So, we'll see where it goes. I I just as much as there's optimism and I get excited about where he's at. I think we also have to be careful. So, we'll continue to work through it. >> Doug and Daker, same question. >> They'll be a little bit further off. Um they'll be they'll be further off down the road at some point this season. I see them coming back. And Austin Jackson, we didn't see him in 11 on 11s at the end of mini camp. Is he >> He's back. >> He is back. >> Jeff, you told us the offseason program that you wanted to keep in that training camp as well. >> Yeah. No, he's going to start off left guard and try to get good at one position. I think that's fair to him and it's the best thing >> ultimately we need to do what's best for our team. In this case, I think it's best for him and I think it's best for our team. So that's what we've decided to start and we'll go from there. >> During the spring, we saw start to build with the receivers. What do you want to see from him during camp, but also at what point do you want to start to see real progress um with the chemistry? >> I saw progress in the last couple OTAA practices. And what I saw was his confidence started to go like this. It was, you know, um not just the reps with the players, but it was the reps of the same plays over and over again and just building those cumulative reps that, you know, he started to feel comfortable with more plays than he did when he started. I think the key for Malik will be um it is his confidence and it is his chemistry with those wide outs and we need to figure out exactly who those wide outs are and and what the chemistry is going to look like. But it's I want to see his confidence and I want him to focus in on that and let me take care of the rest. But um I'm excited for him. He he was he worked really hard this summer. He was in Jacksonville a bunch training. He had a bunch of the receivers uh running routes, running the plays with them, holding workouts out there, which was really cool to see him kind of lead that charge. Um so we'll see. >> When you say confidence, do you mean like his command of the offense stepping into a new role as starter? Kind of a mix of everything. >> A mix of everything. I want to see when he's at the line of scrimmage, there's no hesitation. I want to I want to feel his confidence. I want to see his confidence. I want him not to be discouraged when he has a bad throw or throws an interception. I want him to to step into that role and all the above. >> Your plans for training camp include tackling? >> They do. They do. Are you excited about that? >> Absolutely. >> The the thinking and signing Cleveland for >> Yeah. just we watching him on film and talking to Sully, a guy who plays really hard. Obviously, he was a high draft pick. Um I think it brings competition to that room. He's got good strength. Um he's got some good clips on tape and and hopefully we can get everything out of them. I just the more competition that we can bring in. Um I think you're going to see a lot of that as we turn through things and just see what we can get in him. But I'm excited to work with him. I've really only talked to him briefly because it just happened. Um, but I'm glad that he's here. leaders to kind of focus on or I guess kind of address team first. How do you go about that? >> I think everything we do from coaches to players has to be talked about team first. And I think that just like in anything else when you have team success, you have individual success. Individual success without team success in my opinion is meaningless. Um and we don't want to build our team like that. At the same time, I mean, you're right. We probably have more guys on one-year deals than anybody in the NFL. So, a lot of those guys, rightfully so, are they're going to be fighting for their jobs. So, there's probably going to be times where we have to have those conversations. And I mean, that's our job to figure it out. I'm not just going to sit here and say that that's never going to happen because that's not the real world, right? So, we'll deal with it when it happens. Um, at the same time, I think you're going to see you're going to see a lot of guys playing and practicing at a very high level, pushing each other, competing with each other because they know they're on a one-year deal. And for some of them, this is this is it. This is their shot. >> Based on what you've learned in a short period of time about Brooks and Brewer, who obviously the organization is now committed to how does their approach help you set the tone for what you want here. >> I think it's it kind of goes back to what we just talked about. One, production. They're they're very productive players. We're not just going to reward guys for doing everything the right way, practicing hard, being in the weight room, being great leaders. They are they're productive. they've had success, but on top of that, I mean, the way those guys go out and practice, the way they are in the meeting room, the way they are in the wait room, the way they take care of their teammates and look after their teammates and try to lead the younger guys, I think it says to everybody on our team, okay, if if if I go out and I can produce and I do things the right way, then I will be rewarded here. And I think that sends a very powerful message to all the young players on our team. Um, I think that's very important. And again, I think Sully did a great job there. ranked number one in the NFL report card. How do you translate the player resources? >> I mean, I take all of that with a grain of salt, right? I mean, all that report card, all that stuff is great. I'm just I'm not overly concerned about that. I'm concerned about obviously the support here and Mr. Ross and ownership has done an unbelievable job. The all the resources, everything that they put into it, it's all there for them. And now we need to use all that and we need to use this training camp to go out and get better and develop these players and have the result show up on the field. >> Brooks drove to the facility to reach Jacob after he got drafted. How important is that relationship? >> It would be really important. They also spent time together training this summer which I thought was really cool which when you guys get a chance you guys can talk to them about that. Um obviously there's a connection there with where they went to school, right? So that's pretty powerful. They play a very they both are linebackers, so they're going to be working together. But again, I think it relates back to your question. You get a guy who's a vet and he could kind of probably go out and just do whatever he wants on his own, but instead he's bringing a guy along and trying to help him, which I don't think everybody does in this league. There are some vets that are really good players that all that they come in, they do their job, they focus on themselves, they get their plays done, they work really hard, and they leave. He's taken an extra step on trying to help and bring along a younger player, which I think says everything about him. >> High school football started practice yesterday. >> Enjoy it. Um, you know, a lot of football memories, right? I've been doing this at from college to the NFL. Some of my best memories are still in high school with the guys you kind of grew up with playing with, which is becoming even rare right now in college because your teammates are different teammates every year. So, it's the one time where a lot of times it's the guys you grew up with, the guys you were playing in the backyard with, the guys you're now in the locker room with. Just enjoy it. It's one of the best times of your life. And um I wish everybody good luck. >> Jeff, how did you yourself prepare to leave your first NFL training camp as a head coach? you reach out to certain guys for advice, study things that you've seen in the past? >> Uh, this summer I I rested my mind because I was exhausted. I spent a lot of time with my family. I think the biggest thing for me is always coming in with a clear head. Um, I I do some reading over the summer. It's the only time where I can um do that. I have time. So, sometimes I just look for, you know, different ways to say things and what I want to say, but maybe different ways to say it. I talk to certain coaching friends and bounce ideas off of. But the biggest thing for me is that I have to continue to remind myself is I just want to be myself. And that's I think that's where people can get caught up. At least for me, like I'm just going to do this and be myself and kind of, you know, bounce ideas off of certain guys, but I don't want to change who I am. I want to do it a certain way. I want to trust the guys that we have on this staff to help. I think we have a really good staff put together. uh lean on them um get really tight with these players and and just be myself. >> So there's like a balance between I guess preparing and overpreparing. >> Yeah. Because here Yeah. Because here here's what happens, right? It's all of a sudden it's oh I found this great idea or these great slogans or these great things that I'd like to do for team building, but deep down that's really not you. And then all of a sudden you become someone you're not. and do you really believe in that stuff? So, I'm going to do and preach and talk about the stuff that I truly believe in. So, it's real because I think that's really important. They feel that from me. So, I'm just not BSing them and looking at a book and throwing up quotes that I don't even really know where they came from or what they mean. Um, but sometimes they give you some good thoughts. >> Clear for >> ready to go. >> What did you read? >> I'm not telling. >> What kind of read >> me? >> Yeah. I don't read like story books if that's what you're asking. I don't have time. >> Romance novels. >> I do like No, I'm just joking. >> Did you see Odyssey and IMAX? It was awesome. >> No, you know what? I did see the movie. Can you guess the one movie I went? I did. [laughter] >> It wasn't a bad movie. >> Why is that funny? You see he he went Did you see it? >> I went and saw Toy Story 5. Did you see it, Ann? >> My kids were so excited to see it. It was actually very Did you guys see it? >> It was a good movie. >> So, yeah, some good lessons in that. You can find lessons and you can find thoughts in anything that you watch. No romance novels though. >> I had it on. Yeah, I had it on. As as long as there was a TV, I had it on. Usually I like to check out like the last five minutes when it got really exciting. >> Root for the shootouts, but I always had it on. So, it was fun to watch. I thought that was really cool. >> I didn't. >> Did you go? I did. >> Was it fun? >> I probably should have went, but I was with my family and kind of just getting away. I'll be in the stadium enough this year. >> That's it. >> Yeah. I don't like like in all due respect to the report card, I just I want to win. So they can grade me whatever they want. I want to win and I want to do it the right way. Um that the that's the report card, right? So how we do it, how we build the foundation, how hard we play, how physical we play, how we grow throughout the way, how we develop these players, um finding small victories and little things like those are the report cards, right? Um, and there's going to be some hard conversations with some guys that, you know, we're not going to be able to keep everybody. There's going to be some guys that beat some people out, and I'm going to be honest with them, and not everybody's going to like what I say. And I'm not going to sugarcoat stuff. I'm going to tell them the truth. And there's going to be some people that might not grade me high because of that's just I don't I I don't care, you know? I want to do it the right way and build this thing the right way so we can win. And that's what I care about. >> All right.
