title: GM Nolan Teasley and Head Coach Kevin O'Connell Preview 2026 Training Camp
text: Good afternoon, everybody. Good to see you know all of all you folks back ready to rock and roll. Before we get going, I do want to uh uh just kind of hit on the Gerald Alexander situation. I know we issued a statement earlier. Um first and foremost, um disappointment is the word. Um anytime you know, something like this happens, you know, we go up through a process with with the obviously the league and make sure the legal process plays out and that's been our precedent through these uh through these situations and you know, when that process is complete, which uh you know, has been uh you know, a recent uh situation to be completed, uh we made the decision to suspend Gerald um as coaches uh the expectations and the standards we have um are clear and it's important that we do those things for our players and and be the examples on and off the field in this organization and and we take that very seriously. Um Gerald understands that. He knows he fell short of those expectations and he's taken full responsibility for for what happened and um he understands the consequences and and uh you know, that is uh already a process that's begun and uh he knows he needs to make better decisions moving forward. You know, he's a valued member of my staff. We're you know, fortunate to bring him on. His experience with the flow and you know, he's done a great job on the grass since since he arrived and will continue to do so when when he returns and we're excited to get him back. Um you know, changing gears, you guys know training camp is my favorite time of year, favorite time to get on the grass with the guys and um we get a daily uh we get a daily task of of trying to grow, improve, um continue to build upon you know, one of the tightest tightest groups, tightest knit groups in the in the National Football League from a culture standpoint. We're really excited about our team this year. Every year at TCO here, I think we have the best training camp set up in the National Football League. You guys know, I think we've got the best fans in the National Football League and look forward to welcoming them out starting on on Saturday. So, it's been a good off season for our team. I really like the way we approached the off season program getting the most out of it even though, you know, the circumstances aren't what they're going to be in training camp when we can start applying physicality and and and really going through a very grueling difficult process to to kind of build our team the right way and I think between now and when we open the season, there's a lot of room for improvement, but I know I you know, I speak on behalf of our players when I say they're excited about what the potential of our team can be, but that's what this time of year is for all 32 teams. There's a wonderful opportunity out in front of all of us and and we got to go to work to maximize it every every single day. It's going to be a physical camp. We want to you know, really build our team a certain kind of way. You know, we have enough experience now since you know, since I've arrived here. I know with clarity the type of the type of team that we need to build and and the improvements we need to make and I think a lot of that alignment has been you know, a daily thing that I've really enjoyed growing with with Nolan every single day and his staff. It's been a really cool summer getting to you know, build these relationships and see just so many of the things that made us all so excited about bringing Nolan here. It's it's just awesome when it starts coming to life on a daily basis and it's not only Nolan, but but the staff that he's assembled has has has been just as as good of a staff as I've been around, quite honestly. And I really look forward to see them continuing to build upon that. And then, you know, I'll defer to Nolan on this one, but with with great excitement for me as the head coach to to know that we've got Brian O'Neill under contract for for a long time. He's been such a pillar of this organization and um just the leadership uh as as a guy that from day one when I arrived here, he's been somebody that that uh you know, he's poured in everything uh since I've been here and and a long time before that and and this organization means so much to him, our fans, our ownership. Uh and just to watch this, you know, process play out in the way Nolan and his staff and and everybody handled it to come to this this outcome on the eve of training camp is is is just a really really good thing for our team. And I know Brian is going to go out there and have the best year uh yet with with the type of off season he's had and um his excitement about what we're doing offensively and and where we take it from here. So, I'll turn it over to Nolan. >> Yeah. How's everybody doing? Um just kind of echoing that sentiment. Like, this is an exciting time of year, obviously. And can't wait to uh I mean, just starting to see the the setup come to life out there. I can't wait to to welcome our fans and and get this year started. Again, exciting time of year um as an opportunity to grow as a football team, to grow together as an operation. Um and just getting underway this this summer again, KO kind of touched on it, but working together with this guy every day, um we're it's become clear we're aligned in our vision um both in terms of of where we are uh currently and as we uh you know, embark on the 2026 season, but also uh where we're headed in the future and as we as we build this thing out. Um The connection between the coaching staff and personnel is is already pretty apparent. Uh we've seen it come to life with some of the the recent acquisitions, the extension of Brian O'Neill. I'll talk about that a little bit more in depth, but yeah, just just really really really excited about where we stand today and then where we're going in the future. And just to briefly I haven't seen you guys since we since we added some members of the of the personnel staff, but Andrew Healy, Trent Kirchner, Tyler Hamlin, Ryan Pace, Ezam Kapadia. They have they bring a wealth of experience, very complimentary skill sets, and they've meshed really well with the talent that we already have in the building with with Ryan Monahan and Chiz and Mike Shaladan and and Sam DeLuca to just to name a couple. So to see everybody working together, building out process, being collaborative, being communicative, it's just been it's it just just gives you assurance that that we're headed in the right direction. And it's early in the year still, so. In terms of BO, you know, working in Seattle, you're you're aware of what a great player he is, and then coming into the building, it's a privilege to kind of get to know the person. Spending some time with him and and understanding how how well regarded he is within the building, consummate professional, leader, and everybody just holds him in such in such high regard. It's a foundational piece and we're really really pleased that we're able to to keep him here for a long time. I'd be remiss if I didn't thank Rob Brzezinski for leading that that process. Emily Betis did a wonderful job and obviously he's represented by Ryan Tolner and Rep 1. Those guys are professionals, really good relationship between the Minnesota Vikings and them and we'll look forward to building upon that. And with that, we'll open it up. >> Kevin, you said this game's going to be physical. >> Is that different from other camps? More physical? >> Well, I think we you always want to you always want to find that balance cuz, you know, you you have to build kind of the callus of physicality with the rules that we have now really um you know, and even over the next 3 4 days we're still not going to be in full pads by the rules um I'm until um until Monday. Uh so really you're looking at a pretty significant amount of time between the last guy last time these guys were able to practice, you know, with the physicality specifically along the line of scrimmage. I mean, we're not tackling to the ground every day, but uh you know, we want to make sure our team um it's been a a process throughout the off-season, but also um through the schematics of what we're doing on offense and defense. We want to build our team uh in the ability to play the way we want to play on along the line of scrimmages. And then, you know, obviously both offense and defensively our schemes are you know, layered and built on top of each other, but it still comes down to play style and physicality in so many aspects of this game. And we've got to find a way to practice it on a daily basis when when we can uh all with a mindset of knowing we need a fresh team but a prepared team for the season. >> Is there any way you approach training camp differently now with 4 years under your belt than you might have in your one? >> Well, I just think you know, there's um you know, there's requirements. It's really not as as much time as as I know you know, coaches were always you know, fighting for as much time as we can possibly have with the guys, but when you really look at it and you uh you you know, get with the sports science people and you and you really learn you know, the the to maximize the days and they're not all the same, but they can still be maximized and they still give you a chance to to kind of own that day and make sure that you've uh you know, kind of shown up and put everything you've got into it. That's coaches, that's players, that's our uh staff supporting the players. Um but just from a scheduling standpoint, what works the best, uh always subject to change if if uh circumstances, whether it's uh you know, it's been pretty hot, you know, as of late, or uh weather here or there that uh you know, could force us uh to maybe just have to adjust because we want to maximize the preparation, but it's also really important to me to maximize the ability to to be in front of fans and and the energy that that brings to to practice this time of year. So, I think the joint practices with Baltimore, you guys know how important I believe those are. Um, you know, how we handle the preseason games is one thing, but uh the build-up to um those two days, while while also knowing that we've got to compete within, you know, the Vikings versus Vikings world, and um we hope that's a very competitive thing. >> Kevin, how do you anticipate managing the quarterbacks, uh and especially in the first week or so of camp, in terms of >> [snorts] >> first team, second team, whatever, but also just in terms of how you'll evaluate it? >> Yeah, I met with I met with uh all those guys really uh on an individual basis over the last day or so, and and and really just want to be uh able to articulate the vision and the plan. I feel very good about our plan. Um, both Kyler and JJ will will take reps with the first team. Uh they'll also take reps with uh the second group, and I think that gives uh different layers to the evaluation as well. We want you know, we want an elevator at the the quarterback position, and uh in many ways doing that in this system is um kind of a do-your-job mentality, which is, you know, running the show, throwing completions, and and just showing the ability to execute our offense with comfort, and that offense is an evolving thing, and and we're excited about what this year's offense could look like. Uh but uh we do want to you know, we want to be thorough. We want to be comprehensive with this, but at the same time, I think it's important uh when we feel good about a decision, you know, as a group and and and we're ready to ready to move forward. It'll be it'll be good to do that so we can prepare that player for the season, but also give our team and our players clarity of exactly the direction we're going and and then make sure that that whenever that happens, that's you know, not the end all. I mean, we need to continuously chase improvement amongst our whole team and there's other competitions that will go on and it's going to be a competitive back end of our roster to make our team because of you know, the depth that's been put together by Nolan and his staff. So there's a lot of layers to it, but in regards to those guys, that's how we'll handle it. >> Nolan, how will you like you sort of be involved in that in that situation? Will you just be a third party kind of just viewing it from afar or like will you be involved in the discussions of who's going to start? Just curious how you like envision your role in these types of situations. >> Yeah, just like just like anything and as we've gone through the summer we've actively talked about every decision that we've that we've made big or small and this will this will be no different. When it's decision-making time, I mean, ultimately it's a you want to give your coaching staff that freedom to to make that choice and but certainly I should have the ability to offer a different vantage point and and we'll discuss it actively. >> Yeah, and the only thing I would add is just the perspective. Um you know, I've I've come to Nolan about scheduling questions. I've come to him about um so many unique things just because um his experience and and you know, to have the ability to have that kind of dialogue um you know, about the decision-making process is only um enhancing our organization and making me better um and and that'll be the same case in regards to that conversation for sure. >> Kevin, with Christian Darrisaw, are there any physical concerns or limitations lingering yet with limit or is feet? >> No, there's not. And the the one thing I will say and and and I always want to make sure and I'll keep you guys updated as we go on, but we've got plans for all of our players. Um either players that uh you know, are coming off injury or in Christian's case, he's had a healthy off-season and he's really built up to a place where I know he's excited to get going, but uh throughout the you know, training camp, you know, can be a grind and and we want our players to experience that, but uh by but still taking individual aspect or individual approach, I should say, uh to how we best prepare uh you know, those 53-plus guys to be ready to go and and and we want to be smart about that, but uh I'm excited to get Christian going and and I know he's excited for this training camp. >> As far as the reps go, too, for the QBs in particular, are you going to I think you talked about this in June. Are you going to try to split them up first team by days as opposed to Kyler one series with the first team, JJ the next? Is that still the plan to have >> It's a good question, and I think um having gone through it and Flo and I basically sit down, you know, over the past month and kind of build out, you know, what we need to accomplish for our team. Um and and looking at that, it's probably not um something that we'll do by the day. It's going to be more by certain periods. What maybe a guy's gotten a little bit more third down work, so then we'll make sure we um kind of try to, you know, even it out, but I will say this, you know, and I told the quarterbacks um you know, it we we don't need to make this 50/50, you know, it it it's going to be uh that way to start when we're on kind of a time crunch, but when we get into some longer practices, there's some move the ball periods, there's some periods where uh the the amount of plays is unknown sometimes as you really start to get into what real football is. Um so there may be some where by the day it's going to be hard to really uh to really kind of quantify, okay, what exactly was it? Cuz as practices get going, it's it's not that exact science, but over the sequence of many days or as many days as we hope to have before we make a decision. Um I know we'll be thorough. I know both guys will feel like they've got an opportunity to compete, and they both know, and everybody on our team knows we're going to do what's best to give us the the best possible chance to to be a really good football team this year. >> Kevin, was there a date in your mind, and I'm I'm sure you you won't share it with us, but is there a date in your mind where this has to be decided by to like proceed to properly prepare the the quarterback for the season, Kevin? >> I think there's an ideal uh date based upon training camp uh to make sure, you know, we check a lot of boxes for our team, um but also for uh not only that player, but our entire offense. Um so, yeah, there's absolutely a date in mind, and and uh you know, subject to what we think is best. If If we feel like we can make the decision before that date, we will. If we feel like uh we need a little bit more time, we'll we'll take it. And uh ultimately, uh a lot of work's been done to this point. And been evaluated uh both on the field, uh where we think guys are at from their understanding and comfort of our offense. And now we can apply it and really try to, you know, push this thing to the point where I think it's going to enhance both players, and I think it's going to give us clarity on where we need to go for this year. >> Kevin, what day of the week is today if you know? >> I can't remember right now. >> Can I Can I ask you about the the Ravens uh Ravens joint practice? I mean, you you always have talked about how important that is, and you reiterated reiterated that today. Is Is that the time when you would want to have to know who your starter is? >> I think, you know, it's a critical point in camp for sure. Uh it's our first chance to really in a exhaustive amount of reps for for that first group to really uh go against those guys, but we still have, you know, complete full days, you know, where we're we're getting both groups the ones and twos work, situational work. Um but, you know, there's really a timeline in place that I think I don't want to say yes because you know, we want this to be the right decision when that time comes, but ideally we want to Kevin what I will tell you is we want to make sure that there is a comprehensive decision made, but the understanding that I'm well aware having gone through training camps before as a player and a coach at that position the time it takes to to truly go into week one comfortable and ready to get off to a really good start. >> The offense every quarterback that's come through here has talked about how complex and complicated the scheme is. Where would you say Kyler's comfort level is having gone through OTAs and mini camp? >> Yeah, I think he's you know, I was really impressed with his his ability in training camp to you know, we threw a lot at him and you know, you were and the off season program I should say. And now it's about there's really not going to be a lot that he's hearing for the first time. He's going to be hearing things that he's already practiced or at least you know, maybe maybe not at the full speed variety, but he's been in the huddle calling these plays. He's he's done a really nice job with that. Our offense is is maybe different than than what he's been accustomed to, but what I will say is we also want to make sure we're running an offense that's comfortable and and something where a quarterback has a lot of confidence that they can go be the best versions of themselves in this offense and there's no you know, there's a reason why you know, we make sure that there's always ability to make edits to to the playbook and and all within the understanding of the bigger picture of how we want to play. You know, you know, we want to run the football. We've we've been really excited about what that has looked like from the time we welcomed our players back in the spring and then now we get to put the pads on and really see against one of the hardest defenses in the NFL to run the football against on a daily basis. You know, that there's I think the term iron sharpens iron gets thrown around a lot, but when you're going up against Flo every day that you better be iron. That's all I know because it's going to be a really challenge a really challenging thing. >> When you make that announcement do you anticipate or make that decision do you anticipate making an official announcement to give the the guy ownership? >> Yeah, they'll they'll obviously if you guys are all right with it probably be the first to know but then yeah, this is and I hope you know, it's been as you know, apparent you know, as I've tried to make it you know, I transparency is really important within our building on things like this and but also with you guys as our connection to our fans. So yeah, there's you know, this is going to be a very when the decisions made it's going to be a very you know, a process will take place and then we'll move forward and and go try to win games. >> When you look at your defensive unit what excited you the most about being able to bring in a Jamal Adams type player? >> Yeah, that was a actually the thing that excited me the most was just again you guys will hear me talk about process but just like having the conversations with Flo and the personal staff and kind of bringing those two areas of expertise to life together and first kind of started broaching the subject of Jamal just based on the skill set and my experience with him and you know, the energy and the passion that he brings and then it started to you know, getting in again to the specific uh skill set of what he does well and then what you know, what Flo past players or the what he can um give them the freedom to do within the system and so those things aligned and I think Flo was excited about the acquisition. I know Jamal was excited about the potential and the possibility of being here and those two things came together and so to me that that's good process and then we'll see about the result but I'm really really positive about that direction. >> Couple more questions. >> Are you I'm sorry. Are you actively pursuing another pass pass rusher backup pass rusher? >> Yeah, if there's a if there's a good football out there somewhere we're actively discussing it and pursuing it and then finding ways to improve our roster every day of the week, every every day of the month, and every every day between, you know, now and the trade deadline and the end of the season. >> Is there a guy out there? >> There's always good football players out there, for sure. >> Well, what was your perception of Kyler just competing against him as much as you guys did out west? >> Um listen, he was the number one pick for a reason. Um it's not just about what he can what he can do with his arm and we all know that he can operate on schedule and I was excited about the potential of seeing him in this system and then um how we're going to complement it with the run game, but um rarely do things go as planned in in the National Football League and so it's the it's the extension uh of the play and what he can do um you know, what he can do in in that arena, you know, when he can create as well. >> Hey Kevin, how do you think about the conversation about his play style and system and the good fit between >> Yeah, I think um he's always been an accurate passer um especially when um when you study him, you know, the rhythm of the game, when he's in that rhythm and and and you feel this command uh of his ability to throw completions and move the team and and then, you know, you do feel you you don't have to watch his tape very long to feel that uh play extension and and the ability to, you know, not only steal some first downs with his legs, but uh he can he can go get a lot more than that and and I think the key with that is he's learned and as guys learn throughout their their career, no matter their skill sets, you know, it's about uh it's about maximizing each play with an intent on uh you know, what is the outcome that we're looking for, what has schematically been designed, um but then it's uh on top of that, my ability to extend and and maybe create the play beyond the scheme, which is always a good thing. Uh but then there's the negative outcomes, whether it's guys getting hurt or turning the football over. You know, we know some of the things that are critical to us winning. You know, really since uh since I've been fortunate enough to be the head coach here, and the quarterback position plays uh a huge role in that because they're the guy that uh commands the offense. They've got the ball in their hands making decisions with the football. And Kyler has demonstrated, you know, throughout his career that that he's got a the ability to do that at a high level. And and I think it's the consistency factor of of what we're looking for. But then I think it's also understanding he's got a pretty darn good group of players around him in that huddle. And uh you know, he's simply doing his job and and the effectiveness of doing that consistently uh has proven to be a really good thing for guys that have played in the system. >> Last one for Kevin over here. >> Guys, has anything changed with Harrison Smith and where you guys stand with him? Is that still an open door if he's interested you guys have any clarity there on on the >> Yeah, you know, I would just say I spoke to him recently. Um just like, you know, I always do and we had a great conversation. Nothing has really changed. Um but there was never an expectation, at least on my end or or our end, I I believe that now would be the time we would really um you know, dive into that and and we'll continue to have dialogue with him and and keep you guys updated as as, you know, if there were to be anything come about with that. >> Thanks, everybody. >> Thank you.

text: How you doing, coach? I guess I'm very excited right now. I'm ready for it. >> With the seventh pick in the 2007 NFL Draft, the Minnesota Vikings select Adrian Peterson, running back, Oklahoma. >> [applause] >> You know, just super excited for the opportunity. So, it was like a dream, a dream had came true. >> Adrian Peterson, running back, Oklahoma. >> You know, my dad was the one who put the ball in my hand, my mom, all the sacrifices she made to help me get to that moment. [music] You know, my coach was there and you know, he was the one that convinced me when I was in high school to really get back into football cuz I had kind of got off track and I was just going to focus on on on track. Just having all those people who really impacted my life uh was really special. >> On offense, the day belonged to Adrian Peterson. >> Oh, man, it felt amazing. >> Who began his NFL career with a bang, rushing for a team record 103 yards in his debut. >> Here you are, your first NFL game at home and ironically, my first touchdown of my career was a receiving touchdown, which [music] I never would have thought that in a million years. And a great pass by Tarvaris Jackson. >> And Jackson's back to pass, big rush, right flat, Peterson caught 35, runs through the DEFENSE AND HE'S GONE! 20, 10, TOUCHDOWN, ADRIAN PETERSON! >> I wish there was a view where you can see the face the face of the coaches cuz I kind of bobbled the ball a lot and end up hauling it in and and taking off, but it It something very special. It went for 60 yards. >> You know, I knew you know, Chester Taylor was a heck of a back man and >> [music] >> he was a great leader. Our offensive line, they were doing incredible incredible job blocking up up front. And it was me. Like I was missing holes. I was too fast on on certain plays. Those guys just were like they didn't give me no crap or anything like that. They were just like, "Hey, just keep on to keep on plugging. Keep on plugging. We're going to hit. We're going to hit." >> HE BREAKS THE TACKLE AND ADRIAN PETERSON IS LOOSE. HE HAS SCORED A 65-YARD TOUCHDOWN. THERE HE GOES INSIDE THE 20. TOUCHDOWN! >> YOU COULD feel it. You could feel it, right? The greatest rushing performance in the history of the National Football League. >> Sure enough, man. Came out the second half and we exploded. Touchdown Adrian Peterson, his second of the game. >> I remember I was talking to Peyton Manning and uh he was like, "Adrian, man, you know, I knew that [music] you were going to do something really spectacular in the game because throughout the week I just kind of sat back and [music] watched you. And when I would go and be working out in the weight room, you were in there working out hard as heck. You were locked in and you had a good possibility of of winning the the MVP." >> Peterson with 129 yards rushing, second most in the history of the Pro Bowl. >> It was fun, man. It was a great experience for me to go in my first year for Pro Bowl and win the Pro Bowl MVP. That's all it took for me to really lock in and and go after that. >> Congratulations, Adrian. [cheering] >> The guy was just great, great hands, ran awesome routes. Like I said, if it happens, it'll happen. It'll happen, but don't focus on it. >> And that was the moment I knew that, dang, I was so close to breaking it and didn't even realize it. So, in my mind, I feel like I crushed the record. You know, when you think about coming off the ACL injury, you know, everything that transpired throughout the season, you know, to be 9 yards short from a record that still stands to this day, uh was pretty special within itself. You know, so for me, I broke it in my mind, you know, so on paper and in the record books, it's still there and it it it'll sit there until someone breaks it, [music] but for me, I crushed it. >> Okay, you lose for being a big guy here. >> Let's get it. You know, winning the NFL MVP, it doesn't get any better than that. It goes to show that, you know what, you are the best. It's kind of self-explanatory. Who knows, God's willing, maybe one of my boys will break it. Bro.

title: Jamal Adams Projected Role On Minnesota Vikings Defense
text: The Vikings added Jamal Adams to their defense. How much does this even move the needle? >> You are Locked On Vikings, your daily Minnesota Vikings podcast, part of the Locked On Network, your team every day. >> What's going on everybody? Welcome to the Locked On Vikings podcast, where we're always trying to learn something new. Today's episode is brought to you by Kshi. For a limited time, download the Kali app and use code locked on to get up to $500 in bonus credits with credit credits when you trade 25. Today we got some news. Was going to be a mailbag today. I've decided let's do the mailbag tomorrow. So, you can still get more questions in. Uh Google's form is in the show notes. If you have questions about Jamal Adams or anything else, uh hit me with them and I will answer them tomorrow on a delayed mailbag. But for now, let's let's do the Jamal Adams thing. So, the Vikings added a player. This is the veteran edition. We kind of all saw one coming. Maybe there's still more coming, but especially in what I'll call the secondary, whether he's a safety or a linebacker, it's a whole thing. We'll get to it. But, uh, the addition to the defense, right? Veteran addition to the defense is part of it. And I thought they kind of needed one offball linebacker, which is what Jamal Adams played last year, was probably the last place that they really needed to like inject something. But even there, you had a very clear top four on the roster. You had Blake Hashman, Eric Wilson, Jake, uh, Ivan Pace, and then really only undrafted guys. By the way, they did uh, release a couple and had like a waved injured kind of situation for a couple of people. Kelly Lawson and Luke Weissong, two of the undrafted free agents, uh, have been waved. Weissong has a non- football injury designation. And then they also added Kijijan Owens to the non-Out injury list with an illness, non- football illness list. He's on the active NFI, which means uh, that they expect him to come back at some point. So, that one's not as much of a roster transaction, but Kelly Lawson out, Jamal Adams in, call that like a linebacker switch up, and then they also uh release Luke Weissong. So, there's a little bit more room on the roster for like other stuff. But this isn't the edge rusher, Hassan Reic type guy that we've all kind of been waiting on. But it might be if you see him as a safety like he was for a lot of his career, the injection of a little bit more talent for the room that we don't know if we're getting Harrison Smith back and Theo Jackson and Jay Ward are like competing for a job. You got Matelis and it's this like weird group. I've been kind of concerned about it like all off season. Um, and and maybe Jamal Adams slots in there, but that would be to me a surprise because he hasn't been there for a long long long time. Jamal Adams's story here in the NFL really ended in 2020 and he has been on pause ever since. He's missed two years, the vast majority of two years with injury. Uh, the other three years he's been rotational player in last year in Las Vegas for the Raiders. He was healthy for all 17 games. He was questionable once, but ultimately active for that game. And he played 448, I think is the number snaps for the from the the Star Tribune article on this. That's we're doing Levi Drake Rodriguez numbers. Actually, that's less than Levi Drake Rodriguez, who was not healthy fully for last year. He actually missed a whole game. So it extrapolated to 17, the gap would even be greater. So this is certainly not your uh late 2010s Jamal Adams. This is a different package. And and I'm so glad we had that conversation yesterday about name recognition because name recognition will steer you wrong here. And I have a feeling that the instant reaction from a lot of kind of more shoot by the hip types of analysts, probably more in the national world. I have a feeling that that most of the the local Vikings people are going to be a little more measured. They tend to be, but I have a feeling I'm going to see national people start to go crazy about Brian Flores, Blitz Guy, getting this Blitz guy from Jamal Adams. That's not quite the role as we as as he has played it lately. Jamal Adams has 22 pressures over the last five years. A lot of that's injury. Some I mean he's missed so-called the last three years cuz that's about the amount. That's a thousand snaps still. Like that's still like a really solid amount of time. 22 pressures. You are not a blitz guy. Yeah, that is a I mean we we are talking at best free safety, you know, playing back numbers and he has played at linebacker. He has lined up mostly in that second level of the defense pretty exclusively and it's been that way for a long time. He has been a linebacker. Don't think of him as a safety.
