I'll open up for questions. >> How much uh different or based on everything training camp last year went are you changing anything this year besides like the extra joint practices or you just kind of running everything kind of very similarly? >> Acclamation period is very similar. I think it's important to acclimate these guys. Uh it's a unique setting the way training camp's structured. You go from a extended break right into football activity. And so uh we all have to be really smart with how we progress these guys and it's a team level and an individual level. And so once we get through that then we get through get into uh you know the meat of training camp, the padded practices and all that and we got to push oursel in that in that phase. And so um there'll be a lot of points of emphasis in there as far as the situational football and the themes that we're you know looking at. And then from that standpoint, once we kind of go through that phase, then we get into this awesome opportunity, which is essentially three joint practices and two uh two preseason games within, you know, about a 10day window there. So, that'll be a great evaluation opportunity for us, and then the back end, we we finish it off and get get our eyes towards the regular season. >> The team got the restructured deal with Chimera done. How important was that and how important will it be to this [clears throat] offense this year? >> Fired up, excited. Um Alvin means a lot to our organization. U this community obviously um these things sometimes take a little bit of time just kind of work through and um Alvin was great about the whole process. I think communication was was really good for everyone and um you know the conversation we were able to have you know certainly over the summer I think was great and [snorts] um I think we're we're in a good spot. I think this rainback room has a ton of talent. It's a really talented group. I'm excited to let training camp takes its course to define roles and opportunities but um it's going to be a great group for us. much of that Alvin Chimera decision-m process that went on this whole off season was you guys evaluating whether there was a role for him on this team or have you always like while installing your playbook, you know, had something in vision? >> Yeah, I think that's a fair observation. I think uh you're always looking for a role for guys and I think sometimes getting a chance to evaluate where our roster's at and who we have on the roster and how this thing's developing uh allows us to take a little bit of time to do that the right way. And um and there's a little financial part obviously that you know the business side had to take care of and so uh I thought it was a really good process. You know we didn't anticipate necessarily Alvin doing as much in OTAAS um you know so that kind of gives us a little bit of time to see some of these other guys and see how this would uh fit in this equation and so we all feel really good about it. >> You make adjustments now though like knowing for sure that he's here. I mean because he's such a unique type of player did you already have everything that was going to be installed or are there now different packages? I I think that's uh an ongoing process. I think early in training camp is, you know, still, you know, installation, so to speak. You're kind of teaching systems, getting guys comfortable. I think where you get into the player specific opportunities come a little later in training camp. And I think that's where certainly we will be excited to, you know, have those exploration phases when you have the running back room that we have. And so, um, I think, you know, we feel good about the roles and the opportunities that will be presented to these guys. >> Get it done before camp and I guess you can even throw Cam in there getting it done in June. Like knowing those issues, if you want to call them that or resolve, what does that do for you as a coaching staff now? And all that, >> anytime there's definition, um, allows us to build plans. Um, it's the NFL. There's always a million moving pieces. That's just inevitable. This these rosters are always moving. But, uh, Cam, Alvin, they're really talented players. They mean a lot to this organization. They mean a lot to this community. They do things the right way. And so, um, we're excited to have both those guys. >> You guys been able to go out and get another running back, couple tight ends, few receivers. Um, how much does the offense does does the offense change? Does it expand or is it kind of making it all the same stuff? Are you window dress it different? Like what's what's the difference going forward? I >> think there's more variables for us in a positive way. Um certainly we've been able to feel that just being around OTAAS and seeing the tight end room that we have, the running back room that we have. Um I think it's just going to be exciting to kind of build that as we go. You know, certainly there's things that we already feel comfortable um you know, kind of diving into. There'll be things that I think that's the exciting part of training camp is you get to kind of evolve. you know, uh, OTAAS is a awesome opportunity for us to get better as a football team and individuals, but it's not real football yet, you know, and we're a little closer to real football, which is an exciting part, but that's where you kind of get to, you know, um, get a better feel for it. >> So, going into camp obviously knowing who the quarterback is going to be as opposed to last year benefits that >> um, yeah, I think just continuity. There's only so many reps. You know, you just think about that. Um, you know, we got 10 installation practices and then we're playing Jacksonville in a joint practice. Uh, there's only so many reps and so anytime you can have more defined roles, it allows guys to work with the guys that you anticipate working, you know, come September. And so I think that's a huge advantage. >> To that point, Mickey just praised Tyler's uh initiative and race to be better. We talked about him and a lot of pass catchers going to the West Coast with Drew. What did you think about that? What was your appreciation with seeing that? Yeah, I think it's just a awesome leadership example of what our football team looks like. Um certainly, you know, Tyler gets a lot of uh the lead on this thing, but for guys to want to go do things together, spend time together, do the extra work, uh that means a lot. You know, it's the right kind of guys. It's it's a special group of guys. They know um we did a lot of good work in OTAAS, but to steal a few more days in the summer obviously is a huge benefit. And then we just got to keep it moving. Colin, what did you learn about your team offseason program? And what do you like about this team going into training camp? I'd >> say they competed really well, connected really well. Uh they've put in a lot of time. Um second offseason is always going to be better uh just because of the continuity and the expectations are more aligned and everyone understands what to expect. Um but I felt like it was a good good program. It put us in good position. Now we obviously have to do the the real football part moving forward. What do you think of the chemistry that Chris and Tyler developed last year through obviously they're very successful together and and [clears throat] what excites you the most about how they can kind of keep developing that chemistry this year? >> I just say they've done an awesome job, you know, continuing what they built on late last year. Um Chris had a phenomenal season. I thought Tyler finished off strong. That continuity is obviously a huge asset. You look at a lot of these top quarterbacks in this league, they got consistent guys around them. them a lot of times that they can, you know, lean on and anticipate throws to these guys because they've spent so much time with them. And so, um, they're just continuing to build. They're continuing to grow. Um, good job during OTAAS. Offseason's been good. Now, you know, now we're into training camp mode. with the continuity that you have going from last year to this year and kind of the groundwork now that you have with the offense and defense, do you anticipate using more opportunity or or rather uh what do you anticipate the the sort of role of things like unscripted practices or unscripted sessions this year? >> Yeah, once you get through the initial stage, it becomes more free flowing. Uh those joint practices obviously are good evaluations. You know, we kind of view this almost as like four stages. training camp is uh there's the acclamation phase. There's kind of the compete stage, you know, or the, you know, the competitive stage where we got to go um you know, push push oursel, you know, training camp's going to be a little bit uncomfortable for everyone. That's just how it is. And then you get to go, you know, evaluate yourself against, you know, really good talented teams in these joint practices. And then after that, we kind of come back for a couple weeks to start moving our eyes to the regular season. So, um I feel like it's a good formula. How do you guys manage like the expectations now? Like some people are picking you on big platforms like do a lot of stuff. Tyler's got a lot of expectations. How do you guys manage that this year? >> It's part of the NFL. Uh you much rather have that than the other side of these things. And so uh that's that's the that's what we all want. That's what we all uh expect. And so um you know, you understand the NFL season takes its course and there's highs and lows. And I think the most important thing is that the guys just focus on the task at hand. Get better each and every day. Um, you know, we'll get to the regular season when we get to that. That's still feels a long ways away. So, um, we got some really good work ahead of oursel and if we just keep our eyes on that and focused on that, getting better, everything else will take care of itself. >> Feel that shift at all? I mean, do do you kind of recognize that expectations are higher here than maybe it was a year ago, at least from the outside? >> I I don't know. Um, every season it's the NFL. I mean, everyone everyone has the same goals and aspirations in many ways. Um, we want to be NFC South champs. Like that's our goal, you know, and then ultimately obviously we want to play February 14th. Um, I think a lot of people have shared that uh in all 32 teams, you know, the last couple days. Uh, we're all shooting for the same goals and now it's about what you do each and every day and uh the preparation you make and you know, once the regular season comes, there's a lot of things that come into that that factor into it. How do you balance um you just looked at the caution and the management you all have been doing with Jordan Tyson versus like >> making sure he's ready to go, you know, and and he doesn't have any ground to make up by the time you all get to week one. >> I just think Jordan's done an awesome job through this whole process. Every guy's in a different stage. Again, our objective is to be as healthy as we can in training going into training camp and then build from there. And so, uh, an acclamation phase, um, we all have to get acclimated over the next few days to get ourselves ready to play real football, which is, um, trying to remember the date, um, August 3rd. I think August 3rd is our first padded practice. So, um, we got to build our guys up for that opportunity. And so, I think Jordan's done a nice job. He'll continue to, uh, be able to play play football and keep, uh, building up the right way. And you know, all these guys, you know, there'll be a few guys from whether it's medical or older players that, hey, we, you know, manage them just a touch, but these guys are all ready to roll. >> What do you What do you anticipate his management will look like? Will I mean, will he be out there as early as this week doing more than >> Yeah, I I think we'll see him playing football tomorrow. So, he'll be ready to go and um you know, we'll just build him up as we go, like any player. I mean, he didn't do a ton during OTAA, so we got to build him up the right way just like we will all these other guys. >> Similar with Chris, or is Chris even more ready to do more early? I >> think the same thing as far as just building someone up. I mean, Chris is in a great spot. Um, he's doing an awesome job and so he'll be ready. >> What about Kendrick Miller not to land on PUP coming off that tournament? Yeah. Like, how's he doing and what's it say about him that, you know, he didn't have to go on that at all? >> Yeah, credit to him. Um those are long long journeys when you come off an injury like he had. Uh credit for him, our trainers, everyone who he's worked with to uh work really really hard to put him in position to go compete for a job in August. And so you feel great about that and u yeah I think he's going to do some really good things. >> Hey Kell, are there any areas that you feel like you got better at at since last season? Something that you've improved on as a coach? Personally, um I think you're always just trying to get better. It's as simple as that. Uh no matter what stage you're at, uh every year you're going to do you're going to have things you like, things you don't like. Every meeting you're going to have things you like that you presented, don't like that you presented, and it's just about getting better. And uh I just love the offseason that we had. Um because of the continuity and the consistency that we had that we were able to really dig deep into what our season looked like last year. uh things that you know both positively and things you got to improve on. And then you also get to study, you know, what the league looks like because ultimately you're competing against 31 other teams. And so you got to see where they're at and what what they're doing and uh how can we grow as a football team. >> Kellen, it seems like uh Tyler has really embraced the role as the leader of the team, especially now that he knows he's the starter. >> How do you expect that to show up during training camp? How how does he lead this team through these next several weeks? >> Yeah, I think, you know, Tyler's one example. I think for a lot of our guys, it's it's the leadership that you need. Uh these are days where we're going to we have to build this thing up the right way and we got to push oursel through uncomfortable things. These guys haven't worn pads in a while. And so, you know, when you get to pads, like there's an acclamation, there's a getting used to, okay, the pad level, the physicality that this game requires and we have to keep going. And so, uh, you know, Tyler's a great example of everything that he's brought to this this offseason has been excellent. You know, from an offensive perspective. He'll continue to evolve as as a leader of that group and his communication and his ability to play at the line of scrimmage. That'll all be a growth growth opportunity this training camp. >> How much clearer would you say the vision of an identity is for either offense or defense? Really, the full team just going into this second year? Yeah, I think uh you know time invested together um going back to last year but then you know this offseason I think our guys really have embraced uh you know the adjustments that you want to make and so uh I think our guys know what we need to do. We we know we did not start fast. We know we got to run the football better. We know we got to be more consistent stopping the run you know week in and week out. Um we know that you know situational football is such an important part of this. you know, the margins are really tight and these end of game situations we got to master and so I think we understand where we need to go and uh we just got to get there. >> And how would you describe when you think about where the identity is that you're starting camp with? What would you describe that identity as for this team? >> Yeah, I think our team just realizes, you know, we want to play smart, fast, and physical. You know, that hasn't changed that that's a play style that we want to play with. But, um, what the schematics look like, I thought we did an excellent job. OTAA is building a foundation. And I think a big part of what we're doing is, you know, we're just continuing to go from OTAAS. This isn't a, you know, start at step one and, you know, go back through, you know, the baby steps like our OTAAS was a great growth summer. The expectation was you grew individually and then we just keep going. And so, um, that's where you gain momentum when you, you know, invest that much time into it. the end of last season. Do you feel like you reached kind of the those pillars smart, fast, physical? Like was it all kind of what you that identity that you wanted to see? >> Yeah, I feel like we're we're playing cleaner football. Um you know, I think we needed to play smarter football. Um you know, the penalties and the situational football got better. Um obviously we spent a lot of time investing in that and then uh you know, the play style of being physical, being able to run the football more efficiently, being able to stop the run, you know. Um, I think we have some great examples of that late in the year. And then, uh, fast is just about these guys just playing confident and free. And, uh, I think our guys, you know, we we're finding that as we go. >> I guess just to spin it forward, like is there like one of the three that you're really trying to hammer home this year or like right now? Kind of like I'd like to see like our physicality in the run game for instance or something like that. >> I think I think all of it. Um, yeah. >> Saw Josh Hill officially listed with the tight ends. Are there any other staff movements, configurations that have changed at all? >> I don't think anything new. Uh, obviously Will Clap would be our one main [clears throat] addition. Uh, him coming over during the offseason, but uh, yeah, Josh Josh has been kind of around it, you know, a lot of last year. Uh, you know, kind being in the personnel department, but starting to evolve into the coaching side of this thing. And so, u, Josh is special. He's he's one of the best all time. um great example for our players to see a guy his career and then uh his transition. I think he's awesome for these guys. >> You mentioned starting fast or or wanting to start faster this year. What are some of the things that you can do in are there things that you can do in training camp to kind of help get you ready for that? Is that the thing you got to wait for? >> No. Uh mindset mentality. Right now we're in the installation process. So, it's about, you know, the mindset mentality and getting used to like we got to start practice fast and then there'll be certain periods and situations as training camp evolves where we put a little bit more focus on it. And then, you know, there's plenty of stuff I've done through the offseason where you're trying to study just the the data and the scheme and all that sort of stuff of how we can do a better job here. >> Kool-Aid recently made a comment about he thinks this offense is going to be very explosive, but also his excitement to try to shut them down during training camp. Just from a coaching perspective, how do you sort of bal like I'm sure you don't want one side of the ball just beating up the [laughter] other. Like how do you >> one side has a good day, are you worried about like what's that balance? >> That's how training camp is. Uh >> one side wins, so one side loses and they're both on your side at the end of the day. So uh >> yeah, I think I think the goal at the end day of training camp is um it's an opportunity for these players to learn and grow. So um not expecting it to be perfect. I'm expecting, you know, them to have good moments and I'm expecting them to test their boundaries and uh make a mistake and um you know, I think that's an important part of what training camp is. And uh you know, so just like you know, during the day, I think at the end day, you hope that there's days or periods where offense does well, then defense does well, then offense does well, then defense does well. Same thing in special teams when you rep those periods that u one side is, you know, successful and then the other side re re uh responds the right way. And so, um, that's just what you're looking for. >> Maybe the benefit of having so many joint practices that kind of get a measuring stick where it's not just your guys. >> Yeah, I think it'll be good. It'll be change of environment, change of scenery, so to speak. Um, second off seasonason, so I think our team's more ready for it. And, uh, you'll get some different looks, different personnel, different presentations. Again, a lot of it goes back to getting your starters and that first group really ready to play football. um come you know whatever the second week of September >> that conversation around the league sorry >> sorry did you have any like special message for the team you talked to the team meeting any point of interest >> I think I think the biggest thing is just you know we have a plan let's let's execute the plan um you know we've we've put a lot of work into this thing we've u put oursel in excellent position coming off of otaas in the the summer and now it's about um really focusing on this training camp the season will you know, eventually, you know, we got to get better and we got to focus on this plan and we got to have purpose with it and we got to we got to test oursel. Uh, you know, training camp, you know, when you're in me and training camp, it's going to be hot and humid and there's going to be some adverse uh elements in that. Um, also putting pads on, that's an adverse element when you haven't done it for a while. And so, we got to be comfortable being uncomfortable a little bit and push our boundaries a little bit and that the joint practice will lead into that as well. You mentioned that um you had some players obviously have to manage their reps in camp for age or whatever reason. Is Eric McCoy one of those players coming off those two those injuries? >> I think any guy that's I'm going say eight plus years. I mean they've played a lot of football in the NFL and so you're always going to be uh smart with those guys. Uh everyone's on different trajectory through training camp as far as where we're building them to. Um some guys are obviously going to be competing at a high level through training camp. some guys are getting ready for, you know, early September. And so, um, you know, Eric's done an awesome job, uh, through this whole offseason program. He's in an excellent spot. He's, you know, we'll probably have to make sure he's, uh, you know, maintain this thing the right way and so he's ready to go. With >> all the kind of conversation and emphasis around the multi-tight end sets around the NFL, [clears throat] what are you hoping to see from your room here throughout training camp? >> Yeah, I'm just excited to let those guys compete and uh, you know, they'll define the roles. they we'll sort it all out. We got a really talented group. Uh I think we got seven tight ends and we love all seven of them. They and they've all they're all, you know, tight ends that can play on Sundays uh this fall and so we're excited to let those guys all compete and um you know it's a trend uh to play with multiple tight ends. Um it's an asset and we'll just continue to see how that goes. >> Does that kind of clock into what you were talking about with the uh multiple like more variables and things like that? Is that position where you can really maximize? Yeah, I I think that's a really talented group, very versatile group. Uh when you talk about the traits that those guys have and the ability they have to, you know, not only play like an inline tight end, but play in the back field, play split out. Uh I think that's where the power of that position comes up when you have guys that can uh line up in a number of different ways. >> Kelly, because it's been a focus of yours since you got here, just curious team building activities. What's the schedule look like? What's coming up? >> Yeah. Um, training camp's really about getting ready for football. Uh, you know, we'll still have a couple items, but um, you know, OTAAS, we kind of utilize a little bit more time for that. And then training camp, we'll still have a couple opportunities to kind of spend time. I think a lot of what training camp creates is a day where guys are just around each other a lot. And u, so it's a lot more organic as far as spending time together. You know, when you practice in the morning, you have a little idle time before meetings in the afternoon, these lunches, these dinners. We got a great cafeteria here, so guys get to hang around and it's perfect. >> You was saying that for the team you guys want to be next [clears throat] season that like your young guys are going to have to make a leap. And I'm wondering I I know that like is the case for every team across the NFL, but just curious of like after the season you guys had is that an emphasis for you? Are you excited to see it? What's kind of your mindset going into trying to have these guys take the next step? >> Yeah. Um, I just say everyone has to grow. Um, everyone has to, whether you played last year or didn't play, you got to get better during training camp, you got to be ready to go. And I'd say from a big picture perspective, there's always, you know, people sometimes call the second year jump. You know, those guys who um, play last year as rookies, that rookie year, some of these rookies are going through it now. You go right from your season right into the combine training, right into the draft. OTAAS's summer, they get a couple weeks and they're right in the season. There's a lot going on. And then those guys who come back after that first season, it's like, all right, I got a whole off seasonason to like kind of train myself, get into the system. I'm not learning a bunch of new stuff. I'm building off of what I learned my rookie year. And so, um, I think that that goes for a lot of >> When there is a trend like the the 310 end thing, like are you looking at everything the Rams do like their run game behind it, like all the duo stuff? Like, is it is it all of it? and do you kind of just see what pieces fit? Like how do you adopt something like that? >> Yeah, usually you're going to try and watch a number of teams um you know in those spaces. Um you know studied a lot of league I think studied as much of the league this year as ever which has been a lot of fun I think for our coaching staff on on in all three phases. Um you I think we've studied football really really diligently and so uh the Rams have made headlines for 13 personnel uh get it. they had had a ton of success and you know the numbers obviously you know show that a lot of other teams that did it and you know maybe slightly different ways and so you're kind of constantly trying to look at you know what can probably be best implemented for our football team and tying it together and so um yeah I think it's been a lot of fun. Are you married to like a very specific way of doing things or are you kind of open-minded like a new idea can open new things up? Like some people have their system and then other people are like adaptable and change like how do you >> uh I think I've called plays in [snorts] five systems now. So uh I like to say I'm pretty bilingual in uh football languages. So um you know I think it's important to be able to adapt and adjust while still being defined, you know. And I think that's always the balancing act. And I'm not going to say, you know, it was perfect every every year that I've ever coached. Uh, we've had good years. We've had years where we probably could have done a better job of that. And so, um, I think the flexibility is important for us. And I'm I'm excited with where our roster is at, with the type of players we have, with the versatility that that's going to provide, kind of let training camp, uh, take its course, and then define what those roles look like moving forward. >> How different do you expect your offense to look this year compared to last year? I think you're always trying to evolve. Every year should look a little different. Uh I think that's an important part. Every every top offense is evolving every year because uh the defense has spent the whole offseason looking at all those same offensive trends, too. So, uh they figured out which teams stop those trends. They're going to focus on that as well. And so, uh it's just a fun back and forth in this league. >> And you do do you see that similarly for like Brandon Staley of his defense and how that changes from year to year? for sure. Um, again, there's teams that, you know, trust me, everyone's watched Seattle's defense. Uh, everyone spent a lot of time looking at that that defense and that structure because they had so much success this year. And the year before, you know, everyone watched, you know, our the Philly film on defense and Vic Fangio and those those type of defenses. And so, um, everyone's just trying to grow and learn. Everyone's trying to be the best that they at their profession. And so because of that, you just got to keep growing. >> We saw Sanker and the star y >> throughout the spring. I mean, is now that camp is here, do you experiment with putting different guys there to see different looks or do you want how are you kind of approaching? >> The goal is to get Yonas as much exposure there as we can. Uh his versatility obviously is a huge asset. He played on the back end and played really well there. Um there'll be other guys that have to play star as well. Uh that's just inevitably what training camp and preseason looks like and so um we'll train plenty of guys there. >> Mason Tipton, is that the groin injury he suffered in January that's been limiting him all? >> No, it's an offseason thing. He had a tibia. >> So yeah, surprises good or bad condition? >> No. Uh no, I thought our guys did an excellent job. Um I thought our guys did an awesome job. Ted does a great job through the OTAAS and then kind of giving these guys action plan and vision for what um you know the conditioning test is going to look like and so I thought our guys knocked it out. I mean they were out they were outside and uh it was great. >> Uh Mickey mentioned Xavian Harris might not be too long. You do envision him participating during this training camp >> potentially. I think uh yeah we'll see we'll see where it goes. >> Um but you also saw that there were a few players who caught up and travel. Do you have any clarity on who isn't here yet? Yeah, there's just a couple guys. Um, everyone we view as they're a part of this. You know, there's just a little bit of traveling. So, Justin Reed will be here shortly and Hunter Deckers. So, but it's not really noteworthy. They'll be fine. >> They're just having Connor go back and forth. >> Yeah, they're just Yeah. [laughter] >> You want to spend a certain amount of time outside? You talking about pushing the team. >> Is there a certain goal you have at all? >> The goal is to be outside as much as we can. Um I think outside of one practice we have allocated for inside like pre pre-allocated everything else the goal will be outside and um we'll adjust you know we understand weather's going to be an element of this um I feel like you know we were probably fortunate last year I feel like August wasn't quite as hot as maybe the uh the usual and so um we'll make adjustments here and there you know if we pop in a little bit maybe we start practice inside and then transition out or if we have to um you know let the weather dictate whether we can be outside or not. So we just we follow kind of the rules and the parameters of that. >> Big hit with the players last year with the uh focus on recovery built into the schedule and kind of those gaps and things that do you anticipate that remaining this year or yeah any adjustments? >> Daily schedule's very similar. >> Did have surgery on this? >> Uh yeah, he just had an offseason deal. So he's just working through it still. Just make sure we say that correctly. There was a surgery that was part of All good. >> Thanks, coach. [laughter] at least. >> Yeah.

title: What We're Watching From Jordyn Tyson at Saints Training Camp
text: As we're recording this, we are 16 hours and 23 minutes away from the official start of training camp, which means we are 16 hours and 23 minutes 22 minutes now away from seeing Jordan Addison on the field, not for the first time, but for the second time. We saw him for a brief moment in rookie mini camp. He did some stuff out there, but that he's been on the shelf since then and it sounds like if we're taking Kellen Moore at his word, then we're going to see Jordan Addison doing football stuff tomorrow. Now, this is the acclimation period of training camp and this team does ease into things. I don't think we're going to see a ton of reps tomorrow. It'll probably be a set. I was looking at it earlier today. There there weren't a ton of passes on the first day of camp and it takes them a little bit of of of time to build up as this team is very sports science based, but Jordan Addison is going to be out there and I think that's number one on the watch list. The the thing we're all waiting to see. I think that's the guy that probably hasn't even been talked about enough this offseason because it's been a little bit of a weird ramping up process for him, but we're finally going to see him on the field. We're finally going to see the top 10 pick and we're going to be able to finally start thinking and envisioning what this offense is going to look like with him on one side of the field, Chris Olave on the other, maybe both of them on the same side of the field or one on the outside and one on the slot or maybe one on the outside and one in the backfield or one motioning out of the backfield into the slot and doing all this stuff that they're going to be able to do with two top tier wide receivers on this team and man, that is very exciting. We haven't seen that type of offense since Mike Thomas, Willie Snead, Brandon Cooks. I mean, this is a different day for these guys and you can have a different day too if you drive up to Matt Bowers and buy a new car cuz this video is presented by him, so you should do that if you're looking for one. But, this offense I I think it's going to be off and running and that that's that's one of the top guys to enter the league since I don't even know. Malik Nabers is is maybe on that list. He's on that list. I mean, going back to 2021, I think there's maybe five or six guys that have entered the league with a better pedigree than Jordan Tyson. And if you set the injuries aside, I think you could argue that his tape is as good as anybody that's come into the NFL. And now you're adding that piece to the offense, and I I just want to see what Kellen Moore has in vision for him. But not just him. I want to get a good look at Oscar Dolph. I think that's a guy that's on my high up on my watch list. I don't know if I'm pinning a lot on him in this season, but moving forward from this season, I I think he's a guy that can be a foundational piece of this offense. I want to see what Deonte Hardy can do now that he has a full off-season in the system. He got banged up a little bit in mini camp, but I don't think that's going to be a problem for him. He should be off and running, and then that battle behind them. And then how do AK and HN combine together? What is the vision for both of those guys? David Edwards is on the team. Like there is a lot of reasons to be really excited about this training camp, and I'm not fit to do the math right now, but I think it's 16 hours and 20 minutes away. I can't wait to see what this thing's going to look like tomorrow. It's going to be the start of the story. There is so much optimism around this team. It hasn't felt good here since Drew Brees had that flat jacket on and was trying to win one last game. And this is this feels different. We're going to see if it lives up to the hype, but it's a new day for the Saints. You saw it in those press conferences today. I think that there are just good feelings around this team. Tyler Shucks out there. He's going to be doing his thing. Uh very exciting time to be a a observer of this team. We're going to have all the coverage on New Orleans.football. If you're not signed up for the site, training camp, one word, 20% off your first payment. Get locked in. We're going to have the breakdowns. We have throw charts up there. We're diagramming everything. It's coverage you're not going to get anywhere else. Um and I'm excited to get going on it. So, we'll talk to you tomorrow.

title: Kellen Moore On Continuing to Build Success in Year 2
text: We just got done hearing from Kellen Moore and it sounds like he's feeling good heading into year two. He's got the first year behind him. He's been able to go out and collect some players for his team on offense. And now the defense has another year in Brandon Staley's system. And it just feels like this team's really getting ready to hit the ground running and you could just hear it from Kellen all throughout this. Now, the thing that stands out most to me is if you go back and you watch him in the training camp pre-press conference last year to the one right now, it feels like almost a completely different person. He's confident, he's feeling good. I think his team's feeling good. And you just see him ready to maybe take this to the next level in year two. So, fascinating to see on that. He hit on a ton of topics here, some stuff about Jordan Tyson, where the offense is going, and how he plans on in his words to keep building this thing heading in the year two. >> Excited to be back. Excited for this opportunity to kind of get training camp started here in Medary. We got an awesome setup here obviously being able to stay in house and the the fields and the setup for the fans and it's it's a really cool opportunity for us. We're excited to have the fans here again throughout this entire process. Couple roster moves. Again, I think Mickey had a lot of these. Pups, Mason Tipton. Keshawn Silver's NFIs, Zavian Harris and Cody Hardy. And then we did make one other roster move later today with Mike Reed being signed a corner. And then Binnie Bishop being the the move there. Everyone else is available and ready to go and so uh we're ready to rock and roll. I'll open it up for questions. >> How much different or based on everything training camp last year when are you are you changing anything this year besides like the extra joint practices or you just kind of running everything kind of very similar to what >> Acclimation period is very similar. I think it's important to acclimate these guys. It's a unique setting the way training camp's structured. You go from a extended break right into football activity and so we all have to be really smart with how we progress these guys and that's a team level and an individual level. And so, once we get through that, then we get through get into you know, the meat of training camp, the padded practices and all that. And we got to push ourselves in that in that phase. And so, um there'll be a lot of points of emphasis in there as far as the situational football and the themes that we're, you know, looking at. And then from that standpoint, once we kind of go through that phase, then we get into this awesome opportunity, which is essentially three joint practices and two uh two preseason games within, you know, about a 10-day window there. So, that'll be a great evaluation opportunity for us. And then the back end, we we finish it off and get get our eyes towards the regular season. >> The team got the restructured deal with Kamara done. How important was that and how important will he be to this offense this year? >> Fired up, excited. Um Alvin means a lot to our organization, uh this community, obviously. Um these things sometimes take a little bit of time just to kind of work through. And um Alvin's great about the whole process. I think communication was was really good for everyone. And uh you know, the conversation we were able to have, you know, certainly over the summer, I think was great. And um I think we're in we're in a good spot. And I think this running back room has a ton of talent. It's a really talented group. I'm excited to let training camp takes its course to define roles and opportunities. But uh it's going to be a great group for us. >> Can you describe that Alvin Kamara decision-making process that that went on this offseason with you guys evaluating whether there was a role for him on this team? Or you always like while installing your playbook, it you know, had something envisioned >> I I think that's a fair observation. I think uh you know, you're always looking for a role for guys. And I think sometimes getting a chance to evaluate where our roster's at and who we have on the roster and how these things developing uh allows us to take a little bit of time to do that the right way. And um and there's a little financial part, obviously, that you know, the business side had to take care of. And so, uh I thought it was a really good process, you know. We didn't anticipate necessarily Alvin doing as much in OTAs. Um you know, so that kind of gives us a little bit of time to see some of these other guys and see how this would uh fit in this equation. And so, we all feel really good about it. >> Do you make adjustments now though, like knowing for sure that he's here? I mean, cuz he's such a unique type of player. Did you already have everything that was going to be installed? Are there now different packages? >> I th- I think that's uh an ongoing process. I think early in training camp is, you know, still, you know, installation, so to speak. You're kind of teaching systems, getting guys comfortable. I think where you get into the player specific opportunities come a little later in training camp. And I think that's where certainly we will be excited to, you know, have those exploration phases when you have the running back room that we have. And so, um I think, you know, we feel good about the roles and the opportunities that will be presented to these guys. >> Getting it done before camp. And I guess you can even throw Kam in there getting it done in June. Like, knowing those issues, if you want to call them that, are resolved, what does that do for you as a coaching staff now? And and all that. >> Anytime there's definition, um allows us to build plans. Um it's the NFL. There's always a million moving pieces. That's just inevitable. This These rosters are always moving, but uh Kam, Alvin, they're really talented players. They mean a lot to this organization. They mean a lot to this community. They do things the right way. And so, um we're excited to have both those guys. >> With you guys being able to go out and get another running back, couple tight ends, few receivers, um how much does the offense does does the offense change? Does it expand or is it kind of taking a all the same stuff for you? Window dress it different? Like, what's what's the difference going forward? >> I think there's more variables for us in a positive way. Um certainly we've been able to feel that just being around OTAs and seeing the tight end room that we have, the running back room that we have. Um I think it's just going to be exciting to kind of build that as we go. You know, certainly there's things that we already feel comfortable, um you know, kind of diving into. There'll be things that I think that's the exciting part of training camp is you get to kind of evolve, you know, Uh OTAs is a awesome opportunity for us to get better as a football team and individuals, but it's not real football yet, you know, and we're a little closer to real football, which is an exciting part, but that's where you kind of get to, you know, um get a better feel for it. >> So, going into camp, obviously knowing who the quarterback is going to be as opposed to last year, benefits of that? >> Um yeah, I think it's just continuity. There's only so many reps, you know, you just think about that. Um you know, we got 10 installation practices and then we're playing Jacksonville in a joint practice. Uh there's only so many reps and so anytime you can have more defined roles, it allows guys to work with the guys that you anticipate working, you know, come September and so I think that's a huge advantage. >> Going to that point, Mickey just praised Tyler's initiative and race to be better. We talked about him in a lot of past sketches going to the West Coast with Drew. What did you guys think about that? What was your appreciation of seeing that? >> Yeah, I think it's just a awesome leadership example of what our football team looks like. Um certainly, you know, Tyler gets a lot of uh the lead on this thing, but for guys to want to go, do things together, spend time together, do the extra work, uh that means a lot, you know, it's the right kind of guys, it's it's a special group of guys. They know um we did a lot of good work in OTAs, but to steal a few more days in the summer, obviously is a huge benefit and then we just got to keep it moving. >> So, Calvin, what did you learn about your team off season program and what do you like about this team going into training camp? >> I'd say they competed really well, connected really well. Uh they put in a lot of time. Um second off season's always going to be better uh just because of the continuity and the expectations are more aligned and everyone understands what to expect. Um but I felt like it was a good good program. It put us in good position. Now, we obviously have to do the the real football part moving forward. >> What do you think of the chemistry that Chris and Tyler developed last year through I could see they're very successful together and and what excites you the most about how they can kind of keep developing that chemistry this year? >> I just say they've done an awesome job, you know, continuing what they built on late last year. Um Chris has had a phenomenal season. I thought Tyler finished off strong. That continuity is obviously a huge asset. You look at a lot of these top quarterbacks in this league, they got consistent guys around them a lot of times that they can, you know, lean on and anticipate throws to these guys cuz they've spent so much time with them and so um they're just continuing to build. They're continuing to grow. Um good job during OTAs. Offseason's been good and now, you know, now we're into training camp mode. >> With the continuity that you have going from last year to this year and kind of the groundwork now that you have with the offense and defense, do you anticipate using more opportunity or or rather uh what do you anticipate the the sort of role of things like unscripted practices or unscripted sessions being this year? >> Yeah, once you get through the initial stage, it becomes more free-flowing. Uh those joint practices obviously are good evaluations. You know, we kind of view this almost as like four stages training camp is. Uh there's the acclimation phase. There's kind of the compete stage, you know, or the you know, the competitive stage where we got to go. Um you know, push push ourself, you know, training camp's going to be a little bit uncomfortable for everyone. That's just how it is. And then you get to go, you know, evaluate yourself against, you know, really good talented teams in these joint practices. And then after that we kind of come back for a couple weeks to start moving our eyes to the regular season. So um I feel like it's a good formula. >> How do you guys manage like the expectations now? Like some people are picking you on big platforms. Like you got a lot of stuff. Tyler's got a lot of expectations. How do you guys manage that this year? >> It's part of the NFL. Uh you'd much rather have that than the other side of these things and so uh that's that's the that's what we all want. That's what we all uh expect and so um you know, you understand the NFL season takes its course and there's highs and lows and I think the most important thing is that the guys just focus on the task at hand, get better each and every day. Um, you know, we'll get to the regular season when we get to that. That's still feels a long ways away, so um, we got some really good work ahead of ourselves and if we just keep our eyes on that and focus on that getting better, everything else will take care of itself. >> Feel that shift at all? I mean, do you do you like do you kind of recognize that expectations are higher here than maybe it was a year ago at least on the downside? >> I I don't know. Um, every season is the NFL. I mean, everyone everyone has the same goals and aspirations in many ways. Um, we want to be NFC South champs. Like that's our goal, you know, and then ultimately obviously we want to play February 14th. Um, I think a lot of people have shared that uh in all 32 teams, you know, the last couple days. Um, we're all shooting for the same goals and now it's about what you do each and every day and uh the preparation you make and, you know, once the regular season comes, there's a lot of things that come into that that factor into it. >> How do you balance um you just look at the caution and the management y'all have been doing with Jordan Tyson versus like make sure he's ready to go and you know, and and does he have any ground to make up by the time y'all ready to get to week one? >> I just think Jordan's done an awesome job through this whole process. Every guy is in a different stage. Again, our objective is to be as healthy as we can in training going into training camp and then build from there and so uh an acclimation phase, we all have to get acclimated over the next few days to get ourselves ready to play real football which is um I'm trying to remember the date. Um, August 3rd, I think. August 3rd is our first padded practice, so um we got to build our guys up for that opportunity and so I think Jordan's done a nice job. He'll continue to uh he'll play play football and keep uh building up the right way and, you know, all these guys, you know, there'll be a few guys from whether it's medical or older players that hey, we you know, manage them just a touch, but these guys are all ready to roll. >> What do you what do you anticipate his management will look like? Will I mean will he be out there as early as this week doing >> Yeah. Yeah, I I think we'll see him play football tomorrow. So, he'll be ready to go and you know, we'll just build him up as we go like any player. I mean he didn't do a ton during OTAs. So, we got to build him up the right way just like we will all these other guys. >> Is it similar with Chris or is Chris even more ready to do more early? >> I think the same thing as far as just building someone up. I mean Chris is in a great spot. Um he's doing an awesome job and so he'll be ready. >> How about Kendre Miller not to land on PUP coming in off that ACL? Like how how's he doing and what's it say about him that you know he didn't have to go on that at all? >> Yeah, credit to him. Um those are long long journeys when you come off an injury like he had. Uh credit for him, our trainers, everyone who he's worked with to uh work really really hard to put him in position to go compete for a job in August. And so, you feel great about that. And uh yeah, I think he's going to do some really good things. >> Hey Kellen, what are the areas that you feel like you got better at uh since last season? Like some of the few you've improved on as a coach. >> Personally? I think you're always just trying to get better. It's as simple as that. Uh no matter what stage you're at, uh every year you're going to do you're going to have things you like, things you don't like. Every meeting you're going to have things you like that you presented, don't like that you presented and it's just about getting better. And uh I just love the off season that we had because of the continuity and the consistency that we had that we were able to really dig deep into what our season looked like last year, uh things that you know, both positively and things you got to improve on. And then you also get to study, you know, what the league looks like cuz ultimately you're competing against 31 other teams. And so, you got to see where they're at and what what they're doing and uh how can we grow as a football team? >> Kellen, it seems like uh Tyleik has really embraced the role as the leader of the team especially now that he knows he's the starter. How do you expect that to show up during training camp? How How would How does he lead this team through these next several weeks? >> Yeah, I think, you know, Tyler's one example. I think for a lot of our guys, it's it's the leadership that you need. Uh these are days where we're going to we have to build this thing up the right way, and we got to push ourselves through uncomfortable things. These guys haven't worn pads in a while, and so, you know, when you get to pads, like there's some acclimation. There's a getting used to, okay, the pad level, the physicality that this game requires, and we have to keep going. And so, uh you know, Tyler's a great example of everything that he's brought to this this offseason has been excellent. You know, from an offensive perspective, he'll continue to evolve as as the leader of that group, and his communication and his ability to play at the line of scrimmage, that'll all be uh a growth growth opportunity this training camp. >> How much clearer would you say the vision of an identity is, either offense or defense, or really the whole team, just going into this second year? >> Yeah, I think uh you know, time invested together, um going back to last year, but then, you know, this offseason, I think our guys really have embraced the you know, the adjustments that you want to make, and so, uh I think our guys know what we need to do. We We know we did not start fast. We know we got to run the football better. We know we got to be more consistent stopping the run, you know, week in and week out. Um we know that, you know, situational football is such an important part of this, you know, the margins are really tight, and these end-of-game situations we got to master, and so, I think we understand where we need to go, and uh we just got to get there. >> And how would you describe, you know, when you think about where the identity is that you're starting camp with, what would you describe that identity as for this team? >> Yeah, I think our team just realizes, you know, we want to play smart, fast, and physical. You know, that hasn't changed. That That's a play style that we want to play with, but um what the schematics look like, I thought we did an excellent job OTAs building a foundation. I think a big part of what we're doing is, you know, we're just continuing to go from OTAs. This isn't a you know, start at step one and, you know, go back through, you know, the baby steps. Like our OTAs was a great growth. Summer, the expectation was you grew individually and then we just keep going. And so, um that's where you gain momentum when you, you know, invest that much time into it. >> By the By the end of last season, do you feel like you reached kind of those pillars, smart, fast, physical? Like was it all kind of what you that identity that you wanted to see? >> Yeah, I I felt like we're we're playing cleaner football. Um yeah, I think we needed to play smarter football. Um you know, the penalties and the situational football got better. Um obviously we spent a lot of time investing in that. And then uh you know, the play style being physical, being able to run the football more efficiently, being able to stop the run, you know, um I think we have some great examples of that late in the year. And then uh fast is just about these guys just playing confident and free. And uh I think our guys, you know, we're finding that as we go. >> All right. I guess just just going to put it like is there like one of the three that you're really trying to hammer home this year or like right now kind of like I'd like to see like our physicality in the running game for instance or something like that? >> I think I I think all of it. Um yeah. >> I saw Josh Hill officially listed with the tight ends. Are there any other staff movements, configurations that have changed at all? >> I don't think anything new. Uh obviously Will Clapp would be our one main addition. Him coming over during the off season, yeah, Josh Josh has been kind of around it, you know, a lot of last year. Uh you know, kind being in the personnel department, but starting to evolve into the coaching side of this thing. And so, uh Josh is special. He's he's one of the best all time. Um great example for our players to see a guy his career and then uh his transition. I think he's awesome for these guys. >> You mentioned starting fast or or wanting to start faster this year, what are some of the things that you can do and are there things that you can do in training camp to kind of help get you ready for that? Is that the thing you got to work for? >> No, mindset mentality right now. We're in the installation process, so it's about, you know, the mindset mentality and getting used to like we got to start practice fast. And then there'll be certain periods and situations as training camp evolves where we put a little bit more focus on it and then you know, there's plenty stuff I've done through the off-season where you're trying to study just the the data and the scheme and all that sort of stuff of how we can do a better job here. >> Kool-Aid recently made a comment about he thinks this offense is going to be very explosive but also his excitement to try to shut them down during training camp. Just from a coaching perspective, how do you sort of battle like I'm I'm sure you don't want one side of the ball just beating up the other like how do you One side has a good day, are you worried about the what's that balance like? >> That's how training camp is. Uh One side wins, so one side loses and they're both on your side at the end of the day, so uh Yeah, I think I think the goal at the end of training camp is it's an opportunity for these players to learn and grow, so not expecting it to be perfect. I'm expecting, you know, them to have good moments and I'm expecting them to test their boundaries and make a mistake and you know, I think that's an important part of what training camp is and uh you know, so just like, you know, during the day I think at the end of day you hope that there's days or periods where offense does well then defense does well then offense does well then defense does well. Same thing in special teams when you rep those periods that one side is, you know, successful and then the other side where you responds the right way and so that's just what you're looking for. >> Is that maybe the benefit of having so many joint practices that kind of get a measuring stick at where it's not just your guys? >> Yeah, I think it'll be good. It'll be a change of environment, change of scenery so speak. Uh Second off-season, so I think our team's more ready for it and uh you'll get some different looks, different personnel, different presentations. Again, a lot of it goes back to getting your starters and that first group really ready to play football um come, you know, whatever the second week of September. >> What are the conversations around the league? >> Sorry, did you have any like special message for the team? You talked to them in the team meeting. Any point of emphasis you wanted to set the tone? >> I think I think the biggest thing is just, you know, we have a plan, let's let's execute the plan. Um you know, we've we've put a lot of work into this thing. We've uh put ourself in excellent position coming off of OTAs and the summer and now it's about um really focusing on this training camp. The season will come, you know, eventually. You know, we got to get better and we got to focus on this plan and we got to have purpose with it and we got to we got to test ourself. Uh you know, training camp, you know, when you're in Metairie in training camp, it's going to be hot and humid and there's going to be some adverse uh elements in that. Um also putting pads on, that's an adverse element when you haven't done it for a while. And so we got to be comfortable being uncomfortable a little bit and push our boundaries a little bit and that the joint practice will lead in that as well. >> You mentioned that um you had some players obviously you have to manage their reps in camp for age or whatever reason. Is Eric McCoy one of those players who's coming off this those injuries? >> I think any guy that's I'm going to say eight plus years, I mean they've played a lot of football in the NFL and so you're always going to be uh smart with those guys. Uh everyone's on different trajectory through training camp as far as where we're building them to. Um some guys are obviously going to be competing at a high level through training camp. Some guys are getting ready for, you know, early September and you know, Eric's done an awesome job uh through this whole off-season program. He's in an excellent spot. He's, you know, we'll probably have to make sure he's uh you know, maintaining this thing the right way and so he's ready to go. >> With all the kind of conversation and emphasis around the multi tight end sets around the NFL, what are you hoping to see from your room here throughout training camp and throughout the season? >> Yeah, I'm just excited to let those guys compete and uh yeah, they'll define the roles. They'll we'll sort it all out. We got a really talented group. Uh I think we got seven tight ends and we love all seven of them. They and they've all they're all, you know, tight ends that can play on Sundays uh this fall and so we're excited to let those guys all compete and um yeah, it's a trend uh to play with multiple tight ends. Um it's an asset and we'll just continue to see how that goes. >> Does that kind of clock into what you were talking about with the multiple like more variables and things like that? Is that a position where you can really maximize >> Yeah, I think I think that's a really talented group, a very versatile group uh when you talk about the traits that those guys have and the ability they have to, you know, not only play like an inline tight end, but play in the backfield, play split out. Uh I think that's where the power of that position comes up when you have guys that can uh line up in a number of different ways. >> Kevin, because it's been a focus of yours since you got here, I'm just curious, team-building activities, what's the schedule look like? What's coming up? >> Yeah, um training camp's really about getting ready for football. Uh you know, we'll still have a couple items, but um you know, OTAs we kind of utilize a little bit more time for that and then training camp we'll still have a couple opportunities to kind of spend time. I think a lot of what training camp creates is a day where guys are just around each other a lot and uh so it's a lot more organic as far as spending time together. You know, when you practice in the morning, you have idle time before meetings in the afternoon. These lunches, these dinners, we got great cafeteria here, so guys get to hang around and it's perfect. >> I think you were saying that for the team you guys want to be next season, that like your young guys are going to have to make a leap, but I'm wondering I I know that like is the case for every team across the NFL, but I'm just curious on like after the season you guys had, is that an emphasis for you or are you excited to see it? What what's kind of your mindset going into trying to have these guys take the next step? >> Yeah. Um I'd just say everyone has to grow. Um everyone has to whether you played last year or didn't play, you got to get better during training camp, and you got to be ready to go, and I'd say from a big picture perspective, there's always, you know, people will sometimes call it the second-year jump, you know, those guys who play last year as rookies, that rookie year, some of these rookies are going through it now. You go right from your season right into the combine training, right into the draft, OTAs, summer they get a couple weeks, and they're right into the season. There's a lot going on. And then those guys who come back after that first season, it's like, "All right, I got a whole off season to like kind of train myself, get into the system. I'm not learning a bunch of new stuff. I'm building off of what I learned my rookie year, and so, um I think that that goes for a lot of guys." >> When there is a trend like the the 3-10-1 thing, like, are you looking at everything the Rams do, like, their run game behind it, like, all the duos, stuff like that? Is it Is it all of it, and you kind of just see what pieces fit? Like, how do you adopt something like that? >> Yeah. Usually you're going to try and watch a number of teams, um you know, in those spaces. Um you know, we've studied a lot of league. I think studied as much of the league this year as ever, which has been a lot of fun, I think, for our coaching staff on on in all three phases. Um yeah, I think we've studied football really, really diligently, and so, uh the Rams have made headlines for 13 personnel. Uh get it they had had a ton of success, and you know, the numbers obviously, you know, show that. A lot of other teams that did it in, you know, maybe slightly different ways, and so you're kind of constantly trying to look at, you know, what could probably be best implemented for our football team, and tying it together, and so, yeah, I think it it's been a lot of fun. >> Are you married to like a very specific way of doing things, or are you kind of open-minded, like, a new idea can open new things up? Like, some people have a system, and then other people are like, adaptable and change. Like, how do you view that? >> Yeah, uh I think I've called plays in five systems now, so uh I like to say I'm pretty bilingual in uh football languages, so um yeah, I I think it's important to be able to adapt and adjust while still being defined, you know, and I think that's always the balancing act and I'm not going to say, you know, it was perfect every every year that I've ever coached. Uh we've had good years, we've had years where we probably could have done a better job of that and so um I think the flexibility is important for us and I'm I'm excited with where our roster's at, with the type of players we have, with the versatility that that's going to provide. Kind of let training camp uh take its course and then define what those roles look like moving forward. >> How different do you expect your offense to look this year compared to last year? >> I think you're always trying to evolve. Every year should look a little different. Uh I think that's an important part. title: Pre-Training Camp Updates From Saints GM Mickey Loomis 🎤
