You know, we we hit on a bunch of players and went from having a um a 7-9 record to um having a really good run with that group. And that and I would say that that uh 2017 class was kind of the catalyst for that. just cuz of the way the roster's kind of kind of changed in the last couple years, are you are you a faster team? You like is that is that been like maybe a focus of y'all is just kind of getting speed with some of the people you're drafting and >> Yeah, I I think that there was a little bit of an emphasis on that the last couple years, yes. Yeah, I think we've we recognized that we needed be a little more explosive. >> So, that was just like a like an internal thing you that's something you wanted specifically to address Anything else along those lines that I mean, as you guys have gotten younger, like you feel like we're better in this area or areas, but well, I mean, again, that was a question about was there something that we wanted to emphasize? That was one of the things that we talked about. Now, you don't always get it accomplished. And you know, not necessarily every player, but that specifically was something we talked about we need to be a little more explosive. >> When did you hear or have you heard about the Christian Miller story in Raleigh? >> I heard I heard about that. That's pretty cool. Um you know, I think a lot of our players do things like that pretty often and it doesn't happen to get pep uh publicized, but that yeah, that's a really cool thing. >> I mean, can you foresee any type of trade maybe in August? Remember how significant that was with Jacksonville to trade when Saunders leaves with the Jags and and you know, you always want to have depth and that was a big that was a big trade that really helped the offense line considering the injury. Yeah, I mean, we haven't had any discussions about that yet. I think right now, you know, I've talked to a few guys around the league and it's just about A, what do you feel like you're heavy you know, what are you light? Um, but nothing concrete. Um, that'll happen I think probably two or three weeks into training camp. Some of it's driven by injury. Some of it's driven by, you know, you have a younger player or two that maybe you didn't expect uh, develop to develop as quickly as they they have and so um, but that'll that'll be a large part of the discussions that we have, you know, in the middle of August. >> Do you feel like that precedent or like is that set like a precedent for you like or like the like you feel like you found something there that maybe try and explore it again down the road rather than just like waiting for waivers or something? >> No, I mean, that that's just business as usual. >> And when you look back to where this team was a year ago at this point with Zach Wilson at quarterback, how much better do you think you feel about would you say you feel about where you are now? Well, look, I'm always optimistic. I, you know, I can always envision a a path to success. It doesn't always come out that way, but um, always optimistic. Um, I think last year, you know, the quarterback question was you know, a little more um, up in the air than it is this year and and look, we feel obviously feel good about where Tyler's at, but I also feel good about, you know, Spencer and having Zach Wilson in the building and and so um, I think that's probably the difference between last year and this year. >> How you feel going back to primetime? yeah, I And you know, I I look at it like that's what it is. You know, it is what it is. I don't I kind of like having, you know, a game every Sunday and having a routine. You know, that that that's good. Now, this year it's it's it's going to be different. You know, we have this game in Paris and and you know, as you said, we got a couple of prime time games. So, it's good for that's more about the fans I think than it is about the the players in the team. cuz we like routine. >> Is this a Kellen Moore decision or are you involved but now you see I think there's only three teams that aren't practicing against other teams. When you going to go against the Jags, the Rams and then Dallas. I mean, not so much playing in the preseason game but actually the practice >> guys you counting on participating more in that area than the actual preseason game. >> Yeah, you know, we talked a lot about that. Um we talked about it a year ago and we talked about it beginning of this year and and I think both of us see it the same. We like practicing against other teams and you know, this year we're practicing practicing against three really good teams, three three really good rosters. It's good for us. It's good for particularly, you know, younger guys to measure themselves against um you know, teams that are really good in our league. And so, um it's a controlled environment. And so, you probably feel a little better about that than than, you know, a preseason game in terms of, you know, playing your guys. But but all of it's good development for us. We're we're in the development stage, right? We're in a race to get better. you know, particularly, you know, where we're at in terms of our development. And so, um every opportunity that we can have, uh you know, we're going to take. And this year, you know, we're we're lucky to have, you know, three good opportunities to practice against teams yeah, I'm looking forward to that. >> You guys interested in how the addressing rotation kind of shakes out here? >> I'm sorry, say that again? >> For at rusher, just how the rotation shakes out. Are you you're of interested in seeing how that will unfold. >> Yeah, be because look it it looks like you know we've got some depth there um which is unusual. You know, for any team. Um and you know, we've got a lot of guys that that we think can rush the passer, so um it's a good problem to have. >> You you mentioned uh things for the fans. I know you all are doing a big 60th season celebration all year long. I'm sure you'll reminisce when your career whenever it ends, but given the fact that you've been here for almost half of that, when when you hear 60 seasons, do you talk about it, think about it in some way? >> Um I try not to. Yeah, I try not to. I'd like to have another, you know, 40 seasons, but obviously that's not going to happen. Um yeah, I don't I don't think much about it. Uh in fact, I just saw that it was our 60th season about um two or three weeks ago and that there were some you know, things that we're going to do um but I don't really think about that. I'm just focused on right now. Anything else? >> Thank you, Big Al. >> Will you be in Canton? >> For sure? >> What's that? >> Yeah, absolutely. Yes, wouldn't miss it. >> Thanks, Big Al.

title: Geno Smith Press Conference | Jets Training Camp
text: Good afternoon. Um I want to start by saying, you know, I really feel like uh coming out of OTAs, I feel like we built some positive momentum. And uh you know, really really happy with, you know, where this team is right now. You know, I really hate the fact that, you know, something I was a part of could have been a distraction for, you know, this team, my teammates, this organization because a lot of hard work's been put in and a lot of guys have, you know, put a lot of work in for us to be in a good spot as a team. You know, I'm happy that, you know, I'm able to put this behind me. Um looking forward to moving forward. And uh just continuing to build day by day with my guys. Um you know, I really appreciate being a part of this team, a part of this organization again. And I look forward to just building every single day in training camp, getting better as a team, uh getting better as a player, and uh continuing the positive momentum. >> Geno, what are your expectations for this team entering camp? >> You know, I I have high expectations for the team. I believe we have not only the right guys in the locker room, but you know, in the coaching staff in the front office and you know, there's a lot of things to be positive about, you know, as a as a Jet fan and as a player and as a part of the organization. Um I expect us to go out there every single day, um be who we are, which is a team full of, you know, hard-working men, guys who love the game, and uh a lot of talent a lot of talent on this team as well. So, I look forward to building with these guys. I look forward to being a part of this team and see where we could take it. >> We saw your Instagram post that uh war ready. Uh how motivated are you just to kind of get to see the start and just kind of put the bad things just kind of behind you? >> I'm super excited. You know, I'm I'm very excited just for my teammates. Um you know, we just finished up a conditioning test and I mean, you if you see these guys and the way that they've worked just in the short span that we've been away, everyone came back like I said, war ready and and and ready for long haul, but it's a day-to-day process Um and we're in it for the long haul, like I said, but we're focused on the day-to-day stuff and just getting better each and every day and not really looking too far ahead or behind, but just staying where our feet are and just working every day as a team to get better. >> You said you didn't want to be a distraction. Have you had conversations with Aaron or even some of your teammates to just clear the air on everything or is that >> Yeah, I've had conversations with with coach Glenn, with Moosh and with all of the veterans on the team and and the guys on the team, but you know, like I said, we're we're we're put this behind us and we're moving forward. >> You know, how would you put into words for those of us who were were with you when you were here the first go around, how much of a different player you are and person you are from all the way back then, which seems like a long time ago? >> Yeah, yeah, I would say you know, experience in this league, being around a lot of great coaches, being a part of some great organizations, you know, being under some really great quarterbacks has helped me develop and grow and you know, that's what the NFL's about. It's about the process and so heading into year 14, you know, I'll still have that same edge, that same chip on my shoulder that I had as a rookie, but I'm a lot more wiser. I've obviously developed in many areas, but that process is still ongoing. You can never be you'll never have it. You always got to have that edge and you always got to try and find new ways to get better and so I'm looking forward to the challenges of continuing to get better each and every day. >> As a young guy, and which you were trying to find yourself when you were here initially, could you have imagined standing here and saying year 14? >> You know, I've always had plans to play for a long time in this league and you know, you don't know how you know, where life's going to take you. That's the beauty of life. You kind of just roll with it, but I always believed in myself. I've always believed in my talent and my work ethic and I believe that that's going to carry me forward as well. >> How you viewing this opportunity? Obviously, Uh, there's a lot of speculation that the Jets may draft a quarterback eventually. Uh, just how are you viewing this opportunity with the Jets? And also, would you like to stay here after this past the 2026 season? >> You know, God has blessed me to be able to play this long. And um I view each and every opportunity, each and every day as a blessing. Um, it's truly a blessing and a gift from God. And so, every day I get a chance to go out into this locker room with my teammates, step on that field with my teammates. Um, to be coached by, you know, great coaches. I just I I'm truly humbled by it. And so, I don't look too far ahead. I know that there's a lot of work to be done. And I'm I'm extremely focused on making sure that we do the right thing as far as the process goes. And let everything else handle itself as I've always done. >> So, you've had a number of you've obviously been with a bunch of teams now. What's it What's the difference between coming to a place where you've already been? This is This is something that's new for you. >> You know, it's the same for me. Every single day it still feels like my first year. Um, just that passion that I have for the game, the love I have for the game. Um I you know, I was telling guys, man, I'm so excited just to get back to practice and, you know, to move forward and and to push towards, you know, the season because it's, like I said, such a blessing. And I'm so excited, man. I can't I can't describe how excited I am just to be a part of this team and to go out there with the great, you know, players that we have on this team. To be coached by the great coaches that we have. And um, just just be where my feet are. >> Did Did you seek any advice or tips or anything from from veterans who have had the same experience that you're going through now, which is coming back to a team where you started at Davis? >> Yeah, I would say DeMario. DeMario, and I think he and I share the same sentiment that we're just excited to be here in in in the year that we're here. Um, there's nothing more to it. Um, I'm just excited to go out there and play football. I love football. I love being around my teammates. And, you know, I love the challenge of trying to get better. I think that's what makes the game special. And uh forward to, you know, trying to be the best player that I can be every single day for my teammates. >> Geno, how how would you describe how your experience has been so far working with AG and the kind of head coach he is cuz you obviously never played for him before? >> Yeah, uh I would say um so far so good. You know, AG has done a great job at laying out the blueprint for this team and where he wants to take us. And it's our job to bring that into manifestation. Um but I I love it, man. I think the world of this organization. I think the world of coach coach Glenn. I think he's a great coach, outstanding coach, and uh like I said, it's our job to go prove him right. >> Geno, how do you like Frank's system and and how it fits you? >> You know, uh just being a part of, you know, coach's system in the short time that that I've been a part of it, uh it's it's similar to something I played in in the past, but there also has its differences. And so, the challenge is to learn all the nuances. Um again, to learn get the timing down with the wide outs, you know, get the timing down in the cadence with the with the linemen. Making sure that we're executing the game plan uh the way that coach Reich wants us to execute it. And uh I believe he's a tremendous coach. I mean, his track record speaks for itself, but it's about what we can do now. And so, he's doing a great job of leading the offense. Um he's laying out the blueprint for us. And again, we got to go out there and execute and make it happen. >> Geno, what was your some of the guys down there training down in in Florida during the break? What was that like? You know, how many guys got together and >> Uh yeah, I got I got together with a bunch of the guys. Um you know, we trained on and off the field. We we, you know, we hung out. Um you know, just kind of did what teammates do. And uh some of it was posted online, some of it wasn't. Uh but, you know, I I really think we made some progress, you know, in the in the past few weeks. And I look forward to seeing how we can build on that. >> That's what I was going to ask. Was your training any different? Like I know you went with some of these guys. What What was your training any different coming into this one this year? >> No, uh I feel like every year I just work harder and harder and smarter as well. Um I try to get better in every way that I can and and improvement doesn't just happen um on the field on game day. You know, it starts in the off season and so my preparation for the season um was just the same as it's always been, but again, I've gotten wiser, I've gotten smarter, and uh I feel like I've developed as well. So, um that's something that you have to continue to do. You have to challenge yourself every single day to get better and and so I I look forward to that challenge and I appreciate the fact that um in year 14, I still have a lot of room for improvement. >> Who are you most looking Who are you most looking forward to working with tomorrow morning when you guys get on the field? >> All of the guys. All of the guys. Um again, facing, you know, DeMario and uh you know, just matching wits with him on the field. Uh you know, bringing the offense together. All of us, man. Just, you know, developing as players together, pushing each other to get Um you know, being coachable, learning, and you know, just trying to be the best players that we can be on on the daily basis so that when the time comes, we can showcase >> And how has your relationship with Garrett developed over the past couple months? >> It's been great. You know, get I think the world of Garrett. You know, I followed his career since he was at Ohio State and um I think he's he's a a great receiver, tremendous person. Um the way that he works, his work ethic, uh his talent speaks for itself, but um just a great teammate as well. So, I look forward to building with him, but not only him, all all the guys. And um you know, he's a great leader and I I would say he he probably say the same. >> Geno, when it comes to moving forward and putting this stuff from December behind you, do you feel like you have to do anything differently going forward to avoid those headlines and that stuff kind of happening? >> You know, I just look forward to practice tomorrow and uh you know, moving towards the season. >> You mentioned Garrett. Did you Was he able to come down to Florida with you? Were you able to work out during that last month? >> Uh we he Yeah, we got some work in. Uh we didn't post anything online, but we got some work in and we were able to, you know, kind of build there.

text: you know, Rich is going to be out there. So, just kind of getting us set for training camp. We're going to preview all the big storylines and of course, just all the changes the Jets have made. It's the same head coach, but different quarterback, completely different roster outside of a handful of players here or there. I mean, looking at this team, Rich, what to you is the biggest storyline going into camp next week? >> Yeah, 1 week from today we will be on the practice field at about 8:30 in the morning for practice number one. Yeah, so the biggest storyline for me is well, I'm a coaching quarterback guy. You you guys know that. Uh to me it's it's can they finally get decent quarterback play out of the uh quarterback [snorts] journeyman du jour, which is De'Geno Smith this year, stepping into the role of Justin Fields. A a bridge quarterback, no doubt. A guy who I think is capable of having a decent year, but who has a lot to prove coming off a rough year with the Vegas Raiders last year. So, to me and that and also the backup situation. I think a lot of fans are intrigued by Kade Klubnik and his development. So, this will be a highly scrutinized backup battle for quarterback. And so, to me those are the two big storylines. And of course, the coach has a lot to prove coming off a disastrous first year. A lot of things that Aaron Glennon Glenn needs to improve upon and will be watched very closely. >> I agree, Rich. I mean, all those things uh I certainly would rubber stamp. So, not to be repetitive, I'm going to kind of spin it a different direction, more like just overall macro for the Jets. Like I think this is a pretty common thought and it's proven to be very elusive for the Jets, but like the overall organizational health to me is three-tiered. How's ownership? How's the GM? You really even four-tiered. Ownership, general manager, head coach, quarterback, right? No no disrespect to Woody, but nobody's going to sit up here and say that he's been an asset. He has not been. The quarterback obviously is what he is. He's a stopgap. You know, Muji I believe is is a bit of a rising star. We've talked about that a lot. And Aaron Glenn very well might be one and a half or two and done. So, while we're still steps away from them having that health that we all crave, you know, I I I I look at I do look at Mookie, and I look at some of the moves he's he's made, the draft he's had, the stability on the old line, addressing weaknesses, being aggressive when it calls for it. I want to see the players that he brought in. Now, now now it's now it's time to take him out of the garage, spin him around the block a little bit, and and I think we're going to like what we see, but until we actually see it, we we've got to we've got to see it. >> And to your point, BT, I I think when you look at the roster that they have, and and and it all starts with Geno, as Rich alluded to, just what he is. Is he the guy we saw with the Raiders in the worst team in football, or is he closer to what he was in Seattle, where he had a couple of really nice years, and was certainly an above-average player? Beyond just like Geno, just the roster in general, the offensive line, some of the extensions they got done. I I think at least this roster is in a position where if you had good coaching from Aaron Glenn and his staff, they shouldn't be one of the worst teams in the NFL. I don't think Jet fans are expecting Aaron Glenn to lead the Jets to a division title, or be in the playoffs, but he's lucky to have a job going into his second year, and I think the expectation amongst most people in the fan base is that this is a dramatically improved football team that we see starting week one against Robert Saleh and the Titans. >> Yeah, it would have been nice to have the the Dolphins in week two, or you know, the Raiders early. Instead, it's the gauntlet that is the AFC North, but no, I I think that you lay that out well. Again, I I think that and we we this is episode what, 18? We we've touched on so many of the smaller things, the micro stuff, we've dissected everything, but the bottom line, Rich, I I feel like there's Now, I don't know if it will be rewarded, we'll find out, but I feel like there's a renewed sense of optimism, of vigor, of hope, of possibility. Like, I feel like there's a little bit of an energized base within the Jet fan base, and you guys were out there for the big party in AC a couple of weeks ago. You guys felt it first hand. I I I that that and that needed to happen. I think the jet you look at the empty seats and a bit disenfranchised and certainly disenchanted with the direction of the team for the last decade and a half. I feel like it's turning the corner a little bit. I would think that you share that thought, right Rich? >> Um you know, this reminds me a little of 2017. In a big picture sense that you have some of the fan base that has one eye on next year. And in 17 everyone it was the suck for Sam, right? You know, right now Jake is raising his hand. You know, it was suck for Sam and Josh McCown was the stopgap and actually did a pretty good job that year. And Todd Bowles was the defensive-minded head coach who ended up surviving the year and then you know, they brought in Sam Darnold and and he was everything was a washout that first year. So this kind of has that feel to it cuz I think and tell me if I'm wrong, especially Jake cuz you were talking, you know, you were out there talking to the fans in Atlantic City a couple weeks ago. It feels like half the fan base has one eye on the 2027 draft and the quarterback situation and the other eye is looking at the current situation and might be cautiously optimistic about what they feel. So it's a weird it's kind of a weird cocktail right now of some hope, but yet some reality. So I don't know, maybe I'm wrong, but that's that was my takeaway. >> Well, it's interesting because the the hope is something that BT already alluded to. Like Darren Moji is the hope. The fact that the Jets seemingly have made smart trades, have gotten good value. You feel like you have a smart football guy who set the organization up with three first-round picks. The Jets are doing the opposite of what they did with Sam Darnold where it's get the quarterback and then oh, we need everything around him. It's we're trying to build the infrastructure and then insert the quarterback into the lineup. Like I think what bothers the jet fan more than anything, you actually could pick the right player as we saw Sam Darnold is now a Super Bowl winning quarterback who's won 14 games each of the last two years, but he had no chance with Adam Gase and the Jets. So I think the optimism is Moji in 2027 and beyond. and then there's also some fans like you BT it's like let's at least have a season. Let's let's see if Aaron Glenn could coach and prove us wrong and then it's wow, we have a coach and three first round picks and we have a hundred million in cap space. So kind of depends how you look at it, but I do think there is optimism and just the optimism might not be for most until we get to the 2027 and we see what the landscape of the NFL and the college landscape what it all looks like for the Jets. >> Yeah, I I think I've just been fooled too many times where, you know, this college prospect's going to be the next franchise elevator and he's not or to Jake's point, you draft the right guy to the wrong circumstance. Like we try to fit all these, you know, pegs in these in these holes and it's never it's never always I matter fact it's very rarely ideal especially with the Jets. So I've almost learned to compartmentalize each thing separately. Like I'm going into the season. I expect them to week one to win week one probably a tight game probably a little bit ugly, but I think they'll win that game. And then you go week by week and and I can enjoy and I wasn't always like this guys. It took me a while to get here. I can enjoy the now meaning the current season which is rapidly approaching and also like view separately but also kind of mesh in the back of my mind the college landscape, the quarterback landscape, how much cap space you got, kind of play the financial game and draft equity. Like I've finally learned to separate the two and like the one thing I will never do this. I've done it too many times. I'm not doing it. I'm not playing this game anymore. Where I'm hoping for losses and I don't mean like the last game of the season that's different. But I'm not going into seasons hoping to go two and 15 or one and 16 to get this guy cuz too often we've seen and not just with the Jets, that guy doesn't always equate to being the man. So I've given up on that. >> I think the key and let's face it. The Jets, I'm just talking real I'm going to be real here. The Jets roster right now is probably is a bottom third roster in the NFL. I don't think there's any question about that. I think for them to don't disagree with me BT. I mean there is no question there. >> I didn't say anything. I'm just I'm listening to you. >> I saw that they are a bottom-third roster. However, the one the one caveat is I will say they have a lot of young players, you know, the Baileys, the Sediques, the Coopers, Pounds. Guys like that and even from last year with Membou and Taylor and Azaria Thomas, if those guys progress quickly, especially this year's rookie class, the top three guys in particular, then I think the ceiling for this team can rise quicker than anticipated. I think so much of their immediate future hinges on player development and that's we can ring it right back to Aaron Glenn and his coaching staff of

title: Training Camp Preview: Defense | Big Blue Kickoff Live | New York Giants
text: Welcome to Tuesday's edition of Big Blue Kickoff Live here on giants.com YouTube as well as the mobile app. He's Paul Dino. I'm Lance Meadow with you for the next 60 minutes as we are knocking on the door of the start of training camp in West Virginia. YOU READY FOR SOME FOOTBALL? >> WELL, IF I'M NOT, I'm going to be ready. I can tell you this after the next 60 minutes based on your energy. Yeah, I'm ready. As we'll be previewing the defense today, but a little bit more bookkeeping before we get Paul's thoughts on the defensive front. We're broadcasting from the Giants podcast studio. It is presented by Hackinack Meridian Health. Keep getting better. Multiple ways to interact with us here on the program. You give us a ring 2019-4513. He is at Giants WFAN on Twitter. Amit Lance Meadow one word last name M. And the archive of the show. Our entire podcast network is on the Giants mobile app, podcast platforms everywhere, the Giants YouTube channel and at giants.com/mpodcast. So yesterday you focused on offense. We're going to use the same framework and apply that to the defense today in terms of the top three storylines. Paul and I will give you our own rankings. We want to hear from you as well on the phones and on social media. We'll tally it up at the end. I think there's just as much substance on the defensive side as on the offensive side. So Paul, let's start with our substantive conversation, then we'll open it up to everyone else. I think without hesitation, my number one item to watch >> worth five points >> worth five, three is number two, and then one point for number three is the run defense. I think it was the biggest question coming in even before the off season began. It widened once they traded away Dexter Lawrence and I don't think anything has dramatically changed. It's not as if they haven't addressed that position, but it's going to be stopping the run by committee as opposed to one guy putting on the cape and doing the heavy lifting. And they have some veterans in the mix. And I think DJ Reer certainly with his experience and the attention that he draws should help the cause, but there's still a lot of question marks and it's a new defense to boot and a number of guys that don't necessarily have chemistry. So, of all the other facets and elements in play here, I don't think anything surpasses and anything stops whether or not this unit is going to make huge strides in aiding the cause to stop the run this season. That is easily the only choice for the five-point question. As far as I'm concerned, there is nothing else that's close compared to the rush defense storyline. Now, you mentioned DJ Reer. Uh it's going to be a big second year for Darius Alexander. He has to he has to because they don't have much choice. Step up and build off of his final month of his rookie season when he was really good. I mean, you could see this guy wi with a big upside. He's got to do it. All right. There can be no plateau. There can be no step back. Darius Alexander has to show us that what he did the last five weeks or so of the season last year was for real. and and if he can do that in combination with DJ Reer, in combination with Shelby Harris who's going to see some snaps, uh who knows who the other defensive downlinemen are going to be because the Giants have a lot of numbers there, but I don't think there's a lot of clarity right now. >> Well, they're also not all making the team, too. So, it's another reason Lucky Fu, for example, is another veteran that they brought in in the mold of Reer and Harris, but >> So is Roberts. >> Yeah. It's a numbers game, though, at this point. And and here's the other thing, by the way. It's not just a matter of who comes in to replace Dex. It's also the loss of Roy Robertson Harris who helped in stopping the run. Paul, I'm not saying that he's overlooked, but that is a significant absence given the torn Achilles that he suffered. Now, right now, they have yet to put him on IR. So, the chance of him returning late in the season still exists. But the point is, you're going to be without him for the bulk of the year, and you're already without Deck. So, it's two veterans that have been productive, you know, one a little bit more maybe on the edge, another one obviously that eats up space on the interior. title: 2 minutes at Patriots training camp: Christian Gonzalez speaks, Kayshon Boutte stars on Day 4
text: Two minutes of Patriots training camp wrapping up in here on day four, Tuesday, July 28th, before the Patriots taking an off day, and so do we. title: Florio: 49ers treated Kyle Shanahan accident like a 'state secret' | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: The Kyle Shanahan situation was terrifying, concerning, and as it relates to the inside baseball of the media landscape, it was fascinating to understand that there was clear coordination between the 49ers and ESPN as it relates to the green light being given to the ESPN reporting that went over and above the 49ers announcement that was posted at noon Eastern on Saturday, 12:01 after tweet with more details, 12:02 ESPN article, lengthy article that didn't write itself in 2 minutes, that had quotes from a police lieutenant, that had details about the other driver not being injured, no one being cited, things that just didn't fall out of the sky. It was all lined up, it was all engineered at the behest of the 49ers. And as it relates to the other media outlets, now I've explained this a few times today. I was on radio in San Francisco, 95.7 The Game, I believe. I was on The Score in Chicago, I think it came up there. When you look at a situation like this, because every media outlet, every news outlet that is in a given area, they will have someone who is monitoring the publicly available information. Now, in some cities and towns, they'll just dump whatever public information there is into the newspaper. All the marriage licenses, all the divorce applications, whether a public figure or not. Anything and everything, real estate transaction. Everybody knows what you paid for your home. It's in there on Sunday. All the transactions in the area for the week, and I'm sure that small newspapers throughout the country do the same thing. In the bigger markets, in the markets with sports teams and celebrities and high profile figures, you have people who are constantly monitoring the publicly available information as it relates to, I don't know, arrests and car accidents. you have somebody there paying close attention, checking everything. Is this someone our audience would care about? Is it a public figure? Is this relevant information to the audience we serve? So, as it relates to Kyle Shanahan's accident, which was kept under wraps for 11 days, either the publications in the Bay Area just don't have that capacity, or they were asleep at the switch, or they did a deal with the 49ers to not do anything or say anything about it until the 49ers announced it on their own timetable, or there was some sort of effort by the public agencies to slow play, downplay, and seal. But for other people, including not public figures, those are public records. And after the news finally came out, and there were some members of the San Francisco 49ers press corps who were unhappy with someone having the audacity to question their exercise of discretion. Their decision not to pursue natural curiosity. Well, I knew some of it, but I didn't know all of it. It was a It's a sensitive issue. I didn't feel it was appropriate to act on my curiosity. You can still go find out more. You don't have to report it, but presumably you're curious. presumably you'd like to know what's going on, even if you're not going to report it. Instead of directing their efforts to finding out more, there's enough there for a reasonable person to conclude that maybe there's more to be pursued. Go pursue it. Go pursue it. I don't care why you didn't do your job before. You can do your job now. On that note, Grant Cohn had an item last night on si.com. And he's citing public record records, excuse me, say among other things, and this all comes from Cohn's report based on public records as interpreted by him, that Kyle Shanahan was holding and using a cell phone behind the wheel of the Tesla that he was in. I've heard, and I'm a big believer that if anyone disputes something that's been publicly reported, you need to publicly dispute it. Don't do the per sources thing. It's got far more credibility when you go on the record. If you're pushing back against something someone said, go on the record with it. Say it loudly. Don't hand it to someone who says, "Oh, per sources, that other guy's report's incorrect." That other guy's on the record. He stuck his neck out. If he's wrong, and again, I've heard that the 49ers may believe Cohn's report is wrong. If they believe it, say it. Don't whisper it. Don't sprinkle it around. Say it. So, that's where it currently stands. look, one of the realities of journalism, and I've got no journalism training, and it shows. I've been doing this for 25 years, mainly through trial and error, more error than trial. But, I've kind of figured out how this works. And this business is just curiosity in motion. You see something that you find interesting and you explore it. And the people whose curiosity is best in line with the curiosity of their audience, those are the ones who are going to thrive. Too many reporters, too many writers, too many media members think that they are going to feed you something you don't want. You should want this. So, I'm going to feed it to you. Oh, guess what? They're not going to consume it. Curiosity aligns with the curiosity of the audience. Now, the the best will take something that maybe the audience wouldn't be curious about and make it compelling. But, in this case, curiosity in motion. There are rabbit holes from time to time. The Shanahan situation creates a rabbit hole. There are leads to follow. There are questions to ask. There are things to possibly answer because of the way it was handled. And I had a reader make an interesting point today. Is it possible that there really isn't anything in the rabbit hole and that this is just the 49ers trying to be Belichickian? We're treating it all like a state secret because we're going to treat everything like it's a state secret. We're going to gratuitously be secretive. I don't know that that's a good approach. It doesn't do much to endear you to the people who cover you unless you win. And if you win, it doesn't matter. And the 49ers win, but not like the Patriots did. The 49ers are 32 years removed now from their last Super Bowl championship. But, I don't know what the purpose is, but the way that it was handled creates speculation. It invites suspicion. And for those who put curiosity in motion there is a reason to at least see where that curiosity may lead. Hi, it's Mike Florio. Thanks for watching PFT on YouTube. Hit subscribe for the latest news and analysis from Pro Football Talk.

What other differences have you noticed so far this year than Mike McCarthy's year rather than last year with Tom Cable? >> Um I think the biggest difference for me is it's offensive coach. That's the first time I've had that in my career. So, uh just seeing how you know, when the defense messes up, it's all right, next play. But when the offense messes up, uh we get to go again. So, I've never, you know, had that in my career. Um and uh I think he's still trying to get his feet wet with you know, his messaging and wording. Uh you know, I think with Mike T, we we were so used to you know, a negative day or you know, his sayings, but um I'm looking forward to you know, how he carries himself, the messaging for this year, um and you know, how how he calls plays on offense. >> Any Mike McCarthy is anything you've heard yet repeating? >> Uh no, I I I can't find any right now. They The team meetings are like 5 10 minutes right now. So, uh I'm looking for them to you know be linking them starting today. >> DK, what's this like going into a year or two with Aaron? You're you're teammates again this year. Last year was about getting acclimated with each other. What what's the next step for you and Aaron together? >> Yes, sir. I think since we were you know he was 50 years old and I was 10. Um you know we were kind of like trying to get used to the dynamic of everything. He was in a new place. I was in a new place. I think right now our communication is far beyond where it was last year when we first got to camp. He was at you know a couple OTA practice. So was I. So I think you know we're just leaps ahead of the communication aspect how we view each other, how we communicate on and off the field right now. So I just think that that was the biggest step you know the biggest difference that I seen from last year. And I think it's just only going to continue to grow. >> DK, what's it DK in that being what's it like when you're going into a season where Aaron Rodgers has said it's going to be his last? >> I mean people just say things at the beginning of the year not knowing you know how a year could go. He may not even get hit or touched this year and may say hey let's go out there and do another one. So I mean it just puts a weight off his back like you know he's just out there playing free enjoying possibly his last year with his teammates with a couple of close friends that he's made over the past 2 years. So I think it's just a lot of weight off his shoulders right now. He's just going out there playing free. >> Y'all don't have to play rock, paper, scissors for this one. >> Here Chris you go ahead. >> Thank you. DK, I know that you you only got to spend OTAs and mini camp you know working in this offense but can do you see a difference in just the schematic of how differently that it's going to set you guys up as a wide receiver room in the passing attack to more opportunities. Does that excite you? >> Um I think it excites me cuz it's all on paper right now. Um but until real bullets start flying and we get in the actual game or team setting to where, you know, DBs can go after the ball, defenses can really uh compete for the football. Um I think it's going to be different. So, I can't say for right now, but on paper, yes, I'm very excited. >> You mentioned that your bond is way ahead of I mean, I can battle everybody. the bond with you and Aaron way ahead of where it was last year. You guys are working on your dynamic and you did a bonding week, pass catchers and Aaron out in the wild west. What do you guys get out of a week like that? >> Uh I mean, you take the shoulder pads and helmets off and you get to see people for, you know, who they are on a day-to-day basis instead of, you know, the persona or the the, you know, the mask that we put on for for the field. Um I got to like I said, I got to know Pittman very well, Rome, Pat, Sko, um Mason and Aaron. We all, you know, took off our masks and we really just talked ball, talked personal life, talked everything with each other and uh I mean, that can only make you closer cuz off the off the field, you got a brother, but on the field, like that's that's my boy. Like nobody's going to touch him, nobody's going, you know, harm him. I'm going to sacrifice everything that I got to do just to go catch this ball for him. So, um I think just makes that bond that much deeper. >> Is the cowboy hat going to become a regular look? >> No. That was just I found it in the store cuz I and threw it on. I thought it looked cool. >> You mentioned the offense changing some on paper. Is your role the same? When you look at that paper, are you being used any any differently this year? >> Like I said, man, that's a scouting question or a a scheme question for the coaches, not not me. >> Okay, one of the changes is practice is [clears throat] going to be earlier this year than than it was under Mike McCarthy. So, conceivably, it's not going to be as hot. Is that something as players you guys are consider that a welcome change or do you are you one of those guys who likes to be, you know, be tested in those elements, you know, in the heat of the day in August. >> I trained in Mississippi this offseason, so I'm I'm used to the heat. >> Beyond that symmetry that you alluded to there and that you're hoping to build upon, you think you're ahead on that as opposed to last year, what other things did you look back on last year that you're hoping to be better for yourself individually this season? >> Mainly the communication aspect. It was a lot of times to where, you know, he would ask me what routes I want or, you know, early in the week I could have said, "Hey, I I like this route. I don't like this route." Um early on in the week instead of it letting it bleed until Sunday. Um and then we get in the game and, you know, we're both like on eggshells not knowing what the other one's thinking. Um but now it's like an open form of communication. I like X, Y, and Z. He likes X, Y, and Z and we can both move forward. >> Last year when we first got to talk, you talked about how like, you know, guys like Roman Wilson and Calvin Austin, like other guys you said uh you would you'd let them come to you and that's how your leadership style is. You're Is that changed now because you guys are so close that you're not even letting them come to you? You guys are just naturally talking more? >> Correct. Yes, sir. The open the form of communication is open. Um I mean, uh Germaine and uh Caden came to me early. Uh I've seen them talking in the room. They they've opened up very well to the room. Um Max has come to me a bunch this offseason. We would check in with each other. Uh our group message was popping once a week, twice a week, so uh I just think we're all just that much more comfortable with each other. >> DK, after being here last year for training camp, talk about some of the >> Whoa, I used the first You're supposed to be the first one to ask me a question. Riley, where you been? My bad. >> Talk about some of the value of having training camp here at Latrobe. >> Um well, I was drive I got driven here last year, but I drove in yesterday myself. Um and just seeing, you know, the different aspects of Pennsylvania that I I really don't get to see on a daily uh day-to-day basis. I went to Walmart, got to see, you know, people I don't normally see, uh some Latrobeans, uh if you will, or or Steelers fans from, you know, around the state. Um and I think it's just a great aspect just to you know, see other people that that you normally don't get to see and plus people that don't really get to see us during the season. We come all our way to Saint Vincent and just you know, immerse ourselves in this community. Um, and I'm really looking forward to the Friday night lights. I think that was the one of the coolest things that we did last year. Um, the family day. I think this is just like a great organization and how they do things for training camp. Um, just letting other people you know, get to feel the Steelers uh, who don't get to feel them on a day-to-day basis. >> Do you have any fans approach you in Walmart or come up and talk to you? >> Yeah. >> What was that like? >> Oh, it was cool. He was a little shaky but I was like, I'm cool bro. You good. >> DK, what's your early impressions been of just how much Jeremy wants to learn and how he's been on the field even just a practice here? >> Um, I will say bro, these NIL kids are a little too cocky for me. Um, I'm I'm joking. He's a really good dude. Um, he's he's excited about the rookie gifts. He's excited about learning. Uh, he's excited about being in the offense, being in the room. He's very open, very honest uh, off the rip as soon as I met him. So, um, just looking forward to you know, spending more time with him during the season, see how he works on the field. Um, and yeah, we can we can both learn from each other. >> All right, DK. >> Last one. >> Uh, the Steelers and Saint Vincent have had quite the uh, the history over the decades. How does it feel that you are not only practicing but also training in the same facility and the same ground that so many other Steelers legends have all trained? >> Like I said, it's a great organization, a historic franchise. Um, you know, Santonio Holmes, one of the I remember watching that uh, that Super Bowl game. James Harrison who I've got to got to know very well. Ike Taylor is a like you said, a lot of great players, a great great people but as well that have played for this organization. Um, and they are always willing to pour back into us and into the younger players. So, uh, that's one thing that I I'm very thankful, uh, you know, to be here, um, in this historic franchise and, um, in this historic historic place who, you know, the great players have practiced on this field, uh, who I can just walk on there and, you know, try to mimic their steps, um, and be great as well. So, just looking forward to that.

title: Coach Mike McCarthy Press Conference (July 28) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: You guys missed everybody missed the raetball court, I'm sure. >> All right, we'll have coach open up a few comments and we'll open up for questions. Coach, >> good morning everyone. It's great to see everybody. Um, you obviously training camp is here. Uh, obviously my one of my favorite personal time favorite times of year. Uh, first want to acknowledge, you know, St. Vincent's College. Uh, they they've they've knocked it out of the park. Uh, just to set up, you know, coming up here in the spring. I think we're up here on three different occasions, you know, especially to being year one. Um, and they've just done a phenomenal job of everything that's that's asked. Obviously, the history here, uh, just to see this thing develop from, you know, being up here as a kid in the late '7s. But, uh, the new indoor facilities outstanding. Uh, actually had to use it, uh, this morning for our mo our mobility workout. So, uh, we've completed that with the players. Uh, so everything went smooth there. But, um, excited to be here. It's a great setup. I mean, the function of it, uh, just the way it flows, you know, 21 days of of being here in LRO are critical for us. I look at these as foundation days, and, uh, we couldn't have a better setting for that. So, uh, coming out of the spring, our goal in the offseason program was really just to get the the schematic volume and the communication and language, common language, and all that. I felt I felt our guys did a really nice job situationally. Um, I thought we got off to a good start, but that this is this is where it really starts up here. So, we have the first week uh with the ramp up that the whole league has to do. So, we'll start that tomorrow. Uh, so the limited practices, you know, more meeting times, more walkthroughs and things like that. And then, uh, we'll get going Monday, um, with the first padded practice with the McAfee show here. So, I know everybody's excited about that. So, it'll be a great atmosphere. Um, but it's uh it's here and it's a phenomenal opportunity for our guys. Uh, so far it just the preliminary [snorts] conversations as far as, you know, the health of our team. Uh, you know, we have two players on on PUP. Uh, so, uh, frankly, the the progress that a number of our guys made over the summer and over these last five weeks has has been better than expected. So, feel really good about the overall health of the 90man roster and u looking forward to getting started here. So, anything else, Bert? >> Nope. That's it. >> Okay. >> Questions? >> I'm trying to act like we're connected here. So, trying to improve my relationship. >> How important is it to get up to speed really quickly here in camp? >> Get up to speed. Uh I I think the biggest thing for for you know, for me, the expectation is, you know, is the is the competition. You know, this is your you got to establish your play style. You know, the identity of the Pittsburgh Steelers is, you know, is identified back in the 1970s. So, you don't get to just carry that forward. So, you know, this gives you the opportunity to get the competition level where it needs to be. You know, get as close to the fire as you possibly can. Uh, the connection is very important. Group dynamics through training camp. I mean, being in a dorm room and and [snorts] having, you know, cinder block walls, it's been a minute for me personally. So, I mean, it's first night of sleep was good. Uh, so just the whole, you know, environment for these guys to be around each other. I think it's important. you see the guys riding their bikes uh to the fir, you know, to the, you know, first [snorts] workout over or first meeting over there to the gymnasium area. So, just all those things are are part of a camp atmosphere, but it'll always be about the depth of the details. I mean, this this is why we're here. We're we're we're here to to come together as a football team, and it's always the depth of the details because that's it's the little things. It's the little things you can't really work on in the spring. Really, the little things you can't even work on till you get to next week. uh because the little things turn into big things and that's on both sides of the fence. So um you know we try to train in a perfect environment uh but you don't achieve greatness with perfection. You know the football is 11 on 111. Uh you have to overcome adversity from one player one play to the next and all. So this is the close as close to the fire as we can get and uh so that's really what I'm looking forward. >> All your players have referenced detail of your coaches. How long have you been maniacal about that thing and why? >> Um, you know, I think it's probably, you know, I think like a lot of us, it's it's, you know, goes back to how you're raised. Um, I've been over the top blessed with the the coaches that I've been able to to learn from. Um, the the veteran players that I've been able to learn from as a young coach. So, you know, and I could give you, you know, there's so many quotes. One that's always stuck in my mind from Marty Shottimer is you know when times of crisis think of players not plays and that's I think so much is made of scheme but the rel you know the relative uh part of scheme is it's you know a lot of us run the same plays as far as how it looks conceptually draws up but it's taught differently the techniques the detail the connection the timing the time clocks you know all those things so um I think that's football I I think that's sports you know uh we all look at something tend to see it a little differently. Uh so um and success first comes from being consistent. You know, we got to be consistent in everything we do. We we want to knock on the door every single year to bring the Super Bowl trophy home. We're not just trying to win one more. We're trying to win them all. I mean, if if you're going to take that approach, that's not a quote, that's an example, okay? That's that's a you know, trying to make a point here. But, uh you have to have that consistency in your detail. Mike Omar talked just told us, you know, Broadick's expected to practice tomorrow. Uh, as far >> Yeah, Broadick Jones. Um, and saying that, you know, we want to be safe with his per progress and and making taking steps forward. What is the urgency for you guys to get him back involved and be able to evaluate him to see if he can start again for you guys being a a first round pick here? >> Well, that's that's one of the guys, you know, I talked about that. That was great news uh to see that he was cleared by both, you know, by both doctors. So that that was excellent. I speak I think it speaks volume for Brick and what he's he's been doing here the last couple months. Um so I I just think like anything, you know, when when a player comes off off of the medical clearance, I mean, it's, you know, you can't just go to 100 mph. So, um and I think you'll see that in how his reps go and so forth. But, you know, Brick is a, you know, start start. He's been a starter here. He gives us position flex. Um we have nine, you know, 90man roster. I'm looking for 68 guys to come out of this. Uh that that's, you know, my goal is always when I'm in training camp is, you know, 68 players. You know, obviously 53 players on the active roster, but you know, Brick is, you know, he's a starter. He's a start starter level player. Uh he has position flexibility and that's how we'll get him started. >> That position flex. Do you imagine envision using him primarily at right or or left or how do you kind of develop? We're going to work him back in, you know, so and um that'll be identified as we get going here. >> Mike, what's the impact of not having Jaylen the first couple of weeks, Ramsey the first couple of weeks in are there concerns as you get closer to the season? >> I would say there's concerns. Um, you know, I I think once once again, you talk about, you know, a great player. I've always admired Jaylen from from across the field. Uh but he's, you know, he's he's wired like a coach, you know, so his his involvement, his engagement is is going to be important not only just not not really for him because, you know, we all need it because, you know, he wants to be out there and uh but really the connection with the others. I mean, it's this thing's not about 11 on 111, especially in the defensive backfield. You know, he he's a multiple position player. So, um but we got to be smart. You know, he's played a lot of football. Um, you know, we want to have a hell of a camp, you know, physicality, you know, stressing, you [snorts] know, hitting the stress points that we want to hit. We we want to we want to be smart about it, but we want to take all the football with us. You know, we don't want to leave anything back here. So, that's that's that's what I think about when I'm thinking about does a guy go, you know, how hard, you know, what are you going to do in this drill? I think I've been fortunate. I think I've done every drill in football. So, you know, which drills you do, you know, the science behind the drills, you know, how the players fit in that. So, th those are the conversations you have continuous. And, you know, and you got to be smart with with your players. >> DK us when DK talked to us, you talked about the connectivity with Aaron Rogers and the the conversations and communication with him being better this year in year two. Once the ball is snapped though, like what have you studied from DK that you see that you can get even more out of him in year two as a Steeler? >> Oh, I think you know, number one, you just start with his router. You know, he he's he's a matchup problem. You know, if you you put him on the back side of 3x1, you know, you better help him back. You better get some help for him. So, you know, want to want to move him around a little more, you know. So, um, but you can see that their time clock is, you know, you know, being being new, them two played here last year, and I know it was their first year, but I was impressed with their with their timing together in in the spring in the OTAAS. So, we just want to continue to continue to grow off of that because DK can change games. >> Mike, will you guys tackle uh team drills? >> Will we tackle team drills? We won't do live tackling. No, I've done live tackling in the past. Um, and I think it was kind of where I touched on just briefly is, you know, every drill's every drill's been evaluated. Uh, there's a GCPS component be behind everything that we do. Uh, you know, there's more stress that we need to apply to our to to our training situations and just going to the ground. The footwork's the priority always will be about the feet and and everything that we do with our tackling, blocking, [snorts] you know, ball security, all those things. So the the footwork component about it is important. You have to assess stress in everything you do. That's that's I look at as one of the primary responsibilities of being a head coach and one of the primary focal points of being in charge of a training regimen for your football team. So uh tackling is is a good way to go. I've done it. Um, but I feel like, you know, we'll be able to get it done in in other, you know, ways of training, particularly in our tackling drills, uh, in the team drills. So, uh, injuries are part of the game, you know, and I think you clearly got to do the best you can and it's a jud it's a judgment. U, you try to reduce risk. So, but we will not live tackle. Uh, we will have goal line, but we won't we won't live tackle. And that's, you know, that's that's one of the harder drills to get that done, you know. So, um, but we will definitely save that for the preseason games. >> Why do Mike, why, uh, I'm sorry, over here. >> What's, uh, your philosophy in terms of practicing in maybe more the middle of the day as opposed to late afternoon when it's usually, at least in this part of country, it's hotter than it is maybe at noon, 1:00. >> Um, I I I I'm make sure I understand what you're trying to ask me. You're going from like 11:30 to 1:30 and that's historically what you've done. I'm just wondering is there a philosophy behind having practice maybe at that time of day? >> Yeah. I mean your philosophy on it because that's the way I've done it. Um this setup is very similar. >> Um there's a lot that goes into it. You know um how much time you have between the meetings. I I believe I don't believe in just having a plan and dusting off. There's there's a systematic approach to everything that we do. Um I I like to get up in the morning. I I believe in regularity. That's the way my father raised me. You get your get your heavy lifting done in the morning. You get up, you get them going. So we have our first team meeting will be at 7:30. I believe in starting early. Uh we want to get in there. We want to have our meetings. Um, the commitment that we've had in the offseason gives us the ability to not meet as long in the mornings because the guys they did the work in the spring. Uh, they they paid the price of of learning this scheme. So, we'll be more like when I talk to the team, we won't install, we'll recall. All right? So, we'll have a recall meeting in the morning. Uh, we'll have a walk through over there in the gymnasium and then we'll get up and go get it. Let's let's go. Let's go practice because that's that's the most important part of the day is when we hit that practice field. So, That's why we practice when we practice. If if I felt like they were ready to go and I could have everybody all 90 ready, I'd practice at 7:30 because it's the pri it's the priority. I mean, that's that's the most most important thing we do is practice. So, let's get them in there. Let's get them ready. Let's get out there and get it. And so, then you got to have the rest recovery component into it. Plus, the you know, you'll see more video cameras out there than you've ever seen. All right. So, capturing that video is critical to this environment. So, we'll get the players a chance to go, you know, wait room, lunch, coaches will watch the tape, and then that's probably the second most important part of the day is watching that tape. It's the best video of the year. It's the best video of the year. You'll we'll be cutting this video up for training camps, training camps, offseason program for as long as I'm here. There'll be there'll be plays and schemes and situations that'll happen out here in the next 21 days we'll be able to able to teach off of for a long time. That's been my experience. So point is let's practice. That's why I practice at 11. And I I want to have plenty of time to watch that tape and then when we're done we want to go walk through it one more time. And the CBA has been awesome because they only give you 11 hours to do it, you know. So, we're going to get that done and then get them off to dinner and then they got the night to to do their thing. >> When you're expect from a backup quarterback competition, >> what what should we expect? >> Backup quarterback competition. >> Well, I think the obvious, you know, we have four quarterbacks and I know that's been the precedent here. They they've give carried four in camp uh for a while. Uh I've I've done both. I've been more three in camp since the uh you know the CBA the training um because it is tougher to get the get the reps in the uh in the team periods and seven on sevens just because because of the numbers. Um the quarterback score really helps us you know the we have a we have mock games that we do later in the day that helps. Um we we call two spot where you work two at a time so that definitely helps. Um, but yeah, they're, you know, Aaron will take the ones, you know, Mason will start out with with the second group and and Drew and or Will and Drew will we'll take the, you know, take that third group rep. So, that's that's the way we'll start. Um, and we'll just, you know, we'll just watch as we go. I I' I'd really like the room. Uh I've never really looked at it as you know second and third and for I've you know you got to get your starter ready you know and the responsibility to get the starter ready is not only on the quarterback coach and the play caller but it's also on the other quarterbacks you know and then the starter's responsibility is to make sure those other three are connected because the room has to we we got to move the room along. Okay we know what the starter can do. Okay but we got to make sure he's ready to go. So he's he's got to get his reps and if it's 50% great. If it's 40, awesome. And if it's 60, that's what it'll be. Obviously, with his relationship, our relationship and his experience level, you know, that's, you know, he he's going to have a hand in that. So, um, but we need to get the other three to to grow, especially the two young puppies. So, um, that that'll be the approach. >> Is keeping four an option? >> I'm sorry. >> I don't know why it wouldn't be. >> You're not philosophically opposed? I'm all philosophically opposed of keeping the best players. That that's to me that's the hardest day for a head coach, you know, because when you get down to 53 and and it's a great spot to be in and you're sitting there and you got 54 55 hopefully in great a really good year, you got 58 guys, you say this is how I do it. They've always thought as like who who deserves to be on a 53 and then then then now you gota you got to figure out you know who's 54 and who's 55 who maybe perform better than 51 52 and 53. So um that's why you have camp that's why we're up here to compete. That's what the 21 days will give us a great look into that too. So, um, I think all four of those guys, you know, if you're picking a team today, would be definitely part of that 53 conversation. >> When you're in your >> What's most important to what's most important for you to establish here as you begin your >> I mean, so much uh so much cuz it's year one, you know, it's it's a, you know, our process number one, but the the systems that run the process, we we have to get the systems taught. Everybody does it a little differently. It's It's never exactly the same. So, uh, I have to do a really good job of communicating, making clear, you know, making it clear every single day what the expectations are. Uh, doing the corrections, make sure we continue to grow. Um, creating opportunities. You know, you you know, there's always there's always times where you feel like you may not have created enough opportunity for a certain guy or two. That that's always a big challenge at training camp. Um, just think about some of the things I was, you know, looking at yesterday. Uh, so just just hitting all those targets. But I I think the biggest thing is is is to come out of here ready to win games. You know, that's with the the, you know, the the competitive nature. Uh, because when I get when I get down to the the real stuff, there's two things I really only care about is is the play style of my football team and the production. And that's how you win. So everything that goes into getting that, that's that'll that's what I'll be grinding on. Aaron said during OTAAS [cough] that this would be his last year. This would probably be his last year playing. We just talked to DK Metaf and he said, "Well, that's just something guys say maybe he doesn't get hit and he wants to come back another year." Are you approaching this like it's his last season, like it's Aaron's last season? >> Um, you know, you know, I I think those conversations are are really so personal. I I think, you know, obviously known him since the beginning. Um, you know, I when you get to that point in life and you get into the fourth quarter of a career, um, you do reflect and and I think he's he's he's just, you know, those are honest answers to your question. So, um, but yeah, I I can't speak on on, you know, where where exactly he is. But, you know, I think the biggest thing is um, you know, where he's at in life and, you know, I've watched him grow and, you know, both, you know, personally and professionally. And, you know, his personal life is is is growing. And, you know, and this is such a selfish selfish profession. I mean, let's be honest. Um, you know, my youngest is 15 today. I'm missing a birthday party to hang out with this Jagoff, you know.
