title: T.J. Watt Press Conference (July 28) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Heat. Heat. N. down. Heat. Heat. [laughter] football in the back. >> Good. Okay. Go ahead, >> TJ. What's What's it >> How's it different? Does it feel different with with Mike? The mics hadn't switched. >> Yeah. I mean, there's just a lot of unknown. Obviously, the schedule's going to be new. Um, a lot of new players on top of it as well, but I think the bones are still the same. Obviously, we're still here. um the camaraderie, all those little things are still the same, but uh there's going to be a lot of uh testing the waters type of um action going on over the next couple weeks, but at the end of day, it's football. TJ, are there any conversations between you, Cam, and like other like, you know, long-standing leaders of the defense of like things that you guys have wanted to make sure you continue to implement with Patrick Graham, or is that you guys just kind of feeling this out as it goes? a little bit, but I think the spring was and the summer was more so about him introducing his system and um his what he what he expects out of his defenses um what he likes, what he doesn't like, and then this fall time is when we can kind of make that a cohesive unit and try to get all on the same page. >> He was talking about having an offensive head coach for the first time in his career in a positive way. It'll be the other way for you. What do you anticipate that being like? >> I'm not sure, honestly. I mean, obviously the the summer was different just from everybody feeling each other out and seeing uh how the day-to-day operation was going to go. Um Mike T was around the defense a lot as you guys know. Um I I it really doesn't matter to me where the head coaches as long as we're all on the same page. And it's not like u PG can't do can't uh shoulder all the responsibilities of getting our defense ready to go. >> TJ, how much do you embrace the new >> I I embrace it, man. This is year 10. This is I feel like I'm first day of school for me, first day of everything. So, um still same dorm room, same uh eating in the same spot, same weight room, stuff like that. But there's still so much new that uh it keeps it exciting, keeps it fresh. >> You guys just had your conditioning test in years past. It's been late afternoon, move in day. Any other changes, differences to that conditioning test? >> No, I slept here last night, which is new. Uh I just didn't want to mess with fighting traffic or any opportunity to be late on my first day. Um, so a night away from the family wasn't fun, but uh you got to do what you got to do this time of year. >> How how do you anticipate the rotation with you and Alex and Nick? Obviously, the organiz organization just gave a lot of money to Nick for for the next five years. How do you anticipate that dynamic working? Not just just how do you see it working? >> Very dynamic, very elite group. I think you're going to see us moving all around. I know I say it every year, but I think you're truly going to see us moving all around this year. Um, I mean, it's it's a better problem to have when you have guys that are really capable to affect the game um in any asset uh in in any area. And I think that um if we do things that we really set out to do in this training camp and get this thing like a welloiled machine with us three, um it'll be special. Building off that TJ, you admitted during mini camp, you used the word in the past maybe you've been a little bit stubborn about moving around and this system doesn't allow you to be stable that you have to be moved around. So, how have you found that in the time since mini camp as you looked about looked at it and thought about how it would be implemented in September? Uh just being open-minded. Um just trying to do anything that I possibly can to affect um whether it's how they are doing protection schemes, how they're running the ball, wherever I can move um around or just knock down inside, be able to allow Herb to come outside. Um whatever it takes to win football games, whatever it takes to mess up the offensive scheme, I'm willing to do. >> Do you evolve your game at all now? Like you're in your 30s, 10th season. Do you do you do things differently? Do you do you play more cerebrally? Is there anything different or >> I don't know. I don't I don't think so. >> TJ, how's the new indoor facility been treating you and the rest of the team? >> It was nice. Obviously, we only got a short look at I think we're only over there for 15 20 minutes, but uh it's a really nice facility. It's been a long time coming, but I'm glad that we have somewhere to go when it rains now. >> Is your mindset any different this year? >> Trying to win the Super Bowl every year. I don't think that's changed. >> But personally, the approach change at all of anything? >> No. [clears throat] Have you guys >> have you guys talked about with the coaching staff about elements of the practices at training camp that you want to think like any specific drills or focus points that you're like, "Hey, this has worked for us. We'd like to continue to see this." >> No. >> TJ, one of the changes has been practice is going to be be ended earlier. It's not going to be maybe in the full heat of the day. Is it >> is that as a player, does it matter? I mean, I'm Mike T seem to lean into that and like that. I mean, >> I'm I'm here no matter what. So, I don't really care what time we practice. Um, as long as there's breakfast, lunch, and dinner, I'm I'm cool. Um, but no, I really don't care what time we practice. Obviously, we play at all different times throughout the year, so it doesn't matter to me. >> I know you said you got here yesterday. It seems like a few of the other guys did, too. Did the majority of you guys get here yesterday? Did anyone come today? >> I got in late last night, so I really didn't see many other guys. Um, but the parking lot was full, so I'm sure it was a good amount of people here. >> TJ, I know Nick's been coming up to Wisconsin with you for a while. I think Jack came up and joined this year. I think Riley was even saying he was trying to make it up there. How fun has it been to have more guys kind of follow in line >> with you the older you get in your career and these workouts and in Wisconsin kind of becoming stuff guys are seeking out. >> Yeah, it's special. I mean, I saw Riley's been up there. He's from the area, so he was up there before um the draft and was able to be able to work out with him throughout the summer. Obviously, Jack and Herb, we had like 20 NFL guys. It was the biggest group we've ever had um for the summer up in Wisconsin. It was just a blast, man, to be able to I mean, for me, I always had my brothers to look up to and to ask those questions for and obviously Herb has an older brother who's done it as well. But, um, just to be able to offer up as much as I can to those younger guys to be able to help them grow, whether on the field, whether off the field, I'm willing to do. Um, like I said, especially if they're a Steeler, I'm trying to do anything we possibly can to win the Super Bowl. And to be able to see the growth, to be able to work out and bust chops in the summer. I mean, it's just so much fun. What sense have you gotten of how Patrick Graham looks at the edge position in the three four? He's got you want a ring as a linebacker coach in the past. So, how does he view you guys on the edge as opposed to maybe how Mike and Coach Austin have seen it in the past? >> I mean, I think at the end of the day, it's three four defense Pittsburgh Steelers. I think it's very dynamic group. I mean, we're going to be moving around like I said and um just trying to keep offenses on their toes so we can't be too predictable. >> I know you watch a ton of film. How how much have you kind of watched how PG used Max Crosby and moved him around and how do you think that could kind of fit with the three of you guys uh going there ahead? >> Yeah, we've watched a good admit a good bit of um uh Raiders film, a little bit of Patriots film as well, but obviously we have different personnel. Um some of the calls are same, some of the calls are different, but uh it is nice to see a dynamic player in the system um to see how he um kind of went about each and every call and what kind of freedoms he had on certain calls. TJ, for you personally, what was your biggest focus, biggest goal this off season? >> Uh, I think for me it was just getting back to work. I I think I I really enjoy the process of trying to find ways where I can continue to get better and grow throughout the offseason. And um like I said earlier, it's just so much fun to have guys that are in the locker room come up and train. Um to be able to push you and have that camaraderie. Um just really enjoying the process this summer was huge. You said you're already about having a different coach. Is there something like an adrenaline to the change in kind of outside of your comfort level the last nine years? Is that something that kind of >> you feel? And >> I'm excited. I really am. I This is my 10th year in the NFL, man. This is places I don't know if I ever thought I would truly be now. I'm just really enjoying it. Trying to play balls to the wall every single snap, take in every moment, and uh just embrace it. There's no time to have negativity, no time to be bashing the new. I'm just trying to embrace it and um lead by example and have fun. >> PJ, what have you seen from the growth of Alex from, you know, seven years ago when he got here to now? >> Oh, his Bobby Buchche has gotten a lot better. [laughter] >> I I think with Alex is he's he's grown so much. I mean, first coming in, he was just a cross chop guy. He didn't he was a hand in there might used to call him a a 4-3 defensive end. Um he's really filled out well. He's got a great spin move. Um, plays the run extremely well. Has a great shot and shed. Um, and a great teammate. Really good locker room guy. We'll be here in the next 10 or 15 minutes playing NHL in his room. Um, just a great teammate, a great football player. >> He's here for the third time in five years. It looks like the first round pick is going to line up against you a good bit. What do you like about that part of training camp and how you sort of embraced helping young guys on the other side get better as you get older? Yeah, I mean I worked with Troy a good amount in the years past as well and just trying to get them up to speed as quick as possible, but it's also cool for me because they play me so differently um because they're bringing those what they were taught in college to the NFL. So, um those are always fun battles. >> TJ, Coach Tomlin not being around, can you give us a story that reflect back your favorite camp story? >> There's too many to count, honestly. I don't know. I used to walk around on edge like crazy when Mike T was here, man. I I'll never forget like one of my first camps, we were just talking on the hallway and he was all cool. How's your family? How's everything? And I knew I had like a bad rep or two at practice and he was talking like nothing happened. I was cool. He forgot about it. We go in front of the whole team and he's like, "Wow, what the hell are you doing?" I'm like, "What? We were just cool out in the hallway and now you're you're you're killing me in the team meeting." So, it's just things like that like you were you could never really be like calm. He never knew if you're going to be on the big board. And that's what I really really appreciated about him is he didn't care if you were a first year guy, if you're a 10ear guy, if you lost a rep, he was going to give the guy who beat the vet um his flowers if if it was the other way around. You just never knew if you're going to be up on that big board. So, it was always nerves going into those meetings. >> Every coach is different. What have you learned about what Mike McCarthy's approach might be with that kind of thing? >> Um, I don't know. I mean, honestly, it's the summer is just so different because it's not as intense. So, I'll have a better answer for you here in the fall once we get um some of those serious competition periods going and see um what those team meetings are like. >> Good. >> Thanks, guys. Heat. Heat. Heat. Heat. Heat. [music] [music]

title: Omar Khan Press Conference (July 28) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: All right, guys. Questions for Omar? >> Uh I'm good to go. Get started here? Oh, okay. Great to see everyone, man. This is This is truly an awesome time. I I I love being up here at training camp. Um this is uh I think this is my 24th one here in Latrobe, and it's they've all been very special and anticipating this one being a special one also. Uh I I want to start by just just thanking this community and you know, Father Paul and everyone at Saint Vincent for uh allowing us to be here and for welcoming us. It's It's uh It's It's It's special. As you guys all know, this is the people here are great. You know, I just I went to Walmart last night and got some stuff and ran into a lot of the locals, and it's It's just It's just great catching up with everyone and being here. Um obviously uh you know, coach and I have been working together uh nonstop. It's been a grind since we started, but it's been a lot of fun. I It's uh It's It's been great hearing, you know, about new ideas and, you know, sharing how how we can do things uh how we can improve in certain things, and you know, us getting to know them, them getting to know us. A lot of new faces here uh but it's uh It's It's been fun, and I'm excited, and uh um and, you know, look forward to you guys kind of getting to know every all the new faces a little bit more, and um uh we're we're ready to go. Um I'll touch on a couple things here. First of all, the injuries. Uh you know, we're going through our conditioning some of the conditioning stuff right now, so I'll have more information later in the day, but right now I anticipate Dante Kent starting on PUP. Uh probably uh Jaylen Ramsey will also start on PUP. Uh Jaylen had a injury he suffered during the mini camp. Uh he's recovering, just probably be a couple weeks if I had to guess on on his return. Um but other than that, that'll be it. You guys asked me about Broderick. Broderick's done a a good job of getting better. Uh he's in a good place and uh uh he's been cleared to go. Obviously, we're going to be smart in terms of how we progress him, but um you guys will see him out there on uh on Wednesday. Um with respect to any of the contract stuff, you guys know we're not going to discuss it. Nothing's eminent right now with anyone. Uh but if something happens, you know, we'll obviously let you guys know. Uh but with that said, um feel great about this team. Uh really enjoyed uh getting to know this this coaching staff and some of the other staff that we have here and uh we're ready to go. Feel good. So, open up to any questions here. >> What's the nature of uh Jaylen's injury? >> He had a uh a knee injury during mini camp and um you know, we're just going to be smart about it and he's a pro and um you guys know how hard he works and uh probably if I had to guess, like I said, right be a couple weeks. >> One more uh I know you're not like wanting to talk about contracts and everything, but how motivated are you to possibly get extensions done with some of your internal guys? I know you've already got a couple done with Herbig and Darnell. Uh Joey's going in the last year of his deal. How motivated are you to try to get something done there? >> Yeah, you know, it's um uh it's a good question. I mean, we we uh obviously feel good about some of these young players and we always talk about, you know, drafting, uh developing and uh and extending our guys and um you know, we'll see we'll see how it goes. Obviously, there's an interest in in keeping a bunch of those guys here for a long time and uh we got like you mentioned, we got a couple of those guys done and there's nothing eminent right now, but um you know, I like to keep them all if I could. I know it's not realistic that you can do that the way the cap works, but um you know, we'll we'll see. >> That would almost be a good problem to have where you had a good draft class where so many guys are up and so many guys that are relevant. Like some of these you only have one or two. >> It's a great situation to be in, obviously, you know, and I love perfect world, you'd like to get everybody. It doesn't happen that way, but yeah, it's it's good spot to be in. You feel good about it. >> new ideas. Any of them in particular get your attention or seem like a ideas? >> Um let's see here. What what could I share with you? Um You know, Mike and I have known each other for a long time. So, you know, even before he came on board, we would we would talk about different things and nothing really specific that I'd want to share publicly, but I can tell you like you know, you guys will see some of the changes over the next you know, the way practice things happen at practice um um logistics you know probably uh you know, things are going to tighten up in certain areas and you guys will see it, but it'll all all good. >> Did Jaylen's knee injury require surgery? >> No. >> Omar, you said nothing imminent. Some of the these guys' peers are are getting contracts. Is there a concern that the longer you wait, the cost of business keeps going up? >> You know, it's just the nature of the beast, but we you know, we we understand where we are and you know, we have communication. We we know how the process works, but um um at the end of the day, you know, we we can only go so far with with certain negotiations and you know, see where it goes. >> Did Joey or his reps let you know if he'll be participating or holding in this the start camp? >> You know, I'm not going to go into uh specifics of that, but I you know, I expect anybody that's healthy and able to practice to practice. >> Omar, how do you find reps for four quarterbacks in this short amount of time to be pretty numbers? >> Yeah, that's that's that's a good question. You know, first of all, we have four guys that we feel good about and you know, I'll let coach address some of that, but um you know, we're we're in a good position there. We have four guys that we really uh that we really feel good about. Obviously, those young guys you want to get them some reps here and and that's important to see where those those guys are and see how they develop. You know, Aaron's a vet, Mason's a vet. Um but you know, we'll I'll let coach address more of that when you guys get him. >> With the with the secondary, you guys made some some changes bringing in a couple players and now I guess there's obviously a little bit of a question mark with Jaylen Ramsey. How do you feel just about the depth and where you're at there? And is that an area that you could continue to add to going forward? >> Yeah, you know, I wouldn't say, you know, the concern is is is I mean, I with Jaylen, you know, we're just going to be smart about it. He's a pro, you know, it's going to be a couple weeks. Um you know, this isn't something where we anticipate him not being ready for the season. Uh so, but you know, this this is it's camp's exciting at that position just cuz, you know, we have an opportunity to get J'Mar Dean on the field. He'll be out there. Darnell Savage, you know, Echols, uh you know, Deshaun Elliott you know, uh will be out there. And and those guys, I'm not we'll we'll we'll be smart about how we work those guys and and get them ready, but uh you know, we feel good about the the depth we had and the group we had uh in the offseason and still feel good about it today. >> I'm talking about Mike McCarthy. You mentioned obviously the previous relationship you have with him, but working with him in this capacity you guys have worked together up to this point. What have you learned? >> Um It's a good question. Um you know, uh his a uh his attention to detail has not changed since since I worked with him 25, 26, whatever what would was that would have been 2026 years ago. You know, I when I when I left I when I left New Orleans, I remember uh that year that I spent with that with that staff and he was there just just how how detailed they were and um that that hasn't changed and it's it's it's been uh great great to see. >> Rodgers being medically cleared to practice, does he need still to get into that football shape or or strength-wise from being out so long before he can seriously get into >> Yeah, I'm not sure about strength-wise, but uh condition You know, we'll be smart about it. You know, we're just we're just going to see him here. Actually, right now they're they're going they're they're going through some of that stuff. We'll see where he's at. Um but he's been working hard uh trying to get ready for it, but we'll be smart about it. But yeah, we're not going to, you know, rush it if we don't have to. >> Omar, two things on the receivers. Uh I know in this setting last couple years we've asked you about maybe trying to add to that group during camp. And you felt like this year you properly girded yourself at that position as best as you can. And if so, how would Roman's development dovetail with that? >> Yeah, I mean, you guys you guys have heard me talk uh about how I feel about Roman. I I I just feel really good about him. He's been working hard from day one with this staff here. They're they're they're excited about him. Uh to the first part of your question, Tim, um yeah, I feel good about that that position. Not only that position, um but really throughout the roster, you know, I've been here last couple years sometimes and, you know, I've been back in my dorm room here trying to look into ideas of adding guys at different position. I'm not saying we're not we're we're not going to uh or we couldn't at some point, but I just feel really good about where this roster is. I I I really do. I mean, I don't I don't feel like there's a sense of urgency to jump jump into something else, you know, right now. >> Omar, when we talked to you uh at the combine, you talked about, you know, you you would take 20 Darnell Washingtons on your roster. And obviously, you guys resigned him. Is there like an increased emphasis to make sure he finds more places in the offense to impact games or maybe in the red zone or otherwise? you know, I don't know if there's any added pressure to do it. You know, Darnell's worked hard from the day he first day he got here. And we're excited to have him a part of the team. And we're excited we were that we were able to get a deal done with him cuz uh you know, you can do a lot of things with with Darnell Washington. Um and uh gives you a lot of there's a lot of flexibility with the offense when he's in there. But, you know, we'll let the coaches decide how they utilize him. And I'm sure whoever we're playing on a given week will determine uh how we use him. >> Omar, in terms of roster construction, is keeping four quarterbacks doable or or realistic? >> You know, I I is it realistic? Is it doable? I I mean, sure it is, you know, we'll we'll we'll we'll see how how things go through the through the off season and you know, where we are injury wise and it's it's we don't we don't know how things are going to shake out, but you know, obviously want to keep the top 53 guys that are going to help us win this year. >> Right tackle or left tackle for Broderick to start out? >> You know, we'll see how it goes. It's uh it's early I guess we're we're just getting here and part of the process you know, part of the training camp is letting all that stuff sort out. So, we'll let we'll let we'll let we'll let that stuff sort out. You know, I I would I guess not just at the offensive line position, but other positions you know, we'll be trying guys out at different places and it's just part of the process. It's a great opportunity to do it here. >> Aaron said during OTAs that this would be his last year. When we just talked to DK, he said, "Well, you never know. Maybe he doesn't get hit and he wants to come back another year." Are you approaching this like this is Aaron Rodgers' last year? >> Well, you know, I'm approaching it as I'm we're trying to win a championship this year and Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback and you know, we're focused on uh on this year and we'll see how things go in the future. Obviously obviously Aaron will make that decision. Um he spoke publicly about it, but you know, we signed him to a one-year deal, but we're we're just focused on this year winning a championship. >> What does it mean to be part of what could be what he says is his last year? >> Well, obviously his resume speaks for himself for itself, Brooke. He's he's been one of the best quarterbacks of all time and he's been a great leader to have around here and you know, when you're when you're in my shoes, just it's pretty cool to be around great players, um Hall of Fame type players. You know, I've I've I've been blessed to the point where I've been around a lot of these guys and it's never enough. So, anytime you can be around guys like that, it's it's it's it's pretty cool. >> And in the same in the same in the same vein, when a Hall of Fame quarterback says this could be his last year, he's expecting this to be his last year, were you enticed to push push more chips in and try to give him a real chance to to make a run. >> Uh for the Super Bowl you mean? Yeah, I mean we're we're we're we're trying to win a Super Bowl this year. So. >> Omar, yeah, is the indoor facility operational and do you have access to that this year, Kim? >> Yeah, our our uh I think our guys are are because of the the weather conditions our guys are are doing some of the conditioning stuff in there as we speak at actually. >> That'd be a game changer up here for the weather wise? >> Yeah, it's it's great to have. So, today was a good test run for us. You know, we weren't expecting it to rain the way it did and you know, logistically getting guys from up there to down here. So. >> Let's do two more guys if you have them. >> You talked about going to Walmart. Just your everyday going about yourself in terms of talking with people who support the team. I mean, what's the questions you get peppered with the most? Is it Aaron? Is it Super Bowl? Is it new coach? >> Uh you know, obviously with the new coach he him being from Western PA you get that a lot. You know, I get the how's the coach doing or um cuz you know, people know Mike McCarthy he loves Pittsburgh and this Western PA like I'm not sure I've ever met anybody that loves it and I've been hearing about Western PA and Pittsburgh from him since I met him in 2000. So, and I think the people know that. So, I get that question a lot. You know, how's the coach doing? You know, love the love love the uh the the Pittsburgh connection and you know, that's not necessarily why he's here. His resume speaks for itself, but uh I get that a bunch. Um you know, and the the fans are great. You know, they're very supportive and um you know, I think people are excited about the roster and um you know, as as much as we are and uh a lot of new faces and they're trying to get to know these guys just just like we are and um so, Steeler Nation's great. Second to none. >> One more guys, one more. >> Why did the change with Friday night lights moving to to Saturday? >> Yeah, it it was more of a uh uh logistical thing the way it worked out uh on the schedule and um you guys will see our schedule you know our players day off and things are a little different than maybe they've been in the past and that's just sort of how it worked out. I think it's a positive and I think it's just going to be equally as great if not better than it's than it's ever been. >> All right, thanks guys. >> Thanks guys.

title: 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan Takes the Blame for His Car Crash
text: I was streaming this morning and I got a call from the 49ers PR director telling me to come down to the facility right away. Um Kyle Shanahan got on the phone and told me he wanted to talk to me. I thought I was in trouble. I I I drove down immediately, didn't even brush my teeth. I get to the media room, all the beat writers are in there. So, I realized, okay, I'm probably not getting fired. So, we go into Kyle Shanahan's office >> [snorts] >> and he greets us. And I didn't understand what the purpose of the meeting was going to be. He wanted to talk about the crash. Uh he wanted to apparently set the record straight and tell what really happened. And he starts by saying, you know, Grant uh you wrote last night a bunch of details that were wrong. But he didn't blame me. He said, I understand where you got the details. It was in this online database provided by the police department. They got it wrong. They said the other driver was at fault. Kyle said he was at fault. And he was crying. Um he was really upset. The other driver's young. He has kids. One of one of the kids is about as old as the driver, and he was just horrified at what he'd done. He said he, you know, was driving 20 miles an hour, he dropped his phone, he went to to grab it, veered into the other lane. That was that. Um was really upset. And wasn't expecting to see all that, to hear all that. Now, part of the emotion was the concussion that he's suffering from, which is serious, not severe, but serious. And he says that this is something he goes through every day. But the other part of it is the PTSD that he said he's feeling right now because of this crash. How could you not? So, you know, he'll he's going to come back from this from the broken bones and the concussion. But he's also going to have to, probably, I'm saying, go to therapy and talk through this because it's extremely traumatic what happened. And I just want to say that I have so so respect for Kyle Shanahan for setting the record straight. it was killing him that this other person would take the the blame for this. And as soon as that became the public narrative that it was the other person's fault, he set the record straight immediately. And wasn't easy to do. So, I didn't know he was that kind of guy. He's a stand-up guy and I respect him and I appreciate him for handling it the way he did. So, wish him a speedy recovery.

title: Kyle Shanahan just SHOCKED us…
text: I was just in Kyle Shanahan's office at the 49ers facility and he took responsibility for the accident that happened here on Alma Street in downtown PaloAlto. The article is up on the San Francisco Standard, but this is obviously significant stuff since we had a incorrect report yesterday based on an apparently incorrect log that said that the other driver was at fault. But Kyle Shanahan said, and I quote, "I was driving. I was going 20 miles an hour. I was not on my phone, but I dropped my phone and it was stuck in my seat. I took my eyes off the road looking for my phone and my car veered into someone." It's one of those roads where there's no forgiveness. It's one of those roads where I'll teach my kids, you don't drive in the left lane for no reason. You're only allowed a foot. When I hit her, I'll never forget how violent the impact was. So, just stepping out into the road here, you can see that it's two lanes of traffic in each direction. No median, only a double yellow line. Kyle Shanahan was driving southbound, so he's driving this direction the way that the gimbal is moving. And the other driver was driving northbound. According to the PaloAlto Police Department, no impairment was suspected from either driver and no one was cited. Only Shanahan was taken to the hospital. Now, I saw Kyle Shanahan today. Uh he obviously is not looking fully right, but he also showed a picture of himself laying in the hospital bed at at Stanford Hospital where he had a massive massive gash that narrowly missed his eye. And Shanahan said that his plastic surgeon did one hell of a job. So that was two weeks ago and Kyle Shanahan already looks remarkably better now. He says that the concussion is the main problem. The fractures we we've talked about the broken ribs, the broken nose, obviously the laceration on his face, all of that seems secondary to the concussion. He said that it's the noise actually that bothers him the most out on the 49ers practice field and the noise of multiple people talking at once. Shanahan also said, "I was going 20 m an hour. Thank God. I don't know how I would have handled it going twice as fast as that." Now, many may be wondering how the report that that's been circulating online why it says that the other driver was at fault. This was not the PaloAlto Police Department's fault. Apparently, once the police department submitted it to the state of California, there was a clerical error where there are a couple columns and you check mark who is at fault and the other driver was accidentally uh selected to be at fault. Shanahan says that he feels terrible for the other driver now that this has gone fully public with people saying that it was the other driver's fault. So he wanted to bring in a select group of reporters and set the record straight. And I think that it was big of Kyle Shanahan that he did do that. A few more quotes here. Uh this is from the time when Kyle Shanahan he he showed us his phone of the actual photo from the hospital bed at Stanford. He said that was me 14 days ago. You can see my skull in the photo. That's what he said. That's what I mean when I say my plastic surgeon is awesome. I asked Shanahan if the bright light is affecting him because the weather here across the whole Bay Area or at least on the peninsula it's bright every day. So, he's only been out of practice for about 20 minutes in each of the past two days and a lot of times concussion symptoms are such that it's too bright then then you've got to go back inside. And Shannan said that the brightness actually isn't affecting him. He said, "Every concussion is different, and it's not the light that bothers me. It's more taking stuff in. Like noises bother me when two people talk to me at once. Music out there is killing me, but it's so much better than it was." And Shanahan did express confidence that he's going to be back at full capacity soon. Here's another quote. It crushed me hearing the other driver getting blamed for it and to hear people think that people are hiding something for me. Obviously, there's been some idiotic controversy about how long it it it took to get reported. Uh but that very clearly is is not something that is a cover up in this case. Shanahan said, "I think people are good people and recognize that it's a personal thing." Yes, this what happened right here was an accident. There was no alcohol, no drugs involved, no criminal activity involved. An accident is a personal thing. Now, ultimately, uh, this was going to hit the media and the 49ers figured, well, uh, we'll release this when training camp starts. This happened on July 14th. A lot of people on vacation because this was not a criminal situation. This was an accident. The course of action was to put out that statement which essentially coincided with the ESPN story when training camp began or the the day before training camp began. I think I was on my way or about to leave to the team facility for the opening press conference and obviously only John Lynch handled that. Shanahan said that he wishes that he could go take the lect turn for the press conference now but his concussion symptoms it wouldn't be a good situation. He says he's getting very emotional because of the concussion and he decided that he was okay meeting with a select group of writers in his office. He's wearing sweatpants and obviously still banged up. He's got the the cast on his lower left arm. He was okay meeting with a select group of writers in his office, but once I think that the concussion symptoms subside and he's ready to face the the bigger, brighter lights of an actual press conference, we will see Kyle Shanahan out there. He said, quote, "I was really lucky. I'm just lucky that I survived, that the other driver didn't get hurt, and that I didn't lose my eye." 49ers today had a jog through a training camp. They will continue with another practice tomorrow. We'll probably see Kyle Shanahan on the field for part of it, but you can put all the crazy conspiracies to rest. Kyle Shanahan took responsibility, took fault for the accident. I think kind of something big of him. I think that is something that an honest person would love to do, which which he did because you don't want that weighing on your conscience, especially because of the apparent clerical error that had the other driver at fault. We can continue praying for Kyle Shanahan's recovery. You can pray for his family. The other driver was not injured here, which is part of the good news coming out of all this. But very clearly a traumatizing incident for both Kyle Shanahan, his wife Mandy Shanahan, and of course the the the rest of his family. And we could be all be thankful that Kyle Shanahan is on his way to recovery, but that concussion and those symptoms are still very, very real. 49ers, as I said, had only a jog through today. They worked out four players. All four of them are defensive ends in the context of a 4-3 and outside linebackers in the context of a 34. And the 49ers ended up signing KJ Henry, a Clemson product initially drafted by Washington, a 255 pounder. And we know that Rahee Morris is going to run a little bit of 4-3 and a little bit of 34, probably more 4-3 than 34. title: A 49ers trade for Vita Vea just got WAY more feasible…
text: One of the NFL's largest players and most freakish athletes is right here from the Bay Area. He grew up just 6 miles from Levi's Stadium. And yes, Vita Vea does want a trade from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Maybe to the 49ers. According to The Athletic's Ted Nguyen, Vea wants to be traded to a California team and there are only three options, the Rams, the Chargers, and the Niners, or the Raiders. And yes, the 49ers should be interested. I mean, he rampaged through high school football in Milpitas, which is 6 miles away from Levi's Stadium. When I take BART down from the city here San Francisco to Levi's Stadium, sometimes I don't like to drive, I get off at Milpitas and I think of Vita Vea, who would fit with any team. A lot of people say, "Well, the 49ers have an attacking four-man front." Well, A, things are transitioning under Raheem Morris, and B, Vita Vea has been second in the entire NFL behind only Dexter Lawrence in pressures over the past 3 years with 62 pressures. He does that at the same time that he's a massive run-clogging fire hydrant at about 350 lbs. So, very Bay Area themed discussion here as we pan over towards sunset over the Golden Gate Bridge. Vita Vea played running back in high school at Milpitas. Running back, yes. And he was dominant as you would expect against high schoolers, a man amongst boys. Now, we talk about defensive tackle trades. Dexter Lawrence, the only player with more pressures from the defensive tackle position, that nose tackle position, than Vita Vea over the course of the past three seasons. He just was traded from the New York Giants to the Bengals for the number 10 overall pick. Now, Lawrence though was a couple years younger than Vita Vea. He was 28 years old at the time of the trade. Vita Vea is going to be 31 years old. Lawrence also had more time left on his contract, theoretically making him more expensive. My prediction is this. I think that Tampa Bay uh is not going to be able to trade him here in training camp. He's got 1 year left on his deal, 17 million per year. Premium defensive tackles like Vita Vea are commanding well over 20 million per year. If the Bucks don't want to pay him, I think they're going to hold out for a first or second round pick, but probably a first round pick that probably won't be satisfied here over the course of training camp. I don't think the 49ers would want to give away that premium of pick in what is lining up to be a premium 2027 NFL draft cuz you would have to pay Vita Vea 20 million on top of that. However, as time passes and we get closer to the NFL trade deadline, this is the type of move that the 49ers might really be tempted to make either as a rental for the rest of 2027 or if they have a look at Alfred Collins, C.J. West, obviously Osa Odighizuwa, and they say, "Well, we want to toss in a dominant dual-purpose defensive tackle into that mix to push us over the top into Super Bowl contention." Could be a trade that the 49ers are eventually really motivated to make ahead of the trade deadline, especially if Vita Vea would love to play for the team that is now based what 6 miles away from his high school. 49ers played at Candlestick back in the day when Vita Vea was playing high school ball here in the Bay Area, but now his family very, very near Levi's Stadium. So, the intrigue only grows, but yet this is a guy that you're You're going to say no to on your football team. It is a matter of price and the 49ers have so much salary cap space earmarked for Brock Purdy and and other players in future seasons. So, they've got to be careful with the finances and they've got to be careful with those 2027 draft picks, but some some fits might just be too good to be true. I spoke on 95.7 The Game about not just this, but everything that's happened so far in 49ers training camp. So, go ahead and enjoy. >> Hey David, how you been, man? What's going on? >> Good. I I forgot my glasses today, so it was really bright. Thankfully, didn't have a concussion to deal with, but um yeah, Kyle Kyle's been out there for 2 days and I'm guessing that his his limit time-wise is because it is really bright. There's not a cloud in the sky in July in Santa Clara. So, often coming off of a concussion, if you're still feeling those symptoms, then you have to stay indoors in in darker environment. But, he's been able to be out there for like 20 to 30 minutes per day. >> David, will you share with the audience the process of something like this? I have no idea when you started to get a little bit of info. I've been a little surprised that people I get it if you're curious, that's totally normal, but if you're like angry that you didn't get to know earlier, that kind of escapes me, but can you share with people what happened here for you and and as a journalist kind of how you handle something like this? >> Well, a few days before the announcement, I started to gather that there might be something pertaining to Kyle Shanahan that might limit his availability for the start of training camp, but there was never anything that I was able to to glean that was uh confirmed. So, there was nothing to to report. You know, you you don't just take every single rumor or slight piece of information. I think Tim Kawakami said that he had 15% of the story. You don't take 15% of a story and put it out there if you're a responsible reporter. Now, I know that in this age of clickbait, people will take 15% and fill in the remaining 85% and put out a basically a fake report and they don't care if it's accurate, they just care that they were first. So, maybe that standard or that lowering of standards has created a lowering of expectation for some people, but the truth of the matter in this instance is that Kyle Shanahan nearly lost his eye. Like Chris Sims, his best friend, went on the podcast today and said that Shanahan was very close to losing his eye and this was a traumatizing situation for both Kyle and for his family. The police have come out and said that there was no criminal activity here. There was alcohol or drugs were not involved, which, you know, you put all those things together, that makes this a private matter and it it nobody has to disclose it until it becomes something that affects the professional football team and and the 49ers did disclose it the day before training camp started. So, I don't think anybody missed anything here. I don't think that anything was put on public record because again, there was no uh criminal investigation, alcohol or drugs were not involved and I think that, you know, any reasonable, normal person would recognize that Kyle Shanahan is a human being, he's got a family, and that this was a traumatic event, and no one is entitled to information sooner than it naturally became available in this case. >> No one's entitled to it, David, and you went to Stanford and based on where I think that this happened, it happened right by Stanford University. Are you surprised that, considering it happened at 6:00 in the evening, are you surprised that there aren't other details or eyewitnesses who would have said initially within the first 11 days what had happened and who was involved? >> Yeah, I think that is mildly surprising, right? But it could have just been luck of circumstance that nobody Neither nobody recognized Kyle Shanahan. Uh not everybody in the Bay Area is a football fan, especially in Palo Alto. That area The Stanford football team, they they had some great teams when I was there that struggled to sell out of you know, inventing new prime numbers and develop doing much more important stuff than playing football, right? They were they were working on cures for cancer and stuff in that Stanford area. I don't I don't know what the situation was. I saw that the accident happened in Palo Alto. Um you know, if if there had had been somebody who recognized that Kyle Shanahan was in an accident and had taken it to social media, obviously the world would have known much sooner. Uh but but that didn't happen and instead the world found out what, 11 or 12 days after? And guess what? Nobody's life changed on the outside. And I would say that this was good for Kyle Shanahan and his family because they had to deal with that trauma. They're probably still dealing with that trauma. The last thing that I think they wanted was that and all this rampant speculation to get out in in the media, just knowing how um you know, how irresponsible social media can be. And and I think we also need to think about the other person in this accident. And that's that's nobody is talking about, but nobody goes out wants to get into a car accident. And it's going to be, you know, based on the details that we've heard, probably traumatizing for both parties. >> How How's De'Shawn Shivers look so far? >> He's looked really good. He's I mean, he's tall, right? He's 6'3, so he's got those long limbs, which you always want to see in in a wide receiver, especially somebody who you I think in the future the 49ers would love to see him play that X receiver position. Mike Evans has also looked awesome, though. So, that's his job for the time being, but Shivers the 49ers have this setup where you want So, they need a bigger slot receiver because they love running the the big slot and the small slot. Christian Kirk is probably going to be that small slot, but Shivers can play that big slot, but the way I see the the way he runs routes, the the length, the way I saw the physicality on tape in college, he can block. I think he has all the makings of of an X wide receiver over the course of the long haul in the 49ers uniform, but he he's caught everything thrown his way. He dropped only one pass at Ole Miss last year, so we know that he's got really good hands. I Guys, I just think he's a high floor guy, and I think this is a theme of the 49ers draft class, and this could be a good kind of comparative advantage to glean out of the draft in the new NIL era. You have a lot of players who played at at several different schools, who are transferring between schools, who are, you know, vying for bigger contracts, essentially many professionals, right? So, somebody like De'Shawn Shivers played at Washington State, he played at Oklahoma State, and then he played at Ole Miss. That means he's had to learn three different systems, and all three of those offenses used them in a different way. So, I mean, at Ole Miss it was screen passes and and go balls, and at Oklahoma State it was a lot of intermediate routes. The 49ers got in a guy who they feel is going to to more of a, you know, I I can't say finished product, but more of a complete product early on than receivers that you might have drafted five or six years ago just because he went through so much and so many different systems in college and I think that they're going to really reap the benefits of that here over the next few months. >> Do you think that they're going to change the scheme a little bit this year and go to more 11 personnel three wide receivers? It seems to me with the, you know, with George Kittle going to be trying to work his way into the season and the wide receiver room they have, do you think that that's going to be a shift that Kyle makes? >> Well, they didn't have the receiver help necessary to to do that a lot over the past two seasons. And in 2023 when they had that loaded offense, it was a different type of receiver room. I mean, Deebo Samuel was one of the headliners and he definitely wasn't a prototypical wide receiver. He's a great player, he's Deebo Samuel, but just wasn't what what you would normally think of in terms of a standard separator at at the Z receiver position. So, now that they've restocked that room and they've invested so much in it over the off season, I could definitely see that happening. And that's irrespective of George Kittle's availability. I think that you've got Mike Evans, he plays the X split end, prototypical body there, a future Hall of Famer. I mean, it doesn't get any better schematically than Mike Mike Evans at the X position. Ricky Pearsall is a pure Z flanker receiver who's going to really benefit from coming in motion. I mean, just a smooth smooth route runner. And then we we go to the big slot position with Deebo Samuel. I mean, you compare that with a single tight end set with George Kittle and you got really really good blockers out there, right? You got Evans at the X, you got Kittle at tight end, and you got Stribling at the F at the at the big slot. Even though that's a very very threatening pass formation, right? With three wide receivers and a tight end, this is all on catch the pass catch the ball. That is also something that you can run out of with lethal efficiency. So, that's what Kyle Shanahan is going to be going for and I think that you're on to something. I think you're going to see a lot of these guys on the field at the same time. >> David, how do you handicap the running back race behind Christian McCaffrey between Jordan James and JaMycal Hasty? >> I think that Jordan James has been in the system for a year. That gives him the early leg up. So, obviously Christian McCaffrey is at the top of the list there. Then it's who's going to be that running back two and you know, then the question beyond that is how often does the running back two see the field to give Christian McCaffrey a breather and I think the limiting factor there in the past had been that they didn't really trust anyone nearly as much as Christian McCaffrey to run the right routes and to keep the pass game humming. So, if both James and JaMycal Hasty can earn Shanahan's trust in that regard, I think that they'll be able to spell Christian McCaffrey more than the second running back has in the past. Now, JaMycal Hasty has looked like he's got some juice. He really does. It's going to come down to him learning the route tree and establishing himself as a pass protector at the NFL level because it's all about trust, right? You can't yank Christian McCaffrey off the field and somebody come in and blow off a play, maybe even blow up the season given how competitive this NFC West race is going to be. So, you really have to trust who you're going to put there instead. That's why Jordan Mason Jordan James currently has the leg up and that's the ground that JaMycal Hasty is going to have to try to make up here over the course of training camp in the preseason. >> Impossible to really gauge defensive players when, you know, you haven't padded up yet and you're not really getting after other teams, but just Nick Bosa in his movement, how does he look to you as he tries to come back from another ACL injury? >> So, I stepped out on the field yesterday and I was absolutely floored because Bosa was right in front of me and it does not look like he tore his ACL. Especially does not look like he tore it what his third ACL in his in his football career. And he was I thought I said this to myself and I said this to somebody who's standing right next to me on the field. I thought that he looked in better shape than he did entering last season before the ACL. I said that before Trent Williams did the same exact thing after practice. So, I think that many people who have been around Nick Bosa are are thinking the same thing. He looks in phenomenal shape and I don't know why I was surprised. I I guess I figured, you know, okay, well, if this is the third time that it's happened, it's going to take longer to recover. But I think that Nick Bosa has taken lessons from his battle hall uh notebook, you know, from his from his previous ACL tears. I've I'm sure he's taken and applied lessons of rehab and recovery. And the first really good news of 49ers training camp was that he wasn't on that pup list. And to me that that was mildly surprising because normally they've they played it safe in these situations. When I saw him the next day, I understood why he wasn't on the pup list. It's because he looks completely physically ready to go. >> David Lombardi, SF Standard. I I think we're already starting to hear this D fence um is threatening to look a lot different under Raheem Morris. How how would you sort of describe what you're seeing? >> Paul, I'll tell you what I noticed on like the fifth play on the first day and it was right in front of me. Christian McCaffrey split out into the flat on a pass pattern and who was covering him? Marcellus Hightower was covering Christian McCaffrey in the flat. It didn't go well for Marcellus Hightower, but it doesn't usually go well for anybody trying to cover Christian McCaffrey. That's why he's been a cheat code for 10 years now, but it just gives you a little bit of a glimpse into some of these five-man fronts, which are based in a 3-4 concept, which means that edge rushers are going to be dropping back into coverage a little bit more often. People have raised concerns about Ronald Heights weight or or lack thereof. He's about 240, but uh that's very very intentional. He's a defensive end who has 3-4 outside linebacker flex capability. He dropped into coverage at Texas Tech. He He turn on the tape and the third play he's breaking up the pass at Texas Tech. Now, the reason you do that is not to have to Ronald Heights covering players like Christian McCaffrey on a regular basis. The reason that you do that is that you muddy up the vision for the opposing quarterback and for the opposing offensive lineman. So, I think a five-man front is going to fit the run differently and I think the 49ers own run game has a wrench thrown into it by five-man fronts, which have been adopted by most of the league at this point. But B, in terms of the pass game and rushing the quarterback, and we know the 49ers only had 20 sacks last year, which was the least in the league. You can really throw an offense into a blender if you start rushing less predictably. And and I think that's the main point here. I think most of the time we're going to see Ronald Heights roaring around the edge. We've heard the Dee Ford comparison. He's got tremendous burst. He's going to be opposite Nick Bosa. They'll be rushing with four. I think most of the time we will see that, but I do think that the 49ers will have uh tricks in their repertoire to mix things up to make those standard four-man rushes all the more effective because offenses will just have to think about so much more now that Raheem Morris has incorporated it. >> How much does Omenihu uh make all of that possible? In other words, his presence in the interior of the defensive line, how much does that help something like the things you're describing? >> Well, that was That's a great question because I think it was the biggest weakness of this team last year. Obviously, when they lost Bosa, uh they went from I thought Super Bowl favorites, they beat Seattle on the road, and week one and Bosa sealed the game. But, I think the loss of Bosa last year put the 49ers from Super Bowl favorites to uh a fringe long shot team. And they almost, you know, pulled off a huge miracle. They still won 13 games. But, that was crazy to me because they lost the edge rush with Bosa. The thing about that team though last year is that even with Bosa, they were still suspect at best, and I That's a nice word. They weren't good rushing from the interior. They were relying a lot on somebody like Uche Gross-Matos who had injury issues of his own. He was really a defensive end who flexed out of defensive tackle. They did not have a natural pass rushing defensive tackle. So, why they paid Javon Hargrave all that money heading into the 2023 season. But, he got hurt. That didn't work out. So, that's been a a big glaring gap in this defense. They they need that quality interior rusher, and that's who Osa Odighizuwa is. So, I think it opens up a lot for this defense, man. It becomes especially lethal once you pair him with Nick Bosa. Because Bosa's the guy that commands a lot of attention on the outside. Now, you have somebody who commands a ton of attention on the inside who has a high win rate on the inside. And you could start talking about winning as a pocket collapsing line, not just winning in one spot of the defensive line. With all the mobile quarterbacks that we have in this league now, if you're only winning on one spot, that quarterback can run away. But, if you're rushing in cohesion, and that typically takes at least one plus DT and one plus defensive end. And then all of a sudden you can start collapsing the pocket effectively. >> David, real quick, with this trade request from from Vita Vea to the Tampa Bay Bucs, while we're talking defensive tackle, any chance the 49ers get in on that conversation? >> Well, he's 30 years old, so I don't think that he would cost as much as he did a few years ago. That being said, he's a premium player, so it it probably won't be cheap. Vita Vea went to high school in Milpitas, 6 miles from Levi's Stadium. So, I don't know if he grew up a 49ers fan, but I did see, I think Ted Nguyen, who writes for The Athletic, has a source that says that Vita Vea wants to play in in California or for the Raiders. And so he wants to be close to family, I think is the translation there. Well, you can't be any closer to family than 6 miles from where you grew up. I think he's the biggest dude in the NFL, right? He he weighs 350 plus. Um, Vita Vea is special because normally guys who are 350 plus are just fire hydrants who take up a blockers and and are good run defenders, but he can also rush the passer. So, he is a unicorn in that regard. So, you know, if I'm an executive in the league, if I'm happy to get into a bidding war for this guy because he is such a a unique talent, even if he is 30 years old. And if a lot of executives are thinking that way, then it's probably going to be really hard to to get him, but uh, I also think it wouldn't be very smart of Tampa Bay to to not figure out a way to to resign him because he's been durable as well over the course of his career. But, hey, you can always dream if you're the 49ers, right? I think he'd pair really nicely there as a big DT next to also big Azuwa, who's a smaller defensive tackle. He's like 290. Vita Vea is like 360, so that's actually 60 60 or 70 lbs with this guy. He's He's massive. >> Uh David, great stuff and thank you for your flexibility. Really appreciate you coming on today. >> Yeah, no problem. It was great talking to you guys. Hope to see you around. >> Absolutely, we will, Dave.
