Our defensive coaches have done a great job installing the defense. And then same thing on the offensive side of the ball with the players we brought in. Um the the scheme, the coaching, uh really been pleased with everything that that's gone on. There's a great energy in the building on both sides. So, I think when you you bring all those things together, I think uh you know that the staff has done a really good job of surrounding themselves with with opportunity to win. >> Adam, we've talked to Dan um about this over the offseason, but what do you like about the schemes that Blau and Donte are bringing? Like just schematically, what >> what do you like about you guys are going to feature? Yeah, I you know, me personally, you know, I love I think first off just watching those guys coach and teach and just it's been really impressive to see both of those guys live and in action in the meeting rooms and then on the practice field the way they coach and they teach and and really the whole staff. Uh obviously it starts with Q at the top and then those guys as it trickles down. Um but then offensively, you know, there there we we're going to be more multiple. We have, you know, a lot of different personnel groupings and a lot of different ways to attack you. Um, I think, you know, it it really it's more quarterback friendly, I think, in a way. And I think that'll really help Jaden. Like I said earlier, he doesn't have to always make a play. You know, we're going to try to scheme up things so and and have answers so he doesn't always have to make a play. And I think the same way on defense, you know, the defense is um is designed to, you know, you always want to have the pen last. And so the defense, we have a lot of different ways to attack you and different things we can change up. So, um, you know, we have answers, you know, going into in the play and then, you know, during like at the line of scrimmage as well. So, um, yeah, couldn't be happier with with how everything went in the offseason. Really, really excited for it really. >> Adam, when it comes to the receiver position, um, you know, Terry McLaren is probably the only player that you would lock in as a starter at this point. Uh what made you guys comfortable going into training camp having that position be, you know, pretty wide open as both as slide receiver and on the outside in terms of competition and seeing where that leads you in terms of who's who ends up starting. Yeah, I mean I think just watching those guys, the way they work, the way they've worked in the classroom and and really I'm glad you pointed out Terry, his leadership has been fantastic like throughout the off season and and carrying the young guys along and teaching them and and coaching them and being uh that type of a guy in the room. But just the way the guys have progressed uh how much we've invested in that position in terms of draft capital, I think we've invested a lot. And then our guys have done a really good job in in the free Asia market too, bringing in some real good competition there. So what what it what it does is create great competition and great competition will you know the cream will rise to the top. So I'm confident that those guys will will all uh take a step up. >> Adam, what's your process going through getting this roster from 90 to 53? Where how involved are you in the day-to-day and figuring out who should be there and who shouldn't be? Yeah, it's it's um we're all involved and that that's what's great about this place. We all talk daily and and we're we have meetings all the time about, you know, roster and and just the 53 and it's really, you know, we look at it, we've said it a bunch of times, but it's really 70 and not 53. We we look at those practice squad guys as an extension of our team and and oftentimes they're they're playing quite a bit. So, uh, that makes it a little easier to look at, you know, and understand, okay, we have these guys on the 53, but we also have these guys that that are really, they're all commanders and they're all going to be expected to play at some time. But, um, we're evaluating these guys every day. We're watching practice, during practice, we're watching the tape after practice. We're meeting on it. We're meeting on how they do in the classroom, how they're learning, how they're understanding their positions, how versatile they are. Can they play more than one position? You know, can they be more versatile on game day? Do they play special teams? Does that help their their roster value? And those types of things. I could probably go on and on, but there there's a lot of conversations and just back and forth and and just uh really tons of different things that go into that equation to to get the best team for us. >> Hey guys, DQ, you've mentioned a few times you want to run your most competitive camp. Yep. >> Now that we're here and it's about to start, like what specifically should we be looking for? What might look different? I think what you'll see um you'll find some competitions like in an everyday sense and I think that's one of the very best ways that we'll get better you know like just good on good some situations like into tomorrow there'll be a two-point play competition best out of five and those are the moments I want to I think you'll find some game scenario and situations in every practice two minutes and four minutes last plays setting up field goals so those are the ones we're trying to even a difficult camp also be like stressful you you know, can we put oursel in these spots so when we the air gets thin that we feel like that's our space and we're going to work really hard into that spot. So tough camp doesn't always mean like, you know, banging all the time. It's like the execution, the elevation. Think of like you and I is boxing the sparring to getting ready to go compete. And if we think in those ways, that's what I'm looking for. And there'll be days where it goes one side versus the other. And so I feel a hunger from the team. So they're ready to get into that. And Adam, one for you, just in a general sense, as you're always looking to improve the team, when you're evaluating guys to maybe bring in for workouts, whatever, what role, if any, does kind of a player's social media have in that evaluation process. [laughter] >> That's a good roundabout question. >> Badass. You are straight badass right there. >> But, um, no, we I mean, we look at everything, JP. I mean, it's a great question, but we do look at everything and and um you know, we want to make sure it's the right player to to to be in our locker room, in our bloodstream and in our culture and and you know, we often, you know, we we look at that stuff. I mean, it's not always the first thing we look at. Obviously, you're looking at the tape and you talk to the the the teams that the players have been on and and how they were in the locker room, the players that have played with them and and so on and so forth to to make those decisions. But um you know that's not not usually a huge part of it. Usually >> well played [laughter] both of >> DQ. You mentioned fostering that culture of competition. I'm curious when you're looking back at this camp six weeks from now. How do you know it was successful? How do you define that success? >> Yeah, that's a good way to to go about it. And sometimes we'll let's start at the end and work back. you know, what are some of the things that we want to gain in that space? When you're talking about new systems, you really want to say, how elevated can we get our execution? You know, because through the spring, you're developing your individual skills so much with the players. It's so devoted to them developing their skills. When you get into the fall and in training camp, in the fall, it's really about the team development and the team growth. And so so much of the offseason we try to make so specific about this player, the skills you need for this thing and then as you get into camp. So if we were going to work back from the end, how did our team grow? How did our execution go in all three phases? By that point, you're hopeful some roles begin to emerge. It's way too early to call into that. And so let's let that play and we're we're ready to do that. And so we'd like to see that execution go. We won't be February version of our team will be much better than the August version, but the September one will be much better than the one today and it'll take a lot of work to get there and like the hunger, the competitiveness, the camp that we're going to throw, like all that leads into that. >> Good evening, gentlemen. >> Uh coach, got a question for you. Start off with um you mentioned unscripted periods during your practices to kind of try to ramp up some of that emotional uh competitiveness. like how from your teaching experience kind of how how will that impact the the value that the guys get out of those sessions? >> It's uh it's not just for the players, that's also for the staff as well and uh calling the different down distances, the personnel groups that you have to put in. So, as much as we can to get gameike uh without it being in the game, you want to dig into that space. You'll see shot clocks, you're going to see us trying to fit into those space from officials to being here, the joint practices. So, having having as many of those unscripted as you can. It's not just for the players to put the stress. It's for us as the staff as well. And so that's why in some of these competitions, I I won't tell the players or the staff what is going to be, what's the scenario. I want us to have to think quickly on our feet. And so that's some examples of that where the calls come up and uh different looks, different plays. And so that's one part of it. >> And then Adam with Rul Douglas, just kind of curious what was it a deficiency in the room? Was it something Russul adds that that led to you guys bringing him in? >> Yeah, I think um kind of goes back to we were saying before, too. We're always looking to add really good players and Rul's been a really good player in this league for for a long time. He's he's played at a high level. He's started a lot of games. He started a lot of games recently and he always performs. So, um when you have an opportunity to to add to that to that room, you know, it's not a deficiency in the room at all. You just want to make each room as strong as it can be. So, getting him in, we were really excited about that. And so, uh, we just got a chance to meet him yesterday. He's big and, uh, he's played a lot of good balls, so we're we're excited to have him. >> Guys, good to see you again, Adam. We'll start with you. We're all talking about wide receivers here, but curious your take on Chiga Conquo because he almost plays like a wide receiver and how does he kind of fit into the uh, conversation of do I add a receiver, do I not add a receiver knowing his skill set of he could be a receiver in a sense? >> Yeah, that's a great observation. He's an outstanding receiver. He's outstanding in the pass game. He's great after the catch, you know, and and he's also a really good blocker, a good competitive blocker. He's not the biggest tight end. He's not John Bates, but really [clears throat] love the way he competes as a blocker and how he executes there, too. So, he's got a really good skill set, but he does help us quite a bit in the pass game. So, he allows you to be a little bit more multiple. You know, you can go more two tight end sets, you can go one tight end set, it's like you almost have four receivers on the field. So, uh he provides a lot of versatility in where he can line up and what he can do for us. and and how when he gets the ball in his hands then he's pretty magical. >> And DQ, leadership question for you. Obviously losing Bobby Wagner, big voice in that locker room. You have Terry McLaren, uh, a great voice. Who are you looking for in terms of a leadership perspective? Jaden, year number three, how is he going to evolve as a leader? And then on defense, who are you kind of leaning on to be that voice in that locker room? >> Yeah, I'm excited to to find that out and uh Bobby's rare and uh in the most biggest sense, you know, that you can say that. There's a number of like really strong leaders, you know, some that are still emerging and I'm excited to see that. This off seasonason you felt Serill in every sense of the way. You felt Robertson in the, you know, in this in his sense of like the way he wanted to compete. Lvu has that to him in that same space. So, as we're going into that spot, Reeves has always been somebody that I've looked at as a leader, more on teams, but on the defensive side. Uh, but there's a number of guys that I'm I'm looking to see take that step. And sometimes you need that spot to be available to do that. And so where we all look to Bobby in that spot, maybe now now is my time to go for it and dig in. And so moments like this camp to lead and find your space. It's a new system, so everybody's on the same page in terms of the knowledge of it. I'm excited to see that. >> 100%. I think Adam referred to it earlier. you felt his hunger from the beginning of the offseason, the way he went after it, just his ability to understand this scheme that quickly. It's not easy, you know, for anybody to do and he often makes the difficult things look easy, but through the offseason program in the summer and getting into here, he absolutely has that. >> Uh, hey DQ, this one's for you. uh asked Jaden uh you know in mini camp looking back to last season how much does it motivate him the struggles that he went through he kind of said he's not talking about last season so I'm just curious as coach going into the training camp day one you know this week you know how do you go into this in terms of learning the lessons from last year but also turning the page forward and making sure like everybody knows this is a new year >> yeah you're right and trust me when I say we learned every lesson and took it everyone that we could find from last uh we're ready to apply them. But honestly, it is about the now. Like it'd be crazy not to say you wouldn't take that lesson and pull it forward and apply it, but it is about the here, the now. I'm excited for you guys to feel the energy of the team, uh their readiness, um their swagger. So, as we get started into this, I'm excited for you guys to feel that. >> Super quick for AP, uh the defense as a whole, um you know, this whole group looks totally different from how it did last year. How do you feel about, you know, the whole unit, you know, from the front seven to the secondary and how they are going to be able to gel together? >> Yeah, I think the word excited because there's so many different things we can do. You know, there's it's very multiple. There's and and not only within the scheme, but within the players and how we get different players on the field in different roles and their strengths and these different groups of these three three guys or these four guys and and trying to attack you in different ways. So, uh, really excited with, uh, it's just it gives Dante a lot to to really play with and then, um, just to kind of see the guys grow into their roles. So, I'm excited to see how that unfolds probably just like you guys. >> Uh, DQ, I know you're a guy who likes to come in with a plan for training camp and preseason and all that kind of stuff. As you talk about wanting to get more competition and running more unscripted portions of practice, as much as that happens, you guys are going to the players are going to get to know each other. They're going to get familiar with each other. So, as you have new two new coordinators and you're going into the joint practices and preseason, how much will, I guess, kind of usage be different than maybe in years past based on the fact that there's a lot of new faces and new concepts and new voices in the players heads and >> well, for sure that, you know, like in the two joint practices, those are those are good opportunities where there's new looks, new players, new matchups. So, Adam and I, we both like that and what that is. And so, this year we have Miami that's going to come here. We're looking forward to them being here. We'll also do the one uh at Baltimore. So, those are important evaluation days, you know, like we were talking about the selection of the team earlier and the selection is ongoing and so moments of competition like that going against one another other teams, it all kind of is a big part of it, but at the end of it, I think it still comes down to the execution, the growth and see where these guys can take it. But uh like as far as playing more in the preseason or not, that's something that uh we haven't, you know, dug into at this point this year. There wouldn't be any more or less um you know, from a philosophy standpoint. >> Uh for both of you in terms of uh some of the guys who are on PP list, namely Trey Amos, can I know you don't have to talk about the injuries, but can you shed any light as to why he's still out because it timeline seemed like maybe he should be back by now? >> Yeah, I think with with Trey, he's doing really well. I think the first thing I'll say is he's been outstanding in his rehab and and really, you know, taken all the the things that the medical team has asked him to do and and done them really really well. Um, with him just had a little soft tissue soreness in the offseason, so we wanted to just take it slow. So, he's actually he's doing really well right now. Just had a report on him earlier. He should be back soon as well. Just wanted to be overly cautious there. And, uh, but he's doing he's doing great. He'll be back pretty soon. And then um Adam for you as well. You know, it's fair to say when you when you came in here in 2024 that the roster was not in a great position. You've now had three off seasons. How close do you feel you are to getting it? I know it's always a work in progress, but how close do you feel you are to getting it where you want it to be? >> Um you know, like you said, it's always a work in progress and it's it's always you always want to keep trying to find ways to make it better and and different avenues to do that. So, um, what I what I can say is that really excited about this team, really excited about that the players we've added, the players that that, um, have come in here and the players that were here before us that that are still here now that that have really all grown in their own ways, too. So, um, this is, you know, every year I feel like you say, you're really excited this year. I'm I'm as excited as I've ever been and really, you know, this there's a ton of great energy here u from all aspects of the building to to really see how this is going to unfold and and I'm excited to see it. So, feel really good about it. Ben, >> hi. >> Hi, Adam and Coach. Uh coach, this is for you. Uh as far as learning, uh the offense and the defense, where do you see the players at with uh learning both on both sides of the ball as they head into 2026? Yeah, it started into the offseason program from the learning standpoint into the classroom, the teaching and so could that be in the NFL today where you're adding players to it. It has to be relatable. It has to be learnable. It also has to be from the teaching, you know, standpoint something that they can give back to you. So, I thought they worked hard in that sense to get the system in place. And now over and over and over can we get those repetitions down? Usually you start with the bigger volume and then you start pulling down about the things that you really want to feature. And so that'll take a few weeks for us to get into that. David and Dante, we have like a you know 11 or 12 day install schedule that we go through and you start pairing down after that. But it'll it'll take a few weeks for us to put the whole package in again. They've gone through it entirely once and we'll go through the whole system again. Um now adding different people into it in the spring. maybe somebody's banged up, didn't get enough or vice versa. And so, uh, it is a big part of that process and I'm excited to see where they can take it. >> And, and starting out tomorrow, what would we what would be the major emphasis that you want to hit the ground running and the message to the team as they get started? >> Yeah, we had talked um, right off the bat because we have like practice habits that could really separate us and for us to really play well, we know how important that is. That's the attention to detail. the specifics at, you know, the skills to isolate for this play for this play. And if we can get to that space over and over again, that's what we're looking to do. But I think what you'll see tomorrow is like fantastic energy from the group. I think you're going to see real speed and we're going to try to feature that in the best ways. Tomorrow and the following day are going to be a big red zone emphasis. And so that's part of our ramp up as we're going to go as opposed to the old days. You just went, you know, as fast and as hard as you can from day one. And so it takes about a week to really get the whole ramp up process underway. So the first two days will be more red zone. We'll dip down then go back into the regular field. So a lot of red zone emphasis tomorrow. And that's what will be the emphasis for the team. >> Hey there. Um this one is for coach. >> Okay. >> Um there's been some conversation I guess maybe amongst us about the green dot and who wears the green dot. So what are some of those factors that go into ultimately making the decision about who has that? >> Yep. So first thing I would say it's on the field who's going to play the most in the packages and uh you want elite communication. Um it's from Donte, you know, you know, his voice into the next person to get it out. In practice, we're able to utilize a number of different people and at times you can change from period to period or day to day. And so that will also be part of the ongoing process. Um, I have full confidence in just about all these guys because at some point or another, we put that stress onto them to see where they're at. Uh, Sunny's more than capable of doing that. Frankie as well. It's been nice to see, you know, this version of Frankie with Sunny and we were talking about Wags earlier where it was so nice for Frankie to see Bobby and now you see it in another way and he's got great practice habits, but wondering how that command is. That's part of playing the position. Uh we've done it at safety before in the past. Um but I anticipate it'll likely come from the linebacker group, but um it'll even be in the preseason games honestly to see, you know, who we feel best with, but nothing that has to be decided anytime soon. >> Martenzi Johnson with notice. Uh this can be for both of you. What have you seen from Nick Allegretti to make you comfortable rolling him out as center even though that's not a position he's played for most of his career? >> Yeah, I can start off with it. Um, one like high level competitor and so we've played well with Nick in the lineup uh that be it at guard but interior that's his space. He's played center, he's played guard even though you may not have seen him in some of the games like every week he was you know repping inside to go. So, um, that was a big piece of it. We got a lot of faith and confidence in him. It's another one of the positions that we do have competition that we're going for it. But, um, if Nick was playing on defense, he'd be a green dot. This is one of the smartest guys on our team now. Like, you talk about putting it under control. That's part of playing center. And he has that targeting. Who's this? Where's the protection going? Uh, so we've got a lot of confidence in him. Uh, one hell of a competitor and so he's one of those guys and you don't bet against that. You know, might be a new but you don't do that with everybody but somebody for him no doubt you do it. >> Yeah, I'd probably just echo what DQ said and I think the biggest thing one he's he's played it a lot. He's he's played all the positions inside so he's more than capable of all three of those. Um but what stands out to to me with Nick is just his leadership, his his command, his confidence. Um the way the guys gravitate and listen to them and so that that's a big part of it. Knowing knowing what to do, knowing where to go, knowing where to direct the guys, just the calling up in the huddle, it's a big deal. So, um have a ton of confidence in him, have a ton of confidence in Julie and Matt, too. So, it'll be a great competition, but um you know, uh for Nick just, you know, I think the world of him, the whole the whole team thinks the world of him. And so, um we all have confidence in him. >> He's as easy a trusted competitor as you can find. Like, you just you count on him and he's going to be in the right spot making the right call at the right time even when it gets chaotic I should say especially when it does like this look didn't come up in the practice okay is what we're going to do and you have to be in the fire some to have that calm in the chaos >> it's a big deal >> thanks guys appcate

title: FINAL 53: Commanders Roster Cuts Start With WR, OL And Defensive Front
text: Roster cuts aren't just about internal battles. They're about how Adam Peters and Dan Quinn want to shape the 2026 Washington Commanders. >> You are [music] Locked On Commanders, your daily podcast on the Washington Commanders, part of the Locked On Podcast Network, your team every day. >> Welcome inside today's episode of Locked On Commanders. I'm your host, your guy on the ground, David Harrison. And today's episode is brought to you by Call Sheet. For a limited time, download the Call Sheet app and use the code locked on, all one word, to get up to $500 in bonus credits when you trade $25. On today's episode, cut down choices, decide which good players will still lose out on a roster spot, and the secondary squeeze reaches every corner of the roster. But first, Washington's deepest rooms are competing across positional lines. We're talking about training camp battles here on the eve of training camp. Players, veteran players are reporting literally as we speak. The entire roster is going to be in Ashburn by the time we get the day over with. We'll hear from Dan Quinn, Adam Peters later on Tuesday. And then Wednesday, it all gets started, man. Training camp practice number one, it's here. And then Saturday, I'm going to see a whole bunch of you fans out at practice for back together weekend. It's going to be a great time. So, we're going to talk about training camp battles. Every player's competing inside his own position room for roster spots, of course, but that's not really how the final roster works. The seventh receiver, for example, might actually be competing not just with other receivers, but with a fourth running back, or with a fourth tight end, or a tenth offensive lineman, an extra defensive back, or a core special teams player. Based on the roster, there are five rooms that I see specifically where the numbers get a little bit crowded. And of course, because this is also supposed to be informative, but entertaining, I'm going to make some predictions. So, you can call me out on them, or you can applaud me for them, or you can just kind of stay even-keeled, like Switzerland and just wait to see what the results are later on in the off season or in the preseason at roster cut down day. So, this The order we're going to talk about this, wide receivers, O line, D line, secondary, quarterback, and running back are going to be kind of the same there together. Washington currently has 87 players active on the roster for practice starting on Wednesday. Trey Ames, Dorance Armstrong, Dietrich Wise Jr., and Fred Davis II all active but on the active injury {slash} non-football illness designation list. So, they will not be practicing. Eventually, the Washington Commanders will have to get down to 53 men after preseason, but that means this isn't just about identifying starters. Of course, you're looking at your depth, you're looking at your practice squad. Remember, Dan Quinn always talks about this being a 70-man roster, not a 53-man roster. So, that means those practice squad elements and all those things absolutely play a role in what the Washington Commanders are getting ready to do. So, eventually, the Commanders got to cut this down. How many players do they keep at each position? Which backups can they think they can they might be able to dress on game day? Cuz remember, they only get 47 on game day. Who contributes on special teams? Who provides multiple position flexibility? Which young players are the Commanders willing to expose to waivers? Cuz that's another part of this, too. You want to put a guy on practice squad, you got to waive him first, and that means somebody else might come in and snatch him up, right? They've got 11 active receivers. That's where we're going to start off this conversation. We're not going to name every single player in every single group, but this one is the most talked about position group in the in the entire offseason. So, we are. Terry McLaurin, Antonio Williams, Dyami Brown, Cam Sims, Dax Milne, Kyric McGowan, Jalen Jefferson, Luke McCaffrey, Jeudy Johnson, Chris Hilton Jr., Drayden Jayden Bradley, Jacobi Jones, and Nick Nash. The room has several different competitions all happening at once cuz not all these receivers are the same, and they're not all battling to fill the same role for the Washington Commanders. Now, at the top, you got Terry McLaurin, and of course, Antonio Williams, third-round pick this year. They're going to be a part of the bigger offensive plan this season. Beyond them, training camp is going to establish a lot of these things, right? The pecking order of the receivers that are on the roster. Which players can line up in multiple spots in David Blough's offense? Who can also contribute to special teams? Keeping six receivers is probably the expected number, right? But it's going to require Washington to release five of these guys from their active group. Probably stash some of them, or they will stash some of them on their practice squad, right? Keeping seven of them, you still have four departing names, and the seventh receiver then takes a spot away from another position. So, you got to make sure that math works as well. So, I think the final receiver spot or spots could come down to return ability, kick and punt coverage ability, positional flexibility, blocking availability. Health is obviously going to be a big part of this, whether the offense needs that certain type of receiver on the roster, and whether Washington values a developmental player over, say, a veteran who's more prepared to impact this year. Washington might like seven or eight of these guys by the end of this whole thing, but that doesn't mean it can create all of those jobs on Sunday. So, my prediction right now, Washington's keeping six. And as much as I think Van Jefferson has really showed up, really showed out, and I do think that he's a guy we all need to pay attention to, and I'm certainly going to be paying attention to right now, can't give him too much credit, can't get too far ahead of ourselves. I think he'll be the most notable player left out. Also, by the way, kind of thinking maybe Washington only keeps three tight ends. We're going to see a lot of 12 personnel, and we're going to see some 13 personnel, but then you got enough big guys, additional, you know, eligible eligible receiver linemen that you can use, and you got enough of a combination in the three tight ends, Shuga with John Bates, and Senate. I kind of am I'm on the fence of whether or not I think they're going to keep four tight ends. So, currently, my prediction is three tight ends. Now, you move to the offensive line group, and the Washington Commanders have 15 offensive line men linemen right now. Now, if you look at their official roster, only one is listed as a center. It's Matt Golden, but we know Nick Allegretti has been getting the center reps for the starting team, all this kind of stuff.
